title: Identification of interleukin-11 as a comorbid risk factor for prostate cancer and Alzheimer's disease using integrated bioinformatics and machine learning.
study_design: translational/bioinformatic (multi-cohort transcriptomics + ML gene prioritization + in vitro/in vivo functional validation + ADNI cross-sectional cohort)
data_source_detail: AD: GSE48350, GSE5281, GSE28146 (GEO); PCa training: TCGA-PRAD (n=499 tumor+52 normal); PCa external validation: DKFZ2018 (n=321), MSKCC (n=140), GSE116918 (n=257), GSE21034 (n=131), GSE107299 (n=106); single-cell: GSE141445 (13 PCa tissues); ADNI cohort (n=215) for serum IL11-CSF biomarker cross-sectional analysis
data_modality_detail: bulk RNA-seq (TCGA-PRAD) + microarray (GEO AD datasets, DKFZ2018, MSKCC, GSE cohorts); scRNA-seq (GSE141445) for cell-of-origin localization
algorithm: Random Forest (classification, AD vs control) + LASSO Cox regression (survival, TCGA-PRAD); WGCNA for module/gene discovery upstream
input_features: 10-gene AD-PCa comorbidity signature (NDRG4, ISG15, IL11, ENO2, DYNC1I1, DNASE1, ATP6V1G2, ATCAY, ANLN, AGAP9) derived from intersection of DEGs and WGCNA modules shared between AD and PCa
biomarker_result: 10-gene AD-PCa comorbidity risk score signature anchored by IL11
performance_value: Time-dependent AUC for PCa progression-free interval (TCGA-PRAD training): 1-yr 0.78, 3-yr 0.73, 5-yr 0.70; log-rank P<0.001. External validation: DKFZ2018 log-rank P=0.001 (AUC>0.8 for 3-/5-yr); MSKCC log-rank P=0.023.
validation_detail: Risk score formula and cutoff (derived in TCGA-PRAD) applied unchanged to two independent external PCa cohorts, DKFZ2018 (n=321) and MSKCC (n=140); no indication of re-fitting, consistent with genuine external validation.
key_finding: IL11 was the top-ranked gene in a 10-gene AD-PCa comorbidity risk score that stratifies PCa progression-free survival (AUC 0.78/0.73/0.70 at 1/3/5-yr, TCGA-PRAD; validated in DKFZ2018 and MSKCC); functionally, IL11 promoted PCa growth/invasion (in vitro/in vivo) and induced AD-like cognitive dysfunction and hippocampal amyloid-beta deposition in mice, with corroborating serum-CSF associations in a 215-participant ADNI cross-sectional cohort.
limitations_as_stated: NR (not captured in extracted Abstract/Intro/Methods/partial Results excerpt; Discussion/Limitations section not reached in pilot .txt)
other_key_outcomes: Primary manuscript emphasis is mechanistic/translational (IL11 as bidirectional PCa-AD comorbidity driver, validated via murine orthotopic/subcutaneous xenografts, Morris water maze cognitive testing, and immunofluorescence); the ML risk-score model functions mainly as a gene-prioritization/discovery tool rather than as a standalone clinical prediction target. Single-cell analysis localized IL11 to CAFs (Fibro_IL11+) with distinct EMT/immunosuppressive pathway activation.
extraction_note: Scope borderline per inherited appraisal_note (AD comorbidity focus vs GU biomarker scope): study is primarily a dual-disease mechanistic/functional paper; the prognostic ML signature is a secondary discovery output rather than the central clinical-prediction contribution. Funding/COI/limitations not present in the read excerpt (pp.1-12); would need full PDF read past Results to confirm, not done here since these are not minimum-for-complete fields.

title: Machine learning-based identification of hub genes and prognostic biomarkers in prostate cancer.
study_design: Retrospective TCGA-PRAD bioinformatics with WGCNA, ML BCR prognostic model, and in vitro cell-line qRT-PCR/ELISA validation
data_source_detail: TCGA-PRAD RNA-seq (501 primary tumor + 52 normal); 70/30 stratified train/holdout split for model evaluation
data_modality_detail: Bulk RNA-seq log2(CPM+1)
algorithm: LASSO Cox (10-fold CV) and random forest consensus; SVM and XGBoost compared
input_features: WGCNA/PPI hub genes EZH2, CDK1, AURKA (three-gene risk score)
biomarker_result: Three-gene BCR risk score (EZH2, CDK1, AURKA)
performance_value: Time-dependent AUC 0.821, 0.842, 0.836 at 1/3/5 yr (TCGA-PRAD); HR 3.21 for BCR-free survival (log-rank P<0.0001)
validation_detail: Single TCGA-PRAD cohort with 70/30 holdout; authors state no independent external validation cohort.
key_finding: A three-gene risk score stratified BCR-free survival with strong time-dependent discrimination and linked hub-high tumors to immunosuppressive infiltration patterns.
limitations_as_stated: Model validated only within TCGA-PRAD; immune infiltration from bulk deconvolution; in vitro validation in cell lines only.
other_key_outcomes: Prognostic nomogram with DCA; qRT-PCR/ELISA confirmation of hub gene overexpression in PCa cell lines.
extraction_note: Appraisal flags single-cohort TCGA-PRAD design without independent external validation despite thorough internal nomogram/DCA analyses.

title: Integrative Bioinformatics and Machine Learning Analysis Identifies Novel Molecular Biomarkers in Prostate Adenocarcinoma.
study_design: Integrative TCGA bioinformatics and hybrid ML gene-prioritization with GEO external validation
data_source_detail: TCGA-PRAD discovery (494 tumor Z-score matrix; nodal N0 vs N1 comparison n=420); external validation GSE14206 (50 samples: 15 normal, 35 PRAD)
data_modality_detail: TCGA RNA-seq V2 RSEM Z-scores; GSE14206 microarray (GPL570)
algorithm: Hybrid GBM+RF ensemble after graph-convolutional feature selection on DEGs
input_features: DEGs from N0 vs N1 nodal comparison (524 DEGs) with ML-prioritized genes including XAF1, APP, PLK1, STAT1
biomarker_result: Multi-gene diagnostic/prioritization signature (GBM+RF-selected genes)
performance_value: TCGA AUC 0.9526 (accuracy 97.49%); GSE14206 external AUC 0.9156 (accuracy 91.53%)
validation_detail: Signature evaluated in independent GSE14206 after platform harmonization; authors note limited external sample size.
key_finding: Hybrid GBM+RF achieved high discrimination on TCGA and retained strong performance on GSE14206, prioritizing cell-cycle and interferon-pathway genes.
limitations_as_stated: No protein or functional validation; GSE14206 validation cohort is small.
other_key_outcomes: PPI hub emphasis on STAT1 and PLK1; pathway enrichment (GO, KEGG, Reactome).

title: A Platform-Independent Binary Gene-Pair Signature Derived from CRPC-Enriched Single-Cell Transcriptomics for Predicting Recurrence-Free Survival in Prostate Cancer.
study_design: scRNA-seq CRPC atlas plus bulk multi-cohort ML RFS signature with Ridge regression selection
data_source_detail: Training TCGA-PRAD (n=493); external bulk GSE21034, GSE70770, GSE94767, DKFZ, plus AHMU own cohort (n=70); scRNA PRJNA699369 for gene-pool discovery
data_modality_detail: scRNA-seq (CRPC-enriched epithelial genes) plus bulk RNA for 36 binary gene-pair Ridge model
algorithm: Ridge regression selected among 12 algorithms and 104 combinations (10-fold CV for regularized models)
input_features: 36 binary gene-pair features from CRPC/MaligC5-enriched pool
biomarker_result: 36-gene-pair binary RFS signature
performance_value: TCGA-PRAD C-index 0.759; mean C-index 0.725 across five external cohorts; TCGA time-dependent AUC 0.787/0.788/0.781 at 1/3/5 yr
validation_detail: Feature selection restricted to TCGA; five independent external cohorts used only for final evaluation without refitting.
funding: Supported by Anhui Province clinical translational and higher-education research grants.
key_finding: Rank-based gene-pair signature stratified RFS across six cohorts and linked high-risk tumors to immune-inflamed and TP53-altered phenotypes.
limitations_as_stated: scRNA gene pool from one CRPC dataset; immunotherapy associations are hypothesis-generating.
other_key_outcomes: Optional nomogram with T stage and Gleason; virtual knockout highlighted CKS2.
extraction_note: Co-primary C-index (model selection) and time-dependent AUC reported; C-index used as performance_metric.

title: A Hypoxia and Immune Escape-Related Gene Signature for the Diagnosis of Prostate Cancer: An Integrated Bioinformatics Study.
study_design: Multi-public cohort diagnostic ML signature for hypoxia/immune-escape genes
data_source_detail: Model training/test on merged GTEx+TCGA-PRAD (499 tumor + 152 controls); validation GSE88808 and GSE21034
data_modality_detail: Bulk RNA-seq/microarray after harmonization (RF, SVM-RFE, LASSO feature selection)
algorithm: Random Forest, SVM-RFE, and LASSO with six-gene diagnostic signature
input_features: Six HIERGs: RBMS3, ALDH2, SLC7A11, FGFR2, GDF15, NCAM1
biomarker_result: Six-gene hypoxia/immune-escape diagnostic RiskScore signature
performance_value: AUC >0.9 reported across test and GEO validation cohorts (abstract)
validation_detail: Independent GEO cohorts GSE88808 and GSE21034 used as validation; authors discuss validation limitations in discussion.
key_finding: Six-gene signature showed high diagnostic accuracy with calibration and DCA support across merged TCGA/GTEx and GEO validations.
limitations_as_stated: Authors acknowledge need for further external validation and cautious interpretation of exploratory immune/pathway associations.
other_key_outcomes: Immune infiltration and drug/regulator network analyses tied to RiskScore.
extraction_note: Appraisal_note states authors explicitly acknowledge lack of external validation as a limitation despite GEO validation cohorts in methods.

title: A Metabolic-Related Gene Signature for Predicting Biochemical Recurrence After Radical Prostatectomy: An Integrative Analysis and Targeted Therapeutic Validation.
study_design: GEO training/validation BCR prognostic XGBoost-Cox model with WGCNA and own IHC/docking validation
data_source_detail: Training GSE220095 (n=176); external validation GSE70769 (n=94); own FFPE IHC n=32 (orthogonal, not in ML training)
data_modality_detail: Bulk microarray expression; four metabolic hub genes in XGBoost-Cox
algorithm: XGBoost-Cox with grid search and 10-fold CV; SHAP interpretation
input_features: GDPD1, PLA2G7, PTGDS, SRD5A2 metabolic hub genes
biomarker_result: Four-gene metabolic BCR risk model
performance_value: 5-year AUC 0.858 training (GSE220095); 0.745 external validation (GSE70769)
validation_detail: ComBat harmonization between GEO cohorts; GSE70769 held out for external evaluation; notable AUC drop versus training.
key_finding: Metabolic four-gene XGBoost-Cox model stratified post-RP BCR risk and linked hub genes to M2 macrophage-associated TIME patterns.
limitations_as_stated: NR
other_key_outcomes: In silico EGCG multi-target docking and in vitro binding/suppression assays; IHC on 32 specimens.
extraction_note: Appraisal flags notable training-to-validation AUC drop (0.858 to 0.745) warranting cautious interpretation.

title: Deep learning based on multiparametric MRI for differentiating benign from malignant PI-RADS 3 prostate lesions: a dual-center study.
study_design: Dual-center retrospective mpMRI deep learning radiomics for PI-RADS 3 lesion classification
data_source_detail: 382 PI-RADS 3 patients (Center 1 train n=210, internal val n=90; Center 2 external val n=82)
data_modality_detail: mpMRI T2WI/DWI/ADC with ResNet101 deep features plus mRMR-LASSO radiomics
algorithm: ResNet101 deep features + LASSO radiomics; combined clinical-DLRS logistic model
input_features: Deep learning radiomics signature (DLRS) plus clinical variables in combined model
biomarker_result: Combined clinical-DLRS nomogram for malignancy in PI-RADS 3 lesions
performance_value: Combined model AUC 0.951 (train), 0.964 (internal val), 0.925 (Center 2 external)
validation_detail: Center 2 (n=82) used as external validation; Center 1 split 7:3 train/internal validation.
key_finding: Combined deep radiomics-clinical model outperformed clinical-only model for distinguishing malignant versus benign PI-RADS 3 lesions across three cohorts.
limitations_as_stated: NR
other_key_outcomes: Standalone DLRS and clinical models compared; DCA supported clinical utility.

title: Non-invasive prediction of lymph node involvement in prostate cancer via machine learning on whole-prostate MRI.
study_design: Single-center retrospective MRI radiomics/deep learning DRBN model for preoperative LNI prediction
data_source_detail: 339 PCa patients post-RP with ePLND; random 7:3 stratified train/validation split by LNI status
data_modality_detail: Whole-prostate T2 MRI radiomics and deep learning plus Brigadi-based clinical variables
algorithm: LASSO feature selection then ML comparison (LR, SVM, XGBoost, etc.) with 5-fold CV; DRBN logistic integration
input_features: Clinical Brigadi variables plus selected radiomic and deep learning features
biomarker_result: DRBN integrated LNI prediction model
performance_value: ROC-AUC 0.963 training and 0.920 validation; PR-AUC 0.950 and 0.921 respectively
validation_detail: Random 7:3 internal split only; no independent external center cohort identified in slice.
key_finding: Integrating clinical, radiomic, and deep learning MRI features yielded strong LNI discrimination with acceptable calibration and DCA in train and validation splits.
limitations_as_stated: NR
other_key_outcomes: Comparison to clinical-only Brigadi-based model.
extraction_note: Appraisal flags no external cohort—only internal training/validation split of single-center data.

title: Preoperative dual-ROI mpMRI radiomics integrating intratumoral and periprostatic adipose tissue features with clinical factors for predicting positive surgical margins after radical prostatectomy.
study_design: Two-center retrospective dual-ROI mpMRI radiomics-clinical nomogram for post-RP PSM prediction
data_source_detail: 423 non-metastatic PCa patients (409 center 1, 14 center 2); pooled random 7:3 train (296) / validation (127)
data_modality_detail: Intratumoral and PPAT radiomics on T2WI and ADC with LASSO-selected signatures
algorithm: LASSO radiomics signatures plus multivariable logistic regression nomogram
input_features: TPR combined tumor-PPAT radiomics signature with PSA, ISUP grade, clinical T stage
biomarker_result: Dual-ROI TPR radiomics-clinical PSM nomogram
performance_value: Nomogram AUC 0.908 training and 0.885 validation; TPR signature AUC 0.824 train and 0.816 validation
validation_detail: Two-center data pooled then randomly split 7:3 rather than center-held-out external validation.
key_finding: Integrating intratumoral and PPAT radiomics with clinical factors improved preoperative PSM prediction versus single-ROI models.
limitations_as_stated: NR
other_key_outcomes: Bootstrap stability and subgroup ROC analyses reported.
extraction_note: Appraisal flags validation as random split of pooled two-center data, not a true held-out external cohort.

title: Serum Untargeted Metabolomics Integrated with SHAP-Based Machine Learning for Multiclass Stratification of Prostate Cancer, Prostatitis, and Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia.
study_design: Public MetaboLights serum untargeted LC-MS multiclass ML with nested CV
data_source_detail: EMBL-EBI MetaboLights MTBLS6039 (80 serum samples: 20 PCa, 20 prostatitis, 20 BPH, 20 healthy controls)
data_modality_detail: Untargeted serum metabolomics (LC-MS)
algorithm: Multiclass LASSO feature selection with optimized Random Forest; nested cross-validation
input_features: LC-MS metabolite features selected by multiclass LASSO
biomarker_result: Multiclass metabolic signature distinguishing PCa, prostatitis, BPH, and controls
performance_value: Out-of-fold accuracy 93.8%; macro-F1 0.937
validation_detail: Nested cross-validation on single public cohort; authors state no independent external validation.
key_finding: Random Forest on LASSO-selected metabolites achieved strong multiclass separation of major prostate disease groups with SHAP-interpretable modules.
limitations_as_stated: Small sample size and lack of external independent validation cohort.
other_key_outcomes: SHAP-based metabolic module interpretation.
extraction_note: Appraisal flags n=80 and explicit lack of external validation despite strong nested-CV accuracy.

title: Network toxicology & molecular docking: endocrine-disrupting chemicals induce prostate cancer - a system study.
study_design: Network toxicology and MR-integrated GEO transcriptomics with explainable XGBoost-SHAP
data_source_detail: 402 integrated GEO transcriptomes (GSE46602/GSE55945 training; GSE60329, GSE69223, GSE246282 validation) plus EDC target docking
data_modality_detail: Merged microarray/RNA-seq with WGCNA and network toxicology prior
algorithm: Explainable XGBoost with SHAP for five-gene diagnostic signature
input_features: NR3C1, CALM1, MET, STAT3, CES1 core signature
biomarker_result: Five-gene EDC-linked PCa diagnostic signature
performance_value: AUC >0.90 across multiple independent GEO cohorts (abstract)
validation_detail: Three GEO cohorts held out from discovery pair for signature evaluation after batch correction.
key_finding: Integrative pipeline linked EDC targets to a five-gene transcriptomic signature with high cross-cohort discrimination and in silico binding support.
limitations_as_stated: No matched EDC exposure quantification in GEO; docking static; cross-sectional inferential design.
other_key_outcomes: Molecular docking ΔG < -7 kcal/mol for EDC-target pairs; WGCNA/network toxicology layers.
extraction_note: Paper anchor is EDC network toxicology and docking; ML signature is secondary explainable prioritization layer.

title: A novel prognostic signature based on mitochondrial permeability transition-driven necrosis genes for biochemical recurrence prediction in prostate cancer.
study_design: TCGA-PRAD training with GEO GSE70768 external BCR-FS prognostic model
data_source_detail: TCGA-PRAD training (396 tumors with BCR follow-up); external validation GSE70768 (n=111 with BCR-FS)
data_modality_detail: Bulk RNA-seq MPT-DN-related gene Cox/ML selection
algorithm: WGCNA, Cox regression, and machine learning feature selection (LASSO mentioned in limitations)
input_features: TREM2, FNDC1, S100A8 prognostic genes
biomarker_result: Three-gene MPT-DN-related BCR-FS risk score
performance_value: AUC approximately 0.65–0.70 in external validation (per appraisal_note; numeric detail truncated in slice)
validation_detail: GSE70768 used as independent external BCR-FS validation cohort after TCGA model development.
key_finding: Three-gene risk model stratified BCR-FS with immune and drug-sensitivity differences between risk groups; protein validation in tissues/cell lines.
limitations_as_stated: Limited BCR events vs multi-step selection; public-data-only; drug sensitivity from cell-line databases.
other_key_outcomes: Western blot/qPCR validation of TREM2, FNDC1, S100A8.
extraction_note: Appraisal notes modest discrimination (AUC ~0.65–0.70) despite genuine external cohort.

title: Development and validation of an MRI radiomics-based model for predicting progression risk in prostate cancer after endocrine therapy.
study_design: Retrospective MRI radiomics-clinical nomogram for post–endocrine-therapy progression
data_source_detail: 136 endocrine-therapy PCa patients; train n=95 and internal validation n=41 (7:3); external validation n=52
data_modality_detail: MRI radiomics features combined with clinicopathologic predictors
algorithm: Radiomics feature selection with multivariable Cox/logistic nomogram integration
input_features: PSA nadir time, Gleason score, T stage, bone metastasis, and radiomics score
biomarker_result: Radiomics-clinical progression nomogram after endocrine therapy
performance_value: C-index 0.884 training, 0.839 internal validation, 0.795 external validation
validation_detail: Separate external set (n=52) plus internal 7:3 split for model development.
key_finding: Combined MRI radiomics and clinical factors predicted post–endocrine-therapy progression/PFS with consistent discrimination across train, internal, and external sets.
limitations_as_stated: NR
other_key_outcomes: Kaplan–Meier stratification by nomogram cutoff 79.44; DCA supported utility.

title: Bioinformatics and machine learning integration reveals a novel 4-gene (GFUS, ARHGAP8, NBL1, and ACTB) biomarker model for prostate cancer.
study_design: GEO microarray integration with graph-convolutional feature selection and ensemble classifiers for a four-gene prostate cancer diagnostic signature
data_source_detail: Discovery GSE3325, GSE6919, GSE55945, and GSE26910 (n=179; 19, 127, 21, and 12 samples); external validation GSE46602 (n=50)
data_modality_detail: Harmonized microarray expression collapsed to HGNC symbols
algorithm: Graph-convolutional feature selection with a hybrid random forest and LightGBM classifier; C5, AdaBoost, SVM, random forest, and LightGBM compared under nested cross-validation
input_features: Four-gene panel GFUS, ARHGAP8, NBL1, and ACTB
biomarker_result: Four-gene diagnostic signature for prostate cancer versus non-cancer samples
performance_value: Discovery hybrid model AUC 0.9612 (accuracy 95.37%, sensitivity 94.02%, specificity 95.80%); external GSE46602 hybrid AUC 0.90 with accuracy above 91%
validation_detail: Nested cross-validation on the merged discovery GEO sets, then independent GSE46602 (n=50) covering prostate cancer
funding: Princess Nourah bint Abdulrahman University Researchers Supporting Project (PNURSP2026R751)
key_finding: A hybrid random forest-LightGBM model using GFUS, ARHGAP8, NBL1, and ACTB discriminated prostate cancer in the discovery set (AUC 0.9612) and retained AUC 0.90 on GSE46602.
limitations_as_stated: Public datasets lacked PSA, Gleason score, and stage, so multivariate Cox models were not possible; the study is hypothesis-generating and in silico only.
other_key_outcomes: Discovery AUCs for comparators: C5 0.9257, AdaBoost 0.9098, SVM 0.8926, random forest 0.9519, LightGBM 0.9578. Code: https://github.com/serhatklc/prostate_v1
extraction_note: Primary performance is the discovery hybrid AUC; external GSE46602 AUC is reported as 0.90.

title: Multi-omics analyses related to unfolded protein response in prostate cancer implicate pro-tumor role of IFRD1.
study_design: scRNA-guided bulk UPR signature with integrative ML and multi-cohort validation
data_source_detail: TCGA-PRAD training (496 tumors); scRNA GSE185344/GSE141445; external GSE116918, GSE21034, GSE70769, DKFZ2018 for UPRRS/IFRD1 validation
data_modality_detail: scRNA-seq UPR mapping plus bulk RNA seven-gene UPRRS (LASSO/RF-Cox)
algorithm: Univariate Cox, random forest importance, and LASSO (10-fold CV) integrative selection
input_features: Seven UPR-related genes including IFRD1, DDIT3, HSPA5
biomarker_result: Seven-gene UPR-related prognostic signature (UPRRS)
performance_value: C-index >0.82 and AUC >0.80 in TCGA training and three external cohorts (abstract)
validation_detail: UPRRS tested in TCGA plus three independent public validation cohorts; IFRD1 validated in additional datasets.
key_finding: UPRRS independently predicted prognosis beyond stage/Gleason and associated with immunosuppressive TME and chemoresistance patterns.
limitations_as_stated: NR
other_key_outcomes: In vitro IFRD1 knockdown reduced proliferation/migration; nomogram for clinical use.
extraction_note: GitHub TCGAplot tool noted in appraisal as visualization support, not full pipeline code.

title: Palmitoylation-related gene expression and its prognostic value in prostate cancer: insights into immune infiltration and therapeutic potential.
study_design: Multi-public PRG palmitoylation prognostic signature with ten-algorithm integrative ML
data_source_detail: TCGA training with cross-cohort validation in DKFZ, MSKCC, E-MTAB-6128, GSE70768, GSE70769; scRNA from PCaProfiler; own qPCR on 20 tissues
data_modality_detail: Bulk RNA plus scRNA-derived PRG features and ssGSEA palmitoylation scores
algorithm: Integrative combination of 10 ML algorithms; highest mean C-index model selected
input_features: Palmitoylation-related gene signature (hub CHRNA2 among others)
biomarker_result: PRG-related prognostic risk score (PRGRS)
performance_value: Highest-average C-index model selected by tenfold cross-validation across TCGA and external cohorts, with Kaplan-Meier separation of recurrence-free survival; no numeric C-index or AUC is printed
validation_detail: All algorithm pairs cross-validated with independent DKFZ, ArrayExpress, GEO, and MSKCC cohorts.
key_finding: Palmitoylation score and PRGRS stratified BCR-free survival and immune/drug-response phenotypes with experimental CHRNA2 validation.
limitations_as_stated: NR
other_key_outcomes: oncoPredict IC50 differences by risk group; qPCR in 20 PRAD tissues.
extraction_note: The full text does not report a numeric performance metric.

title: Genetic relationships between the gut microbiota and prostate cancer: Mendelian randomization combined with bioinformatics analysis.
study_design: Two-sample MR of gut microbiota with GEO ML nomogram for PCa risk
data_source_detail: Finnish FINRISK gut microbiota GWAS instruments; PCa GWAS ieu-b-4809; GEO train GSE5377/GSE27616/GSE46602 (83 samples) and validation GSE200879 (138 samples)
data_modality_detail: MR instruments plus GEO expression DEAGs; four ML models for feature genes
algorithm: Four machine learning models compared; nomogram from PLCL1, VSNL1, ROR2, NRXN3, TEAD1 feature genes
input_features: Five DEAG feature genes linked to MR-positive microbiota exposures
biomarker_result: Microbiota-associated five-gene PCa risk nomogram
performance_value: External-validation AUC = 1 for the combined feature-gene diagnostic model (Figure 7F)
validation_detail: GSE200879 held out after training on merged first three GEO sets; MR layer separate from expression ML.
key_finding: MR identified 16 gut taxa causally associated with PCa and a five-gene expression nomogram for risk quantification.
limitations_as_stated: European-focused GWAS; no gender-stratified microbiota; needs experimental verification.
other_key_outcomes: Colocalization yielded 144 shared genes; STROBE-MR checklist referenced.
extraction_note: The full text states an area under the curve value of 1 for the feature-gene model on external validation. That perfect AUC needs review as possible overfitting. Individual-gene AUCs are not printed.

title: Integrative single-cell and spatial transcriptomics with explainable AI reveal lethal prognostic axis in prostate cancer.
study_design: scRNA/spatial atlas plus 101 ML pipelines for C4 epithelial prognostic model with experimental PCSK1N validation
data_source_detail: scRNA GSE274229; spatial GSE278936/10x; bulk TCGA-PRAD (n=498) with external GSE21032 (n=140) and GSE70770 (n=203)
data_modality_detail: 141,986 scRNA cells, spatial deconvolution, bulk RNA Lasso+PLS-Cox C4 risk score
algorithm: 101 ML pipelines benchmarked; Lasso plus PLS-Cox selected with SHAP interpretation
input_features: C4 malignant epithelial program genes (e.g., MT1M, PCSK1N, ACSL3)
biomarker_result: C4-based explainable recurrence-free survival risk score
performance_value: Nomogram C-index 0.751; merged training time-dependent AUC 0.802, 0.776, and 0.739 at 1, 3, and 5 years (HR 4.53, 95% CI 3.19-6.41)
validation_detail: TCGA-PRAD development with MSKCC/GSE21032 and GSE70770 external evaluation; orthogonal organoid/xenograft PCSK1N experiments.
key_finding: C4 lethal epithelial axis risk score predicted RFS independently of age, Gleason, and T stage with experimental PCSK1N functional support.
limitations_as_stated: Modest sample size; spatial technical limits; causality not fully proven.
other_key_outcomes: Spatial immune niche mapping; enzalutamide resistance modulation by PCSK1N.
extraction_note: The algorithm screen used mean C-index, which is not printed as a number. The reported nomogram C-index is 0.751.

title: Development and Validation of a Multimodal Artificial Intelligence-derived Digital Pathology-based Biomarker Predicting Metastasis Among Patients with Biochemical Recurrence After Radical Prostatectomy in NRG/RTOG Trials.
study_design: Post-RP salvage digital pathology MMAI model validated in NRG/RTOG trial cohorts
data_source_detail: Locked MMAI trained on trial development split; validation in 533 NRG/RTOG 9601+0534 BCR patients receiving SRT±HT
data_modality_detail: H&E whole-slide image features plus clinical variables (Grade Group, pT, pre-SRT PSA, age, margin)
algorithm: Multi-modal AI histopathology model with Cox regression on locked MMAI score
input_features: Digital pathology image features and five clinical covariates
biomarker_result: Post-RP MMAI distant-metastasis risk score
performance_value: 10-year time-dependent AUC 0.74 for MMAI vs 0.68 clinical nomogram; SHR 2.17 per SD for DM
validation_detail: Pre-specified validation in combined NRG/RTOG randomized trial cohorts with median 9.3-year follow-up.
key_finding: MMAI score independently stratified 10-year distant metastasis after salvage RT±HT and differentiated HT benefit by risk group.
limitations_as_stated: Archived trial cohorts; external prospective validation ongoing.
other_key_outcomes: Binary high/low risk 10-year DM rates 25% vs 8.8%.
extraction_note: Trial data available by request from NCTN/NRG rather than fully open repositories.

title: Senescence-related gene signature predicts prostate cancer progression and identifies PCNA as a therapeutic target via multi-omics machine learning integration.
study_design: 117-method ML senescence signature with scRNA/bulk trajectory and own 90-patient cohort validation
data_source_detail: Six public BCR cohorts (TCGA-PRAD, Stockholm, Cambridge, CancerMap, GSE54460, Taylor) plus SYSU-PRAD in-house n=90
data_modality_detail: Bulk RNA-seq, scRNA-seq, and proteomics/WES in SYSU cohort
algorithm: 117 machine-learning method screen; highest mean C-index model selected (SuperPC among methods listed)
input_features: Senescence-related gene signature (SRGS) with PCNA highlighted
biomarker_result: SRGS senescence-related prognostic signature
performance_value: SRGS AUC: TCGA-PRAD 0.709, Stockholm 0.693, Cambridge 0.68, CancerMap 0.714, GSE54460 0.6551, Taylor 0.747; SYSU-PRAD AUC 0.6969, 0.7559, and 0.7869 at 1, 2, and 3 years
validation_detail: Cross-cohort C-index ranking plus independent SYSU-PRAD cohort of 90 patients.
key_finding: SRGS predicted progression and AR-inhibitor outcomes with PCNA validated as functional driver via AOH1996 inhibition.
limitations_as_stated: NR
other_key_outcomes: Pseudo-time trajectory linking SRGS to disease progression.

title: DWI-based Biologically Interpretable Radiomic Nomogram for Predicting 1-year Biochemical Recurrence after Radical Prostatectomy: A Deep Learning, Multicenter Study.

key_finding: Multicenter DWI-based nomogram predicted 1-year biochemical recurrence after RP with external center validation.

title: Integrating multimodal data to predict the progression of hormone-sensitive prostate cancer.

key_finding: Integrated proteomics-imaging-pathology nomogram stratified time to CRPC progression with high internal C-index.

other_key_outcomes: Per-modality Boruta feature counts reported in abstract.

title: A retrospective study on predicting clinically significant prostate cancer via a bi-parametric ultrasound-based deep learning radiomics model.

other_key_outcomes: Comparison to clinical-only baseline.

title: AI-Driven Prediction of Cardio-Oncology Biomarkers Through Protein Corona Analysis.

title: Establishing a Prognostic Model Correlates to Inflammatory Response Pathways for Prostate Cancer via Multiomic Analysis of Lactylation-Related Genes.
study_design: Lactylation-related multi-omic ML prognostic signature with TCGA/DKFZ validation
data_source_detail: TCGA-PRAD training with DKFZ external validation; ensemble ML to 10-gene signature
data_modality_detail: Bulk transcriptomics lactylation regulators with immune/deconvolution and drug profiling
algorithm: Ensemble machine learning after Cox preselection
input_features: 10-gene lactylation-related signature (AK5 functionally highlighted)

validation_detail: External DKFZ cohort validation plus TCGA-PRAD development.
key_finding: Ten-gene lactylation score independently predicted BCR with immune and drug-response associations; AK5 validated in PC-3 models.
limitations_as_stated: NR
other_key_outcomes: Immune checkpoint and chemotherapy sensitivity profiling by risk group.

title: Prediction of Prostate Cancer Grades Using Radiomic Features.
study_design: retrospective single-center MRI radiomics cohort
data_source_detail: 112 PCa patients (Houshasen Daiichi Hospital, 2014-2021) after MRI quality exclusions
data_modality_detail: T2WI and ADC radiomics (PyRadiomics) with PSA and PI-RADS v2.1
algorithm: logistic regression (Orange3); LOOCV with Ridge regularization
input_features: five radiomic features plus PSA vs PI-RADS score plus PSA
biomarker_result: Radiomics model for GS>=8 vs GS<8 PCa
performance_value: LOOCV Radiomics 0.799 vs PI-RADS 0.710 (p<0.05); holdout test AUC 0.778
validation_detail: Leave-one-out CV plus 90/22 train-test holdout only; no external cohort.
key_finding: Radiomics with PSA outperformed PI-RADS with PSA for high-grade PCa grade prediction on internal validation.
limitations_as_stated: Biopsy-based GS without RP confirmation; PI-RADS without contrast in some cases; mixed prostate zones.
other_key_outcomes: PSA-only, radiomics-only, and PI-RADS-only LOOCV AUCs were 0.752, 0.778, and 0.590.

title: Machine learning-based identification of co-expressed genes in prostate cancer and CRPC and construction of prognostic models.
study_design: retrospective translational/bioinformatic (public transcriptomic datasets, Cox/LASSO prognostic modeling)
data_source_detail: GEO GSE35988 (training: 12 normal, 49 PCa, 27 CRPC samples, China); TCGA-PRAD (model building via Cox/LASSO, hub gene expression validation); GEO GSE116918 (external validation cohort); GEO GSE66187 (CRPC/PCa hub gene expression validation, 24 LuCaP-PCa xenografts + 71 CRPC metastatic tumors)
data_modality_detail: mRNA microarray (GEO GSE35988, GSE66187, GSE116918) and RNA-seq TPM (TCGA-PRAD)
algorithm: LASSO Cox regression, univariate and multivariate Cox regression
input_features: 7-gene expression signature (KIF4A, UBE2C, FAM72D, CCDC78, HOXD9, LIX1, SLC5A8) selected via LASSO from 182 common DEGs shared between normal-vs-PCa and PCa-vs-CRPC comparisons
biomarker_result: 7-gene prognostic risk score (KIF4A, UBE2C, FAM72D, CCDC78, HOXD9, LIX1, SLC5A8)
performance_value: Training (TCGA-PRAD): AUC 1y=0.754, 3y=0.776, 5y=0.706; KM high- vs low-risk HR=4.72, P<0.001; nomogram AUC=0.775. External validation (GSE116918): AUC 1y=0.728, 3y=0.526, 5y=0.599; KM HR=1.92 (95% CI 1.11-3.31), P=0.020
validation_detail: GSE116918 is an independent GEO cohort distinct from the GSE35988 training set and TCGA-PRAD model-building cohort - a genuine external cohort, not an internal split. Predictive performance degrades markedly at longer horizons (AUC drops from 0.776/0.706 in training to 0.526/0.599 at 3y/5y in GSE116918), consistent with the appraisal_note's flag on borderline generalizability.
key_finding: A 7-gene LASSO-Cox prognostic risk model stratified PRAD patients into high/low risk with significant PFI differences (HR=4.72, P<0.001) and good discrimination/calibration in the TCGA-PRAD training set (AUC 0.754-0.776), but substantially weaker discrimination at 3- and 5-year horizons in external GSE116918 validation (AUC 0.526 and 0.599).
limitations_as_stated: Mechanism of gene action on PCa proliferation/invasion/apoptosis unclear and needs further exploration; small sample size; need for multicenter, large-sample, prospective validation.
other_key_outcomes: Individual hub-gene associations with pathological T/N stage, clinical T stage, PSA, age, Gleason score and PFI reported for each of the 7 genes; differential expression corroborated in TCGA-PRAD and GSE66187 (CRPC vs primary PCa); nomogram integrating risk score with clinical variables achieved AUC=0.775 with favorable calibration/DCA.
extraction_note: n_analytic for the TCGA-PRAD cohort used to derive and validate the prognostic model is never given as an explicit number in the manuscript (only GSE35988 [n=88] and GSE66187 [n=95] component counts are stated); marked NR. Funding statement not located (competing interests declared, funding section absent). The appraisal_note's concern about AUC decline at 3-5y in GSE116918 is corroborated here quantitatively.

title: Construction of regulatory T cells specific genes predictive models of prostate cancer patients based on machine learning: a computational analysis and in vitro experiments.
study_design: retrospective public transcriptomics plus in vitro validation
data_source_detail: GSE116918 training; TCGA-PRAD external validation; SYCP2 validated in C4-2 cells
data_modality_detail: Microarray (GSE116918) and TCGA-PRAD RNA-seq; 2407 literature RTSGs screened
algorithm: LASSO Cox regression after univariate Cox and consensus clustering
input_features: four regulatory T cell-specific genes (CENPK, FBXO45, MXRA7, SYCP2)
biomarker_result: Four-gene RTSG risk score
performance_value: High vs low risk KM separation significant in GSE116918; replicated in TCGA-PRAD; multivariate Cox independent (P<0.01)
validation_detail: Model coefficients from GSE116918 applied to independent TCGA-PRAD cohort.
key_finding: A four-gene RTSG risk score stratified PRAD prognosis and SYCP2 modulated apoptosis and cell cycle in vitro.
limitations_as_stated: Retrospective GEO-based analysis; limited clinical covariates; in vitro work may not reflect in vivo microenvironment.
other_key_outcomes: Immune infiltration and drug sensitivity differed by risk group; consensus clustering of RTSGs identified two prognostic clusters.

title: Autophagy Associated Genes (ARGs) -Based Predictive Model AIDPS for Prostate Cancer.
study_design: retrospective translational bioinformatic cohort
data_source_detail: TCGA-PRAD n=496 used to fit models with LOOCV; validation cohorts GSE54460 n=106, MSKCC n=140, GSE116918 n=248, GSE46602 n=36, GSE70768 n=111, and GSE70769 n=92. scRNA-seq GSE193337 (4 tumor and 4 benign samples) was exploratory.
data_modality_detail: Bulk RNA-seq and microarray expression of autophagy-related genes
algorithm: Ridge, chosen as the best of 101 combinations (RSF, Enet, Lasso, Ridge, stepwise Cox, CoxBoost, plsRcox, SuperPC, GBM, survival SVM) under LOOCV
input_features: Autophagy-related genes prognostic in at least six of seven expression datasets
biomarker_result: AIDPS Ridge autophagy-related prognostic signature
performance_value: 0.726 (mean C-index of the Ridge model across six validation cohorts); TCGA-PRAD 1-, 3-, and 5-year AUC 0.822, 0.734, and 0.694
validation_detail: Models were fit with LOOCV in TCGA-PRAD and scored on six independent public prostate cohorts. The C-index 0.726 is the mean of those cohort-level C-indexes, not a pooled estimate.
key_finding: Among 101 machine-learning prognostic models, the Ridge AIDPS signature had the highest mean validation C-index (0.726) and separated worse disease-free survival in the high-risk group across TCGA-PRAD and six public cohorts.
limitations_as_stated: Expression and clinical data came only from public databases; no prospective multicenter validation and no experiments on autophagy-gene mechanisms. Authors state that clinical applicability of AIDPS remains limited.
other_key_outcomes: Predicted IC50 differed between risk groups for dactinomycin, dactolisib, luminespib, and paclitaxel. BMP6 and CRIP2 were followed with colocalization and Mendelian randomization (rs2743987, rs7768988).
extraction_note: The headline C-index 0.726 is an average of per-cohort validation C-indexes, so no single analytic N is assigned.

title: Biparametric MRI-based radiomics for noninvastive discrimination of benign prostatic hyperplasia nodules (BPH) and prostate cancer nodules: a bio-centric retrospective cohort study.
study_design: retrospective multicenter biparametric MRI radiomics cohort
data_source_detail: 251 patients at Zhongshan and collaborating hospitals; 119 train, 52 internal validation, 80 external validation
data_modality_detail: Biparametric MRI (T2WI, ADC) radiomics plus clinical variables

input_features: fPSA/tPSA, PSAD, PZV, PI-RADS, fusion radiomic score
biomarker_result: Clinical-radiomic nomogram for BPH vs malignant nodule
performance_value: Nomogram AUC 0.925 internal validation; 0.872 external validation (n=80)
validation_detail: External validation on 80 patients from collaborating hospitals not used in training.
key_finding: Combined clinical-radiomic nomogram outperformed clinical and radiomic-only models for discriminating malignant vs benign nodules.
limitations_as_stated: NR
other_key_outcomes: Clinical model AUC 0.814 internal and 0.791 external; fusion radiomic model AUC 0.908 internal and 0.841 external.

title: Development and Validation of an MRI-Based Radiomics Nomogram to Predict the Prognosis of De Novo Oligometastatic Prostate Cancer Patients.
study_design: retrospective single-center cohort
data_source_detail: 165 men with de novo oligometastatic prostate cancer at the First Affiliated Hospital of Fujian Medical University (2019-2022); training n=115 and validating n=50 (30%)
data_modality_detail: MRI T2WI and ADC radiomics
algorithm: LASSO-Cox radiomics score with 10-fold cross-validation for feature selection, then a Cox nomogram
input_features: Five retained radiomic features (four T2WI, one ADC) plus clinical factors; the nomogram uses Rad-score, ECOG, and neutrophil count
biomarker_result: MRI radiomics nomogram (Rad-score, ECOG, and neutrophils) for overall survival
performance_value: 0.703, 0.799, and 0.833 (validating cohort 1-, 2-, and 3-year OS AUC); training cohort 0.734, 0.851, and 0.773
validation_detail: Single 70/30 split of one institutional cohort. Ten-fold cross-validation was used only to tune LASSO feature selection, not to estimate the reported AUCs.
funding: Eyas Plan Youth Top-notch Talent Project of Fujian Province (SCYJHBJRC-XN2021); Class B Talent Research Project of the First Affiliated Hospital of Fujian Medical University (YJCRC-B-XN2022); Natural Science Foundation of Fujian Province (2023J01579)
key_finding: An MRI radiomics nomogram predicted 1-, 2-, and 3-year overall survival in de novo oligometastatic prostate cancer, with validating-cohort AUCs of 0.703, 0.799, and 0.833.
limitations_as_stated: Small single-center retrospective sample with possible selection bias; radiomics limited to T2WI and ADC, excluding dynamic contrast images; feature extraction may vary between observers.
other_key_outcomes: Rad-score alone had validating-cohort 1-, 2-, and 3-year AUCs of 0.666, 0.754, and 0.982. Adding Rad-score improved the clinical model in both cohorts. Same institution and year as Wu 2024 (REC-AIBIOGU-000107), but that study enrolled high-risk non-metastatic patients receiving neoadjuvant chemohormonal therapy.
extraction_note: n_analytic is the validating cohort that supports the primary AUCs.

title: Periprostatic fat magnetic resonance imaging based radiomics nomogram for predicting biochemical recurrence-free survival in patients with non-metastatic prostate cancer after radical prostatectomy.
study_design: retrospective single-center mpMRI radiomics with temporal test set
data_source_detail: 356 non-metastatic PCa post-RP at Fujian Medical University; 118 train, 53 validation, 185 temporal test
data_modality_detail: T2WI and ADC intratumoral and periprostatic fat radiomics

input_features: Periprostatic fat-intratumoral radiomics signature plus pathologic T stage, ISUP grade, surgical margin
biomarker_result: Radiomics-clinical nomogram for bRFS
performance_value: Periprostatic fat-intratumoral model AUC 0.921/0.875/0.854 (1/3/5-yr bRFS, training); nomogram 0.944 vs clinical 0.839 at 1-yr (validation)
validation_detail: Random 7:3 train-validation split plus separate temporal test cohort (2017-2020, n=185).
key_finding: Periprostatic fat plus intratumoral radiomics improved prediction of biochemical recurrence-free survival versus clinical factors alone.
limitations_as_stated: NR
other_key_outcomes: 121 of 356 patients (34%) had biochemical recurrence during follow-up.

title: Unmasking Neuroendocrine Prostate Cancer with a Machine Learning-Driven Seven-Gene Stemness Signature That Predicts Progression.
study_design: integrative public transcriptomics with ML signature and PDX validation
data_source_detail: Seven GEO/TCGA expression cohorts plus nine training and four validation survival cohorts; PDX models
data_modality_detail: Bulk microarray/RNA-seq from public PCa cohorts

input_features: 144 literature stemness genes narrowed to seven-gene signature
biomarker_result: Seven-gene stemness signature (KMT5C, DPP4, TYMS, CDC25B, IRF5, MEN1, DNMT3B)
performance_value: Signature validated across independent cohorts and PDX; prognostic for PFS/RFS/MFS/OS per abstract (numeric C-index not stated in slice)
validation_detail: Five training and four validation transcriptomic cohorts plus PDX orthogonal validation.
key_finding: A seven-gene stemness signature predicted progression and identified NEPC-related molecular subtypes including large-cell NEPC.
limitations_as_stated: Public repository data may not represent global PCa genetic diversity.
other_key_outcomes: Signature linked to NEPC subtypes not always histologically classified as NEPC.

title: The role of NOP58 in prostate cancer progression through SUMOylation regulation and drug response.
study_design: TCGA bioinformatics plus wet-lab functional validation
data_source_detail: TCGA-PRAD transcriptomics; ten ML algorithms; IHC and cell assays for NOP58
data_modality_detail: Bulk RNA-seq, single-cell and functional assays centered on SUMOylation/NOP58
algorithm: Boruta plus ten ML classifiers (GLM, Elastic Net, GBM, SVM, etc.)
input_features: SUMOylation-related prognostic genes; NOP58 as core hub
biomarker_result: NOP58 expression and SUMOylation-linked prognostic axis
performance_value: ROC analysis is described as showing high tumor-versus-normal discrimination for NOP58, and Cox models are described for OS, PFI, and DSS, without a printed AUC, C-index, HR, accuracy, or sensitivity
validation_detail: TCGA-only computational modeling with orthogonal IHC and cell experiments; no independent external ML cohort.
key_finding: NOP58 associated with worse OS/PFI/DSS and promoted proliferation via SUMOylation-related pathways with experimental support.
limitations_as_stated: TCGA may not represent all patients; computational models need larger independent cohort validation.
other_key_outcomes: Dual-gene SUMO molecular subtypes differed in survival; drug response associations reported. A supplementary immunotherapy analysis stated AUC values exceeding 0.8 in some non-prostate datasets (melanoma, NSCLC, GBM).
extraction_note: Appraisal flagged borderline prediction scope because ML outputs are intertwined with mechanistic SUMO/NOP58 analyses rather than a standalone externally validated prognostic model. The full text does not report a numeric metric for the prostate NOP58 model.

title: Disulfidptosis-related subtype and prognostic signature in prostate cancer.
study_design: TCGA/GEO bioinformatics plus in vitro and scRNA validation
data_source_detail: TCGA-PRAD merged with GSE70770 and MSKCC; external GSE46602; scRNA GSE141445
data_modality_detail: Bulk RNA-seq/microarray and single-cell reference for DRG clustering

input_features: 24 disulfidptosis-related genes reduced to four-gene risk label with clinical covariates in nomogram
biomarker_result: Four-gene disulfidptosis-related risk signature and nomogram
performance_value: Four-gene risk label accuracy confirmed in external dataset per abstract; nomogram integrates DRGs and clinicopathology (numeric metrics not in slice)
validation_detail: External validation on GSE46602 for risk label; TCGA used for discovery and immune analyses.
funding: Major Research Project for Young and Middle-aged Scientists of Fujian Provincial Health Commission and Fujian Science and Technology Innovation Joint fund.
key_finding: Disulfidptosis-related clustering stratified immune contexture and a four-gene risk label predicted prognosis with external dataset confirmation.
limitations_as_stated: Public-database prognostic model needs clinical verification; disulfidptosis biology and immunology lack direct experimental proof.
other_key_outcomes: SLC7A11 functional and BAY-876 sensitivity experiments; cluster B showed higher immune infiltration and ICB sensitivity.

title: MulticentricGa-PSMA PET radiomics for treatment response assessment ofLu-PSMA-617 radioligand therapy in patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer.
study_design: retrospective multicenter PSMA PET radiomics cohort
data_source_detail: 45 mCRPC patients (Bonn and Aachen) with pre-treatment 68Ga-PSMA PET before 177Lu-PSMA-617
data_modality_detail: 68Ga-PSMA PET/CT radiomics from bone metastasis VOIs
algorithm: random forest for response; Cox regression for overall survival
input_features: three-feature radiomic signature plus age vs conventional PET parameters
biomarker_result: Combined radiomics-age signature for 177Lu-PSMA treatment response
performance_value: 5-fold CV AUC 0.82±0.07 (radiomics+age) vs 0.75 (age+PET) and 0.76 (radiomics alone); OS Cox C-index 0.67
validation_detail: Five-fold cross-validation on n=45; authors call for prospective multicenter studies.
key_finding: Pretreatment PSMA PET radiomics with age outperformed conventional PET metrics for predicting 177Lu-PSMA treatment response.
limitations_as_stated: Small sample; retrospective design; prospective multicenter validation needed per authors.
other_key_outcomes: Radiomic signature also used in Cox model for overall survival prediction.

title: Machine learning-based cell death marker for predicting prognosis and identifying tumor immune microenvironment in prostate cancer.
study_design: multi-cohort public transcriptomics ML prognostic study
data_source_detail: TCGA-PRAD (n=321) training; GSE116918 (n=247) and MSKCC2010 (n=140) validation
data_modality_detail: Bulk RNA-seq/microarray of programmed cell death-related genes
algorithm: 101 combinations of ten ML algorithms; selected random survival forest (27 genes) PCDI
input_features: 27 PCDRGs forming PCDI (PCD-related index)
biomarker_result: PCDI (programmed cell death-related index)
performance_value: Highest mean C-index across TCGA/GSE116918/MSKCC for RSF-PCDI; time-dependent AUC TCGA 1/3/5-yr BCR 0.965/0.961/0.926; MSKCC 0.837/0.703/0.703
validation_detail: LOOCV model building on TCGA-PRAD with validation on two independent GEO/MSK cohorts.
key_finding: PCDI from random survival forest stratified biochemical recurrence and correlated with immune infiltration and drug sensitivity.
limitations_as_stated: NR
other_key_outcomes: Nomogram for BCR; high PCDI linked to lower immunotherapy benefit.
extraction_note: C-index used for model selection; AUC reported for time-dependent BCR discrimination.

title: Epigenetic profiling of prostate cancer reveals potential prognostic signatures.
study_design: retrospective small-cohort methylation deconvolution with radiomics surrogate attempt
data_source_detail: 30 PCa patients with pre-RP mpMRI; BPH and adjacent benign controls for methylation
data_modality_detail: DNA methylation LCM deconvolution plus mpMRI radiomics
algorithm: LCM clustering; radiomics models to predict methylation clusters (unsuccessful)
input_features: mpMRI radiomic features from PCa and adjacent benign lesions
biomarker_result: Latent methylation components (two prognostic clusters), not predicted by radiomics
performance_value: No radiomics model non-invasively predicted epigenetic clusters (negative prediction result)
validation_detail: No successful predictive radiomics model; epigenetic clusters defined on tissue methylation only.
key_finding: Methylation-based clusters associated with malignancy and immune signatures but mpMRI radiomics could not surrogate them.
limitations_as_stated: Small n; subgroup of prior cohort; radiomics sensitivity may be limited for epigenetic clusters.
other_key_outcomes: Cluster one enriched for advanced stage and reduced CD19/CD4 immune methylation signatures.
extraction_note: Appraisal noted negative/borderline prediction result with poor radiomics performance for epigenetic cluster classification.

title: Magnetic resonance imaging-based radiomics nomogram for the evaluation of therapeutic responses to neoadjuvant chemohormonal therapy in high-risk non-metastatic prostate cancer.
study_design: retrospective single-center cohort
data_source_detail: 162 men with high-risk non-metastatic prostate cancer treated with neoadjuvant chemohormonal therapy and radical prostatectomy at the First Affiliated Hospital of Fujian Medical University (2016-2022); training n=113 and validation n=49
data_modality_detail: mpMRI T2WI and ADC radiomics from periprostatic fat and the intratumoral region
algorithm: LASSO with 10-fold cross-validation for feature selection, logistic regression signatures, and a multivariable logistic nomogram
input_features: Six periprostatic-fat and six intratumoral radiomic features plus initial PSA
biomarker_result: Radiomics-clinical nomogram (PSA, periprostatic-fat signature, and intratumoral signature) for positive pathological response to neoadjuvant chemohormonal therapy
performance_value: 0.886 (95% CI 0.763-0.959) validation-cohort nomogram AUC; training-cohort nomogram AUC 0.908 (95% CI 0.839-0.954); validation sensitivity 0.737, specificity 0.867, accuracy 0.816
validation_detail: Single split of one institutional cohort (113/49). Ten-fold cross-validation selected the LASSO penalty only. No external cohort.
funding: Eyas Plan Youth Top-notch Talent Project of Fujian Province (SCYJHBJRC-XN2021); Science and Technology Innovation Joint Fund of Fujian Province (2021Y9126 and 2023Y9078)
key_finding: A nomogram combining PSA with periprostatic-fat and intratumoral MRI radiomics signatures predicted pathological response to neoadjuvant chemohormonal therapy, with a validation AUC of 0.886.
limitations_as_stated: Retrospective single-center study with a limited sample of patients receiving neoadjuvant chemohormonal therapy; residual observer bias in ROI segmentation; relatively short follow-up.
other_key_outcomes: Validation AUCs were 0.833 for the periprostatic-fat signature and 0.751 for the intratumoral signature. Same institution and year as Liu 2024 (REC-AIBIOGU-000090), which studied de novo oligometastatic survival rather than this non-metastatic neoadjuvant cohort.
extraction_note: n_analytic is the validation cohort that supports the nomogram AUC of 0.886.

title: An 18-gene signature of recurrence-associated endothelial cells predicts tumor progression and castration resistance in prostate cancer.
study_design: integrative bulk and scRNA-seq endothelial heterogeneity study
data_source_detail: TCGA-PRAD plus five GEO validation cohorts and four scRNA-seq datasets; SU2C for CRPC
data_modality_detail: Bulk RNA-seq/microarray and scRNA-seq of endothelial subsets

input_features: 18-gene recurrence-associated endothelial cell signature (RAECsig)
biomarker_result: RAECsig endothelial recurrence signature
performance_value: Higher RAECsig independently predicted recurrence (HR 1.741, 95% CI 1.150-2.635; log-rank P=0.008 in slice example); outperformed clinicopathologic and commercial signatures in multiple cohorts per abstract
validation_detail: Nested CV on training cohorts with validation across multiple independent bulk PCa cohorts and CRPC datasets.

title: Integrated analysis of single-cell and bulk transcriptomics develops a robust neuroendocrine cell-intrinsic signature to predict prostate cancer progression.
study_design: translational/bioinformatic integrative analysis (retrospective multicenter/multi-cohort, single-cell + bulk transcriptomics + experimental models)
data_source_detail: 11 scRNA-seq cohorts (9 discovery + 2 validation; meta-atlas n=210,879 cells from 66 PCa tumors); 15 bulk transcriptomic cohorts (TCGA-PRAD, ICGC-PRAD, SU2C, WCM, MCTP, WCDT, CPGEA, PCaProfiler, MSKCC, CamCap, UM/SPORE, GSE54460, GSE116918, GSE84042, UW/RA), >3000 samples; 13 experimental models (8 CCLE PCa cell lines, 2 PDX models, 3 GEMMs); 1 spatial transcriptomics cohort (GSE230282)
data_modality_detail: scRNA-seq meta-atlas (210,879 cells/66 tumors), bulk RNA-seq/microarray (>3000 samples across 15 cohorts), spatial transcriptomics (1 cohort), and transcriptomic profiles from cell lines/PDX/GEMM experimental models
algorithm: 7 ML algorithms compared (elastic net, LASSO, ridge regression, gradient boosting machine, random survival forest, supervised principal components, support vector machine) plus a ssGSEA/AUCell-based NE_UP_DN signature (final selected model, termed NEPAL)
input_features: NE cell-intrinsic gene signature: NE_UP (n=90 up-regulated genes) and NE_DN (n=40 down-regulated genes), derived by overlapping 771 high-quality NEPC feature markers from scRNA-seq meta-atlas + bulk WGCNA modules with pseudobulk DEGs of NE tumor cells
biomarker_result: NEPAL (Neuroendocrine Prostate cancer ALgorithm) - NE_UP_DN cell-intrinsic gene signature scored via ssGSEA (bulk) / AUCell (single-cell), packaged as an R software package
performance_value: Among 18 candidate models/gene sets, top 3 (NE_UP_DN_ssGSEA, Enet[alpha=0.01], NE_UP_ssGSEA) had highest average C-index and AUC>0.90 across 6 validation cohorts, outperforming 11 published NE gene sets; NEPAL also had the highest C-index vs. 20 published ML prognostic models and clinical parameters across 10 multicenter cohorts. Exact point AUC/C-index values not stated numerically in body text (only qualitative/graphical).
validation_detail: Signature derived from the scRNA-seq meta-atlas (9 discovery cohorts) plus PCaProfiler bulk training set; independently validated in 6 separate bulk/scRNA-seq/spatial cohorts, in PDX/GEMM/cell-line experimental models, and in 10 further multicenter prognostic cohorts not used for signature derivation. The appraisal_note's 'moderate vs low MMAT' concern reflects the marked heterogeneity across platforms and species combined in these validations.
key_finding: An integrative scRNA-seq + bulk transcriptomics pipeline produced a thinned NE cell-intrinsic gene signature (NEPAL/NE_UP_DN) that outperformed 11 published NEPC gene sets and 20 published ML prognostic models across 6 validation cohorts plus experimental models, and predicted biochemical recurrence, overall survival, therapy responsiveness, and epigenetic drivers of NEPC across 10 additional multicenter cohorts.

extraction_note: Study spans >15 bulk cohorts, 11 scRNA-seq cohorts, 13 experimental models and 1 spatial cohort; a single n_analytic/data_source_detail could not be captured without oversimplifying - reported the scRNA-seq meta-atlas (n=210,879 cells/66 tumors) as the primary analytic N. Exact numeric AUC/C-index values for the top model are not stated in body text. title: Utility of diffusion weighted imaging-based radiomics nomogram to predict pelvic lymph nodes metastasis in prostate cancer.

title: Ultrasound-based radiomics score for pre-biopsy prediction of prostate cancer to reduce unnecessary biopsies.
study_design: retrospective single-center cohort
data_source_detail: 196 men undergoing initial transrectal ultrasound-guided prostate biopsy at the First Affiliated Hospital of Sun Yat-sen University (December 2015-March 2018); randomly split 7:3 into training n=137 and validation n=59
data_modality_detail: Transrectal ultrasound radiomics
algorithm: LASSO with five-fold cross-validation for feature selection, then multivariable logistic regression nomograms
input_features: Five ultrasound radiomic features (radiomics score) plus age, total PSA, and prostate volume
biomarker_result: Integrated ultrasound radiomics nomogram for pre-biopsy prediction of prostate cancer
performance_value: 0.835 (95% CI 0.729-0.941) integrated nomogram in the validation cohort; training-cohort integrated nomogram AUC 0.815 (95% CI 0.737-0.893)
validation_detail: One random 7:3 split of a single-center biopsy cohort. Five-fold cross-validation selected the LASSO penalty only. No external cohort.
funding: National Natural Science Foundation of China (81901849)
key_finding: Adding a transrectal-ultrasound radiomics score to age, total PSA, and prostate volume raised validation-cohort AUC for pre-biopsy prostate cancer detection from 0.752 to 0.835.
limitations_as_stated: Retrospective single-center study with selection bias and a limited sample; reproducibility was checked only in an internal validation cohort and still needs external validation; too few clinically significant cancers to build a separate nomogram for that endpoint.
other_key_outcomes: Validation-cohort AUC was 0.745 for the radiomics score alone and 0.752 (95% CI 0.618-0.886) for the clinical nomogram. At a 20% probability threshold the integrated nomogram was reported to avoid unnecessary biopsies.
extraction_note: n_analytic is the validation cohort that supports the integrated-nomogram AUC of 0.835.

limitations_as_stated: NR

title: Prediction of pelvic lymph node metastasis in prostate cancer using radiomics based on T-weighted imaging.
journal: Zhong Nan Da Xue Xue Bao Yi Xue Ban
study_design: retrospective single-center cohort
data_source_detail: 71 men who underwent extended pelvic lymph-node dissection at Peking University First Hospital (January 2017-June 2021). Temporal split: training January 2017-December 2020, n=56 patients (186 nodes); test January-June 2021, n=15 patients (45 nodes)
data_modality_detail: T2-weighted MRI radiomics of individual pelvic lymph nodes
algorithm: Random forest radiomics model and a multivariable logistic nomogram
input_features: Eighteen T2WI radiomic features (Rad-score) plus radiologist-assessed node signal distribution; Model 1 used short diameter and margin
biomarker_result: T2WI radiomics nomogram (Model 3: lymph-node signal distribution and Rad-score) for pelvic lymph-node metastasis
performance_value: 0.96 (Model 3 test set); Model 1 test-set AUC 0.78; Model 2 test-set AUC 0.93 (95% CI 0.82-0.99); nomogram C-index 0.964
validation_detail: One temporal split at the same hospital. The AUCs are lymph-node-level in the test set (45 nodes from 15 patients), not patient-level estimates. The cohort underlying the nomogram C-index of 0.964 is not stated separately from the test-set AUCs.
funding: Capital's Funds for Health Improvement and Research (2020-2-40710)
key_finding: A T2WI radiomics nomogram predicted pelvic lymph-node metastasis on the temporal test set with AUC 0.96, higher than image features alone (AUC 0.78).
limitations_as_stated: Retrospective study with a small sample that needs larger multicenter prospective validation; the radiomics model used only T2WI and not DWI or DCE.
other_key_outcomes: Model 2 and Model 3 outperformed Model 1 on the test set (P=0.019 and P=0.020); Model 2 versus Model 3 was not significant (P=0.649). Decision-curve analysis favored Model 3.
extraction_note: Test-set discrimination is reported at lymph-node level (45 nodes nested in 15 patients). n_analytic is those test-set nodes.

title: Epigenome-wide DNA methylation and transcriptome profiling of localized and locally advanced prostate cancer: Uncovering new molecular markers.
study_design: Small own-cohort epitranscriptomic discovery with public cBioPortal mutation filtering and external ML classification
data_source_detail: PP adipose methylome/transcriptome in 10 PCa patients (4 LPC, 6 LAPC); external mutation and expression cohorts from cBioPortal (MSKCC, Broad/Cornell, Fred Hutchinson, Mangiola PP adipose)
data_modality_detail: Affymetrix expression and Illumina 450k methylation on periprostatic adipose tissue
algorithm: LASSO integrative screening; XGBoost and CART with SHAP for classification
input_features: 30-gene epitranscriptomic signature (anti-correlated hypermethylated downregulated genes)
biomarker_result: 30-gene PP-adipose epitranscriptomic signature
performance_value: AUC 0.81 metastasis vs primary PCa; AUC 0.88 high- vs low-progression risk on external expression cohorts
validation_detail: Signature derived in n=10 PP adipose cohort; ML evaluated on public tumor expression cohorts focused on metastasis and progression because LPC/LAPC external n was too small.
funding: Manitoba Medical Services Foundation Allen Rouse award and CancerCare Manitoba Foundation partial support.
key_finding: Integrative PP-adipose methylation-expression profiling yielded a 30-gene signature with moderate-to-good discrimination for metastasis and progression risk on public PCa expression data.
limitations_as_stated: Discovery cohort is very small; no external cohort with matched methylation and expression; confounding from diet/activity not measured.
other_key_outcomes: Mutation-frequency refinement using >1500 primary vs metastatic samples; LPC vs LAPC differential discovery in PP fat.
extraction_note: Appraisal flags borderline scope because biomarkers come from periprostatic adipose rather than standard tumor tissue and discovery n=10 is tiny.

title: Prediction of clinically significant prostate cancer with a multimodal MRI-based radiomics nomogram.
study_design: retrospective multicenter cohort study
data_source_detail: Cohort 1: Changhai Hospital, Shanghai, China (n=201, Jan 2016-Dec 2019, training/test); Cohort 2 (external validation set 1): Ruijin Hospital Luwan Branch, Shanghai, China (n=66, Jan 2019-Dec 2021); Cohort 3 (external validation set 2): 989th Hospital of the joint logistic support force of the Chinese People's Liberation Army, Luoyang, China (n=122, Jan 2019-Dec 2021)
data_modality_detail: Biparametric prostate MRI (T2WI and DWI, 3.0T), pre-biopsy; PyRadiomics-extracted first-order, shape, texture and higher-order features (1409 features per VOI)
algorithm: Variance threshold + SelectKBest + LASSO feature selection; multivariate logistic regression (radiomics signature + PI-RADS nomogram)
input_features: Radiomics texture/shape/first-order/higher-order features (1409/VOI) from whole-prostate (T2WI) + lesion (DWI) segmentation, reduced via LASSO to 10 optimal features, combined with PI-RADS v2.1 score
biomarker_result: Multimodal MRI radiomics signature (RS) + PI-RADS nomogram for clinically significant prostate cancer (CS-PCa, Gleason score >=7 / ISUP grade >=2)
performance_value: Nomogram AUC: training set n=141: 0.967; test set n=60: 0.964; external validation set 1 n=66: 0.945; external validation set 2 n=122: 0.942 (vs. PI-RADS alone: 0.835/0.843/0.824/0.796 respectively, all p<0.05 by DeLong test); NRI 0.326-0.372; best single radiomics model in training set: sensitivity=92.8%, specificity=90.9%, accuracy=92.2%
validation_detail: Cohort 1 (n=201) randomized 7:3 into internal training (n=141) and test (n=60) sets; Cohorts 2 (n=66) and 3 (n=122) are genuinely independent, different-hospital, different-period external validation sets - true external multicenter validation, not a relabeled internal split.
funding: Project of the Action Plan of Major Diseases Prevention and Treatment (2017ZX01001-S12); Special Project of Integrated Traditional Chinese and Western Medicine in General Hospitals of Shanghai (ZHYY-ZXYJHZX-201901); Changhai hospital discipline construction project (2020YXK034)
key_finding: A radiomics nomogram combining a LASSO-selected whole-prostate(T2WI)+lesion(DWI) radiomics signature with PI-RADS achieved very high AUCs (0.942-0.967) for predicting clinically significant prostate cancer, significantly outperforming PI-RADS alone across training, test, and two independent external validation cohorts from different hospitals.
limitations_as_stated: Relatively small retrospective sample size implying selection bias and low generalizability despite external validation; manual segmentation favoring subjective error and unsuitable for large-scale data processing; no deep learning tools developed/validated for CS-PCa prediction.
other_key_outcomes: 10 different radiomics models compared across T2WI/DWI x lesion/whole-prostate segmentation combinations, training-set AUCs ranging 0.800-0.967; PI-RADS alone AUC=0.835, PSA alone AUC=0.776; excellent inter/intra-observer segmentation reproducibility (ICC>=0.9).
extraction_note: appraisal_note flagged 'very high AUC warrants cautious applicability.' validation_level is genuinely external_multicenter (three distinct hospitals); the very high AUCs together with small, manually-segmented, retrospective per-site cohorts (n=60-201) support the appraisal's applicability caution, documented here in validation_detail/limitations rather than by downgrading the validation_level label.

title: Computational Recognition of a Regulatory T-cell-specific Signature With Potential Implications in Prognosis, Immunotherapy, and Therapeutic Resistance of Prostate Cancer.
study_design: Public multi-GEO immune-cell deconvolution framework with TCGA/ICGC PRAD prognostic signature
data_source_detail: 42 purified immune-cell GEO microarray datasets; TCGA-PRAD RNA-seq n=454; ICGC PRAD-FR n=25; immunotherapy response GEO cohorts
data_modality_detail: Bulk RNA-seq TPM (TCGA/ICGC) plus immune-cell reference expression profiles
algorithm: Machine-learning Treg-specific mRNA discovery pipeline (OCLR stemness referenced); Cox-based signature construction
input_features: Five-gene TILTregSig (SOCS2, EGR1, RRM2, TPP1, C11orf54) from Treg-specific mRNA filtering
biomarker_result: TILTregSig five-mRNA Treg prognostic score
performance_value: 1.170 (multivariate Cox for recurrence-free survival, 95% CI 1.079-1.267, p<0.001; TCGA)
validation_detail: TCGA-PRAD multivariate Cox for recurrence-free survival. ICGC PRAD was also used to monitor prognosis. The time-dependent recurrence-free survival ROC is described as moderate, and the text does not print that AUC.
key_finding: A PBMC-derived five-gene Treg signature was proposed to stratify PRAD prognosis and relate to tumor immunity and immunotherapy response patterns.
limitations_as_stated: NR
other_key_outcomes: Immunotherapy response prediction in five public CIT datasets; GSCALite genetic/methylation analyses; in vitro Treg proliferation assays.
extraction_note: Primary prognostic number printed for TILTregSig is the TCGA multivariate HR. A separate tumor-immune-score AUC of 0.665 is reported. The full text does not print a numeric time-dependent AUC for recurrence-free survival.

title: A Novel Angiogenesis-Related Gene Signature to Predict Biochemical Recurrence of Patients with Prostate Cancer following Radical Therapy.
study_design: Retrospective multi-cohort transcriptomic prognostic signature after hallmark ssGSEA screening
data_source_detail: Training TCGA-PRAD n=327; external validation GSE116918 n=223, GSE70770 n=221, GSE54460 n=93 (844 total after eligibility filters)
data_modality_detail: Bulk RNA-seq and microarray expression after log2 normalization
algorithm: Random survival forest plus univariate/multivariate Cox regression
input_features: Three-gene angiogenesis-related score (NRP1, JAG2, VCAN)
biomarker_result: Angiogenesis-related three-gene ARS signature
performance_value: Pooled meta HR 1.58 (95% CI 1.38–1.81) for BCR; training HR 1.57 (1.21–2.03); validation cohort HRs 1.84, 1.42, 1.44
validation_detail: Signature coefficients fit in TCGA training cohort and tested unchanged in three independent GEO validation cohorts.
key_finding: Angiogenesis was the top BCR-associated hallmark and a three-gene angiogenesis score independently stratified recurrence across four datasets.
limitations_as_stated: Retrospective design needs larger prospective confirmation; high-risk biology and drug-response links require experimental validation.
other_key_outcomes: Immune infiltration and angiogenesis-inhibitor sensitivity analyses in high-risk groups.

title: Contrast-Enhanced Ultrasound-Magnetic Resonance Imaging Radiomics Based Model for Predicting the Biochemical Recurrence of Prostate Cancer: A Feasibility Study.
study_design: Retrospective two-center CEUS-MRI radiomics with random 7:3 split and nomogram

data_modality_detail: MRI radiomics (3D Slicer ROI), CEUS perfusion metrics, and clinical variables
