input_features: Combined clinical, CEUS (PI/TTP/AT), and MRI texture features (e.g., SmallAreaHighGrayLevelEmphasis, RunVariance, Contrast)
biomarker_result: Clinical-CEUS-MRI combinatorial BCR prediction model with nomogram
performance_value: Training AUC 0.914 (95% CI 0.854–0.974); test-set AUC 0.920 (95% CI 0.849–0.991) for combinatorial model
validation_detail: Random 70/30 split of the same pooled two-center cohort; authors label the holdout as external validation but it is not institution-independent.
key_finding: Integrating clinical, CEUS, and MRI radiomics outperformed single-modality models for post-RP BCR prediction on holdout data.
limitations_as_stated: NR
other_key_outcomes: Decision curve analysis favored the combinatorial model over clinical or imaging-only models.
extraction_note: Appraisal flags borderline validation because the 30% test split is from the same pooled cohort rather than independent multicenter validation.

title: Comprehensive assessment of cellular senescence in the tumor microenvironment.
study_design: Pan-cancer senescence resource with PRAD-focused three-gene ML prognostic module and IHC check
data_source_detail: TCGA/GTEx pan-cancer bulk data; PRAD validation in ~660 patients across four public cohorts plus 72-patient IHC set
data_modality_detail: Bulk transcriptomics/proteomics plus scRNA-seq atlas; PRAD IHC validation on TMA
algorithm: Three machine-learning algorithms compared to identify PRAD survival hub genes (methods truncated in slice)
input_features: Three CS hub genes (SPAG5, TACC3, TROAP) selected for PRAD prognosis
biomarker_result: Three-gene CS-based PRAD prognostic predictor
performance_value: approximately 0.7 (average 1-, 3-, and 5-year progression AUC in the TCGA training set and four testing PRAD cohorts)
validation_detail: CS predictor assessed in TCGA and four published PRAD cohorts (PRJCA001124, MSKCC, Setlur et al., and GSE70769), with IHC in 72 in-house PRAD specimens. Authors state an average progression AUC of approximately 0.7.
funding: National Key R&D and CAMS/NNSF grants.
key_finding: Among pan-cancer senescence analyses, three CS genes were prioritized as feasible PRAD prognostic markers with protein-level IHC support.
limitations_as_stated: GSVA-based CS scoring depends on gene-set composition; senescence mechanisms in PRAD need further experiments.
other_key_outcomes: Pan-cancer CS landscape, immunotherapy associations, and TCSER web resource for CS scoring.
extraction_note: The article is a pan-cancer senescence resource; the extracted axis is the prostate three-gene CS predictor (SPAG5, TACC3, TROAP). The full text gives the progression AUC only as approximately 0.7, not as exact per-cohort values. A separate immunotherapy analysis reported a mean AUC of approximately 0.68.

title: Identification of a Steroid Hormone-Associated Gene Signature Predicting the Prognosis of Prostate Cancer through an Integrative Bioinformatics Analysis.
study_design: TCGA-PRAD integrative bioinformatics with LASSO signature and subtype-association external check
data_source_detail: TCGA-PRAD RNA-seq via DriverDB (495 patients with PFI analysis); PCTA PCS/PAM50 subtype labels for association validation
data_modality_detail: Bulk RNA-seq RPKM with steroid-hormone pathway gene filtering
algorithm: LASSO Cox (glmnet) feature selection with weighted expression signature score
input_features: Eight-gene steroid-hormone-associated signature (from 538 pathway genes and DE filtering)
biomarker_result: Eight-gene steroid-hormone PFI signature
performance_value: Univariate Cox HRs up to 2.19 for individual signature genes on 5-year PFI (Table 1; e.g., adjusted p<0.05)
validation_detail: No independent survival cohort; external PCTA cohorts used only to relate signature scores to molecular subtypes (PCS/PAM50), not to validate PFI prediction.
key_finding: Eight steroid-hormone pathway genes associated with poor 5-year PFI were combined into a LASSO-weighted prognostic signature.
limitations_as_stated: NR
other_key_outcomes: Functional annotation of signature genes across GO/KEGG/Reactome steroid-hormone processes.
extraction_note: Appraisal notes single-source TCGA design without independent survival-outcome validation cohort.

title: Utility of Clinical-Radiomic Model to Identify Clinically Significant Prostate Cancer in Biparametric MRI PI-RADS V2.1 Category 3 Lesions.
study_design: Single-center retrospective PI-RADS 3 biparametric MRI radiomics with 7:3 split
data_source_detail: 103 patients with PI-RADS 3 lesions on 3.0-T MRI before biopsy (training n=75, testing n=28 per slice tables)
data_modality_detail: T2WI, DWI, and ADC radiomics with mRMR and LASSO feature selection
algorithm: mRMR and LASSO radiomics selection with multivariable logistic regression nomogram
input_features: Four radiomic features plus age and PSA in integrated clinical-radiomic model
biomarker_result: Radscore plus clinical-radiomic nomogram for csPCa among PI-RADS 3 lesions
performance_value: Testing-set AUC 0.88 (95% CI 0.75–1.00) for clinical-radiomic model vs radiomics alone AUC 0.71
validation_detail: Random 70/30 split within the single-center PI-RADS 3 cohort; training AUC 0.90 (95% CI 0.83–0.97).
key_finding: Integrating age, PSA, and four MRI radiomic features improved csPCa detection among PI-RADS 3 lesions versus radiomics alone on holdout data.
limitations_as_stated: NR
other_key_outcomes: Decision curve analysis suggested clinical benefit of the integrated nomogram.

title: A Novel Artificial Intelligence-Powered Method for Prediction of Early Recurrence of Prostate Cancer After Prostatectomy and Cancer Drivers.
study_design: Deep learning WSI morphometric score trained on TCGA-PRAD with university external validation
data_source_detail: Training TCGA-PRAD WSIs n=243 (92 early BCR, 151 BCR-free ≥3y); external UW-Madison RP WSIs n=173
data_modality_detail: H&E whole-slide images tiled for multiscale CNN attention-based morphometric scoring
algorithm: Multiscale CNN feature extractor with attention-based tile weighting (AI-morphometric score)
input_features: Slide-level AI-morphometric score from ROI heatmaps plus optional pathologic covariates
biomarker_result: AI-morphometric score (AI-MS) for 3-year post-RP BCR
performance_value: External validation AUC 0.78 for 3-year BCR vs GGG AUC 0.62; combined AI-MS plus pathology AUC 0.84; GGG2/3 subgroup AUCs 0.84 and 0.81
validation_detail: Model trained on TCGA-PRAD and evaluated on independent UW-Madison RP archive without retraining.
key_finding: CNN-derived morphometric scores from RP WSIs outperformed Gleason grade groups for 3-year BCR and highlighted ROI biomarker differences including TMEM173.
limitations_as_stated: NR
other_key_outcomes: ROI-level IHC validation for Ki67, PD-L1, CC3, and immune markers in high- vs low-scored regions.
extraction_note: Appraisal notes source code was withheld pending patent approval, limiting reproducibility despite strong external validation.

title: Development and Validation of a Radiomics Nomogram for Predicting Clinically Significant Prostate Cancer in PI-RADS 3 Lesions.
study_design: Single-institution PI-RADS 3 radiomics nomogram with internal train/test split
data_source_detail: 306 PI-RADS 3 patients (institution 1); training n=199 and test n=107 after random split
data_modality_detail: T2WI and ADC radiomics with LASSO and logistic regression nomogram
algorithm: LASSO radiomics selection with logistic regression; optional SMOTE for class balance in signature variant
input_features: Selected MRI radiomic features plus clinical covariates in radiomics nomogram
biomarker_result: Radiomics nomogram (Rad-score) for csPCa in PI-RADS 3 lesions
performance_value: Test-set nomogram AUC 0.884 (95% CI 0.831–0.937); SMOTE-augmented radiomics signature AUC 0.840 (95% CI 0.776–0.904)
validation_detail: Random split within single institution; no external multicenter validation reported.
key_finding: A radiomics-based nomogram improved csPCa detection among PI-RADS 3 lesions compared with radiomics signature alone on internal test data.
limitations_as_stated: NR
other_key_outcomes: SMOTE improved radiomics signature discrimination versus unbalanced training.

title: Deep Learning with Quantitative Features of Magnetic Resonance Images to Predict Biochemical Recurrence of Radical Prostatectomy: A Multi-Center Study.
study_design: Multicenter retrospective MRI deep-learning BCR model with internal and external validation
data_source_detail: Primary cohort n=368 plus validation cohorts VC1 n=34 and VC2 n=83 from three centers
data_modality_detail: Pre- and post-operative MRI quantitative radiomics/deep features for BCR-free survival
algorithm: Deep learning with quantitative MRI features combined in DRS-BCR score
input_features: Deep MRI quantitative feature score (DRS-BCR) with optional clinical combine model
biomarker_result: DRS-BCR deep MRI prognostic score for BCR
performance_value: Combined clinical-model C-index 0.802 (95% CI 0.758–0.846) in primary cohort; 3-year BCR AUC 0.84 (PC), 0.85 (VC1), 0.84 (VC2)
validation_detail: Model developed on primary multicenter cohort and evaluated on two additional center cohorts for time-dependent BCR discrimination.
key_finding: Deep MRI-based DRS-BCR score stratified BCR risk with consistent AUC across primary and two validation cohorts.
limitations_as_stated: NR
other_key_outcomes: Comparison of pre-operative, post-operative, and combined clinical MRI models.
extraction_note: Co-reported C-index and time-dependent AUC; C-index used as model-selection metric.

title: An integrated nomogram combining deep learning, Prostate Imaging-Reporting and Data System (PI-RADS) scoring, and clinical variables for identification of clinically significant prostate cancer on biparametric MRI: a retrospective multicentre study.
study_design: Multicenter biparametric MRI deep-learning integrated nomogram vs PI-RADS and clinical nomograms
data_source_detail: Training 368 patients (PROSTATEx n=204, UH Cleveland n=126, Mount Sinai n=38); independent validation 224 (Cleveland Clinic n=151, LIJ n=73)
data_modality_detail: Biparametric MRI deep learning (DIN), PI-RADS (PIN), and clinical variables integrated in ClaD nomogram
algorithm: Deep learning imaging nomogram integrated with clinical variables (ClaD)
input_features: ClaD integrated nomogram combining deep imaging, PI-RADS, and clinical predictors
biomarker_result: ClaD integrated csPCa detection nomogram
performance_value: Independent validation AUC 0.81 (95% CI 0.76–0.85) for csPCa vs DIN 0.74 and PIN 0.76; RP subset BCR separation HR 5.92 (2.34–15.00, p=0.044)
validation_detail: Training across three sites and validation on two independent sites with fixed model comparison to DIN and PIN.
key_finding: The ClaD integrated nomogram outperformed deep-imaging-only and PI-RADS-only nomograms for csPCa and showed significant BCR stratification in RP patients.
limitations_as_stated: NR
other_key_outcomes: Comparison against PBCG clinical risk calculator referenced in appraisal.
extraction_note: Appraisal notes borderline PROBAST applicability due to inter-reader PI-RADS variability and mixed biopsy/RP reference standards.

title: A Genomic-Clinicopathologic Nomogram for the Prediction of Lymph Node Invasion in Prostate Cancer.
study_design: TCGA genomic-clinicopathologic LNI nomogram with SMOTE-balanced internal validation
data_source_detail: TCGA-PRAD LNI vs non-LNI expression with SMOTE to balance 1:4.4 class ratio; five matched primary/LNI tissue pairs for hub-gene qPCR
data_modality_detail: TCGA RNA-seq DEGs between LNI and non-LNI tumors
algorithm: Support vector machine after SMOTE; genomic-clinicopathologic nomogram with Gleason grade
input_features: 37-gene SVM LNI risk score plus Gleason grade in nomogram
biomarker_result: 37-gene SVM-based LNI risk score with nomogram
performance_value: SMOTE-balanced training AUC 0.947 and validation AUC 0.901 for SVM; nomogram training AUC 0.946 and validation AUC 0.910
validation_detail: SMOTE-balanced validation split from the same TCGA source rather than independent multicenter LNI cohort.
key_finding: A 37-gene SVM LNI score combined with Gleason grade yielded high internal discrimination for nodal involvement in TCGA.
limitations_as_stated: Authors note lack of external multicenter validation.
other_key_outcomes: Hub-gene expression differences validated in five matched primary/LNI sample pairs.
extraction_note: Appraisal flags borderline validation because SMOTE validation remains within single TCGA source.

title: Advanced Imaging Analysis in Prostate MRI: Building a Radiomic Signature to Predict Tumor Aggressiveness.
study_design: Exploratory single-center mpMRI radiomics pipeline for post-RP aggressiveness
data_source_detail: 102 consecutive mpMRI+RP patients screened; n=62 analyzed after exclusions with internal resampling
data_modality_detail: Multiparametric MRI radiomics (T2, DWI, ADC) with reproducibility-focused pipeline
algorithm: Radiomics feature selection with internal resampling (signature accuracy reported)
input_features: Multiparametric MRI radiomic signature for GGG, pN, and EPE endpoints
biomarker_result: mpMRI radiomic signature for tumor aggressiveness proxies
performance_value: Signature accuracy approximately 0.88 (GGG), 0.89 (pN), and 0.84 (EPE) in internal evaluation
validation_detail: Single-center exploratory design with internal resampling only; no external validation cohort.
key_finding: A reproducible mpMRI radiomics pipeline yielded moderate-to-high accuracy for pathologic aggressiveness markers in a small single-center cohort.
limitations_as_stated: Exploratory single-center design requires external validation.
other_key_outcomes: Inter-reader PI-RADS concordance with prostatectomy pathology.
extraction_note: Appraisal notes small n=62 and absence of external validation with accuracy rather than AUC reporting.

title: A Nomogram Based on a Multiparametric Ultrasound Radiomics Model for Discrimination Between Malignant and Benign Prostate Lesions.
study_design: Retrospective multiparametric ultrasound radiomics with five-fold cross-validation
data_source_detail: 112 patients with prostate lesions (54 PCa, 58 benign) undergoing mpUS before biopsy
data_modality_detail: B-mode, shear-wave elastography (SWE), and combined mpUS radiomics plus clinical factors
algorithm: Radiomics with LASSO/feature selection and logistic models; five-fold CV
input_features: Combined clinical factors and mpUS radiomic features
biomarker_result: Clinical-radiomics combined PCa detection model
performance_value: Combined model AUC 0.90 vs radiomics 0.85 and clinical 0.84; training AUC 0.88 and validation AUC 0.84 reported for selected model
validation_detail: Five-fold cross-validation within single retrospective cohort.
key_finding: Combining clinical variables with mpUS radiomics improved PCa diagnosis versus either modality alone under cross-validation.
limitations_as_stated: NR
other_key_outcomes: Decision curve analysis favored the combined model.

title: Identification of a Transcriptomic Prognostic Signature by Machine Learning Using a Combination of Small Cohorts of Prostate Cancer.
study_design: Multi-cohort RNA-seq ML benchmark with random-forest BCR signature
data_source_detail: TCGA-PRAD n=96 (≥60-month follow-up) plus VPCC n=23 (5 BCR events) for external check; 171 patients reprocessed uniformly
data_modality_detail: Bulk RNA-seq reprocessed from TCGA and VPCC with uniform pipeline
algorithm: Random forest selected among 13 benchmarked ML algorithms
input_features: Three-gene BCR signature (JUN, HES4, PPDPF)
biomarker_result: JUN-HES4-PPDPF random-forest BCR signature
performance_value: Signature accuracy 74.2% (BER 27%) vs clinico-pathologic baseline 69.2% (BER 32%) on evaluated cohort
validation_detail: Signature developed on TCGA-PRAD and tested on small VPCC cohort (n=23, five BCR events).
key_finding: A three-gene random-forest signature modestly outperformed standard clinico-pathologic variables for BCR prediction.
limitations_as_stated: Need larger single-cohort validation; VPCC arm is very small.
other_key_outcomes: Benchmark comparison of 13 ML algorithms with featureless control.

title: Immune-Related Gene-Based Novel Subtypes to Establish a Model Predicting the Risk of Prostate Cancer.
study_design: TCGA immune-gene consensus clustering with risk-group survival model
data_source_detail: TCGA-PRAD immune-related gene expression; consensus clusters C1–C4 (487 patients in survival analysis)
data_modality_detail: Bulk RNA-seq with immunologically relevant gene subset and consensus clustering
algorithm: Consensus clustering plus PCA; log-rank survival classification into high-risk C3 vs low-risk groups
input_features: Four immune-based molecular subtypes (C1–C4) collapsed to C3 high-risk vs C1+C2+C4 low-risk
biomarker_result: Immune-related consensus subtype risk grouping
performance_value: DFS log-rank p=0.04 across immune subtypes; C3 high-risk vs C1+C2+C4 low-risk separation on Kaplan-Meier curves
validation_detail: Single TCGA-PRAD cohort without external replication of subtype survival separation.
key_finding: Immune-based consensus clustering identified a C3 subtype with worse DFS and distinct genomic/immune features including CLU CNA and TMPRSS2-ERG frequency.
limitations_as_stated: NR
other_key_outcomes: Immune infiltration differences and AR/TMPRSS2-ERG associations by subtype.

title: Development of a Novel, Multi-Parametric, MRI-Based Radiomic Nomogram for Differentiating Between Clinically Significant and Insignificant Prostate Cancer.
study_design: Multicenter mpMRI radiomics csPCa vs ciPCa with internal and external validation
data_source_detail: 159 path-confirmed PCa patients: training n=54 and internal validation n=22 (center 1) plus external validation n=83 (center 2)
data_modality_detail: Multiparametric MRI radiomics with clinical-radiomic nomogram
algorithm: Radiomics feature selection with logistic regression nomogram
input_features: MRI radiomics signature combined with clinical predictors
biomarker_result: Radiomics nomogram discriminating csPCa from ciPCa
performance_value: Radiomics signature AUC 0.95 (training), 0.86 (internal validation), 0.81 (external validation); nomogram AUC 0.95 training and 0.93 internal validation
validation_detail: Independent external center cohort (n=83) plus smaller internal holdout from second center.
key_finding: MRI radiomics with nomogram achieved high csPCa discrimination in training and remained strong on an independent external validation cohort.
limitations_as_stated: NR
other_key_outcomes: Comparison between csPCa and ciPCa classification tasks.

title: Radiomics Based on Multiparametric Magnetic Resonance Imaging to Predict Extraprostatic Extension of Prostate Cancer.
study_design: retrospective single-center cohort
data_source_detail: Peking Union Medical College Hospital; 95 patients with 115 lesions (49 EPE-positive, 66 EPE-negative) imaged at 3.0T mpMRI
data_modality_detail: Radiomic features from T2WI, DWI, ADC, and DCE; eight features retained
algorithm: LASSO regression
input_features: mpMRI radiomic features for whole-tumor segmentations
biomarker_result: mpMRI radiomics model for extraprostatic extension
performance_value: 0.865 (95% CI 0.738-0.992; validation, 33 lesions); training AUC 0.919 (95% CI 0.861-0.978; 82 lesions). Validation accuracy 81.8%, sensitivity 71.4%, specificity 89.5%
validation_detail: Lesions randomly divided into training (82) and validation (33). Single center, single scanner, no external cohort.
funding: National Natural Science Foundation of China (91859119, 81901742); Non-profit Central Research Institute Fund of CAMS (2019XK320028); Natural Science Foundation of Beijing Municipality (7192176); Central University Basic Scientific Research Business Expenses (3332018022); National Public Welfare Basic Scientific Research Project of CAMS (2019PT320008, 2018PT32003)
conflicts_of_interest: L. Zhao, L. Mao, and X. Li were employed by Deepwise AI Lab, Deepwise Inc. The remaining authors stated that the research was conducted in the absence of commercial or financial relationships that could be construed as a potential conflict of interest.
key_finding: An eight-feature mpMRI LASSO radiomics model predicted pathologic extraprostatic extension with validation AUC 0.865, higher than the clinical model (AUC 0.658) and similar to the combined nomogram (AUC 0.857).
limitations_as_stated: Single-center study with a small sample and no external validation; images from one scanner, so scanner heterogeneity was not assessed; subjective morphologic EPE features were not included in the nomogram.
other_key_outcomes: Validation clinical-model AUC 0.658; combined nomogram AUC 0.857 (P=0.644 versus radiomics). Decision-curve analysis was reported on the internal validation group.
extraction_note: Analytic N is the 33-lesion internal validation set that supports AUC 0.865. Decision-curve analysis was not coded as clinical utility because there was no external or prospective utility study.

title: Multi-omics Biomarker Pipeline Reveals Elevated Levels of Protein-glutamine Gamma-glutamyltransferase 4 in Seminal Plasma of Prostate Cancer Patients.
study_design: multi-center case-control
data_source_detail: Murray Koffler Urologic Wellness Centre (Mount Sinai Hospital), University Health Network, and Calgary Prostate Cancer Centre. SRM verification in 152 prostate cancer and 67 negative-biopsy seminal plasma samples; ELISA in 228 seminal plasma and 80 serum samples. Shotgun data in PRIDE PXD007657.
data_modality_detail: Seminal plasma shotgun proteomics, SRM, and an in-house TGM4 ELISA
algorithm: XGBoost over all 1- to 5-marker combinations with 10x10 stratified cross-validation; headline TGM4 result is an ELISA
input_features: 19 seminal plasma candidate proteins plus seminal KLK3, serum PSA, and age; primary reported marker is seminal plasma TGM4
biomarker_result: Seminal plasma TGM4 (protein-glutamine gamma-glutamyltransferase 4)
performance_value: 0.66 (ELISA, seminal plasma, serum PSA >=4 ng/ml and age >=50)
validation_detail: TGM4 ELISA is described as an independent verification after discovery and SRM qualification, within the same multi-center recruitment. XGBoost panels used 10x10 stratified cross-validation on the SRM feature set. Not an external institution cohort.
funding: Canadian Institutes of Health Research grant 285693 to E.P. Diamandis, K. Jarvi, and A.P. Drabovich; Prostate Cancer Canada RS2015-01 to A.P. Drabovich
key_finding: Seminal plasma TGM4 measured by ELISA distinguished prostate cancer from negative biopsy with AUC 0.66 in men with serum PSA >=4 ng/ml and age >=50, and outperformed age and serum PSA in that comparison; serum TGM4 did not.
limitations_as_stated: Only medium- to high-abundance seminal plasma proteins were evaluated; some negative-biopsy patients may have had missed cancer; Gleason score was used in place of 20-year survival.
other_key_outcomes: XGBoost two-protein panel (TGM4 with PAEP) AUC 0.76 (95% CI 0.74-0.79). SRM TGM4 AUC 0.61. ELISA cutoff >1.74 ug/ml gave 92% specificity at 31% sensitivity. Three-protein panel AUC 0.73 and a four-protein panel plus serum PSA AUC 0.83 for high-grade prostate cancer.
extraction_note: Title result is the ELISA AUC 0.66. The subgroup sample size is given only in supplemental Table S19 and is not stated in the main text, so n_analytic is NR. The machine-learning panel is a separate axis.

title: Temporal Stability and Prognostic Biomarker Potential of the Prostate Cancer Urine miRNA Transcriptome.
study_design: Longitudinal urine miRNA cohort with random-forest aggressive PCa prediction
data_source_detail: 149 PCa patients with urine miRNA profiling; training n=99 (50 high-risk GS>7, 49 low-risk GS6); validation n=40 (11 high-risk, 29 low-risk)
data_modality_detail: NanoString urine miRNA profiles from urinary cell sediments
algorithm: Random forest with intrastable miRNA feature selection
input_features: Intrastable urinary miRNAs reflecting tumor miRNA abundance
biomarker_result: Urine miRNA random-forest aggressive PCa classifier
performance_value: 0.74 (95% CI 0.55-0.92; independent validation cohort)
validation_detail: Training cohort n=99 with 10-times repeated five-fold cross-validation (mean AUC 0.72). Independent validation cohort n=40, AUC 0.74 (95% CI 0.55-0.92).
funding: Ontario Institute for Cancer Research and government of Ontario support.
key_finding: Longitudinal urine miRNA profiling showed within-person stability and supported a random-forest model for aggressive vs low-risk PCa applied to an independent validation set.
limitations_as_stated: Large tightly defined populations needed to validate urine miRNA biomarkers for risk stratification.
other_key_outcomes: Quantification of intra- vs inter-individual miRNA variability (ICC analyses).
extraction_note: Analytic N is the independent validation cohort that supports AUC 0.74. The confidence interval is wide (0.55-0.92).

title: Tissue Phenomics for prognostic biomarker discovery in low- and intermediate-risk prostate cancer.
study_design: retrospective cohort
data_source_detail: Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich radical-prostatectomy archive; Gleason score 6-7b; 90 patients, of whom 40 had PSA biochemical recurrence
data_modality_detail: IHC whole-slide images quantifying CD8-positive cells, CD68-positive cells, and CD34-positive microvasculature around cancerous glands
algorithm: k-nearest neighbor (k=5), support vector machine, and linear predictor, compared under leave-one-out cross-validation
input_features: Tissue phenes describing immune-cell and vessel spatial relations in the tumor microenvironment; models used sets of 8 or 20 phenes
biomarker_result: Multi-phene tissue signature of CD8-positive and CD68-positive cells with local microvasculature
performance_value: 88% (leave-one-out cross-validation; 5-nearest neighbor on 20 phenes and linear predictor on 8 phenes)
validation_detail: Leave-one-out cross-validation on the same 90-patient cohort. No external cohort.
conflicts_of_interest: N. Harder, M. Athelogou, H. Hessel, N. Brieu, M. Yigitsoy, J. Zimmermann, M. Baatz, G. Binnig, G. Schmidt, and R. Huss are or were employees of Definiens AG.
key_finding: Combining tissue phenes with supervised classifiers predicted prostate-cancer progression with leave-one-out accuracy of 88%, above univariate phene accuracies of up to 83.3% and above Gleason-score prediction.
limitations_as_stated: Authors state that with n=90 the approach is prone to overfitting, which is why leave-one-out cross-validation was used. For some patients only an approximated 36-month disease-free interval was available.
other_key_outcomes: Top univariate phene (CD8-positive to CD34-positive ratio in the tumor microenvironment) leave-one-out accuracy 83.3% (log-rank p<3.05e-7). SVM linear kernel accuracy 87% on the 20-phene set.
extraction_note: Authors explicitly warn that the n=90 analysis is prone to overfitting. The 88% accuracy was reached by two different models (5-nearest neighbor on 20 phenes and a linear predictor on 8 phenes).

title: Seminal plasma as a source of prostate cancer peptide biomarker candidates for detection of indolent and advanced disease.
study_design: open-label multi-center case-control
data_source_detail: Three centers; 125 patients (70 prostate cancer, 21 benign prostatic hyperplasia, 25 chronic prostatitis, 9 healthy controls). Diagnostic test set: 48 prostate cancer, 12 BPH, 11 chronic prostatitis, and 4 healthy controls.
data_modality_detail: Capillary electrophoresis mass spectrometry peptide profiles of seminal plasma
algorithm: Support vector machine
input_features: Stepwise 21-peptide and 5-peptide seminal plasma signatures
biomarker_result: 21PP and 5PP seminal plasma peptide signatures for prostate cancer detection
performance_value: 75% (95% CI 64%-83%, P=0.0001; independent test set). Sensitivity 83% (95% CI 70%-93%); specificity 67% (95% CI 46%-83%)
validation_detail: SVM signatures were trained on a discovery cohort (training AUC 100% for 21PP and 99% for 5PP) and applied to an independent test set from the same study. Not an external multi-institutional cohort.
funding: German Ministry of Economy and Technology BMWi grants KF0362802MD8 and EP110141. No additional external funding.
conflicts_of_interest: E. Schiffer and J. Siwy are employees of Mosaiques Diagnostics GmbH. Authors state there are no patents, products in development, or marketed products to declare.
key_finding: A stepwise seminal plasma peptide signature detected prostate cancer in an independent test set with AUC 75%, sensitivity 83%, and specificity 67%, similar to PSA in that comparison.
limitations_as_stated: Restricted sample size was the major limitation. Authors state that prospective validation is still required.
other_key_outcomes: An 11-peptide panel for advanced versus organ-confined disease had validation sensitivity 80% and specificity 82%, with AUC 83% (95% CI 66%-94%) in a preliminary validation set. Discovery training AUCs near 100% are not the test-set result.
extraction_note: Analytic N is the 75-sample independent test set for the diagnostic AUC. Primary axis is prostate-cancer detection; the advanced-disease panel is secondary.

title: Cancer genetics-guided discovery of serum biomarker signatures for diagnosis and prognosis of prostate cancer.
journal: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
study_design: Mouse glycoproteomics discovery with human serum glycoprotein ML for PTEN status
data_source_detail: Pten cKO vs wild-type mouse prostate/serum N-glycoproteomics plus human sera/tissue cohort n=99 (locPCa vs BPH)
data_modality_detail: Enriched N-linked glycoproteomics with machine-learning regression on human samples
algorithm: Machine-learning predictive regression models (methods reference computational modeling pipeline)
input_features: N-glycosite peptide features prioritized from mouse PTEN-loss discovery screen
biomarker_result: Glycoproteomic panel predicting tissue PTEN status
performance_value: NR
validation_detail: Human n=99 cohort used to build/test PTEN-status models after mouse discovery; independent external cohort not described in slice.

limitations_as_stated: NR
other_key_outcomes: Hypothesis-generation workflow from genetically engineered mouse models to clinical specimens.
extraction_note: Slice describes modeling approach but does not report numeric PTEN-prediction performance.

title: Pentachlorophenol enhances bladder cancer cell invasion through altered protein stability
study_design: translational/bioinformatic (in vitro functional assays + bioinformatic/machine-learning prognostic modeling + molecular docking/dynamics)
data_source_detail: TCGA-BLCA (training, 19 normal + 411 tumor); external validation in 4 independent GEO cohorts: GSE13507, GSE31684, GSE32894, GSE5287; plus in vitro T24/SW780 cell line experiments (not part of ML model)
data_modality_detail: Bulk RNA-seq (TCGA-BLCA training + 4 GEO validation cohorts); molecular docking/dynamics simulation as orthogonal in silico validation
algorithm: 101 machine learning algorithm combinations for survival modeling; selected model: Random Survival Forest + Stepwise Cox [both] (RSF+StepCox[both])
input_features: 58 BLCA-PCP overlapping target genes (from intersection of 262 predicted PCP targets and 1580 BLCA-related genes), reduced via ML to 3-gene signature
biomarker_result: PCP-related score (PCPRS), 3-gene signature: EGFR, MAP2K1, NFE2L2
performance_value: Best model mean C-index 0.615 across training+validation cohorts; TCGA-BLCA training: 10-fold CV C-index 0.608 (95% CI 0.599-0.617), bootstrap optimism-corrected C-index 0.606 (95% CI 0.597-0.614); external GEO cohorts moderate but consistent (exact per-cohort values not given as plain text numbers); meta-analysis pooled HR (continuous) 2.04 (95% CI 1.66-2.51), pooled HR (binary) 1.82 (95% CI 1.47-2.26)
validation_detail: Training in TCGA-BLCA (n=411); two rounds of internal validation within TCGA-BLCA (10-fold CV; 1000x bootstrap); external validation in 4 independent public GEO cohorts. Per appraisal_note, applicability is borderline: the prognostic model/PCPRS is validated on public cohorts with no PCP exposure data, decoupled from the actual PCP-exposure biomarker question anchoring the paper's title/abstract.
key_finding: A three-gene PCPRS signature (EGFR, MAP2K1, NFE2L2), selected from 101 ML algorithm combinations (best mean C-index 0.615), was associated with poor overall survival across TCGA-BLCA and four independent GEO cohorts (pooled HR 1.82-2.04); mechanistically, environmentally relevant PCP concentrations enhanced BLCA cell invasion by altering the protein stability of these three targets.
limitations_as_stated: PCP binding to EGFR/MAP2K1/NFE2L2 predicted computationally, not experimentally validated; molecular machinery underlying stability changes undefined; prognostic analyses conducted in public BLCA cohorts lacking PCP exposure data, so the 3-gene signature should be interpreted as a prognostic association rather than an exposure-specific biomarker; experimental evidence limited to 2 cell lines under acute exposure.
other_key_outcomes: Individual-gene meta-analysis (5 BLCA cohorts): pooled HR 1.83 EGFR, 1.75 MAP2K1, 0.59 NFE2L2. Molecular docking/MD simulations: PCP binding affinities to EGFR/MAP2K1/NFE2L2 approximately -5.30, -6.59, -6.27 kcal/mol. Functional knockdown/overexpression experiments confirm EGFR, MAP2K1, NFE2L2 mediate PCP-induced invasion.
extraction_note: Primary AI/ML axis extracted is the PCPRS prognostic gene signature (only element matching the SR's AI-biomarker scope); the paper's own narrative anchor is the mechanistic PCP-invasion finding, which is not itself an AI/ML biomarker discovery. validation_level/validation_detail describe the real design (public-cohort validation decoupled from PCP exposure), consistent with the inherited appraisal_note.

title: Epigenomics-Guided Multi-Omics Integration Uncovers a Lipid-Metabolic Signature with Translational Utility in Bladder Cancer.
study_design: TCGA BLCA random-forest prognostic signature with in vitro validation

performance_value: Stage 3 high-risk vs low-risk HR 2.83 (P=0.007); stage 4 HR 1.72 (P=0.027); TP53-mutant high-risk HR 2.75 (P<0.00001)

title: Centrosome-related gene SPHK1 drives bladder cancer progression and therapeutic vulnerability.

title: A machine learning-guided epithelial plasticity score refines prognostication and immune-context stratification in muscle-invasive bladder cancer.

title: Non-invasive evaluation of muscle invasion and survival prognosis in bladder cancer using enhanced CT-based deep learning radiomics: a multi-center real-world cohort study.

title: Radiogenomic analysis of muscle-invasive bladder cancer using CT-based texture analysis.

title: Machine learning-based determination of sex-related bladder cancer biomarkers.

title: Machine learning-based integration of systemic immune-inflammation and nutritional signatures for predicting disease-free survival in upper tract urothelial carcinoma: a multicenter study.
study_design: Four-center UTUC RSF prognostic score with SHAP and nomogram

title: Ribosome biogenesis programs define a three-gene RBscore with prognostic relevance in bladder cancer.
study_design: TCGA-BLCA RiBi score with ML strategy selection and GSE13507 validation
data_source_detail: TCGA-BLCA training; external GSE13507 validation; three-gene RBscore (PIN4, POP4, PRKDC)

title: Multidimensional transcriptomic analysis and in vitro experiments dissect the landscape of 2',2',4',4'-Tetrabromodiphenyl ether in bladder cancer progression.
study_design: BDE-47 toxicogenomic BLCA risk signature with in vitro exposure assays

title: Comprehensive Analysis Based on the Cancer-Immunity Cycle Identifies a Novel Immunosuppressive Subtype of Bladder Cancer.
study_design: retrospective bioinformatic cohort
data_source_detail: TCGA-BLCA (n=403) and GSE166716 for cancer-immunity-cycle gene discovery; diagnostic AUCs reported in TCGA-BLCA. IMvigor210 used for a secondary BIRC5 immunotherapy analysis.
data_modality_detail: Bulk RNA-seq of cancer-immunity-cycle genes
algorithm: LASSO, SVM-RFE, and random forest; hub genes are the intersection
input_features: Differentially expressed cancer-immunity-cycle genes from TCGA-BLCA and GSE166716
biomarker_result: Hub genes BIRC5, CXCL12, and HSPA12A
performance_value: 0.890 (BIRC5), 0.906 (CXCL12), and 0.867 (HSPA12A) in TCGA-BLCA
validation_detail: Diagnostic AUCs were calculated within TCGA-BLCA, the same cohort used for feature screening. GSE166716 supported gene overlap and WGCNA, not a held-out AUC. No external GU cohort for the reported AUCs.
funding: Social Development Program of the Yangzhou Municipal Bureau of Science and Technology (YZ2023080)
key_finding: LASSO, SVM-RFE, and random forest intersected on BIRC5, CXCL12, and HSPA12A, with TCGA-BLCA diagnostic AUCs of 0.890, 0.906, and 0.867.
limitations_as_stated: No dedicated limitations paragraph. The discussion states that only about 20% of bladder-cancer patients respond to immunotherapy and that biomarkers for resistance are needed.
other_key_outcomes: Unsupervised clustering of TCGA-BLCA (n=403) defined an exhausted immune class versus the remaining tumors. BIRC5 expression was also examined in IMvigor210 for atezolizumab response.
extraction_note: The printed AUCs are in-sample ROC values on TCGA-BLCA after the genes were selected in that dataset, so validation_level is none. Figure confidence intervals are not paired unambiguously with each gene in the text, so only the stated point estimates are recorded.

title: Multi-omics identification of a programmed cell death-related signature and potential target P4HB for bladder cancer based on a 101-combination machine learning and experimental validation.

title: A machine learning-based epigenetic signature reveals YTHDC1 stabilizes POU5F1 to oppose tumor progression.
study_design: retrospective multi-cohort bioinformatic study
data_source_detail: TCGA-BLCA training; external validation in IMvigor210, E-MTAB-4321, GSE31684, and GSE48075
data_modality_detail: Bulk expression of epigenetic-regulation genes, with single-cell RNA-seq used for immune-interaction context
algorithm: Cox univariate screen followed by multivariate Cox linear models over combinations of up to seven genes; benchmarked against 101 other machine-learning algorithms
input_features: Six-gene epigenetic panel: YTHDC1, SIRT6, PCGF5, HDAC6, CREBZF, and ATF7IP2
biomarker_result: Six-gene epigenetic prognostic signature
performance_value: 2.12 (high- versus low-risk overall survival, p=7.7e-7; median survival 20.5 versus 86.8 months)
validation_detail: Signature built in TCGA-BLCA and evaluated in four independent bladder-cancer datasets (IMvigor210, E-MTAB-4321, GSE31684, GSE48075). The text states superior C-index and 1-year AUROC versus other models but does not print those numbers.
key_finding: A six-gene epigenetic score separated bladder-cancer overall survival with HR 2.12 (median 20.5 versus 86.8 months). YTHDC1 was reported to stabilize POU5F1 mRNA and reduce proliferation and migration in T24 and 5637 cells.

other_key_outcomes: Authors report higher C-index and 1-year AUROC than 101 algorithms and 110 published signatures, without printing those values. High-risk scores were linked to advanced stage, PD-1/PD-L1, genomic instability, and an immunosuppressive microenvironment.
extraction_note: The full text prints HR 2.12 but does not print a numeric C-index or AUROC, and it does not state the TCGA analytic sample size.

title: A systematic characterization of amino acid metabolism-related genes reveals molecular subtypes and a prognostic signature in bladder cancer.
study_design: Amino-acid metabolism subtype discovery with MIME-optimized 16-gene prognostic signature
data_source_detail: TCGA-BLCA, GSE13507, GSE32894; scRNA GSE222315; IMvigor210 immunotherapy cohort

other_key_outcomes: PSPH functional assays; PD-1/PD-L1 response association in IMvigor210.
extraction_note: Training time-dependent AUCs (0.97) are much higher than the external cohorts (0.71-0.73 and 0.63-0.69). The selection metric recorded here is the C-index (0.763 training; 0.685 validation).

title: Development and validation of a gemcitabine sensitivity-related long noncoding RNA signature for predicting the prognosis and subtypes of bladder cancer.

other_key_outcomes: Immune infiltration, mutation, and pathway comparisons between risk groups.
extraction_note: Model-selection metric is the average C-index of 0.699. Time-dependent AUCs printed on the TCGA nomogram are 0.79, 0.77, and 0.78.

key_finding: MAM-related four-gene score stratified BCa prognosis and RF models predicted cisplatin resistance with moderate external AUC.

other_key_outcomes: ATAD3A mechanistic validation in cell and animal models.
extraction_note: Primary anchor is mechanistic MAM/ATAD3A biology; prognostic ML components are secondary.

title: Transcriptome and single-cell RNA sequencing analysis with 101 machine learning combinations and experimental verification reveals the mechanism of action of mannose metabolism in bladder cancer.

title: Machine Learning Integration Framework Constructs a Lactylation-Associated Gene Signature to Improve Prognosis in Bladder Cancer.

data_modality_detail: Bulk RNA-seq lactylation-associated gene expression

input_features: Eight lactylation-associated genes: AHNAK, CALM, CALR, G6PD, SATB1, VIM, CACYBP, and XPO5
biomarker_result: Eight-gene lactylation-associated prognostic risk score

validation_detail: Leave-one-out cross-validation inside TCGA for model selection, plus external GSE13507 and GSE32894. Figure 3A-B Cox models are labeled as the TCGA cohort; the ROC panels do not restate a cohort name. Numeric external-cohort AUCs are not printed. Per-cohort C-index values are shown in a figure and are not printed in the text.

title: Integrated multi-omics analysis identifies DARS2, MRTO4, and MRPL37 as novel biomarkers and potential therapeutic targets for bladder cancer.

title: Bladder cancer diagnostic and prognostic models from DNA methylation by multi algorithm machine learning.

title: Integrative pan-cancer analysis of intratumoral microbial communities for biomarker discovery and diagnostic modeling.
tumor_site_detail: Pan-cancer study of intratumoral microbiota across nine cancer types (breast, ovarian, oral, colorectal, lung, gastric, bladder/urothelial [Bca], pancreatic, melanoma) plus normal controls; bladder cancer is only one of nine tumor types and not the study focus. Bca is the largest single subgroup in the pooled discovery cohort (n=610 of 2839 samples) but is NOT represented in the independent external validation cohort (CAMS, n=541: breast/colorectal/lung/normal controls only).
study_design: retrospective, multi-cohort pooled biomarker discovery and diagnostic modeling study
data_source_detail: 11 previously published 16S rRNA microbiome studies pooled, 3151 initial samples reduced to 2839 after QC, covering 9 cancer types (incl. bladder, Bca, n=610) and normal controls; independent external validation cohort of 541 samples from Cancer Hospital, Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences (CAMS) (breast/colorectal/lung/normal controls only - bladder not included)
data_modality_detail: 16S rRNA (V3-V4 region) amplicon sequencing of intratumoral microbiota; genus-level relative abundance matrix (2379 genera retained) plus PICRUSt2-predicted KEGG functional pathways
algorithm: Random Forest (primary), Support Vector Machine, K-Nearest Neighbours, Quadratic Discriminant Analysis; SHAP for feature importance; LEfSe for differential taxa
input_features: Genus-level relative abundance of intratumoral microbiota (2379 genera) from 16S rRNA sequencing
biomarker_result: Microbial genus panel for pan-cancer diagnostic classification (top SHAP-ranked taxa: Pelomonas, Staphylococcus, Cutibacterium, Lactococcus, Shewanella, Streptococcus, Bradyrhizobium, Acinetobacter); tumor-type-specific enriched genera by LEfSe (e.g. Fusobacterium enriched in bladder cancer)
performance_value: Discovery cohort (5-fold stratified CV, n=2839): Random Forest overall accuracy=0.681, AUC=0.937; SVM AUC=0.890; KNN AUC=0.837. Bladder cancer per-class CV: F1=0.93 (AUC approaching 1.00). External validation (CAMS, n=541, no bladder cancer): LC AUC=0.77, CRC AUC=0.73, BC AUC=0.76.
validation_detail: Discovery model trained/evaluated via stratified 5-fold CV on the pooled 11-study cohort (n=2839, 9 cancer types + normal controls). Independent external validation performed using the CAMS cohort (n=541, different center), but this external cohort included only breast, colorectal, lung cancer, and normal controls - bladder cancer (the only GU-relevant tumor type here) was NOT represented in the external validation set. The GU-relevant (bladder) classification performance (F1=0.93 in discovery) therefore rests only on internal cross-validation, not on external validation.
key_finding: In a large pan-cancer intratumoral microbiome study (16S rRNA, 9 cancer types + normal controls, n=2839 discovery plus 541 external validation), a Random Forest classifier achieved strong pan-cancer diagnostic discrimination (AUC=0.937 in discovery CV) using microbial genus-level features, and identified tumor-type-specific microbial signatures including Fusobacterium enrichment in bladder cancer; however, bladder cancer was not represented in the external validation cohort, so GU-specific diagnostic performance is unconfirmed externally.
limitations_as_stated: NR (limitations discussion not visible in the extracted text excerpt); general design limitations evident from methods include potential batch/data-source effects across the 11 pooled studies and reliance on 16S rRNA (genus-level resolution only).
other_key_outcomes: Alpha/beta diversity varied significantly by cancer type; microbial co-occurrence networks most complex in gastric cancer, simplest in melanoma/breast cancer; two alternative cancer-grouping strategies (biological/molecular vs. anatomical/exposure-based) were tested and both improved or matched single-cancer-type classification performance.
extraction_note: Pan-cancer study; bladder/urothelial cancer (the only GU-relevant tumor type) is one of nine cancer types and not isolated for GU-specific model performance beyond discovery-set per-class metrics (F1=0.93). Bladder cancer absent from external validation cohort, so no externally validated GU-specific performance exists. Funding, COI, code/data availability, and limitations not visible in the extracted text excerpt.

title: Construction and mechanistic exploration of a ferroptosis related gene based prognostic model for cisplatin resistance in bladder cancer
study_design: retrospective cohort / translational bioinformatic (public transcriptomic data + machine learning + network pharmacology + IHC validation)
data_source_detail: TCGA-BLCA (44 cisplatin-treated patients for CFRG identification); GSE32894 (training cohort, n=221 with complete grade data); GSE13507 (external validation); GSE149652 (single-cell, via TISCH2); HPA database for IHC
data_modality_detail: Bulk RNA-seq/microarray (TCGA-BLCA, GSE32894, GSE13507); scRNA-seq (GSE149652); molecular docking (AutoDock Vina) for drug-target interaction
algorithm: Random forest (ntree=600), SVM-RFE, LASSO regression, univariate and multivariate stepwise Cox regression
input_features: 16 cisplatin-ferroptosis-related genes (intersection of cisplatin response genes and 473 FerrDB ferroptosis genes), reduced via 3 ML algorithms + Cox regression to 3-gene signature
biomarker_result: 3-gene ferroptosis/cisplatin-resistance prognostic risk score (SLC1A4, TXNIP, PLIN4)
performance_value: Training (GSE32894): AUC 0.76/0.85/0.86 at 1/3/5-year OS; HR=13.00 (95% CI 3.06-55.16, p<0.001). External validation (GSE13507): AUC 0.71/0.68/0.68 at 1/3/5-year; HR=1.68 (95% CI 1.04-2.71, p<0.05). Predictive AUC for chemotherapy response (n=44 TCGA cisplatin-treated): SLC1A4 0.689, TXNIP 0.724, PLIN4 0.705.
validation_detail: Risk model built/trained in GSE32894 (n=221); externally validated in independent GEO dataset GSE13507 - a genuine external cohort, not an internal split.
funding: The author(s) reported there is no funding associated with the work featured in this article.
key_finding: A 3-gene ferroptosis-cisplatin-resistance signature (SLC1A4, TXNIP, PLIN4) stratified patients into risk groups with strong prognostic performance in training (AUC up to 0.86, HR=13.00) and external validation (AUC up to 0.71, HR=1.68); SLC1A4 proposed as candidate prognostic biomarker/therapeutic target.
limitations_as_stated: Initial gene screening used nominal p-value + effect-size filter rather than standard FDR correction because FDR yielded no significant genes in the 44-sample TCGA dataset; generalizability constrained by cohort size and absence of protein-level/functional validation of the 3-gene signature; requires future experimental confirmation.
other_key_outcomes: Nomogram combining risk score + tumor grade with good calibration/DCA net benefit. High-risk group shows immune-excluded/desert phenotype with upregulated checkpoints. Network pharmacology/molecular docking identifies fostamatinib as candidate CFRG-targeting agent (binding energy -9.3 kcal/mol).
extraction_note: No explicit Data/Code Availability statement found anywhere in the article (methods reference only public database URLs); coded NR rather than inferred. n_analytic set to GSE32894 training subset with complete grade data (n=221); other cohort sizes noted in data_source_detail/other_key_outcomes.

title: Constructing a bladder cancer prognostic model related to exosome using machine learning and identifying THBS1 as a potential target.

title: Imidacloprid contributes to bladder cancer progression: preliminary evidence based on network toxicology, machine learning and molecular docking.
study_design: Imidacloprid toxicogenomic DEIRG prognostic ML across public cohorts

performance_value: Highest average C-index 0.763 (RSF, averaged across TCGA-test and GSE32894); ROC AUC in TCGA-train 0.973/0.981/0.982 at 1/3/5-year OS; prognostic value confirmed by significant KM differences in TCGA-all/test, GSE32894, GSE13507, GSE31684.
validation_detail: Signature developed via 100 ML combinations in TCGA-train (1:1 internal split of TCGA-BLCA n=400), optimal model selected by C-index across TCGA-test and GSE32894. Additionally validated in genuinely independent external cohorts: GSE32894, GSE13507, GSE31684 (prognostic) and IMvigor210 (n=298, immunotherapy response) - separate GEO/clinical-trial datasets.

extraction_note: Validation design is mixed (internal TCGA-train/test split for model selection + genuine external cohorts GSE32894/13507/31684 and IMvigor210); coded as external_cohort with full design described in validation_detail. Funding/COI not present in extracted excerpt; coded NR.

performance_value: Combined model (DLRN) AUC: training 0.939 (95% CI 0.911-0.968), internal validation 0.884 (95% CI 0.813-0.953), external validation 0.862 (95% CI 0.756-0.968). External validation accuracy/sensitivity/specificity: 0.85/0.89/0.79.
validation_detail: Model developed/internally validated in Center 1 (training n=226, internal validation n=97, random 7:3 split), independently externally validated in Center 2 (n=52), a genuinely separate hospital with a different recruitment period. True second-center external validation, counterbalanced by authors' acknowledgment of retrospective, single-region (southwest China) selection bias.
key_finding: A CT-based deep learning radiomics nomogram (DLRN), combining handcrafted radiomics and ResNet-50-derived deep learning features, predicted muscle invasion in bladder cancer with AUC 0.884 (internal validation) and 0.862 (independent external validation, second center; total n=375 across 2 centers).
