other_key_outcomes: miRNA/TF regulatory networks and drug-gene interaction screening.
extraction_note: Borderline scope: primary framing is IBD-BC comorbidity pathogenesis rather than BC-specific GU biomarker focus per appraisal_note.

title: CT-based deep learning radiomics nomogram for the prediction of pathological grade in bladder cancer: a multicenter study.
study_design: Multicenter retrospective CT deep learning radiomics cohort
data_source_detail: 688 BCa patients (469 train, 219 external test) from multiple centers.
data_modality_detail: Handcrafted and deep learning CT radiomics with clinical nomogram
algorithm: Eleven ML classifiers; deep learning radiomics nomogram (DLRN)
input_features: DL radiomics features plus clinical variables for grade
biomarker_result: CT-based deep learning radiomics nomogram (DLRN) for pathological grade
performance_value: DLRN AUC=0.961 (train) and 0.947 (external test); outperformed clinical and optimal radiomics models.
validation_detail: 219-patient external test cohort across multiple centers; eleven ML benchmarks per appraisal_note.
key_finding: Multicenter DLRN accurately preoperatively predicts BCa pathological grade with strong external test AUC.
limitations_as_stated: NR
other_key_outcomes: Comparison of 11 ML classifiers for radiomics feature pipelines.
extraction_note: Strong multicenter external validation per appraisal_note.

title: Survival Prediction of Patients with Bladder Cancer after Cystectomy Based on Clinical, Radiomics, and Deep-Learning Descriptors.
study_design: Retrospective single-center cystectomy cohort with CT urography radiomics, CNN descriptors, and clinical nomogram
data_source_detail: University of Michigan: 163 post-cystectomy BCa patients with CTU and clinical/histopathology; train/validation/test split 92/7/64
data_modality_detail: CT urography radiomics and deep-learning image descriptors plus clinical variables in BPNN
algorithm: Back-propagation neural network combining clinical, radiomics, and CNN descriptors
input_features: Clinical nomogram indices, 12 MI-selected radiomics features, deep-learning CT descriptors
biomarker_result: Combined clinical-radiomics-deep learning (CRD) 5-year survival descriptor set
performance_value: Test-set 5-year survival AUC 0.87±0.05 for CRD (vs 0.82 clinical alone); test n=64
validation_detail: Single-site serial train/validation/test split; validation set only n=7 per authors.
key_finding: Integrating clinical, radiomics, and deep-learning CT features improved 5-year post-cystectomy survival discrimination versus clinical or imaging alone on the held-out test set.
limitations_as_stated: Relatively small single-site cohort and non-contrast CT; multisite validation needed.
other_key_outcomes: Kaplan-Meier stratification significant for clinical and CRD models on test set.
extraction_note: Appraisal flags extremely small internal validation split (n=7), limiting rigor of internal validation despite reported test-set AUC.

title: Development and validation of a disulfidptosis and M2 TAM-related classifier for bladder cancer to explore tumor subtypes, immune landscape and drug treatment.
study_design: TCGA discovery with internal test split and GEO external validation of disulfidptosis-M2 TAM risk score
data_source_detail: TCGA-BLCA training/testing for LASSO-Cox risk model; GSE13507 external validation; WGCNA on TCGA for DMRGs
data_modality_detail: Bulk RNA-seq/microarray; 95 disulfidptosis and M2 TAM-related genes
algorithm: WGCNA, consensus clustering, LASSO Cox and multivariate Cox risk score
input_features: 95 DMRGs reduced by LASSO to prognostic gene set with risk-score formula
biomarker_result: Disulfidptosis-M2 TAM-related risk score and two molecular clusters
performance_value: High-risk vs low-risk worse OS in training, internal test, and GSE13507 validation (log-rank; time-dependent ROC planned per Methods; numeric AUC not in slice)
validation_detail: Risk model developed in TCGA with internal test split and validated in GSE13507 without refitting described.
key_finding: A disulfidptosis-M2 TAM-related risk score stratified OS across internal and GSE13507 cohorts and supported nomogram and drug-sensitivity exploration.
limitations_as_stated: Retrospective public cohorts; prospective and experimental validation still needed.
other_key_outcomes: Two DMRG clusters with immune/TMB differences; GDSC drug sensitivity by risk group.

title: Value of the application of computed tomography-based radiomics for preoperative prediction of unfavorable pathology in initial bladder cancer.
study_design: Single-center retrospective cohort
data_source_detail: Initial bladder cancer, Nanchang (2017-2022); 105 patients randomly split 7:3 (training 73: 27 favorable and 46 unfavorable pathology; testing 32: 12 favorable and 20 unfavorable)
data_modality_detail: CT radiomics (PyRadiomics on the DARWIN platform); 1781 features filtered to 16 texture features
algorithm: F-test filter and LASSO, then GBDT, KNN, logistic regression, random forest, SVM, and XGBoost with 10-fold cross-validation; logistic regression selected for the radiomics score and for the clinic-radiomics nomogram
input_features: 16 CT texture features plus tumor size and neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio
biomarker_result: Clinic-radiomics unfavorable-pathology risk nomogram
performance_value: Testing-cohort clinic-radiomics AUC 0.821 (95% CI 0.669-0.972); training AUC 0.895 (95% CI 0.818-0.973). The abstract states testing AUC 0.817 and accuracy 0.750 for the clinic-radiomics model. Radiomics logistic regression testing AUC 0.817; clinical-model testing AUC 0.742.
validation_detail: Single-center random 7:3 split. Ten-fold cross-validation was used to choose the radiomics classifier inside the training cohort. No external cohort.
funding: National Natural Science Foundation of China (81960512 and 82172921) and Young Talent Research and Development Program of the First Affiliated Hospital of Nanchang University (YFYPY202026).
key_finding: A CT clinic-radiomics nomogram discriminated unfavorable pathology in newly diagnosed bladder cancer on an internal test set, with higher AUC than the clinical model.
limitations_as_stated: Retrospective single-center design, small sample, and no genetic features in the model.
other_key_outcomes: Decision-curve analysis favored the clinic-radiomics model. Testing accuracy reported for that model was 0.750.
extraction_note: The results section reports clinic-radiomics testing AUC 0.821 (95% CI 0.669-0.972), while the abstract reports testing AUC 0.817 for the same model.

title: Identification of necroptosis-related long non-coding RNAs prognostic signature and the crucial lncRNA in bladder cancer.
study_design: TCGA prognostic signature with ML feature selection and GSE133624 external validation plus MAFG-DT functional assays
data_source_detail: TCGA-BLCA (400 patients after exclusions); external RNA-seq GSE133624 for crucial lncRNA validation
data_modality_detail: Bulk RNA-seq lncRNA matrix; six NPlncRNAs in Cox risk score
algorithm: SVM-RFE, LASSO, random forest overlap then multivariate Cox risk score
input_features: Six necroptosis-related lncRNAs (PTOV1-AS2, AC083862.2, MAFG-DT, AC074117.1, AL049840.3, AC078778.1)
biomarker_result: Six-lncRNA necroptosis-related prognostic risk score
performance_value: High-risk vs low-risk worse OS and higher ROC/C-index than clinicopathologic variables per abstract (numeric values not in slice); MAFG-DT HR>1 on multivariate Cox
validation_detail: TCGA model evaluated with integrated GSE133624 and in vitro MAFG-DT silencing assays.
key_finding: A six-lncRNA necroptosis signature independently predicted BCa OS; MAFG-DT drove proliferative phenotypes in vitro.
limitations_as_stated: Slice truncates full limitations; public retrospective design.
other_key_outcomes: Nomogram with clinical variables; GSEA of necroptosis pathways in high-risk group.

title: Machine learning models combining computed tomography semantic features and selected clinical variables for accurate prediction of the pathological grade of bladder cancer.
study_design: Single-center retrospective NE-CT radiomics with ML classifiers and combined nomogram for grade
data_source_detail: Nanchang Medical College Hospital 105 BCa patients (2017-2022); 73 train / 32 validation
data_modality_detail: Non-enhanced CT radiomics (15 LASSO features) plus age and tumor size
algorithm: SVM best among six ML models; logistic nomogram combining Rad-score and clinical factors
input_features: 15 LASSO-selected texture features, age, tumor size
biomarker_result: Radiomics score plus clinical nomogram for low- vs high-grade BCa
performance_value: Combined nomogram validation AUC 0.854; best radiomics-only SVM validation AUC 0.842 (accuracy 0.844)
validation_detail: Random 7:3 single-center holdout only; no external cohort.
key_finding: NE-CT radiomics with clinical factors predicted pathologic grade with strong validation-set discrimination versus clinical variables alone.
limitations_as_stated: Retrospective single-center small sample; multi-center validation needed.
other_key_outcomes: Six ML algorithms compared; decision curve analysis for nomogram.
extraction_note: Appraisal notes single-center design, no external validation, and unclear data availability in slice.

title: Crosstalk of disulfidptosis-related subtypes, establishment of a prognostic signature and immune infiltration characteristics in bladder cancer based on a machine learning survival framework.
study_design: Multi-cohort disulfidptosis ML prognostic signature with IHC, scRNA, TIDE and IMvigor210 immunotherapy checks
data_source_detail: TCGA-BLCA, GSE13507, IMvigor210 merged; own Wuxi TURBT/cystectomy samples for IHC; GSE169379 scRNA
data_modality_detail: Bulk RNA-seq with CoxBoost+RSF-selected DRPS genes; orthogonal IHC on local tissues
algorithm: 84 ML algorithm combinations with 10-fold CV; CoxBoost plus RSF selected for DRPS
input_features: Differentially expressed genes between DRG consensus clusters feeding DRPS
biomarker_result: Disulfidptosis-related prognostic signature (DRPS) with risk groups
performance_value: CoxBoost plus random survival forest selected by the highest average C-index of 0.66 across TCGA-BLCA, GSE13507, and IMvigor210. Time-dependent AUCs were above 0.6 in IMvigor210, TCGA, and the meta-cohort; GSE13507 AUCs were described as not ideal.
validation_detail: Merged public cohorts plus TIDE/IMvigor210 immunotherapy response evaluation; local IHC orthogonal to expression model.
funding: Wuxi Taihu Lake Talent Plan, Supports for Leading Talents.
key_finding: DRPS stratified OS and immune/chemotherapy response patterns and was evaluated for immunotherapy utility via TIDE and IMvigor210.
limitations_as_stated: Cox regression limitations; reliance on merged public cohorts and algorithm search.
other_key_outcomes: Nomogram; IC50 comparisons for chemotherapy agents by risk group.
extraction_note: Full text reports an average C-index of 0.66 for the selected model.

title: An MRI-based radiomics nomogram in predicting histologic grade of non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer.
study_design: Single-center retrospective MRI radiomics nomogram for NMIBC grade
data_source_detail: 169 NMIBC patients; training n=118, validation n=51
data_modality_detail: T2WI and ADC MRI radiomics (24 features) plus age and tumor number
algorithm: LASSO feature selection with logistic regression clinical, radiomics, and combined nomogram models
input_features: Rad-score from 24 radiomics features, age, number of tumors
biomarker_result: Radiomics-clinical nomogram for low- vs high-grade NMIBC
performance_value: Validation-set AUC 0.931 for combined nomogram vs 0.910 radiomics-only and 0.745 clinical model
validation_detail: Internal 118/51 split at one center; TRIPOD checklist referenced in methods.
funding: Shaanxi Provincial People's Hospital Talent Program (2021JY-43) and Shaanxi Social Development Project (2023-YBSF-524).
conflicts_of_interest: Authors declare no conflicts stated in data availability section.
key_finding: MRI radiomics nomogram outperformed clinical factors alone for preoperative NMIBC grade discrimination on the validation cohort.
limitations_as_stated: Single-center retrospective design.
other_key_outcomes: Decision curve analysis favored combined nomogram.

title: Development of a Molecular-Subtype-Associated Immune Prognostic Signature That Can Be Recognized by MRI Radiomics Features in Bladder Cancer.
study_design: TCGA/IMvigor210 immune prognostic signature with GEO external validation and in-house MRI radiomics proxy
data_source_detail: TCGA and IMvigor210 for IPS; GEO GSE32894, GSE31684, GSE13507, GSE48277 validation; Shanghai center n=111 RNA+MRI for radiomics-IPS LASSO
data_modality_detail: Transcriptomic IPS from immune genes; MRI radiomics LASSO to predict IPS in local cohort
algorithm: Immune gene selection for IPS; LASSO on ten MRI radiomics features to predict IPS
input_features: IPS gene set from luminal/basal immune differences; ten MRI radiomics features
biomarker_result: Molecular-subtype-associated immune prognostic signature (IPS) with MRI radiomics surrogate
performance_value: MRI radiomics IPS prediction AUC 0.810 validation and 0.839 training (n=111 local); IPS OS validated in four GEO cohorts plus meta-analysis
validation_detail: IPS validated externally on four GEO datasets; radiomics-IPS link validated only internally at one center.
funding: National Natural Science Foundation (82202255) and Shanghai Youth Science and Technology Talents Sailing Program (20YF1437200).
key_finding: IPS linked to molecular subtype, checkpoints, and immunotherapy response and was approximated non-invasively by MRI radiomics in 111 local patients.
limitations_as_stated: Radiomics-IPS model not externally validated beyond local 7:3 split.
other_key_outcomes: GSEA of high-risk IPS; CIBERSORT TIIC differences luminal vs basal.

title: Multimodal investigation of bladder cancer data based on computed tomography, whole slide imaging, and transcriptomics.
study_design: Multimodal CT-pathology-RNA integration with CNN molecular subtyping and SEM cross-modal associations
data_source_detail: 127 patients CT+WSI association; 98 patients five-fold CV molecular subtype CNN (local hospitals plus TCGA-BLCA subset)
data_modality_detail: CT radiomics, pathomics from WSI, RNA-seq molecular subtypes; fused CNN classifier
algorithm: Convolutional neural network on fused radiology-pathology features; structural equation modeling
input_features: 200 CT and 1029 pathologic radiomics/pathomics features fused for subtype CNN
biomarker_result: Multimodal molecular subtype classifier (luminal/basal-like proxy)
performance_value: Fused radiology-pathology subtype model AUC 0.89 (95% CI 0.75-1.0) vs unimodal methods
validation_detail: Five-fold cross-validation on 98-patient subtype cohort; no independent external subtype validation described.
funding: National Natural Science Foundation (61931024) and Shenzhen Science and Technology Program grants.
key_finding: Multimodal CT and WSI features improved molecular subtype classification accuracy versus unimodal models and linked pathology to molecular subtypes.
limitations_as_stated: Retrospective multi-cohort assembly; subtype labels from RNA where available.
other_key_outcomes: Prognosis-related multimodal features identified; cross-modal association blocks between CT and WSI.
extraction_note: Appraisal flags molecular-subtype prediction as borderline surrogate outcome rather than direct clinical endpoint for PROBAST applicability.

title: CT-based deep learning radiomics signature for the preoperative prediction of the muscle-invasive status of bladder cancer.
study_design: Retrospective NE-CT deep-learning radiomics signature for preoperative muscle invasion
data_source_detail: 173 BCa patients; DLRS training n=129 and test n=44
data_modality_detail: Non-enhanced CT radiomics with deep learning signature (DLRS)
algorithm: LASSO with MLP classifier (best among compared models)
input_features: LASSO-selected deep radiomic signature features from CT
biomarker_result: Deep learning radiomics signature (DLRS) for muscle invasion status
performance_value: MLP test AUC 0.884 (95% CI 0.783-0.986); train AUC 0.973
validation_detail: Single-center random train/test split only.
key_finding: DLRS improved preoperative prediction of muscle invasion versus conventional radiomics on the held-out test set.
limitations_as_stated: No external validation; retrospective design.
other_key_outcomes: Compared multiple ML classifiers for DLRS.

title: Characterization of Epithelial-Mesenchymal Transition Identifies a Gene Signature for Predicting Clinical Outcomes and Therapeutic Responses in Bladder Cancer.
study_design: TCGA EMT hallmark-driven ML signature with two GEO external validations
data_source_detail: TCGA training n=393; external GSE13507 n=165 and GSE32894 n=221
data_modality_detail: Bulk expression; EMT-related gene signature from RSF and stepwise Cox
algorithm: Random survival forest and stepwise Cox on EMT DEGs
input_features: EMT-related prognostic gene signature after ssGSEA hallmark ranking
biomarker_result: EMT-related gene prognostic signature
performance_value: EMT ssGSEA hallmark HR=1.43 (95% CI 1.26-1.63) for OS; signature validated in three independent cohorts (log-rank separation)
validation_detail: Signature developed on TCGA and applied to GSE13507 and GSE32894.
key_finding: An EMT-related gene signature predicted OS and therapy response patterns across TCGA and two GEO validations.
limitations_as_stated: Retrospective public data; experimental validation limited.
other_key_outcomes: Immune infiltration and drug sensitivity differences by risk group.

title: Comparison between renal pelvic and ureteral tumors in muscle-invasive upper tract urothelial carcinoma.
tumor_site_detail: Muscle-invasive upper tract urothelial carcinoma (renal pelvis and ureter). The numeric AUC is from a TCGA bladder slide model, not from labeled UTUC cases.
study_design: Retrospective comparative UTUC study with an auxiliary deep-learning molecular-subtype classifier
data_source_detail: MDA-subtype model trained and evaluated on 422 TCGA bladder whole-slide images split 6:2:2. Applied, without a reported accuracy, to an institutional UTUC cohort (32 basal, 44 luminal, 4 p53-like). SEER (9012 patients) and a Dalian UTUC series (248 patients) support the comparative, non-model analyses.
data_modality_detail: H&E whole-slide patches (256x256 at 10x) after Macenko normalization; CycleGAN color transfer for institutional slides
algorithm: Inception V3 transfer learning from ImageNet (SGD, cross-entropy): one model for tumor versus stroma/necrosis and a second for MDA subtype; patient score is the mean of high-confidence tumor-patch predictions
input_features: Tile-level H&E morphology; MDA labels taken from TCGA gene data
biomarker_result: H&E-predicted MDA subtype (basal, luminal, p53-like)
performance_value: Patient-level microaverage AUC 0.74 and macroaverage AUC 0.76 for three-class MDA subtype classification by Inception V3 (Figure 4A).
validation_detail: 422 TCGA bladder WSIs split 6:2:2 into training, validation, and testing. The printed AUC does not cover the UTUC cases, which were labeled by the model without ground-truth accuracy. Not counted as external validation for the upper-tract tumors.
funding: Funding sources not named in the full text.
key_finding: An Inception V3 model classified MDA subtypes from TCGA bladder slides with patient-level microaverage AUC 0.74 and macroaverage AUC 0.76, then assigned subtypes to institutional upper-tract tumors without a reported accuracy.
limitations_as_stated: Authors state that a validation cohort is required to eliminate selection bias. The p53-like class was small.
other_key_outcomes: Comparative UTUC analysis (SEER and 248 institutional patients) is the paper's main aim: ureteral tumors were enriched for basal and p53-like assignments and showed more immune infiltration and matrix stiffness than renal-pelvic tumors. After PSM, location remained associated with survival (HR 1.084, 95% CI 1.014-1.16).
extraction_note: The anchor of the paper is a comparative upper-tract urothelial analysis; the deep-learning subtype classifier is auxiliary. The full text reports AUC only for the TCGA bladder model, not for UTUC.

title: Radiomics Nomogram Based on High--Value Diffusion-Weighted Imaging for Distinguishing the Grade of Bladder Cancer.
study_design: Single-center high-b-value DWI radiomics nomogram feasibility for BCa grade
data_source_detail: Retrospective DWI cohort with internal train/validation split (small feasibility sample)
data_modality_detail: ADC1000/1700/3000 DWI radiomics with LASSO-logistic nomogram
algorithm: LASSO feature selection with logistic regression nomogram
input_features: DWI-derived ADC texture features
biomarker_result: ADC1700/3000 radiomics nomogram for tumor grade
performance_value: Validation AUCs 0.582 (ADC1000), 0.745 (ADC1700), 0.745 (ADC3000) for grade discrimination
validation_detail: Internal split at single center; feasibility-scale sample.
funding: National Natural Science Foundation of China (82102025, 82071889).
key_finding: High-b-value DWI radiomics nomograms discriminated low- vs high-grade BCa with moderate AUC on validation.
limitations_as_stated: Small retrospective single-center feasibility study.
other_key_outcomes: Compared three ADC b-value models.
extraction_note: Appraisal flags small feasibility-style design with internal split only.

title: Artificial intelligence-driven consensus gene signatures for improving bladder cancer clinical outcomes identified by multi-center integration analysis.
study_design: Large-scale multi-cohort AI consensus gene signature (AIGS) benchmarking study
data_source_detail: TCGA discovery plus 11 independent validation cohorts including IMvigor210 and multiple GEO sets
data_modality_detail: Bulk RNA-seq/microarray; consensus immune gene signature AIGS from ML screen
algorithm: Multi-algorithm ML consensus (76 models screened) selecting AIGS
input_features: AI-driven consensus immune gene signature (AIGS)
biomarker_result: AIGS risk score for BCa OS and immunotherapy response
performance_value: Time-dependent AUCs ~0.758/0.780/0.881 (TCGA 1/3/5-yr); IMvigor210 AUCs ~0.712/0.701/0.703
validation_detail: Validated across 11 independent cohorts vs 58 published models per abstract/slice.
key_finding: AIGS outperformed many published BCa models and associated with immunotherapy response across multicenter public cohorts.
limitations_as_stated: High analysis complexity and retrospective public datasets.
other_key_outcomes: Benchmarking against 58 prior signatures; C-index comparisons across models.
extraction_note: Massive ML search increases overfitting risk despite extensive external testing.

title: Gender dimorphism in survival of patients with lymph node metastasis of bladder cancer.
study_design: SEER metastatic BCa gender-by-site survival with TCGA gender signature and local MRI radiomics proxy
data_source_detail: SEER n=1829 metastatic BCa; TCGA gender signature; IMvigor210 validation; local MRI radiomics at center
data_modality_detail: SEER epidemiology, TCGA transcriptomic gender signature, MRI radiomics score
algorithm: Cox and ML gender-associated signature; radiomics score to predict signature
input_features: Gender-differential genes in LNM; radiomics features predicting gender signature
biomarker_result: Gender-associated prognostic signature with radiomics surrogate score
performance_value: High-risk gender signature associated with worse survival and drug sensitivity; nomogram with staging (numeric AUC not in slice)
validation_detail: Signature validated in IMvigor210; SEER primary for epidemiology; radiomics developed locally.
funding: Shanghai Science Committee grants (partial support stated).
key_finding: Gender and metastatic site interact on BCa prognosis; a gender-associated expression signature linked to survival and treatment sensitivity.
limitations_as_stated: Observational registry and public omics; radiomics external validation limited.
other_key_outcomes: Sex-specific metastasis patterns in SEER.
extraction_note: Comorbid/subgroup-stratified gender-by-metastasis design per calibration rule 5; primary anchor spans epidemiology and signature discovery.

title: Study on Molecular Information Intelligent Diagnosis and Treatment of Bladder Cancer on Pathological Tissue Image.
study_design: Digital pathology CNN CAD for molecular subtype, p53, and PD-L1 status
data_source_detail: Three independent internal pathology image cohorts from participating hospitals
data_modality_detail: H&E whole-slide image patches for multi-task CNN
algorithm: Convolutional neural network computer-aided diagnosis system
input_features: Pathological image tiles from bladder cancer slides
biomarker_result: CNN predictions of molecular subtype, p53, and PD-L1 status
performance_value: Molecular subtype recognition AUC 0.98 (accuracy 0.94); PD-L1 AUC/accuracy 0.897; p53 accuracy 0.846
validation_detail: Internal cross-validation across three hospital cohorts; no external institution validation described.
funding: Zhejiang Provincial Research Center support; raw data after ethics approval.
key_finding: CNN on H&E slides predicted molecular subtype and IHC surrogate markers with high internal accuracy.
limitations_as_stated: Requires ethics-approved data release; IHC labels as reference standard.
other_key_outcomes: Multi-task classification for p53 and PD-L1.

title: A Novel Machine Learning 13-Gene Signature: Improving Risk Analysis and Survival Prediction for Clear Cell Renal Cell Carcinoma Patients.
study_design: translational/bioinformatic retrospective cohort study (secondary analysis of public genomic data)
data_source_detail: TCGA-KIRC (training/internal CV, n=530) and ICGC-RECA (n=91, used both for candidate-gene sourcing and as the external validation set)
data_modality_detail: Bulk RNA-Seq gene expression from TCGA-KIRC and ICGC-RECA
algorithm: mRMR ensemble feature selection plus forward-search Variable Ranking by Mutual Information Difference; benchmarked against 5 other feature-selection methods using 8 Cox-based survival models (Lasso-Cox, Ridge, ElasticNet, CoxPH, GLMBoost, GBM, Blackboost, XGBoost)
input_features: RNA-Seq expression of 3284 pre-selected genes narrowed via mRMR to a 13-gene signature (AR, AL353637.1, DPP6, FOXJ1, GNB3, HHLA2, IL4, LIMCH1, LINC01732, OTX1, SAA1, SEMA3G, ZIC2)
biomarker_result: mRMR 13-gene expression signature for ccRCC survival risk
performance_value: Internal (3-fold CV on TCGA-KIRC, 10-year AUC Uno, 100 repetitions): best mean AUC 0.81-0.82 (Lasso-Cox/glmnet). External (trained on TCGA-KIRC, predicted on ICGC-RECA, 7-year AUC Uno, 100 repetitions): mean AUC 0.71; log-rank p<0.05 for risk-group separation in both cohorts, significant only for the mRMR signature among 14 signatures compared
validation_detail: Internal 3-fold CV on TCGA-KIRC plus external validation by training on full TCGA-KIRC and predicting on ICGC-RECA, a genuinely separate public cohort. However, feature selection (13-gene mRMR signature) was performed on the full TCGA-KIRC dataset prior to and outside the CV/train-test split, i.e. not nested within cross-validation folds - appraisal_note flags this as a source of possible optimism bias in the internal AUC estimate.
funding: Federal Rural University of Semi-arid (P. Terrematte); CAPES Brazilian funding agency grants 88887.161820/2017-0 and 88887.600071/2021-0 (D. Souto)
key_finding: A novel 13-gene mRMR-derived expression signature predicted ccRCC survival risk with internal AUC 0.81-0.82 (TCGA-KIRC, 3-fold CV) and external AUC up to 0.71 (trained on TCGA-KIRC, predicted on ICGC-RECA), generalizing better across cohorts than 14 previously published gene signatures.
limitations_as_stated: No explicit itemized limitations section identified. Study is a secondary/bioinformatic analysis of public retrospective cohorts without independent institutional/clinical validation; TCGA-KIRC and ICGC-RECA cohorts differed significantly on nodal staging distribution (p<0.001), a potential source of cohort heterogeneity.
other_key_outcomes: Benchmarked against 14 previously published ccRCC gene signatures using 6 feature-selection methods and 8 survival ML models; 8/13 mRMR-signature genes had been reported previously in other ccRCC signatures.
extraction_note: Coded validation_level as external_cohort (ICGC-RECA is a separate public dataset from a different consortium/population), but flagged the appraisal_note caveat verbatim in validation_detail: feature/gene selection was performed outside/prior to the CV folds used for the internal AUC estimate, so the internal AUC (0.81-0.82) may be optimistic; the external AUC (up to 0.71) on ICGC-RECA partially mitigates this.

title: Prediction of the Immune Phenotypes of Bladder Cancer Patients for Precision Oncology.
journal: IEEE Open J Eng Med Biol
study_design: Bulk and single-cell transcriptomics SVM classifier for three immune phenotypes
data_source_detail: Public BLCA expression cohorts with curated immune phenotype labels (slice cites Lucy S cohort through 2019)
data_modality_detail: Bulk RNA expression features for inflamed/excluded/desert phenotypes
algorithm: Support vector machine with RBF kernel and feature selection
input_features: Gene expression features selected for immune phenotype classification
biomarker_result: SVM immune phenotype classifier (inflamed, excluded, desert)
performance_value: Best SVM averaged AUC ~0.688 for PR/ROC metrics across phenotypes (cross-validation)
validation_detail: Cross-validated SVM without independent external cohort in slice.
key_finding: SVM classified three immune phenotypes from expression with modest cross-validated discrimination for precision oncology use.
limitations_as_stated: Immune phenotype endpoint less standard than OS; limited external validation.
other_key_outcomes: PR and ROC curves per phenotype.
extraction_note: Appraisal flags nonstandard immune phenotype endpoint with limited external validation.

title: Proteomic-Based Machine Learning Analysis Reveals PYGB as a Novel Immunohistochemical Biomarker to Distinguish Inverted Urothelial Papilloma From Low-Grade Papillary Urothelial Carcinoma With Inverted Growth.
study_design: retrospective cohort (diagnostic biomarker discovery + independent IHC validation cohort; translational proteomics)
data_source_detail: FFPE tissue, Seoul National University Hospital (Korea): proteomic discovery cohort n=31 (9 IUP, 12 PUC, 10 normal urothelium); independent IHC validation cohort n=41 (25 IUP, 16 PUC with inverted growth). Secondary axis used TCGA-BLCA (n=405) for gene-expression survival analysis.
data_modality_detail: LC-MS/MS discovery proteomics (FFPE tissue) plus immunohistochemistry (H-score, digital-pathology quantification via QuPath) for validation
algorithm: SVM (radial basis function kernel) feature selection for diagnostic protein biomarkers; ROC/Youden index for cutoff determination
input_features: LC-MS/MS proteomic profiles (5057 quantified proteins) narrowed via SVM feature selection to top-ranked candidates, prioritized to PYGB and SERPINH1 via Human Protein Atlas concordance, then IHC H-score of PYGB
biomarker_result: PYGB (glycogen phosphorylase B) immunohistochemical H-score
performance_value: AUROC 0.923 (p<0.0001); sensitivity 72% (95% CI 50.6-87.9%), specificity 100% (95% CI 79.4-100%) at H-score cutoff 21.4, for PYGB IHC distinguishing IUP from PUC with inverted growth
validation_detail: Independent single-center IHC validation cohort (n=41) distinct from the proteomic discovery cohort (n=31), but same institution; not an externally validated multi-institutional cohort. Authors state a planned future external multi-institutional validation study.
funding: National Research Foundation of Korea (NRF), Ministry of Science, ICT and Future Planning (NRF-2019R1C1C1006640, 2021R1F1A1063982, 2021R1A2C4086635, 2022R1A2C4001439)
key_finding: Proteomics-based SVM feature selection identified PYGB as a diagnostic IHC biomarker distinguishing inverted urothelial papilloma from low-grade papillary urothelial carcinoma with inverted growth, with AUROC 0.923, sensitivity 72%, specificity 100% in an independent validation cohort.
limitations_as_stated: Small number of IUP cases in the IHC validation cohort due to rarity of the entity; authors plan external multi-institutional validation; functional role of PYGB in IUP not validated in vitro/in vivo due to lack of models.
other_key_outcomes: Secondary risk-stratification axis: 'NU-like' (low-risk) vs 'PUC-like' (high-risk) IUP proteomic signatures; univariate Cox survival analysis in TCGA-BLCA (n=405) identified OGDH, SPON1, PYGB, EPHX1, SRP68, SETD3 as significantly associated with urothelial carcinoma outcomes. SERPINH1 also tested as candidate IHC biomarker but not significant (p=0.1333) and dropped.
extraction_note: Primary axis = diagnostic PYGB IHC model (anchors title/abstract) per appraisal_note guidance; TCGA-BLCA survival axis (secondary, associative) recorded in other_key_outcomes. validation_level coded as internal_holdout (independent validation cohort but same single center), not an 'external' multi-institutional validation.

title: A nomogram combined with radiomics features, albuminuria, and metabolic syndrome to predict the risk of myometrial invasion of bladder cancer.
study_design: Single-center multi-phase CT radiomics nomogram for myometrial/muscular invasion
data_source_detail: 100 BCa patients with arterial and venous phase thin-slice CT; training/verification split
data_modality_detail: Multi-parameter enhanced CT radiomics with clinical nomogram
algorithm: LASSO radiomics with logistic nomogram combining radiomics and clinical factors
input_features: LASSO-selected CT radiomics features plus clinical variables
biomarker_result: Combined radiomics-clinical nomogram for muscular invasion
performance_value: Combined radiomics+clinical model AUC 0.8457 (highest among compared models)
validation_detail: Single-center training and verification groups; TRIPOD checklist completed.
funding: Suzhou Science and Technology Project (SLJ201906 and SYS2019053).
key_finding: Multi-phase CT radiomics plus clinical factors best predicted muscular invasion on internal verification.
limitations_as_stated: Small single-center retrospective sample.
other_key_outcomes: Compared radiomics-only and clinical-only models.

title: A Novel CpG Methylation Risk Indicator for Predicting Prognosis in Bladder Cancer.
study_design: TCGA methylation risk score (MRSB) with internal validation only
data_source_detail: 357 BLCA patients; 70/30 train/internal validation (validation n=107)
data_modality_detail: CpG methylation with LASSO and SVM-RFE feature selection
algorithm: LASSO and SVM-RFE with multivariate Cox MRSB
input_features: Eight-CpG methylation risk score for bladder cancer (MRSB)
biomarker_result: Methylation risk score for bladder cancer (MRSB)
performance_value: Internal validation (n=107): PFS log-rank p=0.011; OS/RFS significant in training and validation (p<0.05); ROC AUC for risk groups referenced but not numerically reported in slice
validation_detail: TCGA-only random split; no independent external cohort.
key_finding: MRSB stratified PFS and OS on TCGA internal validation and supported a predictive nomogram.
limitations_as_stated: Needs diverse external validation beyond TCGA Caucasian majority.
other_key_outcomes: Kernel-smoothing hazard curves; subgroup nomogram performance.

title: Identification of CNGB1 as a Predictor of Response to Neoadjuvant Chemotherapy in Muscle-Invasive Bladder Cancer.
study_design: Extreme-phenotype NAC response discovery with RGIFE ML and microarray/TMA validations
data_source_detail: Discovery n=30 extreme responders/non-responders; GSE13507 n=26 and TMA n=99 validations
data_modality_detail: FFPE microarray expression; nine-gene signature with CNGB1 proxy
algorithm: RGIFE feature elimination with random forest cross-validation
input_features: Nine-gene NAC response signature (CNGB1, GGH, HIST1H4F, IDO1, KIF5A, MRPL4, NCDN, PRRT3, SLC35B3)
biomarker_result: Nine-gene signature and CNGB1 proxy for NAC response
performance_value: Discovery cohort 100% responder classification with RGIFE nine-gene panel; GSE13507 validation log-rank p=0.02 (n=26)
validation_detail: Highly selected discovery set; external GSE13507 and TMA cohort 2 for survival correlation.
key_finding: RGIFE selected a nine-gene NAC response panel with perfect discovery separation and CNGB1 proxy; associated with OS in GSE13507.
limitations_as_stated: Requires larger prospective trial validation.
other_key_outcomes: TMA validation cohort for CNGB1.
extraction_note: Appraisal flags non-representative extreme-responder discovery cohort and 100% training accuracy as high optimistic bias risk.

title: Radiomic assessment as a method for predicting tumor mutation burden (TMB) of bladder cancer patients: a feasibility study.
study_design: Feasibility radiomics-from-CECT study to predict TMB status
data_source_detail: 75 BLCA patients with TCIA/TCGA-linked imaging and TMB labels
data_modality_detail: Preoperative pelvic CECT radiomics with LASSO-logistic TMB model
algorithm: Unsupervised clustering plus LASSO/logistic regression with bootstrapping internal test
input_features: Six LASSO-selected radiomic features predicting TMB
biomarker_result: Radiomics TMB prediction model
performance_value: Unsupervised radiomic clusters enriched for high TMB (p=0.039); six-feature logistic model built with bootstrapping (numeric AUC not in slice)
validation_detail: Feasibility single-cohort with bootstrapping only; no external center validation.
key_finding: CT radiomic profiles associated with TMB groups and a six-feature model was proposed for TMB prediction.
limitations_as_stated: Small retrospective feasibility study; TMB cutoff not standardized; external validation needed.
other_key_outcomes: Driver mutation exploratory associations.
extraction_note: Self-described feasibility study without external validation; numeric classification AUC absent from slice.

title: A Novel Nomogram Based on Machine Learning-Pathomics Signature and Neutrophil to Lymphocyte Ratio for Survival Prediction of Bladder Cancer Patients.
study_design: TCGA pathomics ML signature plus NLR nomogram with General Hospital external validation
data_source_detail: 508 WSIs from Shanghai General Hospital and TCGA; external General cohort for MLPS/NLR validation
data_modality_detail: H&E WSI nuclear features with six pathomics MLPS features and NLR
algorithm: Machine learning pathomics feature selection with Cox nomogram
input_features: Six WSI pathomics features (MLPS) and neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio
biomarker_result: MLPS plus NLR nomogram for OS
performance_value: MLPS HR 2.19 (95% CI 1.63-2.94) TCGA and 3.20 General cohort; high NLR HR 2.06 TCGA / 3.69 General
validation_detail: Pathomics and NLR validated in separate General Hospital cohort.
funding: National Natural Science Foundation of China (819723...).
key_finding: Pathomics signature and NLR independently predicted BCa OS and combined nomogram improved decision curve utility.
limitations_as_stated: Prospective validation still needed.
other_key_outcomes: 1-, 3-, 5-year OS calibration for nomogram.

title: Combining Multiparametric MRI Radiomics Signature With the Vesical Imaging-Reporting and Data System (VI-RADS) Score to Preoperatively Differentiate Muscle Invasion of Bladder Cancer.
study_design: Single-center retrospective diagnostic cohort
data_source_detail: 185 pathologically confirmed bladder cancers at Shanghai Tenth People's Hospital (August 2014-April 2020); random 7:3 split (training 129, validation 56)
data_modality_detail: 3T mpMRI radiomics from axial T2WI and dynamic contrast-enhanced images (21 LASSO features: 10 T2WI and 11 DCE) plus VI-RADS score
algorithm: mRMR screening, then LASSO, random forest, and SVM classifiers trained with 10-fold cross-validation; logistic nomogram combining the LASSO radiomics signature with VI-RADS
input_features: PyRadiomics features from the largest lesion on T2WI and DCE, reduced to a radiomics score, plus VI-RADS
biomarker_result: mpMRI radiomics signature plus VI-RADS nomogram for muscle-invasive versus non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer
performance_value: Validation-set nomogram AUC 0.943 and accuracy 89.3% (training AUC 0.970, accuracy 93.0%). LASSO radiomics signature alone: validation AUC 0.906 and accuracy 87.5% (training AUC 0.934, accuracy 90.7%).
validation_detail: Single-center random 7:3 training/validation split. Ten-fold cross-validation was used to tune classifiers on the training set. Authors state that external institutional validation is still needed.
funding: Outstanding Talent of Shanghai Tenth People's Hospital (20215YPDRC048), Shanghai Science Committee Foundation (19411967700), and Shanghai Youth Science and Technology Talents Sailing Program (20YF1437200).
key_finding: An mpMRI radiomics plus VI-RADS nomogram differentiated muscle-invasive from non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer with validation AUC 0.943.
limitations_as_stated: Retrospective single-center validation set, so generalizability is untested; no prognostic follow-up to link the nomogram to outcomes.
other_key_outcomes: Decision-curve analysis supported clinical use of the nomogram. An optimal radiomics-score cutoff of -0.093 gave an AUC of 0.833 in one reported comparison.

title: Clinical use of machine learning-based pathomics signature for diagnosis and survival prediction of bladder cancer.
study_design: Retrospective diagnostic and prognostic pathomics study with an institutional external cohort
data_source_detail: TCGA: 406 bladder-cancer and 37 normal H&E images, split 1:1 into training and test. External cohort: Shanghai General Hospital, 108 bladder-cancer and 53 normal images (2009-2016). Separate glandular-cystitis set of 39 images at the same hospital.
data_modality_detail: Representative 1000x1000 H&E images at 400x; CellProfiler segmentation of nuclei and cytoplasm
algorithm: LASSO logistic model (glmnet) on pathomics features for diagnosis; LASSO-Cox for the secondary survival score
input_features: 345 quantitative H&E features of object shape, size, texture, and intensity
biomarker_result: Pathomics diagnostic signature separating bladder cancer from normal urothelium
performance_value: Diagnostic AUC 96.3% (training), 89.2% (TCGA test), and 94.1% (Shanghai General external validation). Bladder cancer versus glandular cystitis AUC 93.4% in the General cohort.
validation_detail: TCGA images randomly split 1:1 for training and test. External validation is a single-institution Shanghai General Hospital cohort, not a multicenter set.
funding: National Natural Science Foundation of China (81972393 and 81772705).
key_finding: A LASSO pathomics model distinguished bladder cancer from normal urothelium with external-validation AUC 94.1%.
limitations_as_stated: Diagnostic accuracy was lower than pathologist review; the prognostic risk-score cutoff was the cohort-specific median, so high-risk ranges differ between TCGA and the General cohort; the study is retrospective and needs prospective verification.
other_key_outcomes: LASSO-Cox pathomics risk score: TCGA OS HR 2.09 (95% CI 1.56-2.81) and General-cohort HR 5.32 (95% CI 2.95-9.59). Clinicopathologic nomogram AUCs 77.7%, 83.8%, and 81.3% for 1-, 3-, and 5-year OS.
extraction_note: Primary axis is the diagnostic pathomics model. Survival prediction is reported in other_key_outcomes.

title: Identification of a ten-long noncoding RNA signature for predicting the survival and immune status of patients with bladder urothelial carcinoma based on the GEO database: a superior machine learning model.
study_design: Ten-lncRNA RSF signature across three GEO cohorts
data_source_detail: GSE32894 train n=224; GSE32548 test n=131; GSE13507 external n=165
data_modality_detail: Microarray lncRNA profiles from Illumina beadchips
algorithm: Univariate Cox and random survival forest-variable hunting (RSF-VH)
input_features: Ten lncRNAs in risk score nomogram
biomarker_result: Ten-lncRNA prognostic risk score
performance_value: Nomogram C-index 0.94, 0.70, and 0.90 in the three GEO datasets respectively
validation_detail: Train on GSE32894 with two independent GEO validations (GSE32548 and GSE13507).
key_finding: Ten-lncRNA score stratified OS/DSS across three GEO BLCA cohorts with high C-index in training series.
limitations_as_stated: Microarray lncRNA inference from probe annotation.
other_key_outcomes: GSEA immune infiltration differences by risk.

title: Biomarkers of the Response to Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors in Metastatic Urothelial Carcinoma.
study_design: IMvigor210 ML immunotherapy response nomogram with TCGA mUC verification
data_source_detail: IMvigor210 n=298 (200 train/98 test); TCGA stage IV BLCA n=134 verification
data_modality_detail: RNA-seq of metastatic urothelial carcinoma on atezolizumab
algorithm: Machine learning selection of ten genes for ICIR nomogram
input_features: Ten prognostic genes forming immunotherapy response (ICIR) score
biomarker_result: ICIR nomogram for ICI response and OS
performance_value: ICI response prediction AUC 0.815 training, 0.752 testing, 0.805 combined IMvigor210 cohorts
validation_detail: Random split within IMvigor210 plus TCGA mUC correlation analysis.
funding: National Natural Science Foundation support; IMvigor210 public resource.
key_finding: Ten-gene ICIR nomogram discriminated ICI response and OS better than TMB/neoantigen burden at higher threshold probabilities.
limitations_as_stated: Two-stage feature selection may inflate performance.
other_key_outcomes: Immune infiltrate and mutation driver exploratory analyses.

title: Development of a noninvasive tool to preoperatively evaluate the muscular invasiveness of bladder cancer using a radiomics approach.
study_design: MRI radiomics-clinical nomogram for MIBC vs NMIBC preoperative discrimination
data_source_detail: 199 patients; training n=130 and validation n=69
data_modality_detail: T2-weighted MRI radiomics (23 features) plus tumor size
algorithm: LASSO radiomics signature with multivariable logistic nomogram
input_features: 23 MRI radiomics features and MRI tumor size
biomarker_result: Radiomics-clinical nomogram for muscle invasiveness
performance_value: Nomogram validation AUC 0.876 (radiomics signature alone AUC 0.874; training nomogram AUC 0.922)
validation_detail: Temporal single-center train/validation split.
key_finding: MRI radiomics plus tumor size improved preoperative MIBC versus NMIBC discrimination on validation.
limitations_as_stated: Single-center retrospective design.
other_key_outcomes: Decision curve and NRI/IDI for nomogram.

title: A predictive nomogram for individualized recurrence stratification of bladder cancer using multiparametric MRI and clinical risk factors.
study_design: Preoperative MRI radiomics nomogram for two-year recurrence risk
data_source_detail: 71 BCa patients (34 recurrent); training n=50 validation n=21
data_modality_detail: Preoperative MRI radiomics with clinical predictors
algorithm: Radiomics feature selection with logistic nomogram for TFTY recurrence
input_features: Radiomics signature plus clinical predictors in nomogram
biomarker_result: Radiomics-clinical nomogram for first-two-years recurrence
performance_value: Validation AUC 0.838 (accuracy 80.95%); training AUC 0.915
validation_detail: Small single-center internal validation only.
key_finding: MRI radiomics nomogram predicted two-year recurrence with strong training and moderate validation performance.
limitations_as_stated: Small sample; single-center retrospective study.
other_key_outcomes: Decision curve analysis for recurrence threshold.

title: Development and Validation of an MRI-Based Radiomics Signature for the Preoperative Prediction of Lymph Node Metastasis in Bladder Cancer.
study_design: MRI radiomics signature and nomogram for preoperative LN metastasis
data_source_detail: 103 BCa patients; training n=69 validation n=34
data_modality_detail: MRI radiomics (718 features reduced by LASSO) plus MRI-reported LN status
algorithm: LASSO radiomics with logistic nomogram
input_features: LASSO radiomics signature and MRI-reported nodal status
biomarker_result: Radiomics nomogram for LN metastasis prediction
performance_value: Nomogram validation AUC 0.8902 (training 0.9118); radiomics signature validation AUC 0.8447
validation_detail: Single-center internal validation; authors state external validation still required.
key_finding: MRI radiomics nomogram improved preoperative nodal metastasis prediction versus signature alone.
limitations_as_stated: External validation required before clinical implementation.
other_key_outcomes: Performance in cN0 subgroup (AUC 0.8406).

title: The application of artificial intelligence to microarray data: identification of a novel gene signature to identify bladder cancer progression.
study_design: Two-cohort retrospective prognostic study: microarray discovery followed by immunohistochemistry in an independent cohort
data_source_detail: Microarray discovery: 66 tumors from 34 patients, Ludwig Maximilian University. Immunohistochemistry: 262 tumors from consecutive patients, University of Regensburg; progression data in 182; concordance index calculated on superficial tumors (n=134) with at least four successfully stained proteins.
data_modality_detail: Microarray gene expression (2800 genes, Pearson-filtered to 200) with orthogonal IHC of six proteins
algorithm: Artificial neural networks and neurofuzzy models with ensembling, leave-one-out, and cross-validation; committee ranking of genes by induced model error
input_features: Expression of 200 progression-correlated genes, reduced to an 11-gene committee panel
biomarker_result: 11-gene committee progression signature; IHC panel of LIG3, Fas, KRT18, ICAM1, DSG2, and BRCA2
performance_value: Immunohistochemistry committee panel on superficial tumors, concordance index 0.66 (log-rank p=0.01). Multivariate Cox OR for that panel 1.2 (95% CI 1.1-1.3).
validation_detail: Signature discovered on the Munich microarray cohort and tested by IHC in a separate Regensburg cohort. No patient was in both cohorts. Internal microarray neurofuzzy models reached concordance index 1.0 with 11 genes; that figure is not the validation result.
key_finding: An AI-selected progression gene panel identified non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer progression on an independent IHC cohort with concordance index 0.66.
limitations_as_stated: Statistical correlation was used to reduce 2800 genes to 200 before AI analysis, and regression-identified genes were not compared by immunohistochemistry.
other_key_outcomes: In the microarray cohort the 11-gene committee panel had multivariate OR 0.70 (95% CI 0.56-0.87) and outperformed a statistically selected gene panel (OR 1.24, 95% CI 0.96-1.60).

title: Dietary Polyphenol Acteoside-Related Molecular Signatures in Clear Cell Renal Cell Carcinoma: Multi-Omics Profiling and Functional Validation of IMPDH1.
study_design: Retrospective multi-cohort prognostic modeling of acteoside-related genes, with in vitro IMPDH1 assays
data_source_detail: TCGA-KIRC derivation cohort; external ICGC-RECA-EU and E-MTAB-1980. Acteoside-related consensus clusters C1 and C2 comprised 249 and 290 patients. Single-cell and spatial transcriptomic datasets are public; external cohort sizes are not stated.
data_modality_detail: Bulk RNA-seq prognostic signature from acteoside-target genes; single-cell and spatial transcriptomics used for the landscape, not for the reported C-index
algorithm: 101 machine-learning combinations benchmarked on 29 univariate-Cox genes; StepCox[both] plus random survival forest selected by C-index, with RSF tree number tuned by out-of-bag error
input_features: Acteoside-related genes from CTD, GeneCards, and SwissTargetPrediction; 10-gene signature with IMPDH1 as the top RSF feature
biomarker_result: 10-gene acteoside-related prognostic signature led by IMPDH1
performance_value: StepCox[both] plus RSF C-index 0.930 (TCGA), 0.633 (ICGC), and 0.719 (E-MTAB-1980). Five-year AUC 0.979, 0.682, and 0.753 in the same three cohorts, respectively.
validation_detail: Derived in TCGA-KIRC and tested in independent ICGC-RECA-EU and E-MTAB-1980 cohorts. In vitro knockdown and overexpression of IMPDH1 is functional follow-up, not a performance cohort.
funding: Nantong University Special Research Fund for Clinical Medicine (2025JY044) and Jiangsu Association of Chinese Medicine (ZXFZ2024097).
key_finding: A 10-gene acteoside-related signature selected by StepCox plus random survival forest had C-index 0.930 in TCGA-KIRC, 0.633 in ICGC, and 0.719 in E-MTAB-1980.
limitations_as_stated: Direct binding of acteoside to IMPDH1 was not shown, dietary acteoside exposure was not measured, and the prognostic cohorts are retrospective.
other_key_outcomes: Consensus clusters C1 (n=249) and C2 (n=290) differed in survival, immune activity, and genomic instability. IMPDH1 knockdown suppressed ccRCC cell proliferation and invasion.

title: Integrative multi-omics identifies PANX2 as a ferroptosis suppressor and potential therapeutic target in clear cell renal cell carcinoma.
study_design: Multi-omics ferroptosis ML signature with scRNA/spatial discovery and extensive PANX2 experiments
data_source_detail: TCGA-KIRC training; external ICGC n=73, E-MTAB-1980, GSE167573; scRNA GSE159115
data_modality_detail: Bulk RNA, scRNA, spatial transcriptomics; four-gene Cox risk model
algorithm: LASSO, SVM-RFE, GBM, random forest with multivariate Cox
input_features: Four ferroptosis genes CA9, PVT1, RRM2, PANX2 in risk model
biomarker_result: Four-gene ferroptosis prognostic risk score and nomogram
performance_value: Consistent predictive performance in training and external validation cohorts per abstract; GSE167573 time-dependent AUCs referenced but not numerically listed in slice
validation_detail: External ICGC/ArrayExpress/GEO validation of risk model; PANX2 validated orthogonally in vitro/xenograft/murine models.
key_finding: A four-gene ferroptosis score stratified ccRCC prognosis externally and PANX2 drove ferroptosis resistance experimentally.
limitations_as_stated: Mechanistic focus on PANX2 beyond pure prediction.
other_key_outcomes: Spatial and scRNA localization of ferroptosis genes.
extraction_note: Paper anchor is mechanistic ferroptosis/PANX2 biology with ML signature as discovery layer; extensive non-AI validation dominates.

title: NECSO-based classification predicts immunotherapy efficacy and identifies FLAD1 as therapeutic target in kidney renal clear cell carcinoma.
study_design: NECSO-based ML score with pan-cancer ICI validation and FLAD1 functional assays
data_source_detail: TCGA-KIRC NMF subtypes; ICI-treated KIRC and three pan-cancer ICI cohorts; scRNA datasets
data_modality_detail: Bulk NECSO score (13-gene optimal) plus scRNA NECSO activity
algorithm: Machine learning NECSO score optimized by maximum AUC
input_features: 13-gene NECSO score including C4orf3 and related NECSO genes
biomarker_result: NECSO score (NECSOS) for prognosis and ICI response
performance_value: Model selected by maximum AUC; robust when AUC>0.7 in ICI cohorts including Braun anti-PD-1 ccRCC n=181 (exact AUC not in slice)
validation_detail: Validated in multiple ICI-treated cohorts spanning KIRC and pan-cancer settings.
key_finding: NECSO score predicted prognosis and immunotherapy associations across ICI cohorts; FLAD1 functionally linked to NECSO axis.
limitations_as_stated: Novel NECSO biology with emerging evidence base.
other_key_outcomes: FLAD1 gain/loss assays and xenografts.
extraction_note: Pan-cancer ICI validations include non-KIRC cohorts detailed in validation_detail.

title: Development and validation of an integrated machine learning model for recurrence-free survival prediction in clear cell renal cell carcinoma.
study_design: Multicenter multimodal ML for post-surgery ccRCC RFS with external test cohort
data_source_detail: 1284 patients across centers: train n=738, internal val n=317, external test n=229
data_modality_detail: Clinical variables, CT radiomics Rad-sign, 3D-ViT deep learning DL-sign
algorithm: ML ensemble combining clinical, radiomics, and 3D-ViT signatures
input_features: Clinical factors plus Rad-sign and DL-sign imaging signatures
biomarker_result: Multimodal recurrence-free survival prediction model and nomogram
performance_value: External test AUC 0.846 for 3D-ViT DL-sign; Rad-sign C-index 0.729; nomogram time-dependent AUCs up to 0.938 (7-yr RFS)
validation_detail: Dedicated external test cohort n=229 separate from training and internal validation centers.
key_finding: Multimodal ML including 3D-ViT improved external RFS prediction versus clinical or radiomics alone after resection.
limitations_as_stated: Imaging protocol heterogeneity across centers.
other_key_outcomes: Compared Naive Bayes radiomics and clinical-only baselines.

title: Integrative Multi-Transcriptomic Uncovers Actionable Signatures and Drug Repurposing Candidates for ccRCC-Hypertension Comorbidity.
study_design: Hypertension-ccRCC comorbidity integrative transcriptomics with MR and drug screening
data_source_detail: TCGA-KIRC integrated with GeneCards hypertension genes; spatial/scRNA secondary
data_modality_detail: Bulk RNA with WGCNA, ML hub genes, Mendelian randomization
algorithm: WGCNA and machine learning hub-gene selection with diagnostic nomogram
input_features: Four hub genes SCNN1G, CASR, KCNJ1, WNK4 diagnostic model
biomarker_result: Hypertension-related hub gene diagnostic/prognostic panel
performance_value: Diagnostic models showed good tumor vs normal discrimination and nomogram calibration per abstract (numeric AUC not in slice)
validation_detail: TCGA-centric analysis with MR support; no independent external prediction cohort described in slice.
key_finding: Hypertension-related hub genes linked to ccRCC prognosis and comorbidity mechanisms with MR genetic association evidence.
limitations_as_stated: Comorbidity-focused design limits direct GU intervention prediction.
other_key_outcomes: Spatial heterogeneity and in vitro drug candidates ECG and pseudoginsenoside-F11.
extraction_note: Comorbidity-focused ccRCC-hypertension design per calibration rule 5; AI diagnostic piece is secondary to mechanistic/MR aims.

title: Single-Cell and Machine Learning Analyses Identify MYDGF as an Immune-Related Biomarker Associated With the Tumor Microenvironment in Clear Cell Renal Cell Carcinoma.
study_design: Retrospective public-data biomarker study of MYDGF with a preliminary LASSO Cox gene set and in vitro knockdown
data_source_detail: scRNA-seq GSE156632 and TCGA-KIRC (correlation analyses cite N=528; tumor/normal counts cited as T=530, N=168). Cell-line knockdown is functional follow-up.
data_modality_detail: Single-cell RNA-seq plus bulk TCGA-KIRC expression for a MYDGF-associated gene set
algorithm: Univariate Cox prefilter followed by LASSO Cox (glmnet) with 10-fold cross-validation to choose lambda; planned 1:1 training and internal validation split
input_features: Differentially expressed genes between MYDGF-high and MYDGF-low TCGA-KIRC tumors
biomarker_result: Preliminary 19-gene MYDGF-related prognostic gene set
performance_value: No completed performance result. Authors state that risk-score distribution, Kaplan-Meier analysis, time-dependent ROC, and internal-validation performance of the 19-gene set were not evaluated.
validation_detail: A 1:1 TCGA split and 10-fold cross-validation for the LASSO penalty are described, but the authors say the prognostic evaluation was not completed. Not treated as a finished internal holdout.
funding: Dalian Life and Health Field Guidance Plan (2024ZDJH01PT068), Open Fund of the Provincial Key Laboratory of Multidimensional Omics and Molecular Enzymology (2025YB007), and Liaoning Provincial Department of Education (LJ212410161044).
key_finding: MYDGF is presented as an immune-related ccRCC biomarker, but the 19-gene LASSO Cox set is explicitly preliminary and has no reported discrimination metric.
limitations_as_stated: The 19-gene set is hypothesis-generating because its prognostic performance was not assessed. TIDE immunotherapy contrasts are computational predictions.
other_key_outcomes: Figure survival curves print HR 1.97 (95% CI 1.43-2.73), HR 1.47 (95% CI 1.07-2.03), HR 1.98 (95% CI 1.34-2.92), and HR 4.06 (95% CI 1.51-10.95); the text does not assign each HR to the LASSO score. MYDGF knockdown reduced proliferation, migration, and invasion in 769-P and Caki-1 cells.
extraction_note: The full text does not report a numeric metric for the machine-learning gene set. The paper's anchor is MYDGF biology, and the LASSO model is described by the authors as unvalidated.

title: Integrated multi-omics analysis reveals folate metabolism-related genes as prognostic markers and therapeutic targets in clear cell renal cell carcinoma.
study_design: Folate metabolism gene score from TCGA with validation cohort
data_source_detail: TCGA-KIRC discovery with additional validation cohort n=106 cited in slice patterns
data_modality_detail: Bulk RNA folate metabolism-related gene score (FMRG)
algorithm: Univariate Cox with LASSO/random forest feature reduction
input_features: FMRG scoring system from folate metabolism genes
biomarker_result: Folate metabolism-related gene (FMRG) score
performance_value: Signature predictive accuracy reported for risk groups (numeric AUC/C-index not in slice)
validation_detail: TCGA internal split with secondary validation cohort referenced.
funding: National Natural Science Foundation (82203365) and Jiangxi Natural Science Foundation (20232BAB2060).
key_finding: FMRG score stratified ccRCC prognosis and immune phenotypes for risk stratification.
limitations_as_stated: Retrospective public omics.
other_key_outcomes: Immune infiltration and drug response analyses.

title: Radiomics analysis of CT imaging for predicting MIT family translocation renal cell carcinoma: a multicenter retrospective clinical study.
study_design: Multicenter CT radiomics nomogram for MIT-family translocation RCC vs other RCC
data_source_detail: 746 RCC patients (77 MIT-RCC) from primary center; three external centers for validation
data_modality_detail: Preoperative CT radiomics with clinical nomogram
algorithm: LASSO radiomics with logistic nomogram
input_features: LASSO-selected CT radiomics features plus clinical variables
biomarker_result: Integrated radiomics-clinical nomogram for MIT-RCC
performance_value: Training AUC 0.952 (95% CI 0.927-0.971); multicenter validation AUC 0.914 (95% CI 0.879-0.942)
validation_detail: Three additional hospital centers validated the nomogram after primary cohort training.
key_finding: CT radiomics nomogram accurately distinguished MIT-RCC from other RCC subtypes on multicenter validation despite class imbalance.
limitations_as_stated: Rare MIT-RCC subtype with limited positive cases.
other_key_outcomes: Subtype-specific imaging feature interpretation.
extraction_note: Class imbalance (77/746 MIT-RCC) noted in appraisal.

title: Integrative bulk and single-cell transcriptome analyses reveals manganese metabolism-related prognostic genes in clear cell renal cell carcinoma with experimental validation.
study_design: Manganese metabolism prognostic genes in ccRCC with qRT-PCR validation
data_source_detail: Public ccRCC transcriptomic cohorts plus three tumor and three normal tissue qRT-PCR samples
data_modality_detail: Bulk RNA manganese metabolism genes with Cox LASSO score
algorithm: Univariate Cox and LASSO multivariate risk model
input_features: Manganese metabolism-related prognostic gene set
biomarker_result: Manganese metabolism prognostic risk score
performance_value: Nomogram and risk groups showed high predictive accuracy per results text (numeric AUC not in slice)

title: Machine learning-derived cellular senescence index for predicting prognosis and drug sensitivity in patients with renal cell carcinoma.
study_design: retrospective cohort / translational bioinformatic study (scRNA-seq + bulk transcriptomic ML prognostic modeling) with in vitro functional validation
data_source_detail: scRNA-seq GSE210038 (7 ccRCC + 2 normal samples); bulk RNA-seq/clinical TCGA-KIRC (training/testing, 7:3 split) and ICGC-RECA (external validation cohort); own institutional cohort of 8 paired ccRCC/adjacent-tissue samples (First Affiliated Hospital of Harbin Medical University; IHC/Western blot); ccRCC cell lines 786O and A498 (in vitro functional validation)
data_modality_detail: scRNA-seq (senescence landscape) + bulk RNA-seq/TCGA-KIRC and ICGC-RECA gene expression + CNV/mutation genomic data for SRSM construction, plus IHC and Western blot for NME2 protein validation

input_features: Senescence-related gene expression from FRIDMAN_SENESCENCE_UP gene set (MSigDB), reduced via the 101-combination ML framework to a 9-gene signature (ALDH1A3, CREG1, ESM1, MMP1, NME2, RHOB, SERPINB2, TNFAIP2, TSPYL5)
biomarker_result: Senescence-related scoring model (SRSM), 9-gene signature
performance_value: Optimal Lasso+StepCox model selected by highest mean C-index (exact numeric value not reported); time-dependent ROC AUC 0.65-0.74 across TCGA-KIRC training, TCGA-KIRC testing, and ICGC-RECA external validation cohorts; Kaplan-Meier survival difference between high- vs low-SRSM groups p<0.001 in all three cohorts
validation_detail: TCGA-KIRC split 7:3 into training/testing (internal), with ICGC-RECA used as a separate external public cohort. Per appraisal_note, counted here as a prognostic SRSM (C-index/AUC) despite being framed narratively around associative scRNA-seq senescence biology.
funding: National Natural Science Foundation of China (82473337); Natural Science Foundation of Heilongjiang Province (PL2024H042); Outstanding Young Medical Talent Training Program of the First Affiliated Hospital of Harbin Medical University (HYD2020JQ0020); Beijing Medical Award Foundation (YXJL-2021-0302-0292)
key_finding: A 9-gene ML-derived senescence-related scoring model (SRSM, Lasso+StepCox) stratified ccRCC prognosis (AUC 0.65-0.74 across TCGA-KIRC training/testing and ICGC-RECA external validation; KM p<0.001), with high-SRSM tumors showing an immunosuppressive TME and greater sensitivity to axitinib/sorafenib; in vitro NME2 knockdown suppressed ccRCC proliferation/invasion.
limitations_as_stated: Relatively small sample size requiring further validation in larger cohorts; functional experiments relatively basic, no in vivo animal studies; cellular senescence inferred transcriptionally (AddModuleScore) rather than confirmed with gold-standard senescence assays due to lack of freshly isolated tumor material.
other_key_outcomes: scRNA-seq-based cellular senescence landscape in the ccRCC TME (6 major cell subpopulations); differential immune infiltration, TME complexity, CNV burden, and drug-sensitivity differences between high- vs low-SRSM groups; NME2 in vitro functional validation (Transwell, wound-healing, CCK-8/EdU, IHC, Western blot) in 786O/A498 cell lines and 8 paired patient tissue samples.
extraction_note: n_analytic for TCGA-KIRC/ICGC-RECA cohorts used in SRSM construction not given as explicit numbers in text; exact C-index for the selected model likewise not reported numerically. Flagged per instructions given the borderline prognostic-vs-associative framing noted in appraisal_note plus the missing n.
