key_finding: Integrated CoxBoost-Ridge signature predicted ccRCC outcomes with moderate external concordance while linking BPA exposure networks to immune mechanisms.
limitations_as_stated: BPA exposure inferred computationally rather than measured in clinical cohorts used for validation.
other_key_outcomes: Molecular docking of key targets; network toxicology enrichment analyses.
extraction_note: Paper anchor is BPA network toxicology; BPA not measured in prognostic cohorts per appraisal (pilot PCP/ATBC precedent).

title: A SWI/SNF complex-related genes signature predicts prognosis and immune infiltration in ccRCC with KCNK5 as a novel biomarker.
study_design: TCGA molecular subtyping plus multi-ML five-gene prognostic signature
data_source_detail: 532 TCGA-KIRC for clustering/model; E-MTAB-1980 n=101 external validation
data_modality_detail: Bulk RNA with ConsensusClusterPlus subtypes and multivariate Cox
algorithm: Multiple ML approaches integrated with multivariate Cox (five core SCRGs)
input_features: Five SWI/SNF-related genes (TMCC3, TOP2A, EPS8, PIK3R3, KCNK5)
biomarker_result: Five-gene SCRG prognostic signature
performance_value: TCGA training set (n=268) 1/3/5-year AUC 0.780/0.764/0.726; nomogram AUC 0.864. Test set (n=264) and external E-MTAB-1980 and ICGC-KIRC were described as consistent, without printed AUCs.
validation_detail: Developed on TCGA-KIRC and validated on independent ArrayExpress E-MTAB-1980 series.
key_finding: SWI/SNF-related subtypes differed in survival and immune infiltration and a five-gene signature predicted prognosis with KCNK5 functionally suppressing malignancy in vitro.
limitations_as_stated: Mechanisms of core genes incompletely defined; retrospective public data.
other_key_outcomes: SCRGcluster subtyping; scRNA expression patterns of core genes.

title: Identification of plasma cell infiltration-related gene signatures as a novel prognostic model for clear cell renal cell carcinoma.
study_design: PC-infiltration gene discovery with LASSO prognostic PC score and nomogram
data_source_detail: TCGA-KIRC n=530; E-MTAB-1980 n=101; GSE29609 n=39 validation
data_modality_detail: Bulk RNA deconvolution with LASSO and nomogram integration
algorithm: LASSO regression with tenfold CV selecting nine hub genes into PC score
input_features: Nine plasma-cell infiltration hub genes (3 risk, 6 protective)
biomarker_result: Plasma cell infiltration PC score plus age-stage nomogram
performance_value: Nomogram AUC significantly exceeded staging alone (P<0.01); time-dependent AUC values referenced in figures
validation_detail: Model trained on TCGA and validated on E-MTAB-1980 and GSE29609 cohorts.
key_finding: Nine-gene PC score independently predicted OS and improved nomogram discrimination versus TNM stage alone with distinct immune and drug sensitivity profiles.
limitations_as_stated: Public cohort heterogeneity; local cohort validation details limited in slice.
other_key_outcomes: Drug sensitivity differences by risk group; single-cell hub gene validation.

title: The value of dual-energy CT radiomics in evaluating vascular maturity and prognosis in clear cell renal cell carcinoma.
study_design: Single-center DECT radiomics with small external validation for vascular maturity and PFS
data_source_detail: Center I n=87 (60 train, 27 validation); Center II external n=17
data_modality_detail: Dual-energy CT multi-energy radiomics with IHC CD34+/alpha-SMA vascular maturity
algorithm: Radiomics ML models plus combined Rad-score clinical nomogram
input_features: Multi-energy DECT radiomics Rad-score with clinical covariates
biomarker_result: Combined Rad-score-clinical model for vascular maturity and PFS nomogram
performance_value: Combined model AUC 0.967 validation and 0.764 external (n=17); multi-energy radiomics AUC 0.833/0.736
validation_detail: Internal 7:3 split plus second-center external set of only 17 patients.
key_finding: DECT radiomics combined with clinical features predicted vascular maturity and separated PFS by CD34+/alpha-SMA groups with strong internal but modest external AUC.
limitations_as_stated: Very small external validation cohort; single additional center.
other_key_outcomes: Kaplan-Meier PFS differences by vascular maturity groups.
extraction_note: Appraisal notes tiny external validation (n=17) limiting generalizability.

title: Integrating sarcopenia and non-contrast CT radiomics for preoperative prediction of survival in sarcomatoid renal cell carcinoma.
study_design: Single-center retrospective sRCC cohort with sarcopenia plus CT radiomics
data_source_detail: n=121 pathologically confirmed sRCC at one center
data_modality_detail: Non-contrast CT tumor radiomics and L3 sarcopenia metrics
algorithm: LASSO Cox regression for radiomic signature integrated with sarcopenia
input_features: Sarcopenia status, Rad-score, clinical factors (PNR, HALP, size, N stage)
biomarker_result: Combined clinical plus Rad-score sarcopenia-integrated OS model
performance_value: Combined model time-dependent AUC 0.849/0.804/0.819 at 1/2/3-year OS vs radiomics-only (p=0.002)
validation_detail: Single rare-subtype cohort without independent external imaging validation.
key_finding: Integrating L3 sarcopenia with non-contrast CT radiomics improved preoperative OS prediction in sarcomatoid RCC versus radiomics alone.
limitations_as_stated: Rare aggressive subtype with small single-center sample.
other_key_outcomes: Multivariable HRs for sarcopenia and clinical covariates reported.
extraction_note: Appraisal flags rare sarcomatoid RCC and small single-center cohort limiting scope.

title: Machine learning-driven dissection of the obesity-ccRCC interface: FCGR2A emerges as a central coordinator of tumor-immune crosstalk.
study_design: Obesity-ccRCC dual-disease transcriptomic harmonization with ML signature
data_source_detail: Five harmonized ccRCC cohorts total n=876 plus obesity adipose profiles; scRNA GSE159115
data_modality_detail: Bulk microarray/RNA harmonized with ComBat/sva and glmBoost+Stepglm
algorithm: glmBoost plus Stepglm 14-gene signature after ComBat/sva harmonization
input_features: 14-gene obesity-ccRCC interface signature centered on FCGR2A hub
biomarker_result: 14-gene FCGR2A-centered cross-cohort signature
performance_value: Reported mean cross-cohort AUC 0.991; FCGR2A staging AUC 0.998
validation_detail: Multi-cohort harmonization across five ccRCC datasets treated as cross-cohort evaluation.
key_finding: Obesity-ccRCC co-dysregulation highlighted FCGR2A in myeloid crosstalk with a 14-gene ML signature showing very high cross-cohort discrimination.
limitations_as_stated: Observational public data; drug repurposing predictions require experimental confirmation.
other_key_outcomes: Single-cell localization of FCGR2A to M2 macrophages; DSigDB repurposing hits.
extraction_note: Appraisal flags implausible AUC up to 0.998/0.991 suggesting overfitting or leakage for 14-gene signature.

title: TCIRG1 as a Novel Prognostic Biomarker Triggering Immune Infiltration in Renal Clear Cell Carcinoma: An Integrative Study of Single-Cell and Bulk Data.
study_design: Retrospective public-cohort prognostic modeling of KIRC with an external transcriptomic cohort and orthogonal wet-lab assays of TCIRG1
data_source_detail: GEO scRNA GSE139555 for hdWGCNA; TCGA-KIRC training n=529; ArrayExpress E-MTAB-1980 validation n=101. Institutional IHC, western blot, Transwell, and nude-mouse assays were orthogonal and not used to train the model.
data_modality_detail: Single-cell RNA-seq monocyte module plus bulk RNA-seq expression of nine selected genes
algorithm: Best of 101 combinations: stepwise Cox (both directions) plus random survival forest; LightGBM and XGBoost with SHAP used only to rank TCIRG1
input_features: Nine genes: TNFAIP2, TCIRG1, SLC11A1, PLAUR, MYO9B, LRRK2, IQGAP2, EFHD2, and CD44
biomarker_result: Nine-gene risk score; TCIRG1 had the highest SHAP contribution in both LightGBM and XGBoost
performance_value: Training (TCGA-KIRC, n=529) 1/3/5-year AUC 0.948/0.967/0.982; external E-MTAB-1980 (n=101) 1/3/5-year AUC 0.822/0.721/0.682
validation_detail: Model selected on TCGA-KIRC and validated on independent ArrayExpress E-MTAB-1980. The winning combination was chosen by C-index among 101 algorithms; that C-index is not printed.
conflicts_of_interest: The authors declare no conflicts of interest
key_finding: A nine-gene StepCox plus random-survival-forest score predicted KIRC overall survival, with training 1/3/5-year AUCs of 0.948, 0.967, and 0.982 and lower external AUCs (0.822, 0.721, 0.682); TCIRG1 was the top model feature and tracked Treg infiltration.
limitations_as_stated: TCIRG1 and Treg coexpression was shown, but mechanisms of growth, invasion, and metastasis remain insufficiently explored; further in vivo studies are needed, and other immune cells implicated by bioinformatics were not fully studied.
other_key_outcomes: High- versus low-risk survival differed in training (p<0.001) and validation (p=0.032). Risk score was an independent Cox factor. A clinical nomogram had acceptable 1/2/3-year calibration. CIBERSORT showed Treg cells most positively correlated with the risk score.
extraction_note: Primary axis is the nine-gene prognostic model. LightGBM and XGBoost ranked genes after the survival model was built. The selection C-index among 101 algorithms is not printed, so the reported time-dependent AUCs are the performance values.

title: Metal ion transporter SLC39A14-mediated ferroptosis and glycosylation modulate the tumor immune microenvironment: pan-cancer multi-omics exploration of therapeutic potential.
tumor_site_detail: Pan-cancer ferroptosis-glycosylation study; KIRC/GBM among many TCGA tumors with strongest signal in glioblastoma per appraisal
study_design: Pan-cancer multi-omics with ML ferroptosis-related Cox signature
data_source_detail: TCGA pan-cancer bulk with SLC39A14-centric ferroptosis signature (663 ferroptosis genes curated)
data_modality_detail: Bulk transcriptomics/epigenomics plus scRNA references
algorithm: LASSO Cox regression with cross-validation on pan-cancer TCGA
input_features: Ferroptosis-related gene signature anchored on SLC39A14 intersection
biomarker_result: Pan-cancer ferroptosis-related prognostic gene signature
performance_value: Pan-cancer nomogram 5-year AUROC 0.78 in the training cohort and 0.81 in the test cohort
validation_detail: Pan-cancer TCGA evaluation; GU-specific external validation not primary focus.
key_finding: SLC39A14-linked ferroptosis-glycosylation axis associated with prognosis and immune infiltration across tumors with emphasis outside GU.
limitations_as_stated: Pan-cancer scope limits tumor-specific generalizability; mechanistic validation incomplete.
other_key_outcomes: Immune microenvironment and pathway enrichment across TCGA cancer types.
extraction_note: Appraisal: strongest prognostic signal in glioblastoma; KIRC secondary—borderline AIBIO_GU scope (pilot REC-000240 analog). The printed performance is the pan-cancer nomogram 5-year AUROC, not a KIRC-specific C-index.

title: Survival Prediction for Postoperative Patients With Kidney Cancer Based on Computed Tomography Radiomics: Retrospective Cohort Study.
study_design: Retrospective TCIA cohort of postoperative kidney cancer; CT radiomics LASSO-Cox nomogram with bootstrap internal validation
data_source_detail: The Cancer Imaging Archive contrast-enhanced CT; 210 patients screened, 3 excluded for overall survival of 0 days; analytic cohort n=207 after nephrectomy
data_modality_detail: PyRadiomics features from gross tumor volume and healthy kidney (851 features; shape, first-order, texture, and wavelet)
algorithm: LASSO-Cox (glmnet) with 10-fold cross-validation for lambda, then a Cox nomogram (rms); 1000-bootstrap optimism correction
input_features: Five wavelet CT radiomic features (four from gross tumor, one from healthy kidney) plus clinical covariates in the nomogram
biomarker_result: Five-feature radiomic risk score; high- versus low-risk cutoff 0.154921
performance_value: Optimism-corrected C-index 0.73 (95% CI 0.68-0.78); bootstrap-corrected AUC 0.80 (SD 0.03), 0.77 (SD 0.04), 0.74 (SD 0.04), and 0.71 (SD 0.05) at 1, 2, 4, and 6 years
validation_detail: 10-fold cross-validation selected the LASSO penalty. Final metrics are 1000-bootstrap optimism-corrected estimates on the full cohort (N=207). Authors abandoned a 70:30 holdout because of sample size. No external cohort.
key_finding: A five-feature CT radiomics score predicted postoperative kidney-cancer overall survival with an optimism-corrected C-index of 0.73 (95% CI 0.68-0.78) and bootstrap AUCs of 0.80, 0.77, 0.74, and 0.71 at 1, 2, 4, and 6 years.
limitations_as_stated: Public-data selection and heterogeneous CT protocols; n=207 judged too small for holdout validation; TNM stage not retained; peritumoral regions not analyzed. Authors also insert an unrelated hepatocellular-carcinoma staging argument.
other_key_outcomes: Kaplan-Meier separation of radiomic risk groups (P<.001; low-risk n=154, high-risk n=53). Calibration curves were described as good. The clinical-plus-radiomics ROC in Figure 5 has no additional printed AUC.
extraction_note: Performance numbers are the bootstrap-corrected C-index and time-dependent AUCs on all 207 patients. Funding is not stated in the full text.

title: Single-cell transcriptomic insights into ccRCC: a stemness gene signature for prognosis and treatment response prediction.
study_design: scRNA-guided bulk ML prognostic signature across public ccRCC cohorts
data_source_detail: 44-sample scRNA plus 1075 bulk samples (TCGA ccRCC/KICH/KIRP mixes, GSE22541, GSE167573, ArrayExpress)
data_modality_detail: scRNA stemness mapping plus LASSO-XGBoost bulk SGS
algorithm: LASSO-XGBoost stemness-related gene signature (SGS)
input_features: Stemness-related genes from proliferative epithelial ccRCC subtype
biomarker_result: Stemness gene signature (SGS)
performance_value: LASSO plus XGBoost highest average C-index 0.763 in the validation datasets and was selected as the stemness gene signature
validation_detail: Multiple independent bulk cohorts beyond TCGA discovery.
key_finding: AI-derived stemness signature predicted survival and linked to reduced targeted/ICI responsiveness in high-risk ccRCC.
limitations_as_stated: Mixed TCGA kidney histologies in download; needs histology-specific confirmation.
other_key_outcomes: Treatment response associations for targeted therapy and ICI arms.

title: Metabolic heterogeneity and survival outcomes in papillary renal cell carcinoma: insights from multi-datasets and machine learning analyses.
study_design: TCGA-KIRP discovery with GEO external validation and 90-algorithm ML screen
data_source_detail: TCGA-KIRP n=324; GEO GSE2748 n=34 external validation
data_modality_detail: Metabolism-related bulk RNA with RSF-selected MRS
algorithm: Screen of 90 ML algorithms; random survival forest optimal
input_features: Metabolism-related differential genes forming four-gene MRS nomogram
biomarker_result: Metabolism-related signature (MRS) and four-gene OS nomogram
performance_value: 5-year survival AUC 0.989 in discovery; external GSE2748 validation performed
validation_detail: RSF model validated in independent GSE2748 microarray cohort (n=34).
key_finding: Metabolic reprogramming signature predicted KIRP survival and drug response patterns with qPCR/IHC validation of PYCR1, INMT, KIF20A.
limitations_as_stated: Small external cohort; very high 5-year AUC may reflect overfitting.
other_key_outcomes: TMB and sunitinib/pazopanib sensitivity associations by risk group.
extraction_note: Appraisal flags 5-year AUC 0.989 as overfitting concern despite external GEO validation.

title: Unveiling ammonia-induced cell death: a new frontier in clear cell renal cell carcinoma prognosis.
study_design: TCGA discovery with E-MTAB-1980 external validation and spatial/single-cell analyses
data_source_detail: TCGA-KIRC training; E-MTAB-1980 validation; spatial/scRNA GEO sets
data_modality_detail: Bulk RNA plus spatial and scRNA with LASSO/RF/CoxBoost selection
algorithm: LASSO, random forest, CoxBoost with multivariate Cox five-gene score
input_features: Five AICD-related genes (FOXM1, ANK3, ATP1A1, HADH, PLG)
biomarker_result: AICD-related five-gene risk score with nomogram
performance_value: Combined nomogram 1/3/5-year overall-survival AUC 0.873/0.833/0.833 in TCGA-KIRC. The five-gene risk-score ROC in TCGA-KIRC and E-MTAB-1980 is described as high accuracy without printed AUC values.
validation_detail: Independent E-MTAB-1980 cohort used for external validation after TCGA modeling.
key_finding: Five-gene ammonia-induced cell death score predicted prognosis and immune suppression with ATP1A1 functional validation.
limitations_as_stated: Observational omics; in vitro focus on ATP1A1 only.
other_key_outcomes: TMB and immunotherapy response associations; docking-based drug candidates.

title: Alpha-2-Macroglobulin and Signature Genes: Predictive Biomarkers for Prognosis and Immunotherapy in Clear Cell Renal Cell Carcinoma.

validation_detail: External public cohorts used for signature validation beyond TCGA.
key_finding: A2M-linked signature stratified ccRCC prognosis and immunotherapy response with multi-database validation.
limitations_as_stated: Retrospective public expression data; limited prospective clinical confirmation in slice.
other_key_outcomes: Immune infiltration and ICI response analyses.

title: Epithelial-mesenchymal transition classification based on machine learning for predicting prognosis and treatment response in clear cell renal cell carcinoma.

key_finding: EMT-based ML classification predicted prognosis and treatment response with validated performance in external ccRCC cohort.

other_key_outcomes: TME scores, enrichment, and drug sensitivity by EMT class.

title: Interferon Regulatory Factor 4 Recruits Immature B Cells to Signal Tertiary Lymphoid Structure Immaturity and Progression of Clear Cell Renal Cell Carcinoma.

other_key_outcomes: Multiplex IHC/spatial TLS maturation analyses.

title: A manganese metabolism-related gene signature stratifies prognosis and immunotherapy efficacy in kidney cancer.

biomarker_result: MMCG risk score and clinical nomogram
validation_detail: E-MTAB-1980 and TCGA-KIRP cohorts used for external validation of MMCG model.
key_finding: Manganese metabolism subtypes and MMCG risk score independently predicted RCC outcomes and immunotherapy response patterns.

other_key_outcomes: Immune infiltration and ICI response prediction by cluster/risk group.

title: Using Multiomics and Machine Learning: Insights into Improving the Outcomes of Clear Cell Renal Cell Carcinoma via the SRD5A3-AS1/hsa-let-7e-5p/RRM2 Axis.
study_design: Multi-omics FAM-lncRNA ML axis with TCGA internal validation split

input_features: Fatty-acid-metabolism-associated lncRNA prognostic signature and ceRNA axis

other_key_outcomes: TME and treatment response differences by risk group.
extraction_note: The full text does not report a numeric AUC, C-index, HR, accuracy, or sensitivity for the prognostic signature.

title: Palmitoylation regulators drive the progression of clear cell renal cell carcinoma through Inhibition of cuproptosis: insights into the role of ZDHHC18.

other_key_outcomes: Cuproptosis and fatty acid metabolism pathway links.

title: Prediction of metastatic risk of renal clear cell carcinoma based on CT radiomics analysis.

title: Identifying a prognostic signature for clear cell renal cell carcinoma: the convergence of single-cell and bulk sequencing with machine learning.

title: A novel stemness-related lncRNA signature predicts prognosis, immune infiltration and drug sensitivity of clear cell renal cell carcinoma.

title: Contrast-Enhanced CT-Based Radiomics Nomogram for Prediction of Pathologic T3a Upstaging in Clinical T1 RCC.

title: Machine learning-derived prognostic signature integrating programmed cell death and mitochondrial function in renal clear cell carcinoma: identification of PIF1 as a novel target.

TCs and TNFSF13B were associated with worse survival and disease progression after PD-1 blockade in a published nivolumab cohort; no numeric AUC or HR for that comparison is printed.

title: Prognostic model of kidney renal clear cell carcinoma using aging-related long noncoding RNA signatures identifies THBS1-IT1 as a potential prognostic biomarker for multiple cancers.
study_design: translational/bioinformatic

input_features: 5-gene expression signature (TPM values of MMP11, THBS1-IT1, DYNLL2, RMND5A, PEG10)
biomarker_result: LncAging_score, a 5-gene (aging-related lncRNA-network-derived) prognostic model; THBS1-IT1 further characterized as a pan-cancer prognostic biomarker
performance_value: Training cohort AUC for 1-/3-/5-year OS: 0.727/0.696/0.726; nomogram (LncAging_score + age + sex + stage) AUC range 0.796-0.872 for 1-, 3-, and 5-year risk in entire cohort (n=514); LncAging_score, age, grade and stage all independent prognostic factors (P<0.05, HR>1)
validation_detail: Random split of TCGA-KIRC cohort (n=514, complete clinical+survival data) into training (n=345, ~67%) and validation (n=169, ~33%); no independent external cohort was used to validate the 5-gene KIRC prognostic model. The pan-cancer analysis of THBS1-IT1 alone (across 33 other TCGA tumor types) is a separate exploratory extension, not an external validation of the KIRC model.
key_finding: A 5-gene aging-related lncRNA/mRNA model (LncAging_score, including THBS1-IT1) is an independent prognostic factor for KIRC OS/PFI (AUC 0.696-0.727 in training), improved further when combined with clinical variables in a nomogram (AUC 0.796-0.872); THBS1-IT1 alone shows dysregulation and prognostic significance across 12+ additional TCGA tumor types.
limitations_as_stated: NR
other_key_outcomes: Two aging-related subgroups (AR-subgroup A/B) identified in KIRC by unsupervised consensus clustering of 8 candidate aging-related lncRNAs (CarLncs), differing significantly in OS and immune cell infiltration (secondary, exploratory axis, not a predictive model). Pan-cancer analysis of THBS1-IT1 alone across 33 TCGA tumor types: associated with OS/DSS/PFI/DFI in multiple non-GU tumor types, and correlated with TMB, MSI, and immune/stromal infiltration.
extraction_note: Data availability statement explicit in text (available upon reasonable request). Funding/COI statements not visible in the extracted text portion; marked NR. appraisal_note flags the pan-cancer THBS1-IT1 extension as beyond the KIRC model's original scope; documented under other_key_outcomes rather than folded into the main biomarker_result/validation_level.

title: Fifteen-gene expression based model predicts the survival of clear cell renal cell carcinoma.

algorithm: Cox screening plus randomForestSRC variable hunting (100 repeats) and multivariate Cox coefficients
input_features: Fifteen genes (e.g., IL20RB, KL, CDC7) with weighted expression risk score
biomarker_result: 15-gene expression risk score (RS)
performance_value: OS log-rank P=5.6e-16 (TCGA N=533); external E-MTAB-1980 OS P=0.00029 (N=101); three-year AUC curves in Figure 2E (numeric AUC not in slice)
validation_detail: Risk score formula derived in TCGA and applied to independent E-MTAB-1980 without refitting.
key_finding: A 15-gene RS stratified OS and RFS in TCGA ccRCC and reproduced survival separation in E-MTAB-1980.
limitations_as_stated: Retrospective single-database development; needs prospective multicenter validation.
other_key_outcomes: Three-year OS nomogram combining RS with clinical indicators; quartile survival analyses.

title: A novel machine learning approach reveals latent vascular phenotypes predictive of renal cancer outcome.

title: Effective analysis of testicular seminoma toxicity and mechanisms of acetyl tributyl citrate using network toxicology, bulk RNA sequencing data, single-cell RNA sequencing data, and clinical data.
study_design: translational/bioinformatic
data_source_detail: TCGA-TGCT (138 tumor samples with PFI data), GEO GSE3218 (12 tumor/6 control seminoma), GEO GSE228501 (4 tumor scRNA-seq samples); own clinical IHC cohort (First Hospital of Shanxi Medical University, China; 12 TGCT vs 36 control testes)
data_modality_detail: bulk RNA-seq (TCGA-TGCT, GSE3218), scRNA-seq (GSE228501), network toxicology target prediction, molecular docking/MD simulation, immunohistochemistry validation
algorithm: univariate Cox regression, LASSO regression (5-fold cross-validation), risk score model
input_features: 20 candidate genes (intersection of ATBC-predicted targets and DEGs) narrowed via Cox/LASSO to a 2-gene expression signature (PDK1, OARD1)
biomarker_result: PDK1 and OARD1 (2-gene ATBC-associated prognostic risk signature)
performance_value: Training cohort (n=69): AUC 1-yr=0.62, 2-yr=0.66, 3-yr=0.60; validation cohort (n=69): AUC>0.60 for 1-,2-,3-yr survival
validation_detail: 138 TCGA-TGCT tumor samples split 5:5 (69 training/69 validation) from the same cohort; no external cohort. Separate IHC verification (own clinical samples, n=12 TGCT/36 control) confirms protein expression direction but is not a held-out validation of the risk model itself.
key_finding: PDK1 and OARD1, identified as ATBC-associated candidate targets, form a 2-gene prognostic risk model for testicular seminoma with moderate discriminatory capacity (AUC>0.6 for 1-3yr survival) in TCGA-TGCT; both genes were significantly downregulated in tumor vs normal testis by IHC.
limitations_as_stated: NR (not explicitly stated in extracted text); ATBC exposure was not directly measured in patients - targets inferred computationally from toxicology/target-prediction databases per appraisal_note
other_key_outcomes: scRNA-seq identified 5 cell types with B cells as key cells showing dynamic PDK1/OARD1 expression along pseudotime; immune infiltration differences between risk groups; molecular docking (PDK1 binding energy -6.5 kcal/mol, OARD1 -5.5 kcal/mol) and 100ns MD simulation of ATBC-protein complexes; ATBC toxicity predicted as carcinogenic with skin/eye irritation and aquatic environmental risk.
extraction_note: Funding, conflicts of interest, and explicit limitations not visible in the extracted text excerpt. ATBC exposure not directly measured in patients per appraisal_note; targets inferred from public toxicology/target-prediction databases, so the toxicology framing is computational/hypothesis-generating rather than empirically validated exposure-outcome association.

title: Machine Learning Model Integrating Computed Tomography Image-Derived Radiomics and Circulating miRNAs to Predict Residual Teratoma in Metastatic Nonseminoma Testicular Cancer.
study_design: Retrospective post-chemotherapy residual-mass CT radiomics plus miR-371-375 with nested cross-validation
data_source_detail: British Columbia Cancer GU biobank; 111 lesions from 52 mNSGCT patients (78 train / 33 test lesions)

algorithm: LassoCV feature selection with CatBoost, random forest, gradient boosting, and SVM compared (CatBoost best)
input_features: Selected CT radiomics signature plus miR-371 and miR-375 (R+371+375 model)
biomarker_result: Combined radiomics and microRNA signature for teratoma versus nonteratoma histology
performance_value: CatBoost R+371+375 AUC 0.96 (95% CI 0.88-1.0) training and 0.83 (95% CI 0.68-0.98) testing
validation_detail: Lesion-level 70/30 split plus stratified nested 10-fold CV during tuning; seminoma lesions included only for AI training.
key_finding: Integrating miR-371-375 with CT radiomics improved prediction of teratoma in post-chemotherapy residual masses versus radiomics alone.
limitations_as_stated: NR
other_key_outcomes: Multivariate analysis identified radiomics signature as strongest independent teratoma predictor (P<0.0001).

title: A predictive system comprising serum microRNAs and radiomics for residual retroperitoneal masses in metastatic nonseminomatous germ cell tumors.
study_design: Single-center retrospective cohort with a random training/validation split and a later same-center prospective test cohort
data_source_detail: Sun Yat-sen University Cancer Center, Guangzhou. Retrospective Sep 2014-Aug 2022: 105 men, 145 residual retroperitoneal masses (training 75 patients/108 masses; validation 30 patients/37 masses). Prospective Oct 2022-Jun 2024 test set: 34 patients, 42 masses.
data_modality_detail: Contrast-enhanced CT radiomics (LASSO Radscore from six features) plus serum miR-371a-3p and miR-375
algorithm: LASSO radiomic feature selection and regularized logistic regression integrating Radscore with serum miR-371a-3p and miR-375 (best of six supervised classifiers)
input_features: Six CT radiomic features summarized as a Radscore, plus preoperative serum miR-371a-3p and miR-375
biomarker_result: Radiomics-miRNA integrated model for residual retroperitoneal mass histology (necrosis/fibrosis, teratoma, or viable germ cell tumor), with a web nomogram
performance_value: Prospective test macro-average AUC 0.91 (95% CI 0.80-0.99); validation 0.96 (95% CI 0.87-1.00); training 0.98 (95% CI 0.96-1.00)
validation_detail: Retrospective cohort randomly split into training and validation without cross-validation of the final model. Reported AUC is from a later same-center prospective test set (34 patients, 42 masses), not a geographic external cohort.
funding: Cancer Innovative Research Program of Sun Yat-sen University Cancer Center (CIRP-SYSUCC-0014) and Science and Technology Projects in Guangzhou (2023A04J1783)
key_finding: An integrated CT radiomics and serum miR-371/miR-375 model predicted residual retroperitoneal mass histology before post-chemotherapy RPLND, with prospective test macro-average AUC 0.91 (95% CI 0.80-0.99), higher than radiomics alone.
limitations_as_stated: Single-center retrospective design with heterogeneous CT scanners and protocols and a high rate of residual viable disease (22%); radiomic contouring is time-intensive; some classifiers overfit between training and validation; miRNA cutoffs are laboratory-specific. Further external and larger prospective testing is needed.
other_key_outcomes: Radiomics-only logistic regression macro-average AUC 0.76 (95% CI 0.59-0.94) in the validation set; binary benign versus malignant AUC 0.90. Combined miR-371 and miR-375 macro-average AUC 0.89 (95% CI 0.77-0.97) in the test set. Web calculator: https://dingrj.shinyapps.io/pcRPLND_prediction.
extraction_note: Primary axis is the three-class radiomics-miRNA model. n_analytic is the prospective test set of 42 residual masses (34 patients) that supports the reported AUC 0.91.

title: Radiomics and Clinicopathological Characteristics for Predicting Lymph Node Metastasis in Testicular Cancer.
study_design: retrospective cohort
data_source_detail: Single-center cohort, University Hospital of Ulm, Germany; early-stage (stage I) testicular cancer patients, January 2006-December 2016
data_modality_detail: Contrast-enhanced CT radiomics (85 IBSI-standardized texture/first-order features) extracted from 273 segmented retroperitoneal infrarenal lymph nodes, combined with clinical risk factors
algorithm: Random Forest, Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LGBM), Support Vector Machine Classifier (SVC), K-Nearest Neighbours (KNN)
input_features: 85 CT-derived radiomic texture features per lymph node plus 5 clinical features (age, preoperative AFP, B-HCG, histotype, BMI)
biomarker_result: Combined clinical-radiomics Random Forest model for lymph node metastasis prediction
performance_value: Combined clinical-radiomics Random Forest: AUC=0.95, accuracy=87%, precision=89%, recall=86%, F1=87%. LGBM combined: AUC=0.93, accuracy=83%. SVC and KNN performed considerably worse.
validation_detail: Single-center retrospective cohort (n=91 patients, 273 lymph node instances); patient-level group shuffle split into training (70%) and test (30%), tenfold cross-validation used to check robustness. No external or multicenter cohort; authors explicitly call for future prospective, multicentre validation.
funding: NUM 2.0 (FKZ: 01KX2121), part of the Racoon Project
key_finding: A combined clinical-radiomics Random Forest model achieved AUC=0.95 for preoperative prediction of retroperitoneal lymph node metastasis in early-stage testicular cancer, outperforming radiomics-only and clinical-only models; decision curve analysis showed net clinical benefit across a threshold probability range of 0-0.89.
limitations_as_stated: Retrospective design and small cohort size may have introduced selection bias; two different CT scanners used; single-center results; small sample size precluded inclusion of classical pathohistological prognostic factors; prospective and multicentre validation warranted.
other_key_outcomes: Radiomics-only model accuracy 85%; clinical-only model accuracy 79% (RF) vs 73% (LGBM). Compared favorably to a prior SVM-based single-center study (accuracy 81%, n=80 patients/204 lesions) that did not include clinical factors.
extraction_note: The lymph-node-metastasis outcome labels appear to describe baseline/preoperative LNM status in stage I patients prior to treatment, not true disease relapse after treatment. Per appraisal_note, the pathologic gold standard for this LN-level outcome should be verified against the full PDF if used for synthesis.

title: Comprehensive analysis of RNA sequencing and integrated machine learning reveals a metabolism related prognostic signature for improving outcomes in ccRCC
study_design: Retrospective multi-cohort bioinformatic study: scRNA-seq discovery of metabolically active malignant cells and a bulk RNA-seq machine-learning prognostic signature
data_source_detail: TCGA-KIRC training n=266 and testing n=264 (1:1 split); E-MTAB-1980 n=101; Meta cohort n=146 (GSE167573 and ICGC RECA-EU). scRNA-seq from GSE152938, GSE207493, and GSE224630 (26 ccRCC samples) used for discovery only.
data_modality_detail: Bulk RNA-seq risk score from 17 differential metabolism-related genes; scRNA-seq defined the META_active malignant-cell state used to select those genes
algorithm: Random survival forest plus generalized boosted regression (GBM), the top combination by mean C-index among 118 models from 10 survival algorithms, fit with leave-one-out cross-validation in TCGA training
input_features: 17 co-expressed differential metabolism-related genes weighted by GBM relative influence
biomarker_result: Metabolism-related prognostic signature (MRPS), a 17-gene GBM risk score
performance_value: Mean C-index 0.715 for RSF+GBM MRPS across TCGA training, TCGA testing, E-MTAB-1980, and Meta; 1/3/5-year AUC 0.874/0.808/0.823 (TCGA training), 0.675/0.717/0.756 (TCGA testing), 0.690/0.715/0.701 (E-MTAB-1980), 0.613/0.672/0.705 (Meta)
validation_detail: Leave-one-out cross-validation (results also describe tenfold CV) in TCGA-KIRC training and a 1:1 internal TCGA testing split. Independent ccRCC checks on E-MTAB-1980 and the Meta cohort (GSE167573 and ICGC RECA-EU).
funding: National Natural Science Foundation of China (No. 82372200) and the Primary Health Care Foundation of China
key_finding: A 17-gene metabolism-related signature (RSF+GBM) had a mean C-index of 0.715 across ccRCC cohorts and separated overall survival, with 1-year AUC ranging from 0.613 in the Meta cohort to 0.874 in TCGA training.
limitations_as_stated: Findings are based on retrospective public sequencing data and bioinformatics; multicenter prospective studies are still required, and experimental work on the MRPS genes is limited.
other_key_outcomes: Higher META_active malignant-cell fraction was linked to worse overall survival. In 181 nivolumab-treated advanced ccRCC samples, low MRPS risk had longer survival. GGT6 knockdown increased proliferation and invasion in 769-P and 786-O cells.
extraction_note: Primary axis is the bulk MRPS. The mean C-index 0.715 averages cohort-level indices used for model selection; n_analytic is the TCGA training cohort (266) where the model was fit. ResearchSquare preprint. Cell-line assays are orthogonal and were not counted as own-cohort training data.

title: PLA2G2A+ CAFs as a Key Driver of Lymph Node Metastasis in Penile Cancer and Its Underlying Mechanisms
study_design: translational/bioinformatic with prospective clinical validation cohort
data_source_detail: scRNA-seq dataset (University Hospitals Leuven, 17 PSCC patients: 8 LNM-negative, 9 LNM-positive; 60,631 cells after QC); own prospective clinical cohort, Yunnan Cancer Hospital, China (Sept 2022-Apr 2025): bulk RNA-seq validation subset (n=4 patients) and IHC cohort (n=69 patients, 44 LN-negative/25 LN-positive)
data_modality_detail: scRNA-seq (primary ML axis, 17 patients/60,631 cells), bulk RNA-seq (independent validation, n=4 patients), immunohistochemistry (clinical correlation cohort, n=69 patients)
algorithm: LASSO, Random Forest, XGBoost (gene feature selection/classification of LNM status from scRNA-seq); CellChat (ligand-receptor communication); Monocle3 (pseudotime)
input_features: Single-cell RNA-seq gene expression features (top 20 genes per method) used to classify LNM-positive vs LNM-negative samples
biomarker_result: PLA2G2A (top-ranked across all 3 ML methods) and the PLA2G2A+ cancer-associated fibroblast (CAF) subpopulation
performance_value: scRNA-seq classification (n=17 patients): LASSO AUC=0.960, Random Forest AUC=0.931, XGBoost AUC=0.962. IHC cohort (n=69): PLA2G2A positivity not associated with OS (HR=1.21, p>0.05) but associated with worse DFS (HR=3.332, 95%CI 1.156-9.605, p=0.0259)
validation_detail: The LASSO/Random Forest/XGBoost classifiers were trained and evaluated on a single scRNA-seq dataset of only 17 patients, with no described train/test split, cross-validation scheme, or external held-out cohort - the reported AUCs (0.93-0.96) are almost certainly optimistic given this very small patient-level n. A separate bulk RNA-seq cohort (n=4) and an independent IHC cohort (n=69) provide biological/clinical correlation but not a held-out validation of the ML classifier itself.
key_finding: Convergent ML feature selection (LASSO, Random Forest, XGBoost; AUC 0.93-0.96 on scRNA-seq from 17 patients) identified PLA2G2A as a candidate biomarker for lymph node metastasis in penile squamous cell carcinoma; PLA2G2A+ CAFs recruit monocytes and drive M1-to-M2 macrophage polarization, and IHC in an independent 69-patient cohort confirmed elevated PLA2G2A in metastasis-positive tumors and association with worse disease-free survival.
limitations_as_stated: Low incidence of penile cancer with limited available sample size and homogeneous data type introduces selection bias; lack of large-scale public penile cancer cohorts with complete lymph node metastasis follow-up limited external validation; the VEGFA-VEGFR1 CAF-endothelial hypothesis was not mechanistically validated.
other_key_outcomes: No significant difference in major cell-type proportions between LNM-positive and LNM-negative samples; CSF1-CSF1R signaling identified between CAFs and myeloid cells; pseudotime trajectory analysis supported a monocyte-to-M1-to-M2 macrophage differentiation model.
extraction_note: Preprint (Research Square), not peer-reviewed. Per appraisal_note, the ML AUC values (0.93-0.96) on a 17-patient scRNA-seq cohort are likely optimistic given no described external/held-out split - coded internal_split_only rather than accepting an external validation framing.

title: Deep Learning for Subtypes Identification of Pure Seminoma of the Testis.
study_design: translational/bioinformatic
data_source_detail: TCGA-TGCT: all available H&E whole slide images for 64 pure seminoma samples (156 WSIs); 2 samples reclassified as mixed GCT on review and removed
data_modality_detail: H&E whole slide images (TCGA), tiled at 300x300 pixels / 20x magnification with 50% overlap, data-augmented
algorithm: CNN (MobileNet architecture, 85 convolutional layers, top 29 layers frozen during training, ImageNet-pretrained weights, Adam optimizer)
input_features: WSI tile-level deep image features (H&E, 300x300px tiles at 20x, augmented for class balance)
biomarker_result: Deep-learning histopathology classifier distinguishing pure seminoma subtype 1 vs subtype 2 (previously defined by omics/transcriptomic data)
performance_value: Highest AUC=0.896 (tile/sample-level ROC); accuracy and confusion matrices also reported graphically
validation_detail: 62 pure seminoma TCGA samples, tiles from a given sample restricted to a single fold; 3-fold cross-validation, 20 training epochs; no external cohort; small dataset expanded via image augmentation.
funding: National Institute of General Medical Sciences, NIH grant GM127390; Welch Foundation I-1505; National Science Foundation DBI 2224128
key_finding: A MobileNet-based CNN distinguished the authors' previously omics-defined pure seminoma subtypes from H&E whole slide images with AUC=0.896, revealing morphological differences between subtypes imperceptible to the human eye, though the authors conclude these subtypes cannot be reliably classified by histopathological features alone.
limitations_as_stated: Limited dataset size; only one CNN architecture tested; model classification accuracy was lower for subtype 2 than subtype 1 samples; authors state the model should be verified on an expanded dataset and with additional CNN architectures in future work.
other_key_outcomes: Nuclei segmentation found no significant difference in nuclei size distributions between the two subtypes, despite morphological differences detected by the DL model. Sample-level prediction table shows imperfect concordance with prior transcriptomic subtype labels.
extraction_note: n_analytic reported as 62 (64 originally assigned minus 2 reclassified as mixed GCT); exact analytic n used for training/validation vs. n shown in results table may differ slightly. Per appraisal_note, this is a borderline case of clinical vs. research prediction since the 2 subtypes are not established/routine pathology classes.

title: Applying Radiomics to Predict Pathology of Postchemotherapy Retroperitoneal Nodal Masses in Germ Cell Tumors.
study_design: Single-institution retrospective cohort with nested 10-fold cross-validation
data_source_detail: Princess Margaret Cancer Centre and University Health Network institutional testicular cancer database, Toronto; NSGCT with post-chemotherapy RPLND for residual retroperitoneal nodes >1 cm after first-line platinum chemotherapy
data_modality_detail: Contrast-enhanced CT texture features from manually contoured residual nodal volumes of interest
algorithm: Radial basis function support vector machine (LibSVM) with F-statistic feature selection and nested 10-fold cross-validation repeated over 100 outer loops
input_features: 153 CT texture features (11 first-order intensity percentiles and 142 second-order texture metrics) per residual nodal volume
biomarker_result: CT radiomics SVM classifier of fibrosis versus viable germ cell tumor or mature teratoma
performance_value: Fibrosis versus teratoma/viable GCT AUC 0.74 +/- 0.028 (accuracy 71.7 +/- 2.2%; sensitivity 56.2 +/- 15.0%; specificity 81.9 +/- 9.0%)
validation_detail: Nested 10-fold cross-validation on the same 102 regions of interest (100 outer-loop repeats). No external cohort; authors state independent validation is still required.
funding: Children's Oncology Group Adolescent and Young Adult AFLAC Grant 2015-2017; R. Leao supported by the Foundation for Science and Technology, Government of Portugal (SFRH/BD/102232/2014)
conflicts_of_interest: Disclosed compensated relationships include Jewett (family employment/stock in Impact Genetics; Pfizer and Ipsen honoraria), Chung (AbbVie honoraria and research funding; Bayer consulting), Bedard (institutional research funding from multiple companies), and Leao (Roche travel). Several coauthors report no relationship.
key_finding: A nested cross-validated CT radiomics SVM separated fibrosis from teratoma or viable germ cell tumor in post-chemotherapy retroperitoneal nodes with AUC 0.74; adding clinical variables in nodes smaller than 2 cm raised AUC to 0.80.
limitations_as_stated: Retrospective single-institution selected sample without external validation; analysis limited to retroperitoneal nodes; manual contouring is impractical outside tertiary centers; CT cannot detect microscopic viable tumor inside a fibrotic node; no central pathology review.
other_key_outcomes: Clinical variables alone AUC 0.76 (n=40 with complete clinical data). Radiomics plus clinical variables restricted to axial diameter <2 cm: accuracy 88.2 +/- 4.4% and AUC 0.80 +/- 0.05. Size-restricted radiomics-only AUCs ranged from 0.58 +/- 0.05 to 0.74 +/- 0.03.
extraction_note: Primary axis is the unrestricted radiomics classifier on 102 regions of interest (77 patients). The AUC 0.80 result is a size-restricted radiomics-plus-clinical analysis and is recorded under other_key_outcomes.

title: H&E-stained whole slide image deep learning predicts SPOP mutation state in prostate cancer
study_design: Retrospective deep-learning study of prostatectomy whole-slide images with an independent institutional test set.
data_source_detail: TCGA prostate frozen sections (177 patients after quality control, 20 SPOP-mutant) and MSK-IMPACT formalin-fixed slides (152 patients, 19 SPOP-mutant), plus 36 additional MSK-IMPACT mutant slides.
data_modality_detail: H&E whole-slide images; low- and high-magnification salient patches
algorithm: Ensembles of residual networks aggregated into a metaensemble
input_features: H&E whole-slide patches centered on cancer-rich and cytologically abnormal regions
biomarker_result: SPOP mutation state predicted from H&E histology
performance_value: Independent MSK-IMPACT AUROC 0.86 after TCGA training; TCGA held-out metaensemble AUROC 0.74 (accuracy 0.70); expanded MSK-IMPACT internal test AUROC 0.75 and reverse test on TCGA AUROC 0.64
validation_detail: TCGA-trained metaensemble tested on independent MSK-IMPACT slides (frozen versus formalin-fixed preparations), with the reverse experiment also reported. Internal estimates used ensemble trials and Monte Carlo cross-validation.
key_finding: A residual-network metaensemble distinguished SPOP-mutant from non-mutant prostate cancers on H&E slides, including an independent MSK-IMPACT AUROC of 0.86 despite frozen-versus-formalin domain shift.
limitations_as_stated: Few SPOP-mutant examples (about 20–55 positives) and different slide preparations between TCGA frozen sections and MSK-IMPACT formalin-fixed sections.
other_key_outcomes: Content-based image retrieval using ensemble SPOP probabilities grouped mutant and non-mutant patients (Kost p=0.0241 and p=0.0170).

title: Automated tumour budding quantification by machine learning augments TNM staging in muscle-invasive bladder cancer prognosis.
study_design: Retrospective single-center cohort of radical cystectomy for muscle-invasive bladder cancer.
data_source_detail: Edinburgh hospitals, 2006–2013; NHS Lothian tissue bank. 163 cystectomies screened, 100 patients in the final cohort.
data_modality_detail: Pan-cytokeratin immunofluorescence whole-slide images with Hoechst nuclear counterstain
algorithm: Inception-style semantic segmentation CNN ensembled with a fully convolutional network and visual-context random forest; survival classification and regression tree
input_features: Automated tumour-bud counts in tumour core and invasive front, entered with clinicopathologic variables
biomarker_result: Number of tumour buds in the tumour core
performance_value: HR 2.59 (log-rank p=0.0091) for tumour budding among non-metastatic stage II–III patients; TNM first split HR 5.44
validation_detail: Leave-one-out cross-validation on 100 patients. TNM was chosen first in all runs; tumour-bud count in the core was chosen for non-metastatic patients in 97 of 100 runs.
key_finding: Automated tumour-bud quantification stratified disease-specific survival in non-metastatic muscle-invasive bladder cancer (HR 2.59) after TNM separated metastatic disease.
other_key_outcomes: Core tumour-bud count was the strongest image feature for survival (HR 3.22). High budding correlated with higher TNM (p=0.00089) and pT stage (p=0.0078).

title: Pan-Renal Cell Carcinoma classification and survival prediction from histopathology images using deep learning.
study_design: Retrospective TCGA histopathology study of renal cell carcinoma subtype classification and a secondary survival model.
data_source_detail: TCGA whole-slide images: 1027 clear-cell, 303 papillary, and 254 chromophobe tumor slides, plus selected normal slides.
data_modality_detail: H&E whole-slide tiles at 20x and 40x
algorithm: ResNet-18 and ResNet-34, with DAG-SVM on CNN embeddings for three-class subtyping; LASSO-Cox for survival
input_features: 512×512 H&E tiles; for survival, tumor-shape and nuclear morphometry from high-probability regions
biomarker_result: CNN subtype classifier for clear-cell, papillary, and chromophobe renal cell carcinoma
performance_value: Three-class subtype accuracy 94.07% in the abstract; printed DAG-SVM results include patch accuracy 92.62% and slide-wise AUC 0.93. Clear-cell versus normal slide-wise AUC reached 0.99 at 40x.
validation_detail: Tumor versus normal and subtype models used a single 70/15/15 train/validation/test split of TCGA slides. The secondary clear-cell survival model used leave-one-patient-out with inner 10-fold cross-validation.
key_finding: Deep learning separated renal cell carcinoma subtypes and normal kidney on TCGA slides, with a stated three-class accuracy of 94.07% and slide-level AUCs up to 0.99 for clear-cell versus normal.
other_key_outcomes: A LASSO-Cox risk index from tumor shape and nuclear features was associated with clear-cell survival. Papillary tumors were under-represented and were the weakest subtype in the initial CNN.
extraction_note: The abstract three-class accuracy of 94.07% does not match the highest accuracy in the printed subtype table (92.62% for ResNet-18 plus DAG-SVM).

title: Radiomics and machine learning of multisequence multiparametric prostate MRI: Towards improved non-invasive prostate cancer characterization.
study_design: Retrospective single-center cohort of men imaged before robotic prostatectomy.
data_source_detail: Hospital District of Southwest Finland, 3T Philips PET/MR, March 2013–May 2014. 72 enrolled; 62 analyzed after artifact and incomplete-data exclusions.
data_modality_detail: T2-weighted imaging, high-b diffusion-weighted imaging (ADC and kurtosis), and T2 mapping
algorithm: L1- and L2-regularized logistic regression
input_features: Texture features (Gabor, GLCM, Zernike, Hu moments, local binary patterns) and first-order statistics from multiparametric MRI
biomarker_result: Multiparametric MRI texture classifier for Gleason score
performance_value: 0.84 for the best univariate texture feature (T2-weighted MBB-GLCM homogeneity); other single-feature AUCs were 0.80 (ADCm and ADCk Gabor), 0.83 (kurtosis Zernike), and 0.75 (T2 Zernike)
validation_detail: Multivariate regularized logistic models were evaluated by leave-pair-out cross-validation within each sequence and for combined sequences. No external cohort.
funding: Instrumentarium Research Foundation, Sigrid Jusélius Foundation, Turku University Hospital, TYKS-SAPA, Finnish Cancer Society, Finnish Cultural Foundation, Orion Research Foundation, and Academy of Finland clinical researcher funding.
key_finding: Texture features from T2-weighted and diffusion MRI separated prostate cancers by Gleason score, with the best single feature reaching AUC 0.84.
limitations_as_stated: Re-slicing and non-rigid deformation before co-registration with whole-mount prostatectomy remain an untested source of error.
other_key_outcomes: First-order statistical features did not outperform the best texture features. Moment-based texture was highlighted as previously unused for prostate MRI characterization.
extraction_note: The leave-pair-out logistic classifier is the stated model, while the numeric ROC results in the text are univariate feature AUCs.

title: Random forest-based modelling to detect biomarkers for prostate cancer progression.
study_design: Retrospective methylation classifier with external public-cohort validation and orthogonal immunohistochemistry.
data_source_detail: Own formalin-fixed discovery cohort (35 good-prognosis and 35 poor-prognosis tumors after quality control). External validation in ICGC early- and late-onset prostate cancer (n=222) and TCGA-PRAD (n=477).
data_modality_detail: Illumina HumanMethylation450 arrays on formalin-fixed tumor DNA
algorithm: Random forest (randomForest R package)
input_features: Differentially methylated CpG sites (402 sites; at least 10% methylation difference, FDR <0.2) after cell-composition adjustment
biomarker_result: Methylation random-forest classifier of aggressive versus indolent prostate cancer; ZIC2 protein loss as a top candidate
performance_value: Discovery test AUC 95% after an 80/20 split; external sensitivity-analysis AUCs 77.1% (ICGC, n=222) and 68.7% (TCGA-PRAD, n=477)
validation_detail: Random 80/20 split of the discovery cohort, then application to ICGC and TCGA-PRAD using the same good- versus poor-prognosis definitions. Immunohistochemistry of candidate proteins, including ZIC2, in more than 12,000 tissue-microarray cases is orthogonal and was not used to train the forest.
key_finding: A methylation random forest separated good- from poor-prognosis prostate cancer on the discovery test set (AUC 95%) and retained discrimination in ICGC (AUC 77.1%) and TCGA-PRAD (AUC 68.7%).
limitations_as_stated: The 450k array covers only preselected CpG sites, so genome-wide methylation relevant to progression may have been missed.
other_key_outcomes: Loss of ZIC2 protein was associated with shorter time to biochemical recurrence independent of Gleason grade, stage, nodal status, and PSA. Hypomethylation in poor-prognosis tumors was enriched in partially methylated domains.

title: A CT-based radiomics model to detect prostate cancer lymph node metastases in PSMA radioguided surgery patients.
journal: Eur J Nucl Med Mol Imaging
study_design: Retrospective cohort of PSMA-radioguided surgery for recurrent prostate cancer with histologic lymph-node labels.
data_source_detail: Technical University of Munich radioguided-surgery series, April 2013–September 2017. 80 patients after exclusions; training 47 patients (87 lymph nodes) with in-house PET/CT and testing 33 patients (62 lymph nodes) with outside imaging.
data_modality_detail: Contrast-enhanced diagnostic CT; labels from PSMA PET-guided histology
algorithm: LASSO radiomic models; logistic regression for conventional CT parameters
input_features: 156 CT radiomic features of texture, shape, intensity, and local binary patterns from segmented lymph nodes
biomarker_result: Combined CT radiomics model for lymph-node metastasis, dominated by local binary pattern features
performance_value: Testing AUC 0.95 for the combined radiomics model (training AUC 0.89). Local-binary-pattern model testing AUC 0.90. Short-axis diameter testing AUC 0.84.
validation_detail: Single train/test split of one radioguided-surgery series. Test scans were acquired at outside institutions, but surgery and histology remained in the same program. No cross-validation of the final AUC.
key_finding: A combined CT radiomics model detected histologically confirmed lymph-node metastases in the test set with AUC 0.95, above short-axis diameter (AUC 0.84).
limitations_as_stated: Imaging-to-pathology mismatches remain possible; few negative nodes could be segmented; very small histologic nodes were invisible on CT.
other_key_outcomes: SUVmax, used as a PET reference rather than the CT model, reached testing AUC 1.00. Decision-curve analysis showed net benefit above short-axis diameter.

title: Differentiation of low and high grade renal cell carcinoma on routine MRI with an externally validated automatic machine learning algorithm.
study_design: Retrospective multicenter cohort comparing automated and hand-tuned machine learning for Fuhrman grade.
data_source_detail: 482 RCC lesions with Fuhrman grade from the Hospital of the University of Pennsylvania, Mayo Clinic, Second Xiangya Hospital, another Chinese hospital, and TCIA. External test was 43 Mayo lesions; remaining 439 lesions were split 8:2 (351 train, 88 internal test).
data_modality_detail: Routine MRI T2-weighted and contrast-enhanced T1 radiomics (3087 IBSI features)
algorithm: TPOT automatic pipeline (exported random forest) versus a Bayesian classifier with Fischer-score feature selection; tenfold cross-validation during development
input_features: Morphology, intensity, and texture radiomics from T2 and post-contrast T1 MRI
biomarker_result: MRI radiomics classifier of low-grade (Fuhrman I–II) versus high-grade (III–IV) renal cell carcinoma
performance_value: External AUC 0.60 (95% CI 0.50–0.69) for the best TPOT pipeline (accuracy 0.81, sensitivity 0.12, specificity 0.97); Bayesian/Fischer external AUC 0.59 (95% CI 0.49–0.68)
validation_detail: Mayo Clinic lesions (n=43) were held out as a single-institution external test. Internal development used an 8:2 split and tenfold cross-validation. TCIA cases were inside the development pool, not the external test.
key_finding: Automated and hand-tuned MRI pipelines were similar on external testing, with AUCs of about 0.59–0.60 for Fuhrman grade and high specificity but low sensitivity.
limitations_as_stated: Retrospective inclusion was limited to patients who had a reported Fuhrman grade.
other_key_outcomes: Best internal-test AUCs were about 0.67–0.68. High-grade tumors were larger and more often showed vein invasion and higher T stage.

title: Integrative multi-omics analysis of muscle-invasive bladder cancer identifies prognostic biomarkers for frontline chemotherapy and immunotherapy.
study_design: Integrative multi-omics clustering of muscle-invasive bladder cancer with external gene-expression classification.
data_source_detail: TCGA MIBC with complete mutation, copy number, methylation, and RNA-seq (n=388). External gene-expression sets totaling n=844: IMvigor210 (348), E-MTAB-1803 (85), GSE48277 (57), GSE48075 (73), GSE31507 (61), GSE31684 (66), GSE32894 (93), GSE52219 (23), and GSE69795 (38).
data_modality_detail: Somatic mutations, copy number, DNA methylation, and RNA-seq, reduced to a gene-expression classifier
algorithm: iClusterBayes; k-nearest neighbor (k=5 for the 42-gene panel, chosen by cross-validation on TCGA)
input_features: 42 basal-luminal genes derived from integrative clustering, applied to external expression matrices
biomarker_result: 42-gene integrative basal versus luminal panel; low MTAP/CDKN2A/2B expression as a marker of chromosome 9p21.3 loss
performance_value: NR
validation_detail: k-nearest neighbor trained on TCGA expression and applied to nine additional expression cohorts, including chemotherapy-trial and IMvigor210 immunotherapy sets. Cross-validation on TCGA was used only to choose k.
key_finding: Integrative clustering defined basal and luminal muscle-invasive bladder cancer subtypes, and the authors link the basal subtype and 9p21.3 loss to chemotherapy and anti-PD-L1 outcomes.
other_key_outcomes: An 18-gene neuroendocrine-like panel was also classified with k-nearest neighbor (k=15). Basal tumors had worse survival without neoadjuvant chemotherapy and better survival with chemotherapy in two trials.
extraction_note: Survival and response claims are stated qualitatively, without a printed AUC, C-index, hazard ratio, or accuracy for the 42-gene classifier.

title: Machine learning-based analysis of [<sup>18</sup>F]DCFPyL PET radiomics for risk stratification in primary prostate cancer.
journal: Eur J Nucl Med Mol Imaging
study_design: Prospective single-center cohort undergoing preoperative PSMA PET before prostatectomy with extended pelvic node dissection.
data_source_detail: Amsterdam UMC prospective study NL6754; 76 consecutive intermediate- to high-risk patients, of whom 71 underwent surgery.
data_modality_detail: [18F]DCFPyL PET radiomics with and without partial-volume correction
algorithm: Random forest (1000 trees) with nested hyperparameter search; PCA or recursive feature elimination inside each fold
input_features: 480 IBSI radiomic features per tumor (intensity, morphology, texture) at 50–70% peak isocontours
biomarker_result: PSMA PET radiomics random forest for nodal and metastatic risk and high-risk pathology
performance_value: Repeated cross-validation mean AUC 0.86 ± 0.15 for lymph-node involvement; 0.86 ± 0.14 for any metastasis; 0.81 ± 0.16 for Gleason score ≥8; 0.76 ± 0.12 for extracapsular extension
validation_detail: Stratified 5-fold cross-validation repeated 50 times, with preprocessing and tuning nested in the training folds. No external cohort; the authors state multicenter external validation is still required.
key_finding: PSMA PET radiomics predicted lymph-node involvement and any metastasis with mean cross-validated AUCs of 0.86, above models using standard PET metrics.
limitations_as_stated: The cohort was small, no external validation set was available, and cross-validated radiomics versus standard PET metrics could not be compared with an adequately powered test.
other_key_outcomes: Best standard-PET-metric AUCs were 0.77 (nodal), 0.81 (any metastasis), 0.76 (Gleason), and 0.67 (extracapsular extension). Radiomics Brier scores were lower than those of standard PET metrics.

title: Value of radiomics in differential diagnosis of chromophobe renal cell carcinoma and renal oncocytoma.
study_design: Retrospective single-center differential diagnosis of chromophobe renal cell carcinoma and oncocytoma.
data_source_detail: Single hospital, pathologically confirmed cases 2008–2018: 44 chromophobe carcinomas and 17 oncocytomas. Five patients lacked excretory-phase CT.
data_modality_detail: Triphasic contrast-enhanced CT (corticomedullary, nephrographic, and excretory phases)
algorithm: LASSO feature selection; SVM best among k-nearest neighbors, SVM, logistic regression, multilayer perceptron, and random forest
input_features: 1029 radiomic features per phase (intensity, shape, texture, and filtered images); eight features from combined corticomedullary and nephrographic phases
biomarker_result: SVM CT radiomics classifier of chromophobe renal cell carcinoma versus renal oncocytoma
performance_value: SVM AUC 0.964 ± 0.054; accuracy 0.945; sensitivity 0.999; specificity 0.800. All five classifiers had AUC greater than 0.850.
validation_detail: Fivefold cross-validation on the single-center cohort. LASSO penalty was also tuned by fivefold cross-validation. No external test set.
key_finding: An SVM using enhanced-CT radiomics separated chromophobe carcinoma from oncocytoma with cross-validated AUC 0.964 and accuracy 0.945.
limitations_as_stated: Single-center design with few oncocytomas, nonuniform CT scanners and parameters, and no analysis of unenhanced images.
other_key_outcomes: Combined corticomedullary and nephrographic features were the preferred input for most classifiers. Selected features were mainly texture and first-order intensity.

title: Computed Tomography Radiomics for Predicting Pathological Grade of Renal Cell Carcinoma.
study_design: Retrospective single-center cohort of clear-cell renal cell carcinoma graded on preoperative CT.
data_source_detail: Xiangya Hospital, Central South University, nephrectomy June 2010–June 2017. 264 clear-cell carcinomas (206 low-grade, 58 high-grade), randomly split about 3:1.
data_modality_detail: Unenhanced and nephrographic-phase CT, combining semantic measurements and texture radiomics
algorithm: Machine-learning model combining traditional CT features and radiomic texture
input_features: Tumor size and pre- and post-contrast CT density plus radiomic texture features
biomarker_result: Combined CT model of low versus high WHO/ISUP grade clear-cell renal cell carcinoma
performance_value: Combined-model validation AUC 0.9099 (95% CI 0.8324–0.9873) and training AUC 0.9235 (95% CI 0.8646–0.9824). Radiomics-only validation AUC 0.8017; traditional-features validation AUC 0.8088.
validation_detail: Random 3:1 training/validation split of one hospital cohort (199 and 65 patients by the sex counts in the cohort table). No cross-validation or external cohort is described for the reported AUCs.
key_finding: A model combining conventional CT measurements and texture reached a validation AUC of 0.91 for low versus high ISUP grade.
other_key_outcomes: Low-grade tumors were smaller, had lower unenhanced density, and enhanced more than high-grade tumors.

title: Computed Tomography-Based Radiomics Model for Predicting the WHO/ISUP Grade of Clear Cell Renal Cell Carcinoma Preoperatively: A Multicenter Study.
study_design: Retrospective multicenter CT study of WHO/ISUP grade in clear-cell renal cell carcinoma.
data_source_detail: Four hospitals, January 2018–August 2019. Training: 122 patients from the First Hospital of Zhejiang Province. External validation: 75 patients from Ningbo First Hospital, Zhejiang Cancer Hospital, and Yijishan Hospital.
data_modality_detail: Corticomedullary- and nephrographic-phase contrast CT; IBEX features with ComBat harmonization
algorithm: Stepwise logistic regression with Akaike information criterion after Mann–Whitney filtering and mRMR
input_features: Whole-tumor CT radiomics (760 features per phase); final model used corticomedullary and nephrographic texture and intensity features
biomarker_result: CT radiomics logistic model of low versus high WHO/ISUP grade
performance_value: External validation AUC 0.81 (sensitivity 0.58, specificity 0.95); training AUC 0.89 (sensitivity 0.85, specificity 0.84)
validation_detail: Model fit on one hospital and tested on patients from three other hospitals. No cross-validation of the final AUC is described.
key_finding: A CT radiomics logistic model predicted WHO/ISUP grade with external AUC 0.81, sensitivity 0.58, and specificity 0.95.
limitations_as_stated: External AUC and sensitivity fell relative to training, which the authors attribute to differences among the three validation hospitals and unequal low- versus high-grade mix.
other_key_outcomes: Decision curves were presented for training and external sets. The results text retains six features, whereas the abstract says seven.
extraction_note: Abstract reports seven radiomic features and the results text retains six; both sections report the same training and external AUCs.

title: MRI-Based Grading of Clear Cell Renal Cell Carcinoma Using a Machine Learning Classifier.
study_design: Retrospective single-center MRI texture study of clear-cell renal cell carcinoma grade.
data_source_detail: First Affiliated Hospital of Fujian Medical University, July 2016–January 2020. 99 patients (61 low-grade, 38 high-grade), randomly split into 70 training and 29 validation.
data_modality_detail: Corticomedullary-phase MRI texture from the largest axial tumor section (MaZda)
algorithm: Random-forest feature ranking and a multilayer perceptron (one hidden layer, 229 nodes)
input_features: Six reproducible texture features: Kurtosis, 135dr_RLNonUni, Horzl_GLevNonU, 135dr_GLevNonU, S(4,4)Entropy, and S(0,5)SumEntrp
biomarker_result: MRI texture multilayer perceptron for low versus high ISUP grade
performance_value: Validation AUC 0.758 and accuracy 86.2%; training AUC 0.997 and accuracy 95.7%
validation_detail: Single random training/validation split. Random-forest hyperparameters used grid search. The perceptron hidden-node count was iterated to optimize accuracy on the validation set, so that set was not untouched.
key_finding: A six-feature MRI texture network separated low- from high-grade clear-cell carcinoma with validation AUC 0.758 and accuracy 86.2%, after near-perfect training fit.
limitations_as_stated: Manual segmentation can vary between observers. Tumor size is embedded in a selected run-length feature, and clinical factors beyond radiomics were not modeled.
other_key_outcomes: 257 MaZda features were extracted; only features with ICC at least 0.80 were retained. High-grade tumors were larger (6.1 vs 4.0 cm).
extraction_note: Hidden-layer size was chosen to maximize validation-set accuracy, so the reported validation AUC is not an independent holdout estimate.

title: MRI-based radiomics models to assess prostate cancer, extracapsular extension and positive surgical margins.
study_design: Retrospective single-center mpMRI study before prostate biopsy, with prostatectomy labels for extension and margins.
data_source_detail: First Affiliated Hospital of Soochow University. 459 patients after screening (186 benign, 273 malignant). Malignant cases (n=273) were used for extracapsular extension and positive-margin models.
data_modality_detail: T2-weighted and ADC radiomics from 3T mpMRI (Pyradiomics)
algorithm: mRMR selection of the top 10 features and a LASSO classifier; integrated models added clinical variables
input_features: 851 radiomic features per sequence (shape, first-order, texture, wavelet) plus age, PSA, and biopsy variables in integrated models
biomarker_result: ADC-based integrated radiomics model for benign versus malignant prostate lesions
performance_value: Testing-set integrated AUC 0.912 (ADC), 0.905 (ADC+T2WI), and 0.851 (T2WI) for benign versus malignant lesions; radiomics-only ADC AUC 0.863
validation_detail: Stratified 7:3 split (323 train, 136 test) for lesion discrimination. Extension and margin models used 192 train and 81 test among malignant cases. No cross-validation or external center.
key_finding: An ADC radiomics model plus clinical factors discriminated benign from malignant prostate lesions on the test set with AUC 0.912.
limitations_as_stated: Single-center retrospective analysis; pathology came from reports rather than re-reviewed slices, so ROI-to-histology matching is uncertain; DCE-MRI was not included.
other_key_outcomes: Extracapsular-extension integrated AUC 0.728 (best radiomics AUC 0.625 on ADC). Positive-margin integrated AUCs 0.680 (T2WI) and 0.766 (ADC); radiomics-only AUCs were 0.614 and 0.733.

title: MRI-derived radiomics model for baseline prediction of prostate cancer progression on active surveillance.
study_design: Retrospective case-control study within an active-surveillance service evaluation.
data_source_detail: Addenbrooke’s Hospital, Cambridge, May 2013–April 2020. 71 patients and 73 MR-visible lesions (35 progressed, 38 stable), minimum two-year follow-up on one 3T scanner.
data_modality_detail: Baseline T2-weighted and ADC radiomics (PyRadiomics), 128-bin quantization
algorithm: Multiple feature-selection and classifier combinations, including GLMnet penalized regression
input_features: Robust T2-weighted radiomic features plus PSA, gland volume, PSA density, Likert score, zone, and biopsy grade group
biomarker_result: Clinical plus T2-weighted radiomics model for progression on active surveillance
performance_value: 0.75 (95% CI 0.64–0.86) after adding T2-weighted radiomics to clinical variables, versus 0.61 (95% CI 0.481–0.743) for clinical variables alone
validation_detail: Leave-one-out cross-validation. No external cohort; authors describe the work as proof of concept for later multicenter validation.
key_finding: Adding T2-weighted radiomics to clinical variables raised leave-one-out AUC for active-surveillance progression from 0.61 to 0.75.
other_key_outcomes: Progression was histopathological on repeat biopsy (25 lesions) or PRECISE 5 radiologic progression (10). PSA and PSA density were higher in progressors. ADC-only and combined T2/ADC models were also compared.

title: Machine learning-based CT radiomics approach for predicting WHO/ISUP nuclear grade of clear cell renal cell carcinoma: an exploratory and comparative study.
study_design: Retrospective single-center CT study of WHO/ISUP grade in clear-cell renal cell carcinoma.
data_source_detail: First Affiliated Hospital of Chongqing Medical University, nephrectomy January 2013–October 2020. 406 patients (330 low-grade, 76 high-grade) split into training, validation, and testing cohorts.
data_modality_detail: Nephrographic-phase CT radiomics (PyRadiomics) plus clinicoradiologic variables
algorithm: SVM with ReliefF, compared with SVM-LASSO and SVM-RFE; SMOTE for high-grade oversampling
input_features: Nephrographic-phase radiomic features and clinicoradiologic characteristics such as size, necrosis, calcification, and invasion
biomarker_result: Combined clinicoradiologic and radiomics SVM for low versus high WHO/ISUP grade
performance_value: Combined-model AUC 0.828 (95% CI 0.731–0.929) in the testing cohort, 0.859 (95% CI 0.748–0.935) in validation, and 0.887 (95% CI 0.798–0.952) in training
validation_detail: Single-institution split into training, validation, and testing cohorts. SVM-ReliefF outperformed SVM-LASSO and SVM-RFE. No external hospital.
key_finding: A combined CT radiomics and clinicoradiologic SVM predicted WHO/ISUP grade with testing AUC 0.828, above radiomics-only and clinicoradiologic models.
limitations_as_stated: Single-institution retrospective design with possible selection bias despite 406 patients.
other_key_outcomes: High-grade tumors were larger and more often showed necrosis, calcification, capsule violation, angiogenesis, venous invasion, and perinephric metastasis.

title: Magnetic resonance imaging-based radiomics signature for preoperative prediction of Ki67 expression in bladder cancer.
study_design: Retrospective single-center MRI study of preoperative Ki67 status in bladder cancer.
data_source_detail: Shanghai Tenth People’s Hospital, Tongji University, August 2014–April 2020. 179 patients (120 non-muscle-invasive, 59 muscle-invasive; 41 low Ki67, 138 high Ki67), split 7:3 into 125 training and 54 validation.
data_modality_detail: T2-weighted and delayed-phase dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI radiomics (PyRadiomics)
algorithm: SMOTE-LASSO (best); also LASSO, SVM, and SMOTE-SVM, with mRMR prefiltering
input_features: Nine radiomic features from 2436 T2-weighted and DCE features after SMOTE balancing of the training set
biomarker_result: SMOTE-LASSO MRI radiomics signature of high versus low Ki67
performance_value: Validation AUC 0.819 (accuracy 81.5%); SMOTE-training AUC 0.859 (accuracy 80.3%)
validation_detail: Random 7:3 training/validation split. SMOTE was applied only to the training set (99 high and 99 balanced low cases). No external center.
key_finding: A nine-feature SMOTE-LASSO MRI signature predicted Ki67 status with validation AUC 0.819 and accuracy 81.5%, and predicted high Ki67 tracked with worse disease-free survival.
limitations_as_stated: Retrospective design and a single center, so generalizability needs a multicenter study.
other_key_outcomes: Immunohistochemical and radiomics-predicted high Ki67 were both associated with worse disease-free survival in training and validation (all p<0.05). Unbalanced LASSO had high sensitivity and low specificity.

title: Robust Prognostic Subtyping of Muscle-Invasive Bladder Cancer Revealed by Deep Learning-Based Multi-Omics Data Integration.
study_design: Deep-learning multi-omics subtyping of muscle-invasive bladder cancer with public external expression cohorts and orthogonal immunohistochemistry.
data_source_detail: TCGA-BLCA stage II–IV multi-omics from UCSC Xena (copy number, mRNA, miRNA, methylation), randomly split 4:1 for the classifier. External microarray sets GSE19915 (43), GSE48277-GPL14951 (62), and GSE48277-GPL6947 (73).
data_modality_detail: Copy number, RNA-seq, miRNA-seq, and HumanMethylation450 stacked into 350,631 features
algorithm: Keras autoencoder (hidden layers 500-100-500) followed by univariate Cox filtering and K-means (k=2)
input_features: 100 autoencoder bottleneck features, of which 98 were associated with overall survival
biomarker_result: Two deep-learning multi-omics prognostic subtypes; KRT7 as an immunohistochemistry risk marker
performance_value: Log-rank P = 8.11e-5 for overall survival between the two TCGA subtypes; internal and external validation sets also separated survival (P < 0.05)
validation_detail: Subtype discovery used the TCGA muscle-invasive cohort. A classifier was trained on an 80% TCGA split and checked on the remaining 20% and on three GEO microarray cohorts. KRT7 immunohistochemistry on 22 Sun Yat-sen cases is orthogonal and was not part of model training.
key_finding: An autoencoder split muscle-invasive bladder cancer into two subtypes with different overall survival (log-rank P = 8.11e-5), and the poor-prognosis group had more chromosome 3p deletion.
other_key_outcomes: The poor-prognosis subtype was entirely high grade and differed in immune composition (M1 macrophages, resting NK cells, regulatory T cells, plasma cells, and naive B cells). KRT7 immunohistochemistry was explored as a tissue biomarker.
extraction_note: Survival separation is given as a log-rank P value. The TCGA muscle-invasive sample size and a hazard ratio or C-index are not stated.

title: A CT-based radiomics model for predicting renal capsule invasion in renal cell carcinoma.
study_design: Retrospective single-center CT study of renal capsule invasion.
data_source_detail: Chongqing University Cancer Hospital, January 2011–May 2019. 126 RCC patients (46 with capsule invasion, 80 without).
data_modality_detail: Unenhanced, corticomedullary, and nephrographic CT; 119 Pyradiomics features from the largest tumor section and a 3 mm margin
algorithm: Forward neural network, best of five machine-learning classifiers
input_features: Morphologic and texture radiomics from the tumor region, the peritumoral margin, or both, by CT phase
biomarker_result: Corticomedullary-phase tumor radiomics model of renal capsule invasion
performance_value: AUC 0.81 for the forward neural network on corticomedullary-phase tumor features; robustness means 0.76, 0.79, and 0.77 for unenhanced, corticomedullary, and nephrographic phases
validation_detail: Five-fold cross-validation, repeated 100 times for the robustness analysis. No external cohort.
funding: China National Cancer Center Climbing Fund (NCC201822872), Chongqing University Cancer Hospital open research fund (2020), and Chongqing Natural Science Foundation (cstc2021jcyj-msxmX0447).
key_finding: Corticomedullary-phase tumor radiomics with a forward neural network predicted renal capsule invasion with cross-validated AUC 0.81.
limitations_as_stated: Small single-center retrospective sample, two-dimensional rather than three-dimensional features, manual segmentation, and possible selection bias.
other_key_outcomes: Marginal-region AUC was 0.80 on unenhanced CT and 0.73 on the corticomedullary phase. Combining phases generally lowered performance versus the best single phase.

title: An Ultrasonic-Based Radiomics Nomogram for Distinguishing Between Benign and Malignant Solid Renal Masses.
study_design: Retrospective single-center ultrasound study of solid renal masses.
data_source_detail: Tianjin Medical University Cancer Institute and Hospital, surgically confirmed masses January 2013–January 2018. 597 patients with 600 masses (204 benign, 396 malignant) after down-sampling malignant cases; random split 480 train and 120 validation.
data_modality_detail: Preoperative ultrasound radiomics
algorithm: LASSO radiomics score (10-fold cross-validation for lambda) and a logistic nomogram with sex
input_features: 855 ultrasound radiomic features reduced to 30 with nonzero LASSO coefficients, plus sex
biomarker_result: Ultrasound RadScore and a sex-plus-RadScore nomogram for benign versus malignant solid renal masses
