performance_value: Validation radiomics-signature AUC 0.874 (95% CI 0.816–0.932); validation nomogram AUC 0.861 (95% CI 0.802–0.921); nomogram specificity 0.93 versus 0.57 and 0.46 for senior and junior readers
validation_detail: Random training/validation split of one institution. Ten-fold cross-validation was used to tune the LASSO penalty, not as the reported performance design. Authors state external and multicenter validation is still required.
funding: Scientific research program of the Tianjin Education Commission (2020KJ131).
key_finding: An ultrasound radiomics score separated benign from malignant solid renal masses with validation AUC 0.874, and the sex-plus-score nomogram had validation AUC 0.861 and specificity 0.93.
limitations_as_stated: Retrospective single-institute random split, images from two ultrasound machines, and manual regions of interest.
other_key_outcomes: Sex and RadScore were independent predictors. The nomogram beat a junior reader on DeLong testing (p=0.004). Decision-curve analysis was used for clinical usefulness.

title: Application Value of Radiomic Nomogram in the Differential Diagnosis of Prostate Cancer and Hyperplasia.
study_design: Retrospective single-center MRI study differentiating prostate cancer from hyperplasia.
data_source_detail: Jiangxi Provincial People’s Hospital, 3T Siemens MRI, September 2019–September 2020. 146 patients (66 cancer, 80 hyperplasia) split 103 training and 43 testing.
data_modality_detail: T2-weighted MRI texture (396 features, GE Analysis Kit)
algorithm: mRMR and LASSO (tenfold cross-validation for the penalty) with a multivariate logistic nomogram
input_features: T2-weighted histogram, morphology, Haralick, GLCM, run-length, and gray-level zone features plus PSA
biomarker_result: T2-weighted radiomic nomogram combining Radscore and PSA
performance_value: Testing nomogram AUC 0.90 (95% CI 0.81–0.99; accuracy 0.860, sensitivity 0.933, specificity 0.821); testing radiomics-only AUC 0.84 (95% CI 0.72–0.96); training nomogram AUC 0.91
validation_detail: Single 7:3 train/test split. Tenfold cross-validation was used only to choose the LASSO penalty. No external cohort.
key_finding: A T2-weighted radiomic nomogram that included PSA distinguished prostate cancer from hyperplasia with testing AUC 0.90.
other_key_outcomes: Clinical-only testing AUC was 0.74 (accuracy 0.721). PSA and the radiomic signature were independent predictors; age was not.

title: Evaluation of the Efficiency of MRI-Based Radiomics Classifiers in the Diagnosis of Prostate Lesions.
study_design: Retrospective single-center comparison of MRI radiomics classifiers for prostate cancer.
data_source_detail: First Affiliated Hospital of Nanchang University, September 2019–July 2021. 238 patients with pathology (114 cancer, 124 benign), randomly split 6:4 into 142 training and 96 test patients. Lesion-level set: 151 positive and 139 negative lesions.
data_modality_detail: 1.5T biparametric MRI radiomics from ADC, DWI, and fat-saturated T2-weighted images (PyRadiomics)
algorithm: LASSO with fivefold cross-validation for feature selection; decision tree, Gaussian naive Bayes, logistic regression, XGBoost, random forest, and support-vector classifier
input_features: Up to 321 radiomic features per sequence (first-order, shape, GLCM, GLRLM, GLSZM, NGTDM, GLDM)
biomarker_result: Combined-sequence radiomics classifiers for prostate cancer versus benign tissue
performance_value: Patient-level combined-sequence logistic regression AUC 0.865, random forest 0.862, and decision tree 0.852; lesion-level random forest AUC 0.931, with logistic regression and Gaussian naive Bayes 0.922
validation_detail: Single 6:4 train/test split. Fivefold cross-validation was used inside LASSO feature selection. No external institution.
key_finding: On the patient-level test comparison, combined-sequence logistic regression reached AUC 0.865, while lesion-level random forest reached AUC 0.931.
limitations_as_stated: Single-institution retrospective design, and peripheral versus transition zone were not modeled separately.
other_key_outcomes: Random forest was described as the best overall classifier. XGBoost and logistic regression also performed well on the lesion-based set. Patient-level combined random-forest Brier score was 0.105.

title: Feasibility Study on Predicting Recurrence Risk of Bladder Cancer Based on Radiomics Features of Multiphase CT Images.
study_design: Retrospective single-center cohort predicting bladder-cancer recurrence within two years after surgery.
data_source_detail: First Affiliated Hospital of Soochow University, January 2016–December 2019, follow-up through 31 December 2021. 183 patients (76 recurrences), randomly split 128 training and 55 validation.
data_modality_detail: Multiphase CT urography radiomics (plain, corticomedullary, and nephrographic; PyRadiomics)
algorithm: Logistic regression radiomics models; Cox models to select clinical covariates for the radiomics-clinical model
input_features: CT radiomic features reduced to 14 in the three-phase model, plus tumor number and grade
biomarker_result: Radiomics-clinical model of two-year recurrence using tumor number, grade, and Rad-score
performance_value: Validation AUC 0.838 (95% CI 0.733–0.943; accuracy 0.727, sensitivity 0.739, specificity 0.719); training AUC 0.813 (95% CI 0.740–0.886); validation radiomics-clinical C-index 0.750 (95% CI 0.704–0.795)
validation_detail: Random 7:3 split of one hospital cohort. Phase-specific logistic models were compared before the combined clinical model. No external cohort.
key_finding: A CT radiomics score plus tumor number and grade predicted two-year bladder-cancer recurrence with validation AUC 0.838.
limitations_as_stated: Retrospective single-institution cohort with a relatively small sample.
other_key_outcomes: Median relapse-free survival was 10.5 months among patients who recurred. A printed C-index table also lists validation radiomics-only C-index 0.670 and training radiomics-clinical C-index 0.751.

title: Multiparametric MRI and Machine Learning Based Radiomic Models for Preoperative Prediction of Multiple Biological Characteristics in Prostate Cancer.
study_design: Retrospective single-center mpMRI study of several pathologic features after prostatectomy.
data_source_detail: Shanghai General Hospital, radical prostatectomy May 2013–January 2020. 252 patients. Each endpoint was split 4:1; validation counts were 28 (Ki67), 32 (S100), 47 (extracapsular extension), 45 (perineural invasion), and 50 (surgical margin).
data_modality_detail: T2-weighted, DWI, and arterial-phase DCE radiomics (5343 features) plus clinical laboratory variables
algorithm: mRMR and random-forest recursive feature elimination; random forest best for four endpoints and SVM for surgical margin, among six classifiers
input_features: Multiparametric MRI radiomics, with DCE features ranked most important, plus clinical variables in combined models
biomarker_result: mpMRI random-forest models for Ki67, S100, extracapsular extension, and perineural invasion
performance_value: Random forest AUC 0.87 (Ki67), 0.80 (S100), 0.85 (extracapsular extension), and 0.82 (perineural invasion); SVM AUC 0.77 for surgical margin
validation_detail: Each endpoint used a 4:1 training/validation split of the same hospital series. Combined clinical models did not significantly outperform MRI-only models on the validation cohorts by DeLong tests. No external center.
funding: National Natural Science Foundation of China (81871400), Shanghai Science and Technology Committee (19411951403), and Key Project of the Shanghai Education Commission (202101070002E00085).
key_finding: Random-forest mpMRI models reported AUCs of 0.80–0.87 for Ki67, S100, extracapsular extension, and perineural invasion, and an SVM reached AUC 0.77 for surgical margin.
limitations_as_stated: Retrospective single-center study with selection bias, no external verification, and some biomarkers omitted because of incomplete data.
other_key_outcomes: Adding clinical variables did not significantly change validation AUCs. DCE features outranked DWI and then T2 in the combined models.
extraction_note: The printed AUCs are not labeled as training or validation estimates, and each endpoint uses a different sample size.

title: Predictive radiomics signature for treatment response to nivolumab in patients with advanced renal cell carcinoma.
study_design: Retrospective single-institution study of nivolumab-treated metastatic renal cell carcinoma.
data_source_detail: Single institution, 2013–2017. 37 patients identified; 27 analyzed (19 responders, 8 non-responders) with 104 contoured lesions.
data_modality_detail: Contrast-enhanced CT texture of baseline and first post-treatment lesions
algorithm: Radial-basis-function support vector machine (LibSVM) with nested feature ranking
input_features: 191 first-order, Haralick, neighborhood, run-length, size-zone, two-point correlation, cluster, and minimum-spanning-tree texture features
biomarker_result: CT radiomic SVM for nivolumab response by RECIST
performance_value: Baseline CT accuracy 69% (sensitivity 97%, specificity 1%; AUC 0.51, p=0.40); first post-treatment CT accuracy 66% (sensitivity 90%, specificity 8%; AUC 0.46, p=0.30)
validation_detail: Ten-fold nested cross-validation on 104 lesions from 27 patients. No external cohort.
conflicts_of_interest: Several authors report industry research funding, consulting, honoraria, or trial participation, including AbbVie, Bristol-Myers Squibb, and other pharmaceutical companies.
key_finding: CT radiomic classifiers did not meaningfully separate nivolumab responders from non-responders: accuracy was 69% and 66%, but AUCs were 0.51 and 0.46 with specificity near zero.
limitations_as_stated: The authors conclude the radiomic signature had limited discriminative ability, and they note that textures sensitive to acquisition and reconstruction are poorly suited to this use.
other_key_outcomes: Lesions were lymph nodes (60%), lung metastases (23%), and renal or adrenal metastases (17%). Median PFS was 14 months in responders versus 3.7 months in non-responders.
extraction_note: Headline accuracy is high because sensitivity is high and specificity is about 1–8%, while AUC is consistent with chance.

title: Prostate cancer therapy personalization via multi-modal deep learning on randomized phase III clinical trials.
study_design: Pooled analysis of five randomized phase III radiotherapy trials with a patient-level internal holdout.
data_source_detail: NRG/RTOG 9202, 9408, 9413, 9910, and 0126. Histopathology available for 5654 of 7764 randomized patients (16,204 slides); median follow-up 11.4 years. Patients split 80/20 with no patient overlap.
data_modality_detail: 20x H&E biopsy whole-slide images plus six clinical variables (Gleason scores, T stage, baseline PSA, age)
algorithm: MoCo-v2 self-supervised ResNet-50 patch embeddings fused with clinical variables by CatBoost; ResNet-18 tissue-versus-artifact filter
input_features: 256×256 histopathology patches pooled to a 128-dimensional patient embedding, concatenated with clinical variables
biomarker_result: Multimodal AI risk scores for distant metastasis, biochemical failure, prostate-cancer-specific survival, and overall survival
performance_value: 9.2–14.6% relative improvement in time-dependent AUC versus NCCN risk groups on the held-out validation set, across six endpoints
validation_detail: One 80/20 split pooled across five multicenter trials rather than a trial held out as an external cohort. The test set was selected so that NCCN 5-year distant-metastasis AUC fell between 0.70 and 0.75.
key_finding: A multimodal clinical-and-histopathology model improved time-dependent discrimination by 9.2–14.6% relative to NCCN risk groups for long-term metastasis, biochemical failure, and survival endpoints.
other_key_outcomes: Endpoints were 5- and 10-year distant metastasis, 5- and 10-year biochemical failure, 10-year prostate-cancer-specific survival, and 10-year overall survival. The tissue filter reached 97.6% validation accuracy on annotated patches.
extraction_note: Only the relative AUC improvement versus NCCN is printed. The holdout was constrained so the NCCN 5-year distant-metastasis AUC lay between 0.70 and 0.75.

title: A multi-model based on radiogenomics and deep learning techniques associated with histological grade and survival in clear cell renal cell carcinoma.
study_design: Retrospective public imaging-genomics cohort of clear cell renal cell carcinoma.
data_source_detail: TCGA-KIRC imaging and clinical data from TCIA; 237 patients were retrieved and 177 were included (142 training, 35 testing).
data_modality_detail: Nephrographic-phase CT radiomics, deep-learning image features, and RNA-seq.
algorithm: LASSO, with tenfold cross-validation used to build the radiomics, deep-learning, and transcriptomic models.
input_features: CT radiomic features, deep-learning features, and transcriptomic features.
biomarker_result: Multi-model combining radiomics, deep learning, and transcriptomics for ccRCC grade.
validation_detail: Models were built with tenfold cross-validation and then scored on an 8:2 split of the same TCGA-KIRC/TCIA cohort (142/35). There is no separate external cohort.
key_finding: The combined radiomics, deep-learning, and transcriptomic model separated high- from low-grade ccRCC with a testing AUC of 0.864.
limitations_as_stated: The sample was small and the design retrospective; the authors call for prospective multicenter validation.
other_key_outcomes: Testing AUCs were 0.820 for radiomics and 0.840 for deep learning. PFS and OS separation was reported as statistically significant, and high-grade tumors had higher immune-cell abundance.

title: Comparison and analysis of multiple machine learning models for discriminating benign and malignant testicular lesions based on magnetic resonance imaging radiomics.
study_design: Retrospective single-center MRI radiomics cohort of testicular lesions.
data_source_detail: 108 patients with 115 testicular lesions (44 benign, 71 malignant) imaged from February 2014 to July 2022; 394 patients were screened.
data_modality_detail: T2-weighted MRI radiomics extracted with PyRadiomics.
algorithm: XGBoost, chosen among classifiers that included linear discrimination, gradient boosting, and decision trees.
input_features: The 10 most reproducible T2-weighted radiomic features per lesion.
biomarker_result: T2-weighted MRI radiomics classifier of benign versus malignant testicular lesions.
performance_value: Testing-set AUC 0.905 (95% CI 0.886-0.925) on the held-out 30% of 115 lesions; other models AUC 0.697-0.898.
validation_detail: One 70/30 lesion split. Ten random seeds were used to rank algorithms on the training portion. There was no k-fold cross-validation and no external cohort.
funding: National Natural Science Foundation of China (81801668, 62072349, and 82001787).
key_finding: XGBoost on T2-weighted radiomics separated benign from malignant testicular lesions with a testing AUC of 0.905.
limitations_as_stated: Single-center data and a small sample, reflecting the low incidence of testicular cancer.
other_key_outcomes: The analytic unit is the lesion (115 lesions in 108 patients).

title: Deep learning and radiomic feature-based blending ensemble classifier for malignancy risk prediction in cystic renal lesions.
study_design: Retrospective two-hospital CT cohort of cystic renal lesions.
data_source_detail: Development cohort of 159 participants (103 benign, 56 malignant) and a testing cohort of 63 (53 benign, 10 malignant) at the First and Second Affiliated Hospitals of Chongqing Medical University.
data_modality_detail: Arterial-phase CT handcrafted radiomics (PyRadiomics) and pretrained 3D-ResNet50 features.
algorithm: Blending ensemble classifier; tenfold cross-validated LASSO for feature selection; pretrained 3D-ResNet50.
input_features: Handcrafted radiomic features fused with 2048 deep features from a 3D crop of each lesion.
biomarker_result: Fusion-feature blending ensemble for malignant versus benign cystic renal lesions.
performance_value: External-validation AUC 0.934 and accuracy 0.905, compared with Bosniak 2019 accuracy 0.635.
validation_detail: The testing cohort came from a second hospital and scanner. Tenfold CV-LASSO was used for feature selection in the development cohort.
funding: National Key Research and Development Project, No. 2020YFC2005900.
key_finding: A fusion radiomics and 3D-ResNet ensemble distinguished malignant from benign cystic renal lesions with external AUC 0.934 and higher net benefit than Bosniak 2019.
other_key_outcomes: IBSI guidance was applied during feature design. Histopathology was the reference standard.
extraction_note: Reporting guideline is coded other because the authors applied IBSI standards rather than TRIPOD, CLAIM, or STARD.

title: Interpretability of radiomics models is improved when using feature group selection strategies for predicting molecular and clinical targets in clear-cell renal cell carcinoma: insights from the TRACERx Renal study.
study_design: Prospective radiomics analysis of the TRACERx Renal cohort.
data_source_detail: First 101 patients in TRACERx Renal (NCT03226886); 91 lesions were analyzed on nephrographic contrast-enhanced CT from several scanner vendors.
data_modality_detail: Contrast-enhanced CT radiomics from the whole tumor and from core, rim, high-enhancing, and low-enhancing subregions.
algorithm: Conventional and proposed feature-group radiomics pipelines, both evaluated with nested cross-validation.
input_features: Radiomic features from whole-tumor masks and automatic sub-segmentations.
biomarker_result: CT radiomics classifiers of molecular, histopathologic, and clinical targets in ccRCC.
performance_value: Nested-CV AUROC > 0.8 for overall histological stage, linear evolutionary subtype, and loss of 9p21.3; the two pipelines stayed within 0.05 AUROC for most significant targets.
validation_detail: Nested cross-validation with permutation testing on TRACERx Renal only. Performance was significant for 11 of 20 targets against a null AUROC of 0.5.
key_finding: CT radiomics predicted several TRACERx Renal targets, with AUROC above 0.8 for stage, linear evolutionary subtype, and 9p21.3 loss, and a sparser feature-group pipeline kept that performance.
limitations_as_stated: The sample size was small, which motivated the proposed feature-selection approach.
other_key_outcomes: Twenty binary targets were modeled, including necrosis, sarcomatoid change, vascular invasion, stage, evolutionary subtype, and somatic events such as BAP1 and PBRM1.
extraction_note: Only a lower bound (AUROC > 0.8) is printed for three of twenty targets, so a single point estimate for the anchor target remains ambiguous.

title: Magnetic resonance imaging radiomics-based prediction of clinically significant prostate cancer in equivocal PI-RADS 3 lesions in the transitional zone.
study_design: Retrospective bi-institutional MRI cohort with a pooled random split.
data_source_detail: 243 men with transitional-zone PI-RADS 3 lesions at the First Affiliated Hospital of Fujian Medical University and Fuqing Hospital, randomly split into 170 training and 73 testing patients. Thirty had csPCa.
data_modality_detail: T2-weighted and DWI/ADC radiomics plus mean ADC and PSAD.
algorithm: XGBoost and logistic regression, with LASSO radiomic signatures and ten-fold cross-validation for XGBoost tuning.
input_features: Seven T2WI/ADC radiomic features, PSAD, and mean ADC.
biomarker_result: XGBoost model for clinically significant prostate cancer in transitional-zone PI-RADS 3 lesions.
performance_value: XGBoost testing AUC 0.913 (training 0.949); PSAD plus mean ADC testing AUC 0.854 (training 0.888).
validation_detail: Ten-fold cross-validation was used to tune XGBoost, and discrimination was also reported on a random 73-patient test set. The two hospitals were pooled before the split, so the test set is not an external center.
funding: Fuzhou Health System Science and Technology Plan Project (2022-S-wq-17) and the Startup Fund for scientific research of Fujian Medical University (2019QH1097).
key_finding: XGBoost reached a testing AUC of 0.913 for csPCa in transitional-zone PI-RADS 3 lesions; the difference from PSAD plus mean ADC (AUC 0.854) was not significant.
limitations_as_stated: Retrospective biopsy reference without prostatectomy specimens, a small imbalanced PI-RADS 3 sample, and ambiguous lesion identification.
other_key_outcomes: PSAD was the only significant clinical factor (OR 1.068). csPCa prevalence was 30 of 243 men (12.3%).

title: Predicting prostate cancer in men with PSA levels of 4-10 ng/mL: MRI-based radiomics can help junior radiologists improve the diagnostic performance.
study_design: Retrospective single-center MRI cohort with a temporal split.
data_source_detail: 171 men with PSA 4-10 ng/mL at one institution (66 PCa, 105 non-PCa), split by MRI date 7:3 into 119 training and 52 testing patients (January 2019 to June 2021).
data_modality_detail: Radiomics from T2-weighted, diffusion-weighted, and ADC images, compared with PI-RADS v2.1.
algorithm: Multivariate logistic regression.
input_features: Quantitative radiomic features from T2WI, DWI, and ADC.
biomarker_result: MRI radiomics model for prostate cancer when PSA is 4-10 ng/mL.
performance_value: Testing AUC 0.922 versus junior PI-RADS AUC 0.797; training AUC 0.932 versus 0.803; entire-cohort AUC 0.927 versus 0.801.
validation_detail: Single temporal 7:3 split at one institution. No cross-validation or external site is described.
key_finding: The radiomics model outperformed a junior reader using PI-RADS v2.1 for gray-zone PSA, with testing AUC 0.922 versus 0.797.
other_key_outcomes: Among junior-reader PI-RADS 3 lesions, radiomics AUC was 0.854 (sensitivity 84.62%, specificity 84.34%); for PI-RADS 4-5, AUC was 0.967 (sensitivity 98.11%, specificity 86.36%).

title: Prediction of prostate tumour hypoxia using pre-treatment MRI-derived radiomics: preliminary findings.
study_design: Retrospective two-centre pre-radiotherapy cohort.
data_source_detail: 195 men with high-risk prostate cancer treated with radiotherapy at two UK centres (100 and 95); 97 had hypoxic tumors by the Ragnum 32-gene biopsy signature. The cohort was split 156/39.
data_modality_detail: Whole-prostate T2-weighted MRI radiomics (PyRadiomics) after histogram standardisation.
algorithm: Ridge regression, selected among six classifiers and five feature-selection methods.
input_features: Five T2-weighted texture and wavelet radiomic features from the whole prostate.
biomarker_result: MRI radiomics model of biopsy Ragnum hypoxia status.
performance_value: Unseen test AUC 0.69 (95% CI 0.14); mean cross-validation AUC 0.71; clinical-only test AUC 0.57.
validation_detail: Fivefold cross-validation with 20 repeats selected the model, which was then scored on one 80:20 test split of the pooled two-centre cohort. Centres were not held out from each other.
key_finding: A ridge radiomics model predicted pre-radiotherapy tumor hypoxia with test AUC 0.69, above a clinical-only test AUC of 0.57.
limitations_as_stated: Imaging and transcriptomics spanned years of changing 1.5 T protocols, and only T2-weighted whole-prostate segmentations were usable.
other_key_outcomes: On the test set, accuracy was 0.72 and sensitivity was 0.74. The clinical use is radiotherapy individualisation through hypoxia status. The DeLong comparison with the clinical model had p=0.35.

title: The value of a dual-energy CT Iodine map radiomics model for the prediction of collagen fiber content in the ccRCC tumor microenvironment.
study_design: Retrospective single-center dual-energy CT cohort.
data_source_detail: 87 patients with ccRCC at Shandong Qilu Hospital (59 with abundant collagen fibers, 28 with few); random split of 60 training and 27 validation cases.
data_modality_detail: Dual-energy CT iodine-map radiomics, with arterial- and venous-phase models as comparators.
algorithm: SVM, compared with k-nearest neighbors, logistic regression, random forest, decision tree, and XGBoost; LASSO selected features.
input_features: Seven LASSO-selected iodine-map radiomic features.
biomarker_result: Iodine-map radiomics classifier of high versus low collagen-fiber content in ccRCC.
performance_value: Validation AUC 0.722 for SVM; training AUCs 0.997 for random forest and 1.0 for decision tree and XGBoost.
validation_detail: Performance was evaluated with quintuple cross-validation and a random 60/27 split at one center. There is no external cohort.
key_finding: An iodine-map SVM separated high from low collagen content in ccRCC with validation AUC 0.722, while decision-tree and XGBoost training AUCs reached 1.0.
limitations_as_stated: Single-center study with a small sample, so the model needs assessment in a larger dataset.
other_key_outcomes: Arterial- and venous-phase SVM validation AUCs were 0.698 and 0.741. A separate clinical model of collagen content was also built.

title: Value of handcrafted and deep radiomic features towards training robust machine learning classifiers for prediction of prostate cancer disease aggressiveness.
study_design: Retrospective analysis of a public prostate MRI challenge cohort.
data_source_detail: SPIE-AAPM-NCI PROSTATEx examinations from Radboud University Medical Centre; 181 patients remained after segmentation exclusions (122 clinically insignificant and 59 clinically significant glands).
data_modality_detail: Whole-gland handcrafted radiomics from T2-weighted, high-b DWI, and ADC images, plus deep features from U-Net segmentation models.
algorithm: Random forest or logistic regression, depending on the segmentation strategy, with deep features from U-Net variants.
input_features: 3111 radiomic features (1037 per sequence) and deep features from whole-gland segmentation networks.
biomarker_result: Hybrid radiomic and deep-feature classifier of clinically significant prostate cancer trained to tolerate segmentation differences.
performance_value: NR
validation_detail: Hold-out test sets compared seven training strategies on PROSTATEx. Training on randomly resampled radiologist masks had the lowest generalization error.
key_finding: Training on randomly resampled radiologist masks gave the most robust classifier of clinically significant prostate cancer, whereas removing low-ICC features gave the highest generalization error.
limitations_as_stated: The study is retrospective; the authors recommend a multicenter prospective evaluation of clinical impact.
other_key_outcomes: A decision threshold of 0.32 was set to keep training sensitivity at least 0.9, and the authors report that the test sets required a lower threshold.
extraction_note: Hold-out strategies are compared qualitatively, but no AUC, accuracy, or achieved sensitivity is stated for the selected classifier.

title: A nomogram based on peripheral lymphocyte for predicting 8-year survival in patients with prostate cancer: a single-center study using LASSO-cox regression.
study_design: Retrospective single-institution registry cohort.
data_source_detail: 94 patients with prostate cancer in one Chinese institutional registry.
data_modality_detail: Peripheral lymphocyte subset counts plus age and T stage.
algorithm: LASSO-Cox regression.
input_features: Age, T stage, absolute CD3+CD4+ T-cell count, CD3-CD16+CD56+ NK-cell count, and the CD4/CD8 ratio.
biomarker_result: Peripheral-lymphocyte LASSO-Cox nomogram for overall survival.
performance_value: 8-year OS AUC 0.76; 5-year AUC 0.81; 10-year AUC 0.73.
validation_detail: The AUCs are reported for the same 94-patient cohort used to fit the nomogram. No hold-out, cross-validation, bootstrap, or external cohort is described.
key_finding: A five-factor lymphocyte nomogram gave AUCs of 0.81, 0.76, and 0.73 for 5-, 8-, and 10-year overall survival in 94 men with prostate cancer.
limitations_as_stated: Retrospective registry with missing pathology and non-surgical treatment data, no repeated lymphocyte measurements, and a small sample.
other_key_outcomes: Calibration was described as agreeing with observed survival, and decision-curve analysis was presented as clinically useful. A C-index was named as a discrimination measure, but no C-index value is given.
extraction_note: The survival AUCs come from the development cohort without a described partition, so optimism is unquantified.

title: A radiomics-based interpretable machine learning model to predict the HER2 status in bladder cancer: a multicenter study.
study_design: Retrospective four-hospital CT cohort.
data_source_detail: 207 urothelial bladder cancers from four hospitals: 154 training patients from the primary center (June 2015-June 2023) and 53 test patients from the other three centers (June 2019-December 2023). HER2-positive 109, HER2-negative 98.
data_modality_detail: Nephrographic-phase CT radiomics.
algorithm: Random forest, compared with logistic regression, SVM, k-nearest neighbors, and XGBoost; LASSO for feature selection; SHAP for interpretation.
input_features: 11 LASSO-selected features from 1218 nephrographic CT radiomic features.
biomarker_result: CT radiomics random-forest model of HER2 status in bladder cancer.
performance_value: Test AUC 0.815 for random forest (accuracy 75.5%); other test AUCs were 0.803 (logistic regression), 0.794 (XGBoost), 0.709 (SVM), and 0.679 (k-nearest neighbors).
validation_detail: The 53-patient test set was enrolled from three centers other than the training hospital.
key_finding: A random-forest CT radiomics model predicted bladder-cancer HER2 status with a three-center test AUC of 0.815.
limitations_as_stated: The study is retrospective and the sample is limited.
other_key_outcomes: SHAP attributed predictions mainly to gray-level size-zone and co-occurrence texture features. The endpoint is HER2 status rather than treatment response.

title: An Integrated Machine Learning Framework Identifies Prognostic Gene Pair Biomarkers Associated with Programmed Cell Death Modalities in Clear Cell Renal Cell Carcinoma.
study_design: Retrospective public transcriptomic study with an external microarray cohort.
data_source_detail: TCGA-KIRC training set of 518 patients after clinicopathologic filters, and external E-MTAB-1980 (ArrayExpress) with 101 patients. A separate TCIA CT radiomic score was used to classify CDRGPS status.
data_modality_detail: Bulk expression gene pairs related to programmed cell death; CT radiomics on TCIA is a secondary classifier of the score.
algorithm: Lasso plus random forest, selected from 12 algorithms and 113 combinations by mean C-index.
input_features: Programmed cell death-related gene pairs.
biomarker_result: CDRGPS (cell death-related gene pair score).
performance_value: C-index > 0.75 on TCGA-KIRC (n=518) and external E-MTAB-1980 (n=101); combinations were ranked by mean C-index.
validation_detail: E-MTAB-1980 is an independent external microarray cohort. The TCIA radiomic score (AUC 0.813) classifies high versus low CDRGPS and is not the survival validation. In vitro PRSS23 experiments are orthogonal.
funding: This research received no external funding.
key_finding: A Lasso-random forest gene-pair score, chosen by mean C-index among 113 combinations, exceeded a C-index of 0.75 for overall survival in TCGA-KIRC and E-MTAB-1980.
other_key_outcomes: CDRGPS was reported as more prognostic than seven published cell-death signatures. High-risk patients were described as more responsive to TKIs, mTOR inhibitors, and immunotherapy. The TCIA Rad_Score AUC was 0.813 for high versus low CDRGPS.
extraction_note: Survival performance is reported only as a C-index above 0.75, without a point estimate.

title: Assessing muscle invasion in bladder cancer via virtual biopsy: a study on quantitative parameters and classical radiomics features from dual-energy CT imaging.
study_design: Retrospective single-hospital dual-energy CT cohort.
data_source_detail: 126 patients with bladder cancer who underwent dual-energy CT urography at one hospital, randomly split 7:3 into 88 training and 38 test patients.
data_modality_detail: Venous-phase dual-energy CT iodine parameters and radiomics from 40, 70, and 100 keV images plus iodine material-decomposition images.
algorithm: Support vector machine for radiomics and logistic regression for normalized iodine concentration, combined in a fusion model.
input_features: Normalized iodine concentration and radiomic features from virtual monoenergetic and iodine images.
biomarker_result: Fusion of dual-energy CT iodine concentration and multi-image radiomics for muscle-invasive bladder cancer.
performance_value: Multi-image radiomics test AUC 0.867; fusion model AUC 0.893; normalized iodine concentration AUC 0.704.
validation_detail: One random 7:3 split at a single hospital. No cross-validation or external cohort is described.
key_finding: Multi-image dual-energy CT radiomics predicted muscle invasion with test AUC 0.867, above normalized iodine concentration (AUC 0.704), and a fusion model was reported at AUC 0.893.
limitations_as_stated: Segmentation was manual, dual-energy CT was less available than conventional CT, and imaging was limited to a single mode.
other_key_outcomes: For lesions smaller than 3 cm the fusion model AUC was 0.911. The multi-image model training AUC was 0.943.
extraction_note: The abstract places 0.893 next to the phrase difference in AUC, so it is unclear whether 0.893 is the fusion model's test estimate.

title: Clinical application of machine learning models in patients with prostate cancer before prostatectomy.
study_design: Retrospective surgical cohort with multicenter external validation.
data_source_detail: 139 men from Hospital da Luz for training and 55 men from 15 other institutions for external testing, all treated with robotic-assisted radical prostatectomy.
data_modality_detail: T2-weighted MRI radiomics plus clinical variables and radiologist semantic features.
algorithm: Machine learning models on clinical, clinical-semantic, clinical-radiomic, and clinical-semantic-radiomic feature sets.
input_features: Clinical variables, semantic MRI features, and T2-weighted radiomic features.
biomarker_result: Clinical-semantic-radiomic model of pathologic extracapsular extension.
performance_value: External clinical-semantic-radiomic AUC 0.928 (n=55); discovery mean AUC 0.880 across 1000 cross-validation splits (n=139).
validation_detail: The external test set came from 15 institutions. Discovery AUC was the mean of 1000 cross-validation splits. External scans were still read by the same radiologist, and surgery was by the same surgeon.
key_finding: The model using clinical, semantic, and radiomic features had the highest decision-curve net benefit for extracapsular extension and an external AUC of 0.928.
limitations_as_stated: The sample is small, and external examinations were interpreted by the same radiologist and operated by the same surgeon.
other_key_outcomes: Ranking by AUC favored clinical plus semantic features, whereas ranking by decision curve favored the full three-feature model. The decision supports nerve-sparing versus non-nerve-sparing prostatectomy.

title: Comparison in prostate cancer diagnosis with PSA 4-10 ng/mL: radiomics-based model VS. PI-RADS v2.1.
study_design: Retrospective single-center MRI cohort.
data_source_detail: 221 men with PSA 4-10 ng/mL at one center (60 with prostate cancer, 161 without); 154 training and 67 validation.
data_modality_detail: ADC and T2-weighted radiomics, compared with PI-RADS v2.1.
algorithm: LASSO regression followed by logistic regression.
input_features: 10 ADC features, 13 T2WI features, and 7 features in the combined model, drawn from 851 extracted features.
biomarker_result: Combined ADC and T2WI radiomics model for PSA 4-10 ng/mL.
performance_value: Validation AUC 0.959 (combined), 0.942 (ADC), and 0.943 (T2WI), versus PI-RADS v2.1 validation AUC 0.853.
validation_detail: Single-center split into 154 training and 67 validation patients. No external cohort is described.
key_finding: The combined ADC and T2WI radiomics model reached a validation AUC of 0.959 for prostate cancer at PSA 4-10 ng/mL, above PI-RADS v2.1 (AUC 0.853).
limitations_as_stated: Retrospective single-center study with a relatively small population.
other_key_outcomes: Training AUCs were 0.979 (combined), 0.945 (ADC), and 0.939 (T2WI); the PI-RADS training AUC was 0.825. Reference pathology was MRI-TRUS fusion targeted biopsy or systematic TRUS biopsy.

title: Contrast-enhanced computed tomography-based radiomics nomogram for predicting HER2 status in urothelial bladder carcinoma.
study_design: Retrospective single-institution contrast-enhanced CT cohort.
data_source_detail: 124 patients with urothelial bladder carcinoma at one institution (January 2022 to December 2023), split into 100 training and 24 test patients.
data_modality_detail: Contrast-enhanced CT radiomics plus clinical predictors of HER2 status.
algorithm: Random forest radiomics model integrated with clinical features; eight classifiers were compared, including SVM, logistic regression, MLP, ExtraTrees, LightGBM, XGBoost, and k-nearest neighbors.
input_features: Contrast-enhanced CT radiomic signature and independent clinical predictors.
biomarker_result: Clinical-radiomics model of HER2 status in urothelial bladder carcinoma.
performance_value: Clinical-radiomics test AUC 0.857 (accuracy 0.760, sensitivity 0.643, specificity 0.900); random-forest radiomics test AUC 0.814.
validation_detail: One 100/24 split at a single institution. The radiomics classifier was selected by test-set AUC.
funding: Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region Health and Family Planning Commission (Z20210478 and Z20190813).
key_finding: A clinical-radiomics model predicted HER2 status in urothelial bladder carcinoma with a test AUC of 0.857.
other_key_outcomes: Training clinical-radiomics performance was AUC 0.935, accuracy 0.870, sensitivity 0.881, and specificity 0.854. Random-forest radiomics training AUC was 0.880.

title: Interpretable machine learning model for predicting clinically significant prostate cancer: integrating intratumoral and peritumoral radiomics with clinical and metabolic features.
study_design: Retrospective single-institution mpMRI cohort with a later temporal validation set.
data_source_detail: 350 men with suspicious lesions at one institution (173 csPCa, 177 non-csPCa): training 191, testing 83, and temporal validation 76.
data_modality_detail: Intratumoral and peritumoral T2-weighted and ADC radiomics, clinicoradiologic features, and MR spectroscopy.
algorithm: XGBoost, with recursive feature elimination for the radiomic scores and SHAP interpretation.
input_features: An intratumoral radiomic score from 10 features, a peritumoral score from 16 features, clinicoradiologic variables, and MRS metabolites.
biomarker_result: Combined intratumoral, peritumoral, clinical, and spectroscopic model for clinically significant prostate cancer.
performance_value: Temporal-validation AUC 0.940 (accuracy 0.895); testing-set AUC 0.968 (accuracy 0.928, sensitivity 0.932, specificity 0.923).
validation_detail: A random testing set (n=83) and a later temporal validation set (n=76) came from the same institution. There is no external site.
key_finding: The combined radiomic, clinical, and spectroscopic XGBoost model detected csPCa with temporal-validation AUC 0.940 and testing AUC 0.968.
limitations_as_stated: The study is single-center and retrospective.
other_key_outcomes: The stated clinical aim is to avoid unnecessary biopsies. Testing-set F1 was 0.927.

title: Machine learning based on radiomics features combing B-mode transrectal ultrasound and contrast-enhanced ultrasound to improve peripheral zone prostate cancer detection.
study_design: Prospective single-center transrectal ultrasound cohort.
data_source_detail: 166 peripheral-zone lesions (72 benign, 94 malignant) in men prospectively enrolled at Aerospace Central Hospital from January 2021 to August 2022; 176 inpatients were screened.
data_modality_detail: B-mode transrectal ultrasound and contrast-enhanced ultrasound radiomics, plus clinical and time-intensity-curve features.
algorithm: Multivariable logistic regression.
input_features: 32 radiomic features from B-mode and contrast-enhanced ultrasound, plus age, PSAD, total PSA, and rise time.
biomarker_result: Combined B-mode, contrast-enhanced ultrasound radiomics, and risk-factor model for peripheral-zone prostate cancer.
performance_value: Validation combined-model AUC 0.89; risk-factor model AUC 0.84; B-mode plus CEUS AUC 0.83; B-mode AUC 0.79; CEUS AUC 0.78.
validation_detail: A validation cohort is reported separately from a training cohort at the same hospital, but the validation headcount is not stated.
key_finding: Adding B-mode and contrast-enhanced ultrasound radiomics to age, PSAD, total PSA, and rise time gave a validation AUC of 0.89 for peripheral-zone prostate cancer.
other_key_outcomes: Age, PSAD, total PSA, and rise time were independent predictors. Targeted biopsy was the reference. The full series contains 166 lesions.
extraction_note: The validation AUC of 0.89 is not tied to a printed validation-cohort size; 166 is the total lesion count.

title: Machine learning pipeline to analyze clinical and proteomics data: experiences on a prostate cancer case.
study_design: Retrospective clinical-proteomic pipeline applied to two prostate datasets.
data_source_detail: A two-year project produced a serum dataset, stated as 143 samples (79 prostate cancer and 84 benign prostatic hyperplasia), and a urine dataset of 121 samples (67 prostate cancer and 54 benign prostatic hyperplasia).
data_modality_detail: Mass-spectrometry proteomics integrated with serum or urine clinical biomarkers.
algorithm: Feature selection, multiple classifiers, and a voting ensemble, evaluated with 10-fold cross-validation.
input_features: Blood analytes, mass-spectrometry peptides, and urine biomarkers.
biomarker_result: Ensemble proteomic-clinical classifier of prostate cancer versus benign prostatic hyperplasia.
performance_value: Serum 10-fold CV AUC 0.87 (accuracy 0.83, sensitivity 0.84, specificity 0.81); urine 10-fold CV AUC 0.88 (accuracy 0.83, sensitivity 0.85, specificity 0.80).
validation_detail: Ten-fold cross-validation was run inside each dataset. No external cohort is described.
key_finding: The same selection, training, and voting pipeline separated prostate cancer from benign hyperplasia with 10-fold AUCs of 0.87 in serum and 0.88 in urine.
other_key_outcomes: Six serum peptides and two urine peptides were highlighted. The pipeline code was released on GitHub. The stated serum subgroup counts, 79 and 84, sum to 163 rather than 143.
extraction_note: The serum analytic size is internally inconsistent: 143 samples are stated, while 79 prostate cancer and 84 benign cases sum to 163.

title: Multi-sequence MRI-based radiomics model to preoperatively predict the WHO/ISUP grade of clear Cell Renal Cell Carcinoma: a two-center study.
study_design: Retrospective two-center MRI cohort.
data_source_detail: 334 patients with ccRCC from two centers. Center 2 supplied the external validation set (n=131); Center 1 was split 7:3 for development.
data_modality_detail: Dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI, axial fat-suppressed T2-weighted imaging, diffusion-weighted imaging, and in-phase/out-of-phase images.
algorithm: Logistic regression for the radiomics and combined models, with seven other classifiers compared and 10-fold cross-validation of the combined logistic model.
input_features: A multi-sequence MRI radiomic score plus intra-tumoral vessels.
biomarker_result: Combined clinical-radiomics model of high versus low WHO/ISUP grade in ccRCC.
performance_value: External combined-model AUC 0.855; external radiomics AUC 0.834; external clinical AUC 0.762.
validation_detail: External validation is a second center (n=131). Ten-fold cross-validation of the combined logistic model produced AUCs of 0.849-0.856. The external cohort is ccRCC, so the level is not downgraded.
key_finding: A multi-sequence MRI radiomics model plus intra-tumoral vessels predicted high-grade ccRCC with external AUC 0.855, above the clinical model (AUC 0.762).
limitations_as_stated: Even with two centers, the sample is small and imbalanced between high and low grade, and the design is retrospective.
other_key_outcomes: Intra-tumoral vessels were the independent clinical predictor. Decision-curve net benefit favored the combined model between risk thresholds 0.04 and 0.54. The Delong p-value versus the clinical model was 0.003.

title: Optimizing radiomics for prostate cancer diagnosis: feature selection strategies, machine learning classifiers, and MRI sequences.
study_design: Retrospective multicenter MRI benchmark with a public external dataset.
data_source_detail: ProstateNET, 465 patients from 12 centers and multiple vendors, for development; ProstateX2, 204 patients, for external validation. ProstateX2 lesion masks are public.
data_modality_detail: Biparametric MRI radiomics from T2-weighted images, ADC maps, or both (1246 features per sequence).
algorithm: Boosted generalized linear model with Boruta in nested cross-validation and with L1-lasso on external testing; SVM, random forest, and LASSO were also compared across 10 feature-selection methods.
input_features: Radiomic features from T2-weighted images, ADC maps, or their combination.
biomarker_result: Biparametric MRI radiomics classifier of clinically significant prostate cancer.
performance_value: External AUC 0.71 (L1-lasso plus boosted GLM, F1 0.47); nested cross-validation AUC 0.71 (Boruta plus boosted GLM, F1 0.76).
validation_detail: Nested cross-validation was performed on ProstateNET (n=465), and external testing used ProstateX2 (n=204). The best external pipeline was not the best nested-CV pipeline. In total, 480 models were compared.
key_finding: Across 480 biparametric MRI radiomics pipelines, the best external model reached AUC 0.71 on ProstateX2, the same AUC as the best nested cross-validation model on ProstateNET.
other_key_outcomes: ADC-derived features discriminated better than T2-weighted features, and the feature-selection method mattered more than the classifier. Public ProstateX2 masks are at github.com/rcuocolo/PROSTATEx_masks; that repository holds masks rather than the analysis code.

title: Predicting first-line VEGFR-TKI resistance and survival in metastatic clear cell renal cell carcinoma using a clinical-radiomic nomogram.
study_design: Retrospective single-center CT cohort of metastatic ccRCC.
data_source_detail: 110 patients with metastatic ccRCC treated with first-line VEGFR-TKI from 2009 to 2019 at one center; 77 training and 33 test patients.
data_modality_detail: Baseline contrast-enhanced CT radiomics (1316 features) plus clinical factors.
algorithm: LASSO radiomic score combined with clinical factors in a nomogram.
input_features: LASSO radiomic score plus T stage, N stage, and IMDC score.
biomarker_result: Clinical-radiomic nomogram for early VEGFR-TKI resistance.
performance_value: Test combined-nomogram AUC 0.88 (accuracy 0.818); test radiomic AUC 0.79; test clinical AUC 0.77.
validation_detail: Single-center assignment to 77 training and 33 test patients. No cross-validation is described, and the authors state that an external cohort is still needed.
key_finding: A clinical-radiomic nomogram predicted early VEGFR-TKI resistance in metastatic ccRCC with a test AUC of 0.88.
limitations_as_stated: Single-center retrospective series, very few IMDC favorable-risk patients in the split, and overall survival influenced by later treatment.
other_key_outcomes: Training AUCs were 0.83 for the combined nomogram, 0.81 for radiomics, and 0.75 for the clinical model. A nomogram score of at least 1.18 had training hazard ratios of 0.22 for progression-free survival and 0.38 for overall survival.

title: Prediction of clear cell renal cell carcinoma ≤ 4cm: visual assessment of ultrasound characteristics versus ultrasonographic radiomics analysis.
study_design: Retrospective ultrasound cohort with external validation at two hospitals.
data_source_detail: 302 small renal tumors (maximum diameter at most 4 cm; 182 ccRCC and 120 angiomyolipomas) at Tianjin Medical University Cancer Institute and Hospital, split 7:3 for training and internal validation. The external set comprised 69 patients from 230 tumors at Tianjin First Central Hospital and Tianjin Occupational Disease Hospital.
data_modality_detail: Ultrasound radiomics extracted with PyRadiomics, plus clinical ultrasound features; contrast-enhanced CT was the comparator.
algorithm: Random forest.
input_features: Nine ultrasound radiomic features and clinical ultrasound characteristics.
biomarker_result: Comprehensive ultrasound clinical-radiomics model separating small ccRCC from angiomyolipoma.
performance_value: External comprehensive-model AUC 0.90 (sensitivity 85.0%, specificity 85.5%); external radiomics AUC 0.89; external clinical ultrasound AUC 0.73; external contrast-enhanced CT AUC 0.91.
validation_detail: External patients came from two hospitals that were not used for training. Internal validation was a 7:3 random split of the index center, where the comprehensive-model AUC was 0.88.
key_finding: A random-forest ultrasound radiomics model separated small ccRCC from angiomyolipoma with external AUC 0.90, close to contrast-enhanced CT (AUC 0.91).
limitations_as_stated: The cases were collected retrospectively.
other_key_outcomes: Internal contrast-enhanced CT AUC was 0.90. The external DeLong comparison of the comprehensive model with contrast-enhanced CT was Z=-0.252, P=0.801.

title: Prediction of prostate cancer aggressiveness using magnetic resonance imaging radiomics: a dual-center study.
study_design: Retrospective dual-center MRI cohort.
data_source_detail: 218 men with biopsy-proven prostate cancer from Gansu Provincial Hospital (training n=117, internal validation n=50) and Zhangye People's Hospital (external n=51).
data_modality_detail: Small-field-of-view high-resolution T2-weighted imaging and delayed post-contrast MRI radiomics.
algorithm: Logistic regression, chosen among support vector machine, linear discriminant analysis, logistic regression, and LASSO logistic regression.
input_features: 11 radiomic features for Gleason score and 5 features for positive systematic-biopsy cores.
biomarker_result: MRI radiomics model of Gleason score greater than 7 versus 7 or lower.
performance_value: Gleason-score external AUC 0.717 (training 0.811, internal validation 0.814); positive-needle external AUC 0.791 (training 0.806, internal validation 0.811).
validation_detail: Center B (n=51) is one external hospital. Center A was randomly split 7:3 into training (n=117) and internal validation (n=50).
key_finding: T2-weighted and delayed-contrast radiomics predicted Gleason score above 7 with external AUC 0.717 and a high positive-core burden with external AUC 0.791.
limitations_as_stated: The study is retrospective, the sample remains small despite an external set, and DWI, ADC, and lesion-based segmentation were not used.
other_key_outcomes: Positive-needle count is a second endpoint built with the same imaging pipeline. Gleason score above 7 accounted for 152 of 218 patients.

title: Radiomics predicts the prognosis of patients with clear cell renal cell carcinoma by reflecting the tumor heterogeneity and microenvironment.
study_design: Retrospective three-hospital CT cohort with a TCGA imaging validation set.
data_source_detail: 512 patients with ccRCC from three hospitals (358 derivation and 154 held-out test cases) plus 96 TCGA-KIRC/TCIA cases used to validate the deep-learning radiomics score. Matching TCGA sequencing compared tumor heterogeneity and the microenvironment.
data_modality_detail: Contrast-enhanced CT deep-learning radiomics (3566 features from 3D regions of interest) plus clinicopathology.
algorithm: Deep-learning radiomics score combined with clinicopathologic variables in a Cox model, interpreted with SHAP.
input_features: Deep-learning radiomics features and postoperative clinicopathologic factors.
biomarker_result: Combined deep-learning radiomics and clinicopathologic model for overall survival after surgery.
performance_value: Internal test combined-model AUC 0.879, 0.854, and 0.831 for 1-, 3-, and 5-year overall survival.
validation_detail: Inside the three-hospital cohort, 358 patients were used for derivation and 154 were held out as the test cohort that carries the quoted AUCs. The score was also applied to TCGA-KIRC/TCIA (n=96), which covers ccRCC.
key_finding: A CT deep-learning radiomics score independently predicted overall survival, and the combined model had internal-test AUCs of 0.879, 0.854, and 0.831 at 1, 3, and 5 years.
limitations_as_stated: The sample was limited, the link between radiomics and prognosis needs further validation, and the authors call for a multicenter prospective cohort.
other_key_outcomes: In the same test cohort, the radiomics score alone had AUCs of 0.814, 0.796, and 0.782 for 1-, 3-, and 5-year overall survival. High- and low-score groups differed in tumor-cell heterogeneity and the microenvironment on TCGA sequencing.
extraction_note: The quoted AUCs belong to the internal test cohort of 154 patients. Application to TCGA-KIRC is described, but those external AUC figures are absent, so external performance is incomplete.

title: The value of radiomics based on 2-[18 F]FDG PET/CT in predicting WHO/ISUP grade of clear cell renal cell carcinoma.
study_design: Retrospective single-center FDG PET/CT cohort.
data_source_detail: 209 patients with 214 ccRCC lesions (141 low grade, 73 high grade) scanned with 2-[18F]FDG PET/CT from December 2016 to December 2023 and randomly split 7:3.
data_modality_detail: FDG PET/CT radiomics at SUVmax thresholds of 0, 2.5%, 25%, and 40%.
algorithm: Minimum-redundancy maximum-relevance and LASSO models for clinical, radiomics, and combined predictors.
input_features: PET radiomic features inside a 40% SUVmax contour, plus clinical variables.
biomarker_result: PET radiomics model at a 40% SUVmax threshold for WHO/ISUP grade in ccRCC.
validation_detail: Lesions were randomly split 7:3 at one center. The testing-group headcount is not stated. There is no external cohort.
key_finding: Radiomics from the 40% SUVmax PET volume predicted high versus low WHO/ISUP grade with a testing AUC of 0.882.
limitations_as_stated: The study is retrospective, monocentric, and based on a small sample.
other_key_outcomes: Testing AUCs were 0.878, 0.876, and 0.871 for the 0, 2.5%, and 25% SUVmax contours. Clinical and radiomics training AUCs were 0.859 and 0.909. A combined-model AUC of 0.916 is reported for the training group.
extraction_note: Testing AUC 0.882 follows a 7:3 split of 214 lesions, but the testing-group size itself is not stated.

title: Ultrasound-based deep learning radiomics nomogram for risk stratification of testicular masses: a two-center study.
study_design: Retrospective two-center cohort of testicular masses, with a random internal split and a separate external hospital.
data_source_detail: First Affiliated Hospital of Guangxi Medical University (training 158, internal validation 68) and Baise People's Hospital (external test 49), January 2018 to April 2023.
data_modality_detail: Preoperative grayscale ultrasound, one maximal cross-section per lesion.
algorithm: LASSO with 10-fold cross-validation for feature selection, then logistic regression for a deep-learning radiomics signature and a clinical nomogram.
input_features: Ultrasound radiomics and deep-learning features, plus clinical variables including AFP, beta-HCG, and Doppler flow.
biomarker_result: Clinical deep-learning radiomics (CDLR) nomogram for testicular masses.
performance_value: External-test AUC 0.835 for tumor versus non-tumor and 0.834 for malignant versus benign; internal-validation AUC 0.909 and 0.851.
validation_detail: Center 1 was split 7:3 into training and internal validation. Center 2 (n=49) was the external test. Ten-fold cross-validation was used only inside LASSO.
key_finding: The CDLR nomogram separated testicular tumors from non-tumors and malignant from benign masses on an external ultrasound cohort, ahead of the clinical model, imaging signature, and two radiologists.
limitations_as_stated: The study is retrospective, so selection bias is expected, and ultrasound examinations by different operators can introduce error.
other_key_outcomes: Decision-curve analysis favored the CDLR nomogram over the clinical and deep-learning radiomics models.

title: Using apparent diffusion coefficient maps and radiomics to predict pathological grade in upper urinary tract urothelial carcinoma.
study_design: Retrospective single-institution cohort of upper-tract urothelial carcinoma with a random train-test split.
data_source_detail: Peking University First Hospital; 215 patients after radical nephroureterectomy (training 151, test 64), MRI from 2010 to 2023 on scanners from eight vendors.
data_modality_detail: ADC maps derived from multiparametric MRI diffusion-weighted imaging.
algorithm: Gradient boosting on two radiomic features; 5-fold cross-validation on the training set was used to select the model.
input_features: 1070 PyRadiomics features from the ADC volume; retained features were log-sigma GLCM ClusterProminence and wavelet-LLL first-order 10th percentile.
biomarker_result: Two-feature ADC radiomics model for high- versus low-grade upper-tract urothelial carcinoma.
performance_value: Test-set AUC 0.786 (95% CI 0.651-0.921); training-set AUC 1.000. Mean-ADC test AUC 0.628.
validation_detail: Single-center 7:3 split. Five-fold cross-validation selected the model on the training set; the reported AUC is the held-out test set. No external cohort.
key_finding: An ADC radiomics model graded upper-tract urothelial carcinoma better than mean ADC on the internal test set, although that difference was not significant (DeLong p=0.071).
limitations_as_stated: Authors cite inherent design bias and state that larger samples and external validation are required.
other_key_outcomes: A mean-ADC cutoff above 1313 x 10^-6 mm^2/s had training sensitivity 50.4% and specificity 89.3%. Low-grade cases were upsampled before training.

title: A Robust [<sup>18</sup>F]-PSMA-1007 Radiomics Ensemble Model for Prostate Cancer Risk Stratification.
study_design: Retrospective single-center cohort evaluated by repeated cross-validation, without an external test set.
data_source_detail: Cannizzaro Hospital, Catania; 143 biopsy-confirmed prostate cancers with [18F]-PSMA-1007 PET/CT from October 2021 to April 2023 (72 high-risk, 71 low-risk).
data_modality_detail: [18F]-PSMA-1007 PET radiomics from manually contoured intraprostatic disease.
algorithm: LASSO feature selection and an ensemble of neural network, discriminant analysis, and SVM, tuned with five-fold cross-validation over 30 iterations.
input_features: 1781 IBSI-compliant PET radiomics features; the selected ensemble used robust plus fine-tuning subsets, mostly wavelet and Laplacian-of-Gaussian texture.
biomarker_result: Ensemble PSMA-PET radiomics signature for high- versus low-risk prostate cancer (Gleason 4+3 or higher versus 3+3 or 3+4).
performance_value: Mean AUC 0.8575 and mean accuracy 79.52% for the robust-plus-fine-tuning ensemble, averaged over 30 iterations.
validation_detail: Five-fold cross-validation repeated 30 times on one center. Authors state there is no external test set.
key_finding: A PSMA PET radiomics ensemble separated high- from low-risk prostate cancer with mean AUC 0.8575 in internal cross-validation.
limitations_as_stated: Single-center design, manual segmentation, small cohort, no external test set, and a biopsy rather than prostatectomy reference standard.
other_key_outcomes: Before ensembling, SVM had the highest average AUC among single classifiers (0.7626).

title: A multi-modal deep learning framework for predicting PSA progression-free survival in metastatic prostate cancer using PSMA PET/CT imaging
study_design: Retrospective single-institution cohort with five-fold cross-validation. medRxiv preprint.
data_source_detail: One academic institution; 99 patients with metastatic prostate cancer and 396 Ga-68 PSMA-11-positive lesions. Median follow-up 22.4 months.
data_modality_detail: Lesion-cropped PSMA PET and CT fused with clinical variables.
algorithm: 3D ResNet-18 with a Cox proportional-hazards loss. Clinical inputs were preselected with LASSO Cox. ResNet-18 was the best backbone tested.
input_features: Cropped PSMA PET/CT lesion volumes plus 12 clinical features, including BMI, ECOG, PSA, Gleason score, stage, castration status, and treatment.
biomarker_result: Multimodal PSMA PET/CT deep-learning score for PSA progression-free survival.
performance_value: Five-fold C-index 0.75-0.94 for the multimodal model; imaging-only 0.70-0.89; clinical-only 0.53-0.65.
validation_detail: Five-fold cross-validation at one institution. No external cohort. Model-based risk groups had median PSA progression-free survival of 19.7 versus 26 months (P<0.001).
key_finding: A multimodal ResNet-18 using PSMA PET/CT and clinical features predicted PSA progression-free survival better than imaging-only or clinical-only models.
other_key_outcomes: High- versus low-risk groups from the deep-learning score separated PSA progression-free survival (median 19.7 versus 26 months).
extraction_note: The source is a medRxiv preprint, and performance is reported as a cross-validation range rather than one pooled C-index.

title: A novel MRI-based habitat analysis and deep learning for predicting perineural invasion in prostate cancer: a two-center study.
study_design: Retrospective two-center cohort with an internal split at the first center and an external cohort from the second.
data_source_detail: Tongde Hospital of Zhejiang Province (training 173, internal validation 74) and Taizhou First People's Hospital (external 150), prostate cancer diagnosed January 2018 to December 2022.
data_modality_detail: mpMRI habitats on T2-weighted, diffusion-weighted, and ADC images.
algorithm: ResNet-101 deep features, minimum-redundancy maximum-relevance, and LASSO with 10-fold cross-validation. K-means defined three habitats. A clinical logistic model was combined with habitat scores.
input_features: Deep features from T2-weighted, diffusion-weighted, and ADC habitats, plus age, MRI T stage, and PI-RADS.
biomarker_result: mpMRI habitat deep-learning radscore and a combined clinical-habitat model for perineural invasion.
performance_value: Habitat-model external AUC 0.859-0.939; clinical-model external AUC 0.789; combined-model training AUC 0.999 (sensitivity 1, specificity 0.955).
validation_detail: Center 1 was randomized 7:3 into training and internal validation. Center 2 (n=150) was external. External AUCs are given for habitat and clinical models.
key_finding: Habitat deep-learning models predicted perineural invasion on an external mpMRI cohort (AUC 0.859-0.939). The combined model is presented as superior, with a training AUC of 0.999.
limitations_as_stated: Analyzing the tumor as one region is said to lose heterogeneity information, and habitat borders remain difficult to define without subjective radiologist judgment.
other_key_outcomes: Age (OR 0.92), MRI T stage (OR 1.83), and PI-RADS (OR 3.12) were independent clinical predictors. Decision-curve analysis was reported for the combined model.
extraction_note: The combined model is given a training AUC of 0.999. External discrimination is printed for the habitat models and the clinical model, so the external estimate for the combined model is uncertain.

title: A predictive model for WHO/ISUP pathologic grading of renal clear cell carcinoma based on CT radiomics: a multicenter study.
study_design: Retrospective multicenter cohort with internal development at one cancer hospital and external cases from three other hospitals.
data_source_detail: Zhejiang Cancer Hospital (104 patients) plus Hangzhou First People's Hospital, Zhejiang Provincial People's Hospital, and Quzhou People's Hospital (65 external cases), November 2017 to February 2022. Overall 169 clear-cell RCCs (93 low grade, 76 high grade).
data_modality_detail: Corticomedullary-phase contrast-enhanced CT.
algorithm: Random forest on six radiomic features, with logistic regression for clinical predictors. Nested 5-fold cross-validation and mRMR were used for feature selection.
input_features: 2264 CT radiomic features reduced to six, plus tumor size, hemorrhage, and tumor thrombus.
biomarker_result: Combined CT radiomics and clinical-imaging model for WHO/ISUP grade of clear-cell RCC (grades I-II versus III-IV).
performance_value: Combined-model AUC 0.895 in training, 0.885 in validation, and 0.860 in the external cohort. Radiomics-only training AUC 0.873; clinical-imaging training AUC 0.712.
validation_detail: Development used the primary center with an internal train-validation partition and nested 5-fold cross-validation for feature selection. Sixty-five patients from three other hospitals were the external cohort.
key_finding: A CT radiomics-clinical model predicted high versus low WHO/ISUP grade in clear-cell RCC with external AUC 0.860, above the clinical-imaging model.
limitations_as_stated: The multicenter sample is small, especially for grades III and IV; grade groups are imbalanced; radiomics used only the cortical phase.
other_key_outcomes: DeLong tests: combined versus clinical-imaging Z=3.023 (P=0.002); combined versus radiomics Z=1.627 (P=0.103). Decision-curve net benefit spanned thresholds 0.1-0.84.

title: An MRI radiomics model for predicting a prostate-specific antigen response following abiraterone treatment in patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer.
study_design: Retrospective two-hospital cohort randomly split into training and validation rather than held out by site.
data_source_detail: Sixty patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer treated with abiraterone at two hospitals; training n=48 and validation n=12. Thirty-nine PSA responders and 21 non-responders.
data_modality_detail: Biparametric MRI radiomics from T2-weighted, diffusion-weighted, and ADC images.
algorithm: LASSO radiomics signature combined with a clinical Cox nomogram.
input_features: Seven radiomic features from T2-weighted, diffusion-weighted, and ADC images, plus clinical factors including ISUP grade.
biomarker_result: Biparametric MRI Rad-score and combined nomogram for PSA response to abiraterone.
performance_value: Integrated-model validation AUC 0.875 (95% CI 0.564-0.991); training AUC 0.889 (95% CI 0.764-0.961); Rad-score HR 2.21 (95% CI 1.01-4.44).
validation_detail: Patients from two hospitals were randomized 48/12 into one validation split. Site-wise AUCs are tabulated (institution I 0.889, institution II 0.817) but sites were not held out as an external test.
funding: No financial support was received for the research, authorship, or publication.
conflicts_of_interest: YX and FS were employed by Shanghai United Imaging Intelligence Co., Ltd. The remaining authors declared no commercial or financial conflicts.
key_finding: A biparametric MRI radiomics-clinical model predicted PSA response to abiraterone with validation AUC 0.875, and the Rad-score independently predicted response (HR 2.21).
other_key_outcomes: T2-weighted imaging alone had validation AUC 0.778. On 12 validation patients the integrated model had sensitivity 75% and specificity 100%.
extraction_note: The validation cohort has 12 patients, and the AUC confidence interval is wide (0.564-0.991).

title: An interpretable CT-based deep learning model for predicting overall survival in patients with bladder cancer: a multicenter study.
study_design: Retrospective multicenter prognostic study with three independent validation sets, including TCGA.
data_source_detail: Own CT cohorts: training n=765, validation cohort 1 n=438, validation cohort 2 n=181; TCGA n=72. Centers include the Affiliated Hospital of Qingdao University and Guangdong Provincial People's Hospital.
data_modality_detail: Preoperative nephrographic-phase contrast-enhanced CT.
algorithm: Interpretable CT deep-learning model (BCDL) with SHAP pixel attributions. The network name is not stated.
input_features: Nephrographic-phase CT of the bladder tumor. Clinical Cox covariates included age, tumor contour, and size.
biomarker_result: BCDL score for overall survival, used to define high- and low-risk groups.
validation_detail: The model was trained on 765 patients and tested in two independent clinical cohorts and TCGA. n_analytic is validation cohort 1, the largest external clinical set supporting the lead C-index.
key_finding: A preoperative CT deep-learning score stratified bladder-cancer overall survival in three external cohorts (C-index 0.621, 0.682, and 0.701), and adjuvant therapy was associated with longer survival in the high-risk group.
limitations_as_stated: Prospective validation is still needed beyond the Chinese cohorts and TCGA. The endpoint is overall survival only, variant histologies were not stratified, and only nephrographic-phase CT was used.
other_key_outcomes: Adjuvant therapy was associated with better overall survival in high-risk patients (p=0.028). RNA sequencing linked the high-risk group to an immunosuppressive microenvironment. Code: https://github.com/zyzlw16/Bladder.

title: An interpretable contrast-enhanced CT radiomics-based pipeline incorporating automatic segmentation for predicting ISUP grade group in ccRCC.
study_design: Retrospective single-center cohort with a train-test split and no external validation.
data_source_detail: Hangzhou TCM Hospital Affiliated to Zhejiang Chinese Medical University; 276 clear-cell RCCs with preoperative contrast-enhanced CT (training 193, test 83).
data_modality_detail: Corticomedullary-phase contrast-enhanced CT with automatic tumor segmentation.
algorithm: Recursive feature elimination with cross-validation across five classifiers, then radiomics, clinical, and combined models. The five classifier names are not listed.
input_features: Radiomic features from automatically segmented corticomedullary-phase tumors, plus clinical variables.
biomarker_result: Combined clinical-radiomics model for ISUP grade group in clear-cell RCC (1-2 versus 3-4).
performance_value: Combined-model test AUC 0.834 (95% CI 0.737-0.931); training AUC 0.907 (95% CI 0.868-0.947). Test radiomics AUC 0.796; test clinical AUC 0.698.
validation_detail: Single-center split of 193 training and 83 test patients. Cross-validation was used inside feature elimination, not as the reported test. Authors state there is no external validation.
key_finding: An interpretable CT radiomics pipeline with automatic segmentation predicted ISUP grade group with test AUC 0.834, above the clinical model.
limitations_as_stated: Retrospective single-center sample without external validation, and the analysis was limited to the tumor region.
other_key_outcomes: On the test set the combined model was not significantly better than radiomics alone (p=0.328). SHAP, calibration, and decision-curve analysis were reported.

title: An interpretable machine learning model based on CT imaging for predicting lymphovascular invasion and survival in bladder urothelial carcinoma: a multicenter study.
study_design: Retrospective three-center cohort, with one hospital for training and two hospitals pooled as the test set.
data_source_detail: 495 patients undergoing radical cystectomy for urothelial carcinoma. Hospital 1 training n=400; Hospital 2 n=56 and Hospital 3 n=39 formed the test set.
data_modality_detail: Preoperative contrast-enhanced CT with manual tumor segmentation.
algorithm: LASSO feature selection and an SVM trained with five-fold cross-validation, then a combined model with clinical factors. SHAP was used for interpretation.
input_features: CT radiomic shape and texture features plus clinical risk factors.
biomarker_result: Combined CT radiomics-clinical model for lymphovascular invasion in bladder urothelial carcinoma.
performance_value: Combined-model test AUC 0.901 and training AUC 0.952 (95% CI 0.914-0.983). SVM-only test AUC 0.872 (95% CI 0.789-0.944).
validation_detail: Training and five-fold cross-validation used Hospital 1 (n=400). Hospitals 2 and 3 (56 and 39 patients) were the external test set. n_analytic is that pooled test set.
key_finding: A CT radiomics-clinical model predicted lymphovascular invasion with test AUC 0.901, and patients predicted to be invasion-negative had better disease-free survival.
limitations_as_stated: The study is retrospective and based on historical cases.
other_key_outcomes: The SVM test set had accuracy 0.832, sensitivity 0.591, and specificity 0.904. Predicted lymphovascular-invasion status separated disease-free survival.

title: An unsupervised learning model that integrates clinical and MRI radiomics features outperforms existing models in predicting the 5-year progression-free survival of prostate cancer patients after prostatectomy: a multicenter study
study_design: Retrospective three-center cohort after radical prostatectomy, with two external hospitals. Research Square preprint.
data_source_detail: Three hospitals, January 2010 to July 2019. Training n=212, external validation 1 n=111, external validation 2 n=77. Fudan University Shanghai Cancer Center is a lead site. Endpoint is 5-year progression-free survival.
data_modality_detail: MRI radiomics without contouring of contrast-enhanced images, combined with clinical factors.
algorithm: LASSO-Cox retained five clinical factors and 13 radiomic features, which were clustered with K-means into three risk groups.
input_features: Clinical variables and MRI radiomic features selected by LASSO-Cox.
biomarker_result: Unsupervised radiomic-clinical clusters (low, intermediate, and high risk) for 5-year progression-free survival after prostatectomy.
performance_value: Five-year progression-free survival 90%, 73%, and 17% across low, intermediate, and high clusters in external validation 1 (n=111); 92%, 59%, and 12% in external validation 2 (n=77). Training rates were 90%, 56%, and 5% (all p<0.05).
validation_detail: Clusters were fit at the training hospital and applied to two external hospitals. n_analytic is the larger external set. No AUC or C-index is printed.
funding: National Cancer Center of China, grant NCC201909B03.
key_finding: Unsupervised MRI radiomic-clinical clusters separated 5-year progression-free survival after prostatectomy in two external cohorts, with high-risk rates of 17% and 12%.
limitations_as_stated: Retrospective selection bias, no contouring of enhanced images, manual regions of interest, and relatively small external sets.
other_key_outcomes: EAU, CAPRA, and PIPEN clinical systems also separated progression-free survival. The radiomic-clinical clusters redistributed patients relative to those scores.
extraction_note: Preprint. Group separation is reported as 5-year progression-free survival rates rather than AUC or C-index.

title: Biparametric MRI-based radiomics for prediction of clinically significant prostate cancer of PI-RADS category 3 lesions.
study_design: Retrospective single-center cohort with a random training-validation split.
data_source_detail: Wuxi No. 2 People's Hospital / Jiangnan University Medical Center; 233 men with PI-RADS 3 lesions who had biparametric MRI and MRI/ultrasound fusion biopsy, September 2020 to October 2023 (training 160, validation 73).
data_modality_detail: Biparametric MRI radiomics from T2-weighted and diffusion-weighted images.
algorithm: LASSO radiomics signature combined with PSA density.
input_features: Thirty-four radiomic features (12 from T2-weighted images and 22 from diffusion-weighted images) plus PSA density.
biomarker_result: Biparametric MRI radiomics signature plus PSA density for clinically significant prostate cancer in PI-RADS 3 lesions.
performance_value: Validation AUC 0.856 (95% CI 0.750-0.962) for radiomics plus PSA density; radiomics alone 0.810 (95% CI 0.682-0.937); PSA density alone 0.690 (95% CI 0.524-0.855).
validation_detail: Single-institution split into training n=160 and validation n=73. No external cohort.
key_finding: In PI-RADS 3 lesions, biparametric MRI radiomics plus PSA density reached a validation AUC of 0.856 for clinically significant prostate cancer, above either predictor alone.
limitations_as_stated: Manual contours were drawn on single slices rather than the whole lesion volume, which limits volumetric characterization.
other_key_outcomes: Training AUCs were 0.887 for the combination, 0.858 for radiomics, and 0.658 for PSA density. The training PSA-density cutoff was 0.21 ng/ml/ml.

title: CT Urography-Based Radiomics to Predict ISUP Grading of Clear Cell Renal Cell Carcinoma.
study_design: Retrospective institutional cohort with an internal split and a TCGA external validation set.
data_source_detail: Renmin Hospital of Wuhan University CT urography, 328 clear-cell RCCs split 7:3 into training and testing; TCGA cohort n=175 for external validation.
data_modality_detail: Corticomedullary-phase CT urography radiomics.
algorithm: LASSO feature selection followed by logistic regression, a multilayer perceptron, SVM, and XGBoost. SHAP was applied to the best model.
input_features: 1218 PyRadiomics features reduced to 20, including wavelet-LHL GLCM Idn and wavelet-LHL GLRLM LongRunEmphasis.
biomarker_result: XGBoost CT-urography radiomics model for WHO/ISUP grade of clear-cell RCC.
performance_value: XGBoost external AUC 0.78 (95% CI 0.74-0.83); internal-test AUC 0.80 (95% CI 0.75-0.85); training AUC 0.96 (95% CI 0.92-0.99).
validation_detail: Own-hospital data were split 7:3, then TCGA (n=175) was the external set. n_analytic is the TCGA cohort that supports the external AUC.
key_finding: XGBoost using corticomedullary CT-urography radiomics predicted clear-cell RCC ISUP grade with external AUC 0.78, the best of four classifiers on TCGA.
other_key_outcomes: External AUCs were 0.74 for logistic regression, 0.68 for the multilayer perceptron, and 0.67 for SVM. XGBoost external sensitivity was 0.91 (95% CI 0.86-0.95).
extraction_note: The GitHub link in the paper points to PyRadiomics, not a study-specific model repository. Data are available from the corresponding author on request.

title: Clinical-radiomics hybrid modeling outperforms conventional models: machine learning enhances stratification of adverse prognostic features in prostate cancer.
study_design: Retrospective single-cohort study with a random training-validation split.
data_source_detail: 137 prostate-cancer patients with preoperative MRI and postoperative pathology, January 2021 to April 2023 (85 with adverse features, 52 without). Training n=95, validation n=42.
data_modality_detail: Biparametric MRI radiomics from ADC and T2-weighted images.
algorithm: LASSO feature selection, then logistic regression, decision tree, random forest, SVM, and AdaBoost. Random forest performed best and was combined with clinical variables.
input_features: Thirty-one PyRadiomics features from ADC and T2-weighted regions of interest, plus biopsy Gleason grade, total PSA, and prostate volume.
biomarker_result: Clinical-radiomics hybrid random-forest model for adverse pathologic features.
performance_value: Hybrid validation AUC 0.909 (95% CI 0.822-0.995); radiomics random-forest AUC 0.832 (95% CI 0.706-0.958); clinical model AUC 0.772. Hybrid sensitivity 0.813, specificity 0.885, and accuracy 0.857.
