validation_detail: One cohort randomly split into training n=95 and validation n=42. No external cohort.
funding: Jiangsu Province Capability Improvement Project through Science, Technology and Education (JSDW202242) and Suzhou Key Laboratory of Medical Imaging (SZS2024032).
key_finding: A biparametric MRI random-forest model plus clinical variables predicted adverse pathologic features with validation AUC 0.909, above radiomics or clinical models alone.
other_key_outcomes: Calibration and decision-curve analysis supported the hybrid model (p<0.01 versus the single models).

title: Computed tomography-based radiomics predicts prognostic and treatment-related levels of immune infiltration in the immune microenvironment of clear cell renal cell carcinoma.
study_design: Retrospective public-data study linking TCGA-KIRC transcriptomes to TCIA CT to classify immune infiltration.
data_source_detail: TCGA-KIRC (539 tumor samples; 470 with survival beyond 30 days) paired with TCIA CT. After quality filters, 163 cases entered the radiomics analysis.
data_modality_detail: Non-contrast CT radiomics. Immune labels came from TCGA RNA-seq single-sample gene-set enrichment and Boruta clustering.
algorithm: LASSO radiomic features with eight classifiers, including logistic regression, SVM, ExtraTrees, LightGBM, and a multilayer perceptron. ExtraTrees had the highest AUCs.
input_features: PyRadiomics features from resampled CT tumor regions, labeled by high versus low immune-infiltration groups.
biomarker_result: CT radiomics classifier of immune-infiltration level in clear-cell RCC.
performance_value: ExtraTrees test-set AUC 1.000 and training-set AUC 0.753. Logistic regression and LightGBM had test-set sensitivity 0.615.
validation_detail: Train and test performance is reported on the 163 paired TCIA/TCGA cases. The test-set size is not stated. There is no additional external cohort.
key_finding: ExtraTrees is reported as the best CT radiomics classifier of clear-cell RCC immune-infiltration groups, with a test AUC of 1.000 and a training AUC of 0.753.
other_key_outcomes: Immune groups were also compared for survival and for immunotherapy response estimated with TIDE. Those analyses are secondary to the CT classifier.
extraction_note: The reported test AUC of 1.000 is higher than the training AUC of 0.753, and the test-set size is not stated.

title: Development and validation of a radiomics deep learning signature from MRI-guided transrectal ultrasound combined with ultrasound imaging parameters for prostate cancer prediction
study_design: Retrospective two-hospital study of MRI-guided transrectal ultrasound and contrast-enhanced ultrasound. Research Square preprint.
data_source_detail: Inner Mongolia People's Hospital and Tongliao People's Hospital, November 2019 to September 2023. Methods list 443 patients (training 270, internal test 68, external 105). Results list 338 participants (188 cancers and 150 controls) split into training 270 and validation 68, and a table also shows a cohort of 108.
data_modality_detail: MRI-transrectal ultrasound fusion B-mode images plus contrast-enhanced ultrasound time-intensity parameters.
algorithm: Radiomics deep-learning signature combining ultrasound images and contrast-enhanced ultrasound parameters. The network is not named.
input_features: Transrectal ultrasound radiomics, contrast-ultrasound wash-in parameters, PSA, and prostate size.
biomarker_result: Integrated MRI-guided ultrasound and contrast-enhanced ultrasound signature for prostate cancer.
performance_value: NR
validation_detail: Methods describe a second-hospital external cohort of 105 patients. No model metric is printed for that cohort, and the methods and results cohort totals do not match.
funding: Science and Technology Program of the Joint Fund of Scientific Research for the Public Hospitals of Inner Mongolia Academy of Medical Sciences (2023GLLH0020).
key_finding: The study sets out to predict prostate cancer from MRI-guided ultrasound radiomics and contrast-enhanced ultrasound in a two-hospital cohort, but no model performance number is printed.
other_key_outcomes: In training, age, PSA, prostate diameters, resistive index, and contrast-ultrasound area differed between benign and malignant groups.
extraction_note: Methods and results give different cohort totals (443 versus 338), and no AUC, accuracy, or C-index is printed.

title: Development of a deep learning system for predicting biochemical recurrence in prostate cancer.
study_design: Retrospective two-center digital-pathology cohort, with one hospital for training and another for testing.
data_source_detail: Training at Tianjin Medical University Cancer Institute and Hospital, 254 patients; testing at TBH, 63 patients. Overall 317 patients with five tumor-containing whole-slide images each (1585 images).
data_modality_detail: H&E prostate-biopsy whole-slide images. Inception-v3 patch features were pooled by multiple-instance learning.
algorithm: Inception-v3 patch encoder, multiple-instance learning with average pooling, and patient-level multilayer perceptron, logistic regression, and random forest.
input_features: Deep features from tumor patches on biopsy slides, aggregated to the patient.
biomarker_result: Biopsy whole-slide deep-learning system for biochemical recurrence before prostatectomy.
performance_value: Patient-level testing AUC 0.911 (95% CI 0.840-0.982). Patch-level Inception-v3 test AUC 0.803. Average-pooling patient-level AUC 0.908 with multilayer perceptron and logistic regression.
validation_detail: Training used 254 patients at one cancer hospital and testing used 63 patients at TBH. n_analytic is the external test cohort.
key_finding: A biopsy whole-slide deep-learning system predicted biochemical recurrence with external AUC 0.911, and performance rose when more slides per patient were included.
limitations_as_stated: Only patients with at least five tumor-containing biopsy cores were included, which introduces selection bias, and the cohort is retrospective.
other_key_outcomes: Random-forest slide-level AUC was 0.848. Decision-curve analysis was reported, and deep features were compared with pathologic findings.

title: Efficacy of PSMA PET/CT radiomics analysis for risk stratification in newly diagnosed prostate cancer: a multicenter study.
study_design: Retrospective four-center study, with development on two centers and a separate external set.
data_source_detail: 243 men with newly diagnosed prostate cancer and [68Ga]Ga-PSMA-11 PET/CT from Razavi Hospital (Mashhad), Khatam Hospital (Tehran), the Persian Gulf Nuclear Medicine Research Center (Bushehr), and Shariati Hospital (Tehran). Development used 186 cases from two centers; the external set had 57 cases.
data_modality_detail: PSMA PET/CT radiomics from avid intraprostatic lesions, the whole prostate on PET, and the whole prostate on CT.
algorithm: Principal-component reduction, then random forest, nearest centroid, SVM, a calibrated classifier with cross-validation, and logistic regression. Development used 10-fold cross-validation.
input_features: 1746 radiomic features per contour (PSMA-avid PET lesion, whole-prostate PET, whole-prostate CT, and concatenated PET/CT).
biomarker_result: PSMA PET/CT radiomics classifier for Gleason grade group (1-3 versus 4-5) and for PSA below versus at or above 20 ng/ml.
performance_value: External mean performance 73.8% for grade-group classification with random forest on PSMA-avid PET lesions; 73.7% for the calibrated classifier across internal and external sets. External mean performance for PSA classification was 76.4%.
validation_detail: Ten-fold cross-validation was used on 186 development cases from two centers. An external set of 57 cases supplied the external figure. The paper calls the quantity mean performance and does not name AUC or accuracy.
key_finding: PSMA PET radiomics separated Gleason grade groups 1-3 from 4-5 with external mean performance 73.8%, and classifier differences were not statistically significant.
limitations_as_stated: High Gleason scores above 7 were too few for subgroup analysis, and biopsy grade may not match the true tumor grade.
other_key_outcomes: Internal mean performance was 78% for grade group and 75.4% for the PSA split. Model differences were not significant (p>0.05).
extraction_note: External results are given as mean performance (73.8% and 73.7%) without stating whether that figure is AUC, accuracy, or another score.

title: Enhancing prediction accuracy for muscle invasion in bladder cancer using a dual-energy CT-based interpretable model incorporating habitat radiomics and deep learning.
study_design: Retrospective single-center cohort with a 7:3 training-test split.
data_source_detail: One hospital; 200 patients with bladder urothelial carcinoma and dual-energy CT (141 non-muscle-invasive, 59 muscle-invasive), training n=140 and test n=60.
data_modality_detail: Dual-energy CT iodine maps, habitat radiomics, and 2.5D deep learning.
algorithm: ResNet18, ResNet50, ResNet101, and DenseNet121 2.5D networks, four K-means habitats, and logistic regression on dual-energy parameters. The selected model combines effective atomic number, habitat features, and ResNet101 (DECT-DLH).
input_features: Effective atomic number, habitat radiomic features, and ResNet101 deep features from iodine-based images.
biomarker_result: DECT-DLH model for muscle-invasive bladder cancer.
performance_value: DECT-DLH test AUC 0.874 (95% CI 0.785-0.964) and training AUC 0.981 (95% CI 0.963-0.998). ResNet101 alone had test AUC 0.833 (95% CI 0.730-0.935).
validation_detail: Single-center 7:3 split (140/60). No external hospital cohort.
key_finding: A dual-energy CT model combining effective atomic number, habitat radiomics, and ResNet101 features predicted muscle invasion with test AUC 0.874.
limitations_as_stated: The 2.5D design is described as a compromise between 2D models that miss tumor context and 3D models that need more data.
other_key_outcomes: Effective atomic number was the only independent quantitative predictor (OR 0.619, 95% CI 0.424-0.902). SHAP was used to explain the model.

title: Evaluating the prognostic value of radiomics and clinical features in metastatic prostate cancer using [<sup>68</sup>Ga]Ga-PSMA-11 PET/CT.
study_design: Retrospective single-center prognostic cohort using bootstrap internal validation.
data_source_detail: Sir Charles Gairdner Hospital and the University of Western Australia. Of 238 patients enrolled, 180 with metastatic prostate cancer were analyzed using [68Ga]Ga-PSMA-11 PET/CT. Fifty-seven deaths were recorded.
data_modality_detail: PSMA PET/CT radiomics, mainly from the largest lesion, plus clinical variables.
algorithm: Univariable Cox models and LASSO Cox models (radiomics only, clinical only, and combined). Each multivariable model used six features and 1000 bootstrap resamples with optimism correction.
input_features: Eighty-nine radiomic features and eight clinical features, including lesion count, age, PSA, and Gleason score.
biomarker_result: Clinical Cox model for overall survival; radiomic features did not improve it.
performance_value: Optimism-corrected C-index 0.722 (95% CI 0.653-0.784) for the clinical model, 0.681 (95% CI 0.616-0.745) for radiomics, and 0.704 (95% CI 0.648-0.768) for the combined model. Lesion count HR 1.31 (95% CI 1.12-1.54).
validation_detail: Concordance was estimated by 1000-bootstrap optimism correction on one cohort of 180 patients. There is no held-out split, k-fold cross-validation, or external cohort.
key_finding: Many PSMA PET radiomic features were associated with overall survival, but adding them did not improve on the clinical model (C-index 0.722 versus 0.704 for the combined model).
limitations_as_stated: Some radiomic features may reflect imaging artifacts, and features from one or a few lesions may not represent the whole metastatic burden.
other_key_outcomes: The highest univariable radiomic C-indices were 0.707 for TLU, 0.704 for TLV, and 0.704 for GLDM dependence entropy. Lesion count had a clinical C-index of 0.654.
extraction_note: Validation is optimism-corrected bootstrap on a single cohort, which is neither a holdout split nor explicit k-fold cross-validation.

title: Evaluation of a PSA and transrectal prostate ultrasound video-based machine learning model as a tool for prostate cancer diagnosis.
study_design: Retrospective single-center cohort with a random 80:20 train-test split.
data_source_detail: Dongyang Hospital of Wenzhou Medical University, August 2021 to September 2023. 928 men (429 with prostate cancer and 499 without); training n=742 and test n=186.
data_modality_detail: Transrectal prostate ultrasound video features plus serum PSA.
algorithm: LightGBM, logistic regression, decision tree, SVM, random forest, and XGBoost, with SHAP applied to XGBoost.
input_features: Seven ultrasound-video features plus age, prostate volume, total PSA, and free PSA.
biomarker_result: XGBoost model using PSA and transrectal ultrasound video features for prostate-cancer diagnosis.
performance_value: Test-set AUC 0.800-0.881 across six models; XGBoost was the best (P<0.05).
validation_detail: Single-center random 80:20 split (742/186). No external cohort. The authors plan a later set from Zhejiang Cancer Hospital.
key_finding: Models using PSA and transrectal ultrasound video features detected prostate cancer with test AUCs from 0.800 to 0.881, and XGBoost performed best.
limitations_as_stated: The retrospective single-center sample limits generalizability, and prospective multicenter validation is still needed.
other_key_outcomes: SHAP ranked PSA, prostate volume, age, a wavelet first-order median, wavelet zone entropy, and minor-axis length as the leading XGBoost features.
extraction_note: The test AUC is reported as a range across models. XGBoost is identified as best without its own point estimate.

title: Fully automated segmentation and classification of renal tumors on CT scans via machine learning.
study_design: Single-center analysis of a prospectively enrolled nephrectomy registry, with separate training and test image sets.
data_source_detail: Seoul National University SUPER-RCC-Nx registry, March 2016 to December 2020. 561 renal masses: 233 clear-cell, 82 papillary, and 74 chromophobe RCCs, plus 172 angiomyolipomas. The subtype model used 389 RCCs; the benign-versus-malignant model used 391 masses of 4 cm or smaller.
data_modality_detail: Contrast-enhanced CT in precontrast, corticomedullary, and excretory phases.
algorithm: 3D U-Net for automated segmentation and a random-forest classifier using radiomic and conventional CT features.
input_features: Hounsfield-unit measurements and radiomic features taken from the U-Net tumor mask.
biomarker_result: Automated CT segmentation and random-forest classifier for RCC subtype and for benign versus malignant renal masses.
performance_value: Subtype accuracy 0.77 (95% CI 0.69-0.86) for tumors larger than 4 cm and 0.68 for smaller tumors; benign-versus-malignant accuracy 0.85 (95% CI 0.74-0.93).
validation_detail: One center with designated training and test sets. The test-set count is not printed. Reader cross-checking of annotations is not model cross-validation.
key_finding: A fully automated CT pipeline classified RCC subtypes with accuracy 0.77 for masses larger than 4 cm and separated benign from malignant small masses with accuracy 0.85.
limitations_as_stated: Only three RCC subtypes and angiomyolipoma were included, and enrollment from one center limits generalizability.
other_key_outcomes: Segmentation Dice was 0.83 above 4 cm and 0.65 below 4 cm. Adding conventional radiologic features changed benign-versus-malignant accuracy only from 0.83 to 0.85.
extraction_note: Accuracies are printed, but the training and test counts are not readable, so the sample size behind those accuracies is uncertain.

title: Integration of multi-scale radiomics and deep learning for Ki-67 prediction in clear cell renal carcinoma.
study_design: Retrospective three-center cohort with an internal split and a two-hospital external test set.
data_source_detail: 627 clear-cell RCC patients. First Hospital of Shanxi Medical University: training n=290 and internal validation n=125. Shanxi Bethune Hospital and Shanxi Provincial People's Hospital: external test n=212.
data_modality_detail: Preoperative CT multi-scale radiomics (intratumoral, habitat, and peritumoral) plus 2D/3D deep-learning features and clinical variables.
algorithm: Random forest, AdaBoost, XGBoost, LightGBM, and ExtraTrees unimodal models, stacked into a fusion model.
input_features: Intratumoral, peritumoral (1, 3, and 5 mm), and habitat CT radiomics, 2D/3D deep features, and clinical variables including platelet count, diameter, and hematuria.
biomarker_result: Stacked CT radiomics and deep-learning model for high Ki-67 in clear-cell RCC, using a 5% threshold.
performance_value: Fusion-model external AUC 0.756 (95% CI 0.692-0.821). On internal comparison, the 1 mm peritumoral model reached AUC 0.836 and the intratumoral AdaBoost model AUC 0.787.
validation_detail: One hospital was split 7:3 into training and internal validation. Two other hospitals supplied the external test set of 212 patients, which is n_analytic.
key_finding: A stacked CT radiomics and deep-learning model predicted high Ki-67 in clear-cell RCC with external AUC 0.756, with habitat radiomics the leading SHAP contributor.
limitations_as_stated: All centers were in Shanxi Province, the 5% Ki-67 cutoff is not universal, and multi-regional prospective validation is still needed.
other_key_outcomes: Internal peritumoral AUCs were 0.836 at 1 mm, 0.816 at 3 mm, and 0.782 at 5 mm. Platelet count, diameter, and hematuria were independent clinical predictors.
extraction_note: Feature-selection and modeling code is linked to the Onekey AI platform (https://github.com/OnekeyAI-Platform). Other study code is available from the corresponding author on request.

title: Interpretable multiparametric MRI radiomics-based machine learning model for preoperative differentiation between benign and malignant prostate masses: a diagnostic, multicenter study.
study_design: Retrospective two-hospital diagnostic cohort with internal and external test sets.
data_source_detail: Two hospitals, May 2016 to May 2023. 567 patients: training n=352, internal test n=152, and external test n=63.
data_modality_detail: Multiparametric MRI radiomics from T2-weighted and diffusion-weighted tumor regions.
algorithm: LASSO with five-fold cross-validation for feature selection, then five machine-learning models. Random forest was best. SHAP was used for interpretation. The other four algorithms are not named.
input_features: 2632 PyRadiomics features from T2-weighted and diffusion-weighted images, reduced to 18.
biomarker_result: Multiparametric MRI random-forest radiomics model for benign versus malignant prostate masses.
performance_value: Random-forest AUC 0.929 (95% CI 0.885-0.963) on the internal test set and 0.852 (95% CI 0.758-0.934) on the external test set.
validation_detail: Training and internal testing used the development hospital. The external test set had 63 patients from a second hospital, which is n_analytic. Five-fold cross-validation was used inside LASSO.
key_finding: An interpretable multiparametric MRI random-forest model distinguished benign from malignant prostate masses with external AUC 0.852.
other_key_outcomes: Calibration and decision-curve analysis supported clinical use, and SHAP ranked the leading radiomic features.

title: Intratumoral and peritumoral radiomics using multi-phase contrast-enhanced CT for diagnosis of renal oncocytoma and chromophobe renal cell carcinoma: a multicenter retrospective study.
study_design: Retrospective five-center cohort that was pooled and randomly split 70:30 into training and validation.
data_source_detail: Five centers; 92 patients (41 renal oncocytomas and 51 chromophobe RCCs). Training n=65 (29 oncocytoma, 36 chromophobe) and validation n=27 (12 oncocytoma, 15 chromophobe).
data_modality_detail: Corticomedullary and nephrographic contrast-enhanced CT, with intratumoral and 1-3 mm peritumoral radiomics.
algorithm: LASSO feature selection and SVM. Cross-validation is mentioned as a safeguard against overfitting in addition to the 70:30 split.
input_features: Intratumoral and peritumoral radiomic features from corticomedullary and nephrographic CT.
biomarker_result: SVM corticomedullary CT radiomics model (Model 4) separating renal oncocytoma from chromophobe RCC.
performance_value: Validation AUC 0.900 for Model 4 (sensitivity 88.89%, specificity 77.78%, accuracy 81.48%). Validation AUCs across models were 0.600-0.900; training AUCs were 0.828-0.942.
validation_detail: Five centers were pooled and randomly split 70:30, so the validation set is not an external-center holdout. The reported figure is that validation split (n=27).
funding: Basic Research Project of the Shenzhen Science and Technology Innovation Bureau, 2025 (Natural Science Foundation JCYJ20240813114631042).
key_finding: Corticomedullary CT radiomics SVM models separated renal oncocytoma from chromophobe RCC, with a best validation AUC of 0.900, above radiologist reads.
limitations_as_stated: Only 92 patients and 41 oncocytomas were available, CT protocols differed across centers, and the authors plan further external centers.
other_key_outcomes: Manual diagnosis accuracy was 52.27-59.78%. Clinical reports alone had no diagnostic value. Nephrographic and fusion models had lower validation AUCs, about 0.728-0.756.
extraction_note: Five centers contributed images, but they were pooled and randomly split, so validation is an internal holdout.

title: Machine learning models for discriminating clinically significant from clinically insignificant prostate cancer using bi-parametric magnetic resonance imaging
study_design: Retrospective single-institution lesion-level study with a training-test split made before augmentation.
data_source_detail: Istanbul University radiology practice, 2016-2022, with MRI/ultrasound fusion biopsy. Of 108 patients screened, 77 remained (47 clinically significant and 30 clinically insignificant cancers). Scanners were Siemens 1.5T and Philips 3.0T.
data_modality_detail: Biparametric MRI radiomics from axial T2-weighted and ADC images.
algorithm: Logistic regression and SVM after correlation filtering and wrapper-based sequential feature selection, using PyRadiomics with Laplacian-of-Gaussian filters.
input_features: Five T2-weighted features, five ADC features, and 15 combined features, drawn from 444 features per sequence.
biomarker_result: Biparametric MRI radiomics models separating clinically significant from clinically insignificant prostate cancer.
performance_value: Test AUC 0.86 (95% CI 0.85-0.88) for combined T2-weighted plus ADC features and 0.86 (95% CI 0.85-0.88) for ADC in one model series; logistic-regression combined test AUC 0.85 (95% CI 0.83-0.87).
validation_detail: Single institution, split into training and test groups before augmentation. The test-set size is not printed.
key_finding: Biparametric MRI radiomics separated clinically significant from insignificant prostate cancer, with combined-model test AUC about 0.85-0.86.
limitations_as_stated: Retrospective selection, manual segmentation, a small sample, and class imbalance that can favor the majority class.
other_key_outcomes: Logistic-regression combined test accuracy was 77%, and SVM combined test accuracy was 72%. T2-weighted-only test AUC in the same series was 0.64.
extraction_note: Test AUCs are printed, but the training and test counts are not, so the N behind the test AUC is uncertain. The 0.86 combined figure is taken from the model series reported before the logistic-regression AUCs.

title: Machine learning-based radiomics for bladder cancer staging: evaluating the role of imaging timing in differentiating T2 from T3 disease.
study_design: Retrospective single-center cohort using CT radiomics to separate intravesical (≤T2) from extravesical (≥T3) bladder cancer, with a comparison by the interval between TURB and CT.
data_source_detail: University Hospital Ulm, 2012-2020; 97 patients after exclusions (51 with ≥T3 disease). The delayed-imaging cohort (TURB at least 14 days before CT) was 55 training and 24 test patients.
data_modality_detail: Contrast-enhanced CT with full-volume 3D tumor segmentation and 77 IBSI radiomic features
algorithm: Random forest in scikit-learn, with grid-search tuning and the top 35 features retained
input_features: 3D CT shape, first-order, and GLCM texture features, plus preoperative creatinine, hemoglobin, and tumor size in the combined model
biomarker_result: CT radiomics and clinical-radiomics classifier of ≤T2 versus ≥T3 bladder cancer
performance_value: Fivefold cross-validation: radiomics-only AUC 0.68±0.08 in the full cohort and 0.80±0.08 when TURB preceded CT by more than 14 days; combined clinical-radiomics AUC 0.76 and 0.82 in those cohorts
validation_detail: The printed AUCs come from fivefold cross-validation. A 70:30 split is also described (full cohort 67/30; delayed cohort 55/24). There is no external center.
funding: The authors declare that no financial support was received for the research or publication.
key_finding: The combined clinical-radiomics CT model separated ≤T2 from ≥T3 bladder cancer with AUC 0.82 when imaging was delayed more than 14 days after TURB, higher than the radiomics-only AUC of 0.80 in that cohort.
limitations_as_stated: Findings come from a retrospective single-center cohort. The authors call for multicenter prospective validation and note that the analysis used CT rather than MRI.
other_key_outcomes: Age- and sex-specific sensitivity and specificity were also reported. The abstract calls cohort 1 the ≤14-day subgroup, while the methods treat cohort 1 as all 97 patients.
extraction_note: The abstract and methods disagree on whether cohort 1 is a timing subgroup or the full cohort. Analytic N follows the methods count for the delayed cohort (55+24) that supports AUC 0.82.

title: Machine learning-based radiomics from multiparametric MRI for predicting aggressive pathology in clear cell renal cell carcinoma.
study_design: Retrospective multicenter radiomics study distinguishing aggressive from indolent clear cell renal cell carcinoma on multiparametric MRI.
data_source_detail: First Affiliated Hospital of Nanchang University, Central Hospital of Jiangmen, and TCIA, pooled (n=157; 114 indolent and 43 aggressive).
data_modality_detail: T1WI, T2WI, and corticomedullary, nephrographic, and excretory contrast-enhanced fat-suppressed T1WI
algorithm: Random forest with ICAP selection, chosen from 8 classifiers and 21 feature-selection methods; SMOTE was applied inside training folds
input_features: Multiparametric MRI radiomic features, dominated by T2WI shape features
biomarker_result: T2WI radiomic classifier of aggressive ccRCC (WHO/ISUP grade 3-4, stage ≥pT3a, or sarcomatoid or dedifferentiated histology)
performance_value: RF+ICAP AUC 0.960 (accuracy 86.1%, sensitivity 86.4%, specificity 86.0%); the highest configuration, RF+CMIM on T2WI plus nephrographic and excretory phases, reached AUC 0.966 under fivefold cross-validation
validation_detail: Fivefold cross-validation on the pooled three-source cohort. TCIA was not held out as a separate external test.
funding: National Natural Science Foundation of China (82371908, 82572381, 62262029), GuangDong Natural Science Foundation (2024A1515012177, 2024A1515012100), and Jiangxi provincial support including 20242BAB25546.
key_finding: T2WI radiomics, especially shape features, separated aggressive from indolent ccRCC with a fivefold AUC of 0.960 for the RF+ICAP model.
limitations_as_stated: The retrospective design and only 43 aggressive cases limit generalizability. Fivefold cross-validation and SMOTE do not remove the risk of overfitting, and diffusion-weighted imaging was not included.
other_key_outcomes: Thirty-one sequence combinations were compared across 168 classifier-selector pairs. Three shape features each exceeded 75% unilateral accuracy at the median threshold.
extraction_note: Hospital MRI and TCIA cases were pooled in the same cross-validation, so the source is public plus own data.

title: Multi-channel multiphase CT-based deep learning and radiomics fusion model for noninvasive pathological grading of clear cell renal cell carcinoma.
study_design: Retrospective single-center study of a multichannel multiphase CT deep-learning and radiomics model for WHO/ISUP grade in clear cell renal cell carcinoma.
data_source_detail: First Affiliated Hospital of Harbin Medical University, June 2021 to December 2024; 496 patients randomly split 347 training and 149 testing.
data_modality_detail: Arterial, medullary, and excretory CT stacked as a multichannel input, including a 5 mm peritumoral expansion
algorithm: ResNet50 transfer learning fused with LASSO radiomics and a random-forest clinical-imaging model
input_features: Deep features from the 5 mm expanded multichannel ROI, radiomic features, and clinical variables; age was the only independent clinical associate of grade
biomarker_result: Clinical-radiomics-deep learning fusion model for high-grade (WHO/ISUP 3-4) versus low-grade ccRCC
performance_value: Combined model AUC 0.855 in training and 0.849 in the test cohort; ResNet50 with the 5 mm ROI had AUC 0.791 (95% CI 0.740-0.842) in training and 0.780 (95% CI 0.700-0.859) in testing
validation_detail: One 70/30 random split. LASSO used 10-fold selection, but the reported AUCs are on a single held-out test set. There is no external center.
funding: Foundation of the First Affiliated Hospital of Harbin Medical University (2023T01), provided by co-first author QC.
key_finding: Fusing multichannel multiphase CT deep features with radiomics and clinical variables predicted ccRCC grade with a test AUC of 0.849, above the ResNet50-only test AUC of 0.780.
limitations_as_stated: The cohort is retrospective and single-center. The authors state that multi-center external validation across scanners and protocols is still required.
other_key_outcomes: A random-forest radiomics model had AUC 0.849 in training and 0.831 in testing. Decision-curve analysis favored the combined model.
extraction_note: Analytic N is the 149-patient test set that supports the combined-model AUC of 0.849.

title: Multicenter study demonstrates unsupervised learning derived from magnetic resonance images identify prognosis in prostate cancer patients after prostatectomy
study_design: Retrospective three-center study using unsupervised clustering of preoperative MRI radiomics and clinical features to stratify progression-free survival after radical prostatectomy.
data_source_detail: Three centers totaling 400 patients: training n=212, external validation group 1 n=111, and external validation group 2 n=77.
data_modality_detail: Preoperative MRI radiomics plus clinical variables; contrast-enhanced contours were not used
algorithm: LASSO-Cox feature selection followed by K-means clustering
input_features: Five clinical features and 13 MRI radiomic features
biomarker_result: Radiomic-Clinical three-subgroup model for post-prostatectomy progression-free survival
performance_value: Radiomic-Clinical C-index 0.82 in training, 0.78 in external group 1, and 0.79 in external group 2, compared with EAU 0.68/0.70/0.65, CAPRA 0.71/0.67/0.70, and PIPEN 0.71/0.70/0.68
validation_detail: Center 1 developed the clusters. Centers 2 and 3 were separate external validation sets, and 5-year progression-free survival differed across clusters in both.
funding: National Cancer Center of China, grant NCC201909B03.
key_finding: Unsupervised radiomic-clinical clustering separated post-prostatectomy progression-free survival with C-indices of 0.82, 0.78, and 0.79, above EAU, CAPRA, and PIPEN in the same cohorts.
limitations_as_stated: The study is retrospective and may have selection bias. Enhanced images were not outlined, regions of interest were manual, and the external sets were relatively small.
other_key_outcomes: Cluster 3 had the worst and cluster 1 the best 5-year progression-free survival in training and both external groups. This record is a Research Square preprint.
extraction_note: Analytic N is the training cohort of 212 that supports the lead C-index of 0.82. External C-indices are reported with their own sample sizes.

title: Multimodal deep learning framework integrating multiphase CT and histopathological whole slide imaging for predicting recurrence in ccRCC.
study_design: Retrospective single-center multimodal study predicting postoperative recurrence of clear cell renal cell carcinoma from multiphase CT and histopathology whole-slide images.
data_source_detail: Jiangmen Central Hospital; 274 patients split 164 training and 110 test (6:4), with at least 3 years of follow-up for recurrence versus non-recurrence.
data_modality_detail: Multiphase CT (precontrast, corticomedullary, and nephrographic) fused with H&E whole-slide images
algorithm: CPNet cross-modal fusion of CT and pathology deep features
input_features: Precontrast-phase CT features fused with histopathological whole-slide features
biomarker_result: PCP-Pathology Fuse CPNet model for postoperative recurrence versus non-recurrence
performance_value: Test-set PCP-Pathology Fuse AUC 0.8363, sensitivity 0.8611, specificity 0.7027, and accuracy 75.45% (83/110); the three-phase fusion model had test AUC 0.8341
validation_detail: Single 6:4 split of one center. Table 2 labels these AUCs as test-set performance. The authors state that external multi-institutional validation is still required.
funding: Guangdong Basic and Applied Basic Research Foundation (2021A1515220080) and Jiangmen Science and Technology Plan Program (2024YL01033).
key_finding: The precontrast CT plus pathology CPNet model predicted postoperative ccRCC recurrence on the internal test set with AUC 0.8363 and accuracy 75.45%, similar to a three-phase fusion model.
limitations_as_stated: The retrospective single-center cohort is geographically homogeneous. Clinical comorbidities and molecular markers were omitted, and slide selection may introduce bias.
other_key_outcomes: Test-set AUCs were 0.7965 for corticomedullary-pathology fusion and 0.798 for nephrographic-pathology fusion. CPNet improved on unimodal CT and whole-slide models.
extraction_note: Analytic N is the 110-patient test set in Table 2, which reports AUC 0.8363.

title: Multimodal fusion radiomic-immunologic scoring model: accurate identification of prostate cancer progression.
study_design: Retrospective single-center cohort combining mpMRI radiomics and CD3/CD8 immunohistochemistry to classify prostate cancer progression.
data_source_detail: Second Affiliated Hospital of Chongqing Medical University, diagnoses 2019-2022. The methods enroll 157 patients (43 with progression and 114 without). The performance table lists training n=141 and validation n=59.
data_modality_detail: mpMRI radiomics from T2WI, DWI, and ADC plus quantitative CD3-positive and CD8-positive immunohistochemistry
algorithm: Logistic regression after AIC, mRMR, and LASSO; the limitations also mention SMOTE
input_features: Selected radiomic features and CD3/CD8 immunologic features combined as a radiomic-immunologic score
biomarker_result: Radiomic-Immunologic Score (RDIS) for prostate cancer progression
performance_value: Validation RDIS AUC 0.874 (sensitivity 0.960, specificity 0.765), versus radiomic AUC 0.844 and immunologic AUC 0.767; training RDIS AUC 0.911 (95% CI 0.866-0.956)
validation_detail: A 7:3 stratified split produced the validation AUC. Tenfold cross-validation was used for LASSO selection rather than as the reported performance. There is no external cohort.
funding: Science and Health Joint Medical Research Project of Chongqing (2024ZDXM004). Additional Chongqing Natural Science support is declared, but the grant number is not cleanly separated from the reference list.
key_finding: The combined radiomic-immunologic score identified prostate cancer progression with a validation AUC of 0.874, above the radiomic-only (0.844) and immunologic-only (0.767) models.
limitations_as_stated: This was a retrospective single-center study without external validation. Progression was a binary endpoint, and the median 36-month follow-up may miss later events.
other_key_outcomes: Secondary RDIS AUCs were 0.642 for bone metastasis (n=12) and 0.605 for castration-resistant disease (n=11).
extraction_note: Enrollment is stated as 157 patients, but the performance table sums to 200 (141 training and 59 validation). Analytic N follows the validation column that reports AUC 0.874.

title: Radiogenomic correlation of hypoxia-related biomarkers in clear cell renal cell carcinoma.
study_design: Radiogenomic correlation study linking clinical CT texture to hypoxia-related gene expression in clear cell renal cell carcinoma.
data_source_detail: TCGA-KIRC expression with matched CT from The Cancer Imaging Archive; 190 patients with both imaging and genomic data.
data_modality_detail: Clinical CT radiomics correlated with RNA expression of 13 hypoxia-related genes
algorithm: High-performance random forest in SAS Enterprise Miner 15.1
input_features: 388 robust radiomic features with ICC at least 0.70, especially GLDM and GLCM texture, drawn from 2,824 extracted features
biomarker_result: CT radiomic correlates of KLF6, ETS1, BCL2, PLOD2, and PPARGC1A expression
performance_value: Unstratified random-forest Pearson r was 0.27 (95% CI 0.14-0.41) for KLF6, 0.25 (0.11-0.39) for ETS1, 0.19 (0.05-0.33) for BCL2, -0.19 for PLOD2, and -0.15 for PPARGC1A; high-grade KLF6 r was 0.35 (0.14-0.56)
validation_detail: Tenfold cross-validation inside the single TCGA-KIRC imaging cohort. There is no independent external cohort.
funding: The study received no research funding. Open-access charges were supported by SCELC.
conflicts_of_interest: Vinay A. Duddalwar reports consulting fees from Radmetrix, Roche, Deeptek, and Westat. The other authors declared no relevant financial interests.
key_finding: Random-forest models found modest correlations between CT texture and hypoxia-gene expression, strongest for KLF6 (r=0.27 overall and r=0.35 in high-grade tumors).
limitations_as_stated: The sample is limited to TCGA-KIRC cases with usable imaging, is predominantly White and male, lacks external validation, and uses whole-tumor features without biopsy-site matching.
other_key_outcomes: Stratified models improved prediction of RORA, BCL2, and KLF6 in high-grade tumors. The endpoint is expression correlation rather than a clinical classification AUC.
extraction_note: No AUC, C-index, accuracy, or sensitivity-specificity pair is printed. The performance field records the Pearson correlations from the random-forest model.

title: Reproducibility of MRI-derived radiomic features in prostate cancer detection: a methodological approach.
study_design: Methodologic retrospective study of MRI radiomic reproducibility and machine-learning classification of prostate cancer versus controls.
data_source_detail: 82 MRI examinations, 41 with prostate cancer and 41 controls.
data_modality_detail: T2-weighted and ADC radiomic features extracted with SERA (215 features)
algorithm: Ten classifiers, including SVM, random forest, neural networks, logistic regression, CatBoost, and AdaBoost, after PCA and other dimensionality-reduction methods
input_features: T2-weighted and ADC radiomic features with ICC above 0.75, reduced mainly by PCA
biomarker_result: Reproducibility-filtered MRI radiomic classifier of cancer versus non-cancer prostate
performance_value: AUC up to 0.93 and accuracy 0.88-0.9 for SVM, neural networks, and logistic regression using good and excellent reproducibility features
validation_detail: Tenfold cross-validation on the 82-case cohort. There is no external test set.
funding: None. Financial support and sponsorship are stated as none.
key_finding: Radiomic features with ICC above 0.75 classified prostate cancer versus controls with accuracy 0.88-0.9 and AUC up to 0.93, and PCA was the most stable reduction method.
limitations_as_stated: The dataset has only 82 individuals, and clinical variables such as age, PSA, and prostate volume were excluded.
other_key_outcomes: Some algorithm and reduction pairs were unstable, including accuracy of 0.10 for k-nearest neighbors with an autoencoder. Reproducibility is the paper's main theme.
extraction_note: The peak AUC is reported as up to 0.93 rather than one model-specific point estimate.

title: Subregion-based radiomics analysis for predicting the histological grade of clear cell renal cell carcinoma.
study_design: Retrospective subregion radiomics study predicting histologic grade of clear cell renal cell carcinoma, with an internal split of public CT and a local external set.
data_source_detail: TCIA discovery cohort of 186 patients, split 7:3 into training and internal test, plus a local-hospital external set (methods n=64, July 2016-December 2023; the abstract says 65).
data_modality_detail: Parenchymal-phase contrast-enhanced CT radiomics from the whole tumor and two intratumoral subregions
algorithm: Logistic regression and support vector machine on subregion radiomic scores
input_features: Subregion radiomic features; the radscore used three candidate features from subregion VOI1
biomarker_result: Subregion CT radscore for high-grade versus low-grade ccRCC, with cutoff 0.576
performance_value: Logistic regression and SVM AUCs 0.74 and 0.77 on the external set, and 0.78 and 0.77 on the internal test set
validation_detail: TCIA was split internally 7:3. One local hospital supplied the external test. Those local cases validate the model, so the source is public plus own data.
funding: Internal Research Fund of The Third Affiliated Hospital of Chongqing Medical University (KY24041).
key_finding: Subregion CT radiomics classified ccRCC histologic grade with external AUCs of 0.74 and 0.77, close to the internal-test AUCs of 0.78 and 0.77.
limitations_as_stated: The sample is small, especially the external set. Differences in scanners, reconstruction, and contrast timing across centers may change the radiomic features.
other_key_outcomes: Weighted gene co-expression analysis linked radiomic-feature genes to migration, adhesion, and signaling. The radscore also separated some overall-survival groups.
extraction_note: Analytic N is the external set of 64 patients in the methods. The abstract states 65 local patients.

title: The interpretable CT-based vision transformer model for preoperative prediction of clear cell renal cell carcinoma SSIGN score and outcome.
study_design: Retrospective multicenter study of an interpretable CT vision-transformer model for preoperative SSIGN score and progression-free survival in clear cell renal cell carcinoma.
data_source_detail: 845 patients: training 592 from five hospitals and test 253 from three hospitals.
data_modality_detail: Corticomedullary-phase and renal parenchymal-phase contrast-enhanced CT, using the largest cross-section resized to 224 by 224 pixels
algorithm: Pretrained Google ViT-base-patch16-224 features in a combined two-phase model, interpreted with SHAP
input_features: 768 vision-transformer features from each of the corticomedullary and renal parenchymal phases
biomarker_result: Combined corticomedullary and renal parenchymal vision-transformer model (CRVM) for SSIGN and progression-free survival
performance_value: Test-cohort SSIGN AUC 0.895 for the combined model (0.859 corticomedullary-only and 0.883 parenchymal-only); test-cohort progression-free survival C-index 0.840 (0.719 and 0.773 for the single-phase models)
validation_detail: Test patients came from three hospitals and training patients from five hospitals. Cross-validation is not described for the reported test metrics.
funding: Taishan Scholar Foundation of Shandong Province (tsqn202408392) and the Science and Technology Project of the Southern District of Qingdao (2022-2-008-YY).
conflicts_of_interest: Y.W. is affiliated with GE Healthcare. The remaining authors declared no competing interests.
key_finding: The combined CT vision-transformer model predicted SSIGN on the multicenter test set with AUC 0.895 and progression-free survival with C-index 0.840.
limitations_as_stated: The study is retrospective, and scans from different scanners may affect transformer features. Clinical and conventional CT features were not fully integrated.
other_key_outcomes: The combined model also had training SSIGN AUC 0.895. Decision-curve analysis favored it over the single-phase models. The cited vision-transformer repository is the public backbone, not study code.
extraction_note: AUC for SSIGN is the primary metric, and the progression-free survival C-index is co-reported. Analytic N is the 253-patient test cohort.

title: The predictive value of radiomics and deep learning for synchronous distant metastasis in clear cell renal cell carcinoma.
study_design: Retrospective two-center study of CT radiomics and deep learning for synchronous distant metastasis in clear cell renal cell carcinoma.
data_source_detail: Training at Gansu Provincial People's Hospital, January 2019 to February 2024 (n=143, including 58 with synchronous metastasis). Validation at Gansu Second People's Hospital (n=62, including 19 with metastasis).
data_modality_detail: Contrast-enhanced CT, with 3D radiomics and a largest-cross-section deep-learning crop
algorithm: LASSO radiomics with a support vector machine, fused with ResNet101
input_features: 15 LASSO-selected features from 944 CT radiomic features, plus ResNet101 image features
biomarker_result: Combined CT radiomics and ResNet101 model for synchronous distant metastasis
performance_value: SVM AUC 0.860 (95% CI 0.789-0.931) in training and 0.813 (0.694-0.931) in validation; ResNet101 AUC 0.815 and 0.743; combined model AUC 0.863 (95% CI 0.804-0.921)
validation_detail: One external hospital supplied the 62-patient validation set. The combined AUC of 0.863 is not explicitly assigned to training or validation.
funding: Natural Science Foundation of Gansu Province (22JR5RA650) and Gansu Provincial Hospital Scientific Research Foundation (23GSSYD-12).
key_finding: An SVM radiomics model predicted synchronous distant metastasis with validation AUC 0.813, and a fused radiomics-deep learning model reached AUC 0.863.
limitations_as_stated: As a retrospective study, the model indicates whether metastasis is present rather than its probability. The validation sample is small, and CT parameter differences limit use across devices.
other_key_outcomes: The authors thank the Onekey AI platform for technical support. Decision-curve analysis favored the combined model.
extraction_note: The validation SVM AUC is tied to 62 patients. The combined AUC of 0.863 has no cohort label, so the N for that headline figure is uncertain.

title: The role of endothelial cell-related gene COL1A1 in prostate cancer diagnosis and immunotherapy: insights from machine learning and single-cell analysis.
study_design: Bioinformatic machine-learning study of endothelial-cell genes in prostate adenocarcinoma, with a diagnostic model and orthogonal tissue staining.
data_source_detail: TCGA-PRAD training used 498 tumors and 52 normal samples. External sets were GSE14206, GSE46602, GSE6956, and GSE71016, with single-cell data from GSE141445. Immunofluorescence used 100 cancers and 50 adjacent samples from Shanghai Outdo Biotech.
data_modality_detail: Bulk RNA-seq for the diagnostic model, with single-cell RNA-seq used to nominate endothelial genes
algorithm: Screen of 108 machine-learning combinations; XGBoost and random forest highlighted COL1A1
input_features: Endothelial-cell-related gene expression, reduced to a diagnostic panel in which COL1A1 was prominent
biomarker_result: COL1A1-centered endothelial diagnostic signature for prostate adenocarcinoma
performance_value: TCGA-PRAD training AUC 0.917; external AUCs 0.693 (GSE14206), 0.742 (GSE46602), 0.808 (GSE6956), and 0.715 (GSE71016)
validation_detail: Four GEO cohorts externally tested the diagnostic model. Multiplex immunofluorescence and cell-line knockdown are orthogonal and were not used to train the model.
funding: Nantong Health Commission (ONZ2023055, MS2023063, and MS2022041) and the Nantong University Clinical Medicine Special Research fund.
key_finding: Endothelial-gene models diagnosed prostate adenocarcinoma with a TCGA AUC of 0.917, and external GEO AUCs ranged from 0.693 to 0.808, with COL1A1 as a leading gene.
other_key_outcomes: Endothelial-gene clusters were associated with prognosis and immunotherapy response. Immunofluorescence linked COL1A1 with AR and EGFR, and knockdown reduced malignant behavior in cell lines.
extraction_note: Analytic N is the TCGA diagnostic set of 498 tumors plus 52 normal samples that supports AUC 0.917. Source data are public even though the authors say no new datasets were generated.

title: Unsupervised learning-based quantitative analysis of CT intratumoral subregions predicts risk stratification of bladder cancer patients.
study_design: Retrospective two-center study using unsupervised CT subregion radiomics to predict muscle invasion and AJCC stage in bladder cancer.
data_source_detail: Center A training n=778 (2006-2022) and center B external validation n=239 (2018-2022), for 1,017 patients.
data_modality_detail: Venous-phase CT radiomics of the whole tumor and three unsupervised intratumoral subregions
algorithm: Unsupervised clustering of tumor subregions followed by nested cross-validated radiomics models, including a fusion model
input_features: Radiomic features from the whole tumor and three subregions, fused with clinicopathological variables
biomarker_result: Fusion intratumoral-subregion CT model for muscle invasion and AJCC stage
performance_value: External fusion-model AUROC 0.884 (95% CI 0.842-0.926) for muscle invasion and 0.832 (95% CI 0.768-0.897) for AJCC stage
validation_detail: Nested cross-validation was used during development at center A. The reported AUROCs are from one independent external center.
funding: National Natural Science Foundation of China (82271993 and 82471978).
key_finding: An unsupervised CT subregion fusion model predicted muscle-invasive bladder cancer with external AUROC 0.884 and AJCC stage with external AUROC 0.832.
limitations_as_stated: The retrospective design may bias comparisons between centers. Venous-phase CT alone may miss intratumoral heterogeneity, and prospective confirmation is needed.
other_key_outcomes: The merged subregion model outperformed the whole-tumor model. Code is available at https://github.com/Leon-skops/Unsupervised-learning-based-quantitative-analysis-for-bladder-cancer.
extraction_note: Analytic N is the external cohort of 239 that supports both AUROCs. Muscle invasion is co-reported with the AJCC risk-stratification task named in the title.

title: A perioperative multi-modal fusion and deep learning-based prognostic system for upper tract urothelial carcinoma: a multi-institutional study.
study_design: Retrospective six-center study of a perioperative multimodal model for overall survival after radical nephroureterectomy for upper tract urothelial carcinoma.
data_source_detail: 623 patients: centers 1-2 split into training n=331 and internal validation n=142; external validation n=150 from centers 3-6.
data_modality_detail: Baseline CT urography radiomics and 2D and 2.5D deep-learning features, plus perioperative clinical data
algorithm: Fusion of clinical, radiomics, 2D ResNet-50, and 2.5D ResNet-50 prognostic scores
input_features: Perioperative clinical variables and CT-urography radiomic and deep-learning features
biomarker_result: Combined clinical-radiomics-deep learning score for overall survival in upper tract urothelial carcinoma
performance_value: External combined-model C-index 0.704 (95% CI 0.631-0.777); internal validation 0.725 (0.651-0.798); training 0.758 (0.712-0.804); external 3-year AUC 0.766
validation_detail: The external set came from four additional centers. In training, the 2.5D ResNet-50 C-index was 0.705 versus 0.681 for the 2D model.
funding: Graduate Education and Teaching Reform Project of the First Affiliated Hospital of Chongqing Medical University (jgxm-202502) and that hospital's Medical Health Care Ecosystem Innovation Team.
key_finding: A fused clinical, radiomic, and CT deep-learning model predicted overall survival after nephroureterectomy with an external C-index of 0.704 and a 3-year AUC of 0.766.
limitations_as_stated: All data were retrospective, CT urography protocols differed across centers, and adjuvant treatment and clinical N stage were too incomplete to include.
other_key_outcomes: The combined model had higher decision-curve net benefit than single-modality models. The intended use is perioperative risk stratification for surveillance or adjuvant therapy.
extraction_note: Analytic N is the external set of 150 that supports the external C-index of 0.704.

title: CT-based radiogenomic prediction of ICAM1 and RAET1E as biomarkers of NK cytotoxicity in clear cell renal cell carcinoma.
study_design: Radiogenomic study predicting ICAM1 and RAET1E expression, as NK-cytotoxicity markers, from CT in clear cell renal cell carcinoma.
data_source_detail: TCGA-KIRC provided 538 tumor transcriptomes, of which 143 had matched contrast-enhanced CT. Independent immunohistochemistry used 26 ccRCC cases.
data_modality_detail: PyRadiomics features (3,176 per tumor) from preoperative contrast-enhanced CT linked to TCGA RNA expression
algorithm: L1-regularized support vector machine with leave-one-out cross-validation
input_features: CT radiomic features selected for association with ICAM1 and RAET1E expression strata
biomarker_result: CT radiogenomic predictors of ICAM1 and RAET1E
performance_value: ICAM1 AUC 0.757 and RAET1E AUC 0.673, also printed as AUROC 0.76 and 0.68 with accuracies 0.71 and 0.66; external IHC accuracy 76.92% (sensitivity 100%, specificity 53.85%) for ICAM1 and 73.08% (sensitivity 100%, specificity 46.15%) for RAET1E
validation_detail: Leave-one-out cross-validation was used on 143 TCGA cases with CT. An independent 26-patient immunohistochemistry cohort tested protein-level predictions and was not used for training.
funding: Financial support was declared from the Suzhou Key Laboratory for Integrated research. The grant identifiers are split across the PDF columns and are not recovered as a clean list.
key_finding: CT radiomics predicted ICAM1 and RAET1E expression with AUCs of 0.757 and 0.673, and an independent immunohistochemistry set had accuracies of 76.92% and 73.08% with sensitivity of 100% and specificity near 50%.
limitations_as_stated: The authors attribute the external result to the small validation sample of 26, class imbalance, and possible overfitting of an exploratory single-center set.
other_key_outcomes: Both genes were linked to NK-cell context and survival differences in TCGA. Sensitivity of 100% with specificity near one half on 26 cases is unstable.
extraction_note: The same AUCs are printed both as percentages (75.7% and 67.3%) and as proportions (0.76 and 0.68). External sensitivity of 100% on 26 cases needs review. Own immunohistochemistry does not change the model source from TCGA.

title: Combined radiomics, PI-RADS, and clinical model improve significant prostate cancer prediction and guide biopsy decision.
study_design: Retrospective observational study combining MRI radiomics, PI-RADS, and clinical variables to detect significant prostate cancer and estimate avoided biopsies.
data_source_detail: 1,497 MRI cases from 1,395 men, randomly split into training n=1,194 (80%) and test n=303 (20%). Biopsy was the reference, and significant cancer was Gleason grade group 2 or higher.
data_modality_detail: Handcrafted radiomic features from automatically segmented prostate glands, plus the index-lesion PI-RADS score and six clinical variables
algorithm: Machine-learning comparison of radiomics, PI-RADS, PI-RADS plus radiomics, and the full clinical model, with SHAP explanation
input_features: Whole-gland MRI radiomics, PI-RADS, and clinical variables
biomarker_result: Radiomics plus PI-RADS plus clinical model for significant prostate cancer
performance_value: Test AUC 0.891 (95% CI 0.853-0.930) for radiomics plus PI-RADS plus clinical variables, versus radiomics 0.838 (0.792-0.884) and PI-RADS 0.833 (0.788-0.878)
validation_detail: One 80/20 random split. Cross-validation and an external cohort are not described for the reported AUCs.
funding: European project FLUTE, funded under Horizon Europe HORIZON-HLTH2022-IND-13.
conflicts_of_interest: C.P.L., A.J.P., and A.N.I. are employed by Quibim S.L. A.J.P. is a member of the Scientific Editorial Board of Insights into Imaging.
key_finding: Adding radiomics and clinical variables to PI-RADS raised significant-cancer discrimination to a test AUC of 0.891, above PI-RADS alone at 0.833.
limitations_as_stated: Deep radiomics and lesion-mask features were not tested, and the differences in specificity and avoided biopsies were not statistically significant.
other_key_outcomes: At a fixed sensitivity of 97.4%, specificity was 29.41% and the biopsy-avoidance rate was 18.15% (p=0.313). Part of the cohort overlaps a 2022 Barcelona clinical prediction model.
extraction_note: Analytic N is the 303-case test partition. The unit is images because 1,497 examinations came from 1,395 men.

title: Deep learning models built from PSMA PET of the primary tumor can predict synchronous and metachronous prostate cancer metastases.
study_design: Retrospective single-center deep-learning study using primary-tumor PSMA PET to predict synchronous metastases and later metastatic progression.
data_source_detail: VA Greater Los Angeles; 94 patients split into training 47, validation 19, and test 28.
data_modality_detail: 18F-DCFPyL PSMA PET of the primary tumor with auto-segmented intraprostatic lesions, plus clinicopathologic variables
algorithm: Modified 3D SqueezeNetv2 combined with clinicopathologic and imaging parameters
input_features: Two-channel 3D cuboid of the prostate PET volume and lesion mask, plus clinical variables
biomarker_result: Multimodal PSMA-PET model for synchronous and metachronous prostate cancer metastases
performance_value: Multimodal AUC 0.839 (95% CI 0.676-1.000) for metachronous metastatic progression, versus CNN-only AUC 0.723 (0.497-0.949). Synchronous AUCs of 0.82 and 0.72 are printed with the CNN and multimodal labels swapped between sentences
validation_detail: Stratified 50/20/30 train, validation, and test split of one center. There is no cross-validation and no external cohort.
funding: Cooperative Research and Development Agreement between VA Greater Los Angeles and Lantheus. The funder supported salaries for authors who contributed to the CNN code.
conflicts_of_interest: Dr. Nickols reported grants from Janssen, Lantheus, and Bayer and personal fees from PrimeFour. Dr. Rettig reported speaking or consulting relationships with several companies, including Amgen and Johnson & Johnson, outside the submitted work.
key_finding: A multimodal model trained on primary-tumor PSMA PET predicted later metastatic progression with AUC 0.839 on the internal test set.
limitations_as_stated: The authors cite the modest sample, single-center source, and risk of overfitting, and they request validation in a larger cohort.
other_key_outcomes: For metachronous progression, the multimodal AUC also exceeded CAPRA (0.742) and the UCLA PSMA Risk Score (0.677). Identifiable health information will not be shared.
extraction_note: Two results sentences exchange which of the CNN and multimodal models has synchronous-metastasis AUC 0.82 versus 0.72. The metachronous AUC of 0.839 is consistent and is assigned to the 28-patient test set.

title: Developing an interpretable clinical-radiomics machine learning model using whole transition zone MRI analysis for improving diagnosis of transition zone prostate cancer.
study_design: Retrospective two-center study of a biparametric-MRI clinical-radiomics model for transition-zone prostate cancer versus benign prostatic hyperplasia.
data_source_detail: Center A in Hangzhou contributed 203 patients (training 142 and internal validation 61). Center B in Ningbo contributed external validation n=77.
data_modality_detail: Whole transition-zone T2-weighted and ADC radiomics from biparametric MRI
algorithm: Support vector machine radiomics model combined with clinical variables and interpreted with SHAP
input_features: Whole-transition-zone ADC and T2-weighted radiomic features plus clinical variables including total PSA
biomarker_result: Clinical-radiomics model for transition-zone prostate cancer versus benign prostatic hyperplasia
performance_value: Clinical-radiomics AUC 0.963 (95% CI 0.897-1.000) in training, 0.889 (95% CI 0.786-0.991) in internal validation, and 0.829 in external validation; SVM using ADC plus T2WI had AUC 0.865 in training and 0.850 in internal validation
validation_detail: Center A was randomly split, and that internal set was used for model selection. Center B is one independent external cohort. The authors emphasize the external AUC of 0.829.
funding: Medical Health Science and Technology Project of the Zhejiang Provincial Health Commission (2025KY1161, 2025KY1160, 2025KY1217) and Zhejiang Traditional Chinese Medicine Science and Technology Program (2024ZL668).
key_finding: A whole-transition-zone clinical-radiomics model distinguished transition-zone prostate cancer from benign hyperplasia with an external AUC of 0.829.
limitations_as_stated: The retrospective two-center design may introduce selection bias. Segmentation was manual, stromal versus glandular hyperplasia was not analyzed, and internal-validation performance may be mildly optimistic because it was used for model selection.
other_key_outcomes: On internal validation the combined AUC of 0.889 exceeded the clinical and radiomics-only models, which were about 0.850.
extraction_note: Analytic N is the external set of 77 that supports AUC 0.829. The internal combined AUC confidence interval is 0.786-0.991 from the results table.

title: Integrating single-cell analysis and machine learning algorithms to explore lactylation-related molecular mechanisms and therapeutic responses in clear cell renal cell carcinoma and identifying CDT1 as a potential biomarker.
study_design: Integrative single-cell and bulk-transcriptomic machine-learning study of lactylation-related prognosis in clear cell renal cell carcinoma, with experimental follow-up of CDT1.
data_source_detail: TCGA-KIRC bulk RNA-seq from 529 patients for training; external GSE29609 and E-MTAB-1980; single-cell transcriptomes used to derive lactylation programs. In vitro and in vivo CDT1 assays are orthogonal.
data_modality_detail: Bulk RNA-seq prognostic modeling informed by single-cell lactylation scores
algorithm: 101 combinations of 10 algorithms, including LASSO, ridge, random survival forest, and elastic net, with 10-fold cross-validation for the penalty
input_features: Lactylation-related expression reduced to a 13-gene risk score centered on CDT1
biomarker_result: Lactylation-related prognostic risk score with CDT1 as the core biomarker
performance_value: Selected random survival forest plus elastic net (alpha 0.1) C-index 0.710 across cohorts (training 0.686; external range 0.672-0.771, with 0.771 in one independent set); a 50% TCGA internal split remained at C-index 0.677; TCGA time-dependent AUCs were 0.72, 0.71, and 0.70
validation_detail: GEO and ArrayExpress ccRCC cohorts externally tested the score. Tenfold cross-validation chose the penalty, and a 50% TCGA holdout gave C-index 0.677. Knockdown experiments did not train the model.
funding: National Natural Science Foundation of China (82402695 and 82402683); the funding statement continues with additional grants.
key_finding: A lactylation-related machine-learning score had a cross-cohort C-index of 0.710 and nominated CDT1, whose knockdown reduced invasion and changed intracellular lactate.
limitations_as_stated: The score is inferred from transcriptomic programs. The authors note that direct lactylation assays, such as pan-lactyl-lysine or site-specific chromatin assays, were not the basis of the model.
other_key_outcomes: LASSO and ridge had C-indices of 0.706 and 0.713, but random survival forest plus elastic net was preferred for balance across cohorts. GSE29609 time-dependent AUCs were about 0.68.
extraction_note: C-index is the algorithm-selection metric. Analytic N is the 529-patient TCGA training set that supports the training C-index of 0.686 within the reported 0.710 summary.

title: Multimodal deep learning for prediction of postoperative recurrence in clear cell renal cell carcinoma: a clinical-radiologic-pathologic approach.
study_design: Retrospective multicenter clinical, radiologic, and pathologic deep-learning study of 5-year postoperative recurrence in clear cell renal cell carcinoma.
data_source_detail: 270 patients from three hospitals: 215 from hospitals A and B for development and 55 from hospital C for independent testing. The characteristics table lists 175, 40, and 55 patients.
data_modality_detail: Clinical variables with non-enhanced CT, ultrasound, and pathology radiomics and ResNet features
algorithm: Logistic regression, random forest, and boosting radiomics models plus ResNet, fused after 5-fold out-of-fold scoring
input_features: Radiomic and deep-learning scores from CT, ultrasound, and pathology, combined with clinical features
biomarker_result: Multi-modality radiomics-deep learning model for 5-year postoperative ccRCC recurrence
performance_value: Independent-test AUROC 0.967 (95% CI 0.929-1.0) for the fused model; a non-enhanced fused model had AUROC 0.837 (95% CI 0.729-0.946)
validation_detail: Hospital C (n=55) is an independent external test. Five-fold cross-validation generated out-of-fold scores during development.
funding: Natural Science Foundation of Shandong Province (ZR2023MH042), Shandong Provincial Healthcare Workers' Technological Innovation Collaborative Project (SDYWZGKCJHLH202434), and Qingdao Key Clinical Specialty Project Fund (QDZDZK-2024-067).
conflicts_of_interest: Authors J.W. and F.S. are employed by United Imaging Intelligence. The remaining authors declared no commercial or financial conflict.
key_finding: A fused clinical, imaging, and pathology model predicted 5-year ccRCC recurrence with an independent-test AUROC of 0.967 (95% CI 0.929-1.0).
limitations_as_stated: Acquisition limits differ by modality and center, and the authors note that the modeling choice has to be matched to the prediction task.
other_key_outcomes: Single-modality AUROCs included 0.640 for an ultrasound model and 0.741 for a stronger single modality. A discussion comparison also cites a radiomics C-index of 0.924.
extraction_note: The external AUROC of 0.967 on 55 patients has a confidence interval that reaches 1.0 and should be checked for overfitting or an unusually separable test set.

title: Multiphase CT-Based Tumor and Peritumoral Radiomics for Characterization of Clear Cell Renal Cell Carcinoma.
study_design: Retrospective single-center comparison of tumor, peritumoral, and combined multiphase CT radiomics for stage, grade, and aggressiveness of clear cell renal cell carcinoma.
data_source_detail: Single-center cohort of 250 patients with pathologically confirmed ccRCC and four-phase CT.
data_modality_detail: Four-phase CT radiomics from the tumor and a 5 mm peritumoral shell, with 1,874 features per region per phase
algorithm: Elastic-net logistic regression and random forest with tenfold stratified cross-validation
input_features: Tumor-region radiomic features, with the nephrographic phase compared against peritumoral and multiphase sets
biomarker_result: Nephrographic-phase tumor-region radiomic models for binarized stage, grade, and aggressiveness
performance_value: Best tumor-region elastic-net AUCs 0.915 (95% CI 0.881-0.949) for aggressiveness, 0.875 (0.822-0.928) for stage, and 0.697 (0.628-0.765) for grade
validation_detail: Tenfold stratified cross-validation on one center, with feature selection inside each fold. There is no external cohort.
funding: No external research funding. Open-access charges were supported by SCELC.
conflicts_of_interest: V. Duddalwar has consultancy engagements with Radmetrix, Roche, Deeptek, and Westat.
key_finding: Tumor-only nephrographic CT radiomics outperformed peritumoral and combined regions, with cross-validated AUCs of 0.915 for aggressiveness, 0.875 for stage, and 0.697 for grade.
limitations_as_stated: The single-center design and sample size limit generalizability, there is no external validation, clinical variables were omitted, and sensitivity for high-grade tumors was low (0.147 for the best grade model).
other_key_outcomes: Peritumoral and multiphase inputs did not beat the tumor-region nephrographic model. Stage models had specificity above 0.94 and sensitivity of 0.34-0.44.
extraction_note: Analytic N is the full 250-patient cohort used in tenfold cross-validation. Aggressiveness is listed first because it has the highest tumor-region AUC; stage and grade are co-reported.

title: Predicting Response to Neoadjuvant Hormonal Therapy and Prognostic Outcomes in High-Risk Prostate Cancer Using MRI-Based Radiomics
study_design: Retrospective single-center radiomics study predicting pathological complete response to neoadjuvant hormonal therapy, and related disease-free survival, in high-risk prostate cancer.
data_source_detail: Fudan University affiliated Huadong Hospital, January 2017 to January 2025; 140 patients split into training n=95 and internal validation n=45 (44 complete responses and 96 incomplete responses).
data_modality_detail: Radiomic features from preoperative ADC maps
algorithm: Support vector machine radiomics signature (C=12, gamma=0.0012) combined with clinical MRI and pathology features; logistic regression and random forest were compared. Classifier choice used 10-fold cross-validation repeated 5 times
input_features: Eight ADC radiomic features, seminal-vesicle invasion, and cribriform adenocarcinoma
biomarker_result: Combined ADC radiomics model for pathological complete response to neoadjuvant hormonal therapy
performance_value: Combined model AUC 0.909 (95% CI 0.852-0.965) in training and 0.947 (95% CI 0.882-1.012) in internal validation; SVM radiomics AUC 0.872 in training and 0.923 in validation
validation_detail: One center was split 95/45. Repeated 10-fold cross-validation selected the classifier, while the reported AUCs are on the internal validation split. There is no external cohort.
funding: Not applicable, as stated by the authors.
key_finding: A combined ADC radiomics model predicted pathological complete response with an internal-validation AUC of 0.947, and a higher predicted probability was associated with better disease-free survival.
limitations_as_stated: The preprint presents a larger single-center series with internal validation, but it remains retrospective and single-center.
other_key_outcomes: Clinical-feature AUCs were 0.723 in training and 0.784 in internal validation. This Research Square preprint was later published as REC-AIBIOGU-001023. The authors cite a high Radiomics Quality Score.
extraction_note: This is the same Huadong Hospital enrollment window as the published Zhou 2026 paper, with a different split and a validation confidence interval that exceeds 1 (1.012).

title: Predicting response to neoadjuvant hormonal therapy and prognostic outcomes in high-risk prostate cancer using MRI-based radiomics.
study_design: Retrospective single-center radiomics study predicting complete or minimal residual response to neoadjuvant hormonal therapy, and related disease-free survival, in high-risk prostate cancer.
data_source_detail: Fudan University affiliated Huadong Hospital, January 2017 to January 2025; 140 patients split into training n=98 and internal validation n=42.
data_modality_detail: Radiomic features from preoperative ADC maps and T2-weighted MRI
algorithm: Support vector machine radiomics signature combined with clinical MRI and pathological features; nested cross-validation checked feature-selection optimism
input_features: Thirteen radiomic features (eight from ADC and five from T2-weighted images), seminal-vesicle invasion, and cribriform adenocarcinoma
biomarker_result: Combined ADC and T2-weighted radiomics model for complete response, defined as pathological complete response or minimal residual disease
performance_value: Combined model AUC 0.932 (95% CI 0.884-0.980) in training and 0.979 (0.939-1.000) in internal validation; ADC plus T2-weighted radiomics validation AUC 0.952 versus 0.923 for ADC alone
validation_detail: One center was split 98/42. Tenfold and nested 5-fold checks were used during training; the headline AUC is the internal validation split. There is no external cohort.
funding: Key Specialized Disease Construction Project of Huadong Hospital (ZDZB2222).
key_finding: Adding T2-weighted features to ADC radiomics predicted complete response to neoadjuvant hormonal therapy with an internal-validation AUC of 0.979, and higher predicted probability tracked longer disease-free survival.
limitations_as_stated: The series is larger than earlier work and uses internal validation, but it is still a single-center retrospective cohort without an external test.
other_key_outcomes: Clinical-only AUCs were 0.723 in training and 0.784 in validation. This published paper shares the center and enrollment window with preprint REC-AIBIOGU-001020 but uses a different feature set and split. A high Radiomics Quality Score is cited.
extraction_note: This is the published counterpart of REC-AIBIOGU-001020. The shared cohort should be checked before synthesis, and the validation confidence interval reaches 1.000.

title: Radiomics-based interpretable machine learning model from multiphasic CT imaging for predicting pathological grade in upper tract urothelial carcinoma: a multicenter study.
study_design: Retrospective multicenter radiomics study predicting pathological grade of upper tract urothelial carcinoma from multiphasic CT urography.
data_source_detail: 338 patients after radical nephroureterectomy: training n=236 at center 1 (June 2015-June 2024) and external test n=102 from centers 2 and 3 (June 2017-June 2024).
data_modality_detail: Multiphasic CT urography radiomics from non-contrast, arterial, and venous phases
algorithm: LightGBM, compared with XGBoost, SVM, and a multilayer perceptron; LASSO with five-fold cross-validation for feature selection and SHAP for interpretation
input_features: Sixteen LASSO-selected radiomic features (4 non-contrast, 9 arterial, and 3 venous), including wavelet NGTDM contrast
biomarker_result: LightGBM multiphasic CT radiomics model for high-grade versus low-grade upper tract urothelial carcinoma
performance_value: LightGBM AUC 0.945 in training (sensitivity 84.5%, specificity 91.2%) and 0.829 in the external test set (sensitivity 71.8%, specificity 77.4%); XGBoost training AUC was 0.930
validation_detail: The test patients came from two additional centers. Five-fold cross-validation selected the LASSO penalty and was not the reported test metric.
funding: Medical Health Care Ecosystem Innovation Team of the First Affiliated Hospital of Chongqing Medical University (CYYY-DSTDXM-202409), Chongqing Municipal Education Commission 14th Five-Year Key Discipline Support Project (20240101), and an annual Chongqing research project.
key_finding: A LightGBM model of multiphasic CT urography predicted high-grade upper tract urothelial carcinoma with an external AUC of 0.829.
limitations_as_stated: Although the data are multi-center, the sample is still relatively small, and larger datasets from more diverse regions are needed.
other_key_outcomes: LightGBM had the smallest drop from training to test among the compared algorithms. SHAP highlighted wavelet texture features linked to high-grade tissue.
extraction_note: Analytic N is the 102-patient external test set that supports AUC 0.829.

title: Radiomics-based tumor heterogeneity augments clinicopathological models for predicting recurrence in high-risk clear cell renal cell carcinoma after nephrectomy.
study_design: Retrospective multicenter study of CT radiomic heterogeneity for recurrence-free survival after nephrectomy in high-risk clear cell renal cell carcinoma.
data_source_detail: 194 high-risk non-metastatic ccRCC patients from hospitals including the First Affiliated Hospital of Zhejiang University School of Medicine, the Second People's Hospital of Yuhang District, and the First Affiliated Hospital of Ningbo University. Training n=147 and external test n=47.
data_modality_detail: Preoperative corticomedullary-phase CT radiomics (107 IBSI features extracted with PyRadiomics)
algorithm: Random survival forest, with Boruta selection and 10-fold cross-validation on the training set, compared with the Leibovich score and a combined model
input_features: Corticomedullary-phase texture, shape, and intensity features, with tumor volume among the most important inputs
biomarker_result: CT radiomics risk score for recurrence-free survival, alone and combined with the Leibovich score
performance_value: External-test time-dependent radiomics AUC 0.882 at 1 year (95% CI 0.779-0.986), 0.865 at 2 years (0.707-1), and 0.793 at 3 years (0.616-0.969), versus Leibovich 0.781, 0.762, and 0.797; combined-model test AUCs 0.853, 0.851, and 0.780
validation_detail: The paper reports one external test cohort within a multicenter series. Tenfold cross-validation was limited to training-parameter selection. The test set is not described as several held-out centers.
funding: Zhejiang Provincial Natural Science Foundation of China (LTGY24H180003) and the General Project of the Hangzhou Health Science and Technology Program (B20253445).
key_finding: A corticomedullary CT radiomics model predicted recurrence-free survival better than the Leibovich score at 1 and 2 years on the external test set (AUC 0.882 and 0.865).
limitations_as_stated: The sample is small, with selection bias and class imbalance. Predominance of high-stage tumors limits generalizability, and prospective validation is needed.
other_key_outcomes: The combined model had the highest decision-curve net benefit at 2 and 3 years. Training radiomics AUCs were 0.929, 0.895, and 0.886 at 1, 2, and 3 years. The authors state that no datasets were generated or analyzed.
extraction_note: Analytic N is the external test set of 47 patients in Table 2. Time-dependent AUC is the printed metric; a C-index is not given.

title: Urinary volatilomics using liquid-liquid extraction and gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS) combined with machine learning algorithms as a tool for diagnosis and surveillance of urothelial bladder cancer.
study_design: Case-control urinary volatilomics study using liquid-liquid extraction GC-MS and machine learning to diagnose urothelial bladder cancer.
data_source_detail: Urine from 50 patients with urothelial bladder cancer and 50 healthy controls. Among the patients, 36 had recurrence and 14 were new diagnoses. Sample collection was supported through Liverpool Biobank.
data_modality_detail: Urinary volatile organic compounds measured by liquid-liquid extraction and gas chromatography-mass spectrometry
algorithm: XGBoost, compared with AdaBoost, gradient boosting, random forest, logistic regression, and naive Bayes
