input_features: GC-MS volatile features reduced to an eight-metabolite panel
biomarker_result: Eight-metabolite urinary volatile panel for urothelial bladder cancer versus controls
performance_value: XGBoost AUROC 0.869 (95% CI 0.740-0.988), versus a classical statistical AUROC of 0.752; the eight-metabolite panel had balanced sensitivity and specificity of 85%, or 95% sensitivity with 70% specificity at a screening threshold
validation_detail: Five-fold cross-validation repeated 10 times, plus additional random splits. There is no external cohort.
funding: Cancer Research UK grant C45856/A21068 (Chris Probert and Henry Lazarowicz), with support from the University of the West of England and the Bristol and Weston Hospitals Charity.
key_finding: An XGBoost model of urinary volatiles separated bladder cancer from controls with AUROC 0.869, above a classical statistical model at AUROC 0.752.
limitations_as_stated: The study is not longitudinal, so surveillance over time is untested. The authors recommend a longitudinal design to evaluate whether the markers track cancer progression.
other_key_outcomes: AdaBoost, gradient boosting, and random forest had AUROCs of 0.846, 0.823, and 0.814. The recurrence subgroup of 36 patients is described but is not the primary diagnostic comparison.
extraction_note: Analytic N is the 100-participant cross-validation cohort that supports AUROC 0.869.

title: Connecting Histopathology Imaging and Proteomics in Kidney Cancer through Machine Learning.
study_design: CPTAC ccRCC proteomics and histology with random-forest and CNN classifiers of tumor versus normal.
data_source_detail: CPTAC clear-cell renal cell carcinoma discovery cohort; 194 samples (110 tumor, 84 normal) with 9964 proteins.
data_modality_detail: TMT proteomics of the top 10% most variable proteins, paired with H&E images.
algorithm: Random forest (500 trees) on proteomics; VGG16 CNN for histology.
input_features: 997 most-variable proteins for the random forest; H&E image tiles for the CNN.
biomarker_result: Proteomic panel used to separate ccRCC from normal kidney.
performance_value: Proteomics random forest AUC 0.99 and accuracy 0.98 on 10-fold cross-validation; histology model accuracy 0.95 on the held-out image test set.
validation_detail: Ten-fold cross-validation for proteomics. Histology used a separate image test set from the same CPTAC cohort.
key_finding: A proteomic random-forest classifier separated CPTAC ccRCC from normal kidney with AUC 0.99, and proteins correlated with the histology predictions mapped to immune, matrix, and metabolic pathways.
limitations_as_stated: NR
other_key_outcomes: Histology CNN accuracy 0.95 on the test images, with sensitivity 1 and specificity 0.93.
extraction_note: The performance endpoint is tumor versus normal classification in one public cohort, not a prognostic or treatment-response biomarker.

title: A Critical Analysis of the Robustness of Radiomics to Variations in Segmentation Methods in 18F-PSMA-1007 PET Images of Prostate Cancer.
study_design: Single-center 18F-PSMA-1007 PET radiomics study of segmentation robustness and low- versus high-risk classification.
data_source_detail: 78 patients (43 low risk, 35 high risk) with three segmentation methods.
data_modality_detail: 18F-PSMA-1007 PET radiomics (original, LoG, and wavelet features).
algorithm: Hybrid feature selection with KNN, SVM, and LDA classifiers.
input_features: 1781 radiomic features extracted after manual, threshold, and region-growing segmentation.
biomarker_result: Region-growing LDA radiomic model separating low- from high-risk prostate cancer.
performance_value: Region-growing LDA: accuracy 74.49%, AUC 79.20%, sensitivity 84.38%.
validation_detail: Performance is reported by segmentation method on the same 78-patient cohort. No external center is described.
key_finding: PSMA-PET radiomics separated low- from high-risk prostate cancer, with the best LDA result after region-growing segmentation (AUC 79.20%). Shape features were the least robust to segmentation.
limitations_as_stated: Radiomics reproducibility is limited by segmentation method.
other_key_outcomes: GLCM features were the most robust feature class across the three segmentation methods.
extraction_note: The primary aim is segmentation robustness. The risk-model AUC is reported, but the split used for that AUC is not stated as an external cohort.

title: A disease-centric vision-language foundation model for precision oncology in kidney cancer.
study_design: Multi-center kidney CT vision-language foundation model evaluated for anatomy, diagnosis, and survival.
data_source_detail: Pretraining 21819 CT series from 6867 patients. Evaluation 1942 patients, including an internal test of 100, a five-center external cohort of 1017, and a TCIA cohort.
data_modality_detail: Contrast and non-contrast kidney CT aligned with radiology-report text.
algorithm: RenalCLIP two-stage vision-language pretraining with task-specific fine-tuning.
input_features: Kidney CT volumes and paired report text.
biomarker_result: RenalCLIP imaging representation used for malignancy, aggressiveness, and survival.
performance_value: Internal-test ROC AUC 0.908, 0.646, 0.857, 0.747, and 0.713 for R.E.N.A.L. features R, E, A, L, and N.
validation_detail: Fine-tuning on 400 internal patients, internal test n=100, combined external test n=1017 from five centers, plus a TCIA cohort.
key_finding: RenalCLIP outperformed general-purpose foundation models on kidney CT anatomical, diagnostic, and survival tasks and kept performance on external centers.
limitations_as_stated: NR
other_key_outcomes: External-test ROC AUC 0.902, 0.610, 0.715, and 0.727 for R, E, N, and L.
extraction_note: n_analytic is the internal test set that supports the printed R.E.N.A.L. AUCs. Survival metrics are described but the printed numbers in the crop are the anatomical AUCs. Code and data availability were not in the first pages.
